sig_0f15f690a6a1f19f021a.description: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales. These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: - An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. - A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense. - An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System - A Warehouse Management System - Other BI Reporting Systems The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment. The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement. The main objectives of this exercise are to: - Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS), - Test market capability and capacity, - Validate the proposed scope and service model, - Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and - Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project. Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk). When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that: - the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions; - they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the service; and - they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments. Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October. There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered. Lot 1: . None

sig_0f4c5d5d65aa6b4c1926.description: This competition replaces the previously announced competition 2026/2237, which was cancelled 14.08.2026. The system shall contribute to strengthening situational comprehension in Norwegian sea areas by using image forming sensors (optical and SAR – Synthetic Aperture Radar). This shall enable: verification of AIS data detection of vessels that do not send AIS (so-called "dark vessels") improved situation understanding and decision support in the operative contexts The coastal system has tested the use of non-cooperative sensor data from satellites in the summer and autumn 2025 through the company Vake AS's presentation and analysis system (vake.ai.). The testing of data in Vake is based on optical and SAR sensor data from Sentinel-1 and 2 satellites in the EU's Copernicus programme and on AIS data from the Norwegian Coastal Administration. Developments in this procurement cannot be included. Tenderers shall document that the offered system was established and operative at the tender deadline. The documentation shall, at a minimum, consist of: A technical description of the offered system, including main functionality, used data sources and central analysing functions. Screen images showing central functions in the system, including visualisation of satellite data, object detection and analysis functionality. Information on the date of production of the system to the customer. Description of the system's operative use for at least one customer or final user. Documentation that substantiates actual operative operations before the tender deadline expiry, e.g. customer confirmation, operational reports, uptime reports, user statistics or equivalent. The contract will be valid for one (1) year, with an option for an extension.

sig_0f53a03dbad4c54b0407.description: The purpose of this contract is the SERVICES FOR THE ANALYSIS, DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A VIRTUAL AGENT COORDINATION SYSTEM (CoVA) APPLIED TO INTERGENERATIONAL ASSISTANCE FOR THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE PRINCIPALITY OF ASTURIAS which enables a proactive and efficient administration, covering both processes and people and the technology necessary for its proper use, security and management. This contract is part of Public Procurement of Innovative Technology (CPTI), its purpose has an innovative content and employs functional specifications, rather than technical requirements: It is aimed at the acquisition of a service that does not exist in the Principality of Asturias, but can be developed in a reasonable time, given that the technology is at a degree of development that allows it to do so. The main tasks included in this contract are the following: a. Implementation of a virtual agent coordination system based on artificial intelligence applied to intergenerational assistance for the Administration of the Principality of Asturias that allows the exploitation of the data generated and managed. b. All services necessary for the commissioning of the contracted elements, necessary subscriptions/licences, as well as their management and maintenance during the pilot demonstration phase. c. The exploitation of the potential of the data of the Administration of the Principality of Asturias (hereinafter, APA) to implement new forms of public management based on interoperability and data analytics. d. Establish the technological and procedural bases for the implementation of a proactive administration that allows the optimisation of public expenditure while maximising its performance. e. The development of techniques/rules for the automated management and classification of data, documents and files using advanced Artificial Intelligence techniques. f. The incorporation of deep learning techniques since these digitalisation processes can produce immense amounts of data for training and thus be able to provide processing that increases efficiency, effectiveness and intelligence in the processing of data in the processes of Public Administrations. g. The creation of a corporate data space that includes origin data, those that may have been inferred during the scope of use of the system, as well as facilitating interoperability and administrative processing circuits. h. Creation of a proactive care and assistance environment with citizens. i. Creation of a specialised sandbox that serves as an ideation and experimentation environment. j. Integration with the APA's electronic file processing system (SITE), and other applications and systems indicated in these specifications. k. Ensuring the artificial intelligence (AI) supply chain, for which measures will be implemented to guarantee the integrity and security of the artificial intelligence models at all stages, components and data used, with strict legal compliance with EU Regulation 2024/1689, and compliance with the decree 98/2025 regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the Administration of the Principality of Asturias.

sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.description: The Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications for research on the impact of technology and digital media on children and adolescents. Technology and digital media (TDM) encompasses social media, applications, websites, television, motion pictures, artificial intelligence, mobile devices, computers, video games, virtual and augmented reality, and other content, networks, or platforms disseminated through the internet, broadcasted, or other media technologies, as applicable. Collectively, they have become an integral part of our children’s and families’ daily lives. Most children and adolescents now engage with TDM starting from an early age, often with high levels of exposure across multiple devices and contexts and involving a wide range of content. There is therefore an urgent need to understand how TDM use and exposure impacts children’s health and development, as well as how it alters the very nature of interactions between children and their family members, peers, and society at large. As TDM has evolved with breathtaking speed, our understanding of its impacts – whether positive, neutral, or negative – on children’s health and development has not kept pace. This initiative intends to address this expanding gap by inviting research proposals on the impact of TDM on children and adolescents, including potential broader effects on their families and communities. Please note that applications are not being solicited at this time . This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize a phased R61/R33 mechanism. Investigators with interests at the intersection of TDM and child/adolescent development are encouraged to apply. In addition, collaborative teams that combine expertise across domains such as behavioral sciences, cognition and learning, computational and statistical modeling, computer science, geographic information science, library and information sciences, neurodevelopment, pediatrics, social and affective development and social sciences will be encouraged, and these investigators should also consider applying for this opportunity.
sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.title: Notice of Intent to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Impact of Technology and Digital Media Exposure Usage on Child and Adolescent Development

Askerkart is a web-based map system, but in connection with the current system supplier having notified transition to cloud, the municipality wants to update itself on the market situation and the different possibilities that exist. The dialogue meetings will be held in Asker municipality ́s premises in the period 3.11-7. 11.2025. The GIS tool shall be able to support the municipality ́s work with knowledge based decisions. We would like the map system to be easy to administer and it has a user friendly interface. We would like tenderers to give a general system demonstration so that we can get an understanding of whether this will fit into Asker municipality ́s ICT architecture/portfolio. We want the demo to say something about: • User administration of the system • Inhabitant services • 3D display in the system. • Analysing and reporting possibilities • data flow and possible system integrations • How the system itself is administered - what can we do ourselves Each tenderer can have up to three persons with good competence in the system. Asker municipality will provide an ICT consultant, as well as three representatives from the department Analyse og Geodata. Business sensitive information that is shared in the individual meetings will be handled confidentially. Tenderers wishing to participate can register their interest by email to elfrid.nygaard.stabellini@asker.kommune.no and at the same time state the preferred date for holding the meeting (03.11, 04.11, 05.11, 06.11 or 07.11). Any questions to the market dialogue can also be directed here and will be answered continuously. The registration deadline is 31.10.2025 Agenda for the dialogue meeting: 1. Presentation of meeting participants and cards on the municipality ́s need for a GIS tool. 2. General demo of the supplier ́s system. Documentation that shall be submitted after the dialogue meeting (deadline: 14.11.2025) 1. Presentation from the dialogue meeting. 2. Three reference customers with an equivalent system (with contact information). 3. Upper and lower price estimates for licences/subscriptions, rolling out and training per annum, including support. The estimates are not binding.

sig_0fb50bed29e9ea0eee15.description: The Trust is seeking a single strategic partner to deliver an integrated suite of corporate and professional services that enable school leaders to focus on educational outcomes while ensuring the Trust operates efficiently, safely, compliantly and sustainably. The successful supplier will provide integrated professional support services that are reliable, compliant, responsive and strategically aligned to the Trust’s objectives, through a single accountable management structure combining strategic advice, operational delivery, performance management, continuous improvement and innovation. The Services comprise the following ten service areas, described in full in the Specification: Financial Services- Operational and transactional financial management, management accounts, 5-year planning, VAT/ONS returns and audit liaison (Sage 200; circa 20,000 transactions per year). Communications, Marketing & PR - Brand and reputation management, media and PR, website and social media, prospectus and admissions materials, internal communications. sig_102ff7ec4d6d25cad1ab.description: The subject of the contract is a research and development project for the investigation and further development of AI-supported methods for side-channel analysis of cryptographic implementations. The focus is in particular on post-quantum cryptographic procedures as well as, as a reference, symmetric procedures (e.g. AES) on microcontroller and FPGA platforms. The contractor shall set up a measurement/test environment, select or generate data sets (current/EM, where applicable multimodal) and investigate robust model architectures, trace compression, test-time tuning as well as suitable evaluation metrics and workflows for reproducible evaluations. Optionally, approaches for the auto-formalisation of selected security proofs are examined as examples. Deliverables include reports and presentations, executive summaries, a practice-oriented guide, data sets, source code as well as an extended software toolbox incl. installation instructions, user manual and a short quick-start tutorial. sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.description: Die Bäder, Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH (BSF) originated from Thermalsolbad Salzgitter GmbH and Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH. BSF is a subsidiary of the City of Salzgitter and performs numerous tasks, particularly in the field of public services of general economic interest. It operates the thermal brine baths in Salzgitter-Bad with their extensive offerings, the municipal pool in Salzgitter-Lebenstedt with attractive family offerings, and the ice sports centre at Salzgittersee with various leisure offerings. In addition, BSF is the point of contact for organised sport in Salzgitter provided by the district sports association (Kreissportbund) and its numerous sports clubs, as well as the primary contact address for all queries relating to Lake Salzgitter. The contracting authority is planning the introduction of a uniform, cloud-based point of sale and administration system for its three facilities - the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad, the Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt, and the Eissporthalle am Salzgittersee. The aim is to optimise internal working processes and create a seamless, consistent customer experience across all premises. Currently existing, disparate software systems lead to significant organisational and technical challenges. Customers cannot use products (e.g. value cards or vouchers) across different premises, and support provided by various service providers complicates administration. A uniform system with central support by a single supplier is intended to solve these challenges, standardise technical operations, and improve customer service. A solution involving multiple different systems and subsequent connection to a common back-end system is not considered expedient from a technical and economic perspective. The subject matter of the contract comprises the following partial services: a. Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Eissporthalle Salzgittersee b. Optional: Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Stadtbad - Salzgitter-Lebenstedt c. Optional: Delivery of new access hardware and point of sale hardware for the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad d. Provision and operation of the SaaS-based back-end solution. The introduction is to take place in phases: - Eissporthalle Salzgittersee: after the season 2025/2026 from the 2. quarter 2026. Completion by no later than 15.09.2026 (season opening of the ice sports centre is on the last weekend of September). - Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt: expected in the 4. quarter 2026 - Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad: expected from the 1. quarter 2027.
sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.title: Cloud-based point-of-sale and management system for the Salzgittersee ice rink, the Salzgitter-Lebenstedt municipal pool, and the Salzgitter-Bad thermal brine bath

sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.description: Nordhessischer VerkehrsVerbund (NVV) has been 1995 the pace-setter for mobility in the North Hesse region. As a management level, we combine planning, financing and quality management for buses, trams and trains in the districts of Kassel, Hersfeld-Rotenburg, Werra-Meißner, Schwalm-Eder and Waldeck-Frankenberg as well as the city of Kassel. The subject of this tender is the commissioning of an agency or a service provider for the comprehensive support and strategic further development of our social media channels. The service contract is awarded for a fixed term of 3 years with options for the client to extend twice by one further year each time. The contractor must provide the following services: 1. The core task of the service provider consists in the long-term support of the existing social media channels of NVV. This includes the continuous adaptation of content and strategies to the changing dynamics of the respective platforms in order to ensure optimal reach and interaction with the target groups. The service provider creates a monthly editorial plan that prepares relevant topics of NVV, regional events (e.g. events with combo tickets such as ski jumping in Willingen or the Kassel Kulturzelt) and product presentations in a channel-specific manner. The plans are drawn up in close coordination with NVV and can be adapted at short notice if necessary. Furthermore, the service provider is responsible for planning and carrying out cross-platform campaigns (such as competitions etc.) taking data protection into account. Another important aspect is the maintenance of cooperations with regional providers and content creators. An advent calendar for one of the platforms is to be conceived and implemented annually, including the required photo production. In the field of photography and videography, the service provider is responsible for the needs-based creation and editing of image material. This includes at least one video shoot per month on site (A-content), the creation of at least two video contents with existing material (B-content) as well as at least two moving-image contents with animations (C-content). 2. The tasks of the contractor also include the strategic further development of the social media presence of NVV. 3. Furthermore, the contractor has to fulfil the task of community management including dialogue management. For this purpose, the necessary tools for processing social media activities must be provided and compliance with the community guidelines of NVV must be ensured. A prompt response to comments, fan posts, messages and reviews within eight hours during working hours (working days 8-17 o'clock) must be ensured. 4. The success of the social media activities is measured by quarterly reports from the contractor, which contain the most important key performance indicators (KPIs) of the platforms. The service provider interprets the statistics and derives recommendations for action. In addition, an annual report is produced. 5. For the fixed contract term of 3 years, a total budget of 400.000 euros net is available. This includes an annual advertising budget of 18.000 euros for all channels.
sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.title: Social Media

Installation of server-side components will be managed by the DDU Data Management and Computational Chemistry teams, with network provisioning supported by DTS. You will be able to access a range of open banking services including: payment initiation service providers (PISPs): let you pay companies directly from your bank account rather than using your debit or credit card through a third party, such as Visa or Mastercard account information service providers (AISPs): being an authorised AISP means that a company can access an individual’s bank account data from their financial institution with their explicit consent To help you find the services and suppliers to meet your needs you will be able to use the following filters: service type total contract value hosting and delivery capabilities This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) will run for 8 years. Benefits open banking will reduce customer transaction costs where card payments are the existing and only method of payment payments can be made directly from bank account to bank account without the need to repeatedly input details existing customers of the Payment Acceptance framework can transition to Open Banking includes real time bank account data to confirm payee account details reducing the risk of error payments and minimising losses due to fraud Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS Expires: 07/12/2031 How to buy You can access the Open Banking DPS through the Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace. you will need to select the ‘financial services’ section, and scroll to ‘Open Banking’ Select the ‘access as a buyer’ link. you will then be asked to either sign into your Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace account or register for one Accept the terms and conditions of the DPS as a buyer. You can then view and manage your ‘DPS category exports’ page where you will have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export (this is how you filter the suppliers to find those that can meet your needs) When creating a new category use the filtering tool to specify your needs and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘save category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From the ‘manage your category exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (the export is to an Excel spreadsheet). Close the DPS. Use your supplier shortlist to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers in your shortlist to bid against your detailed statement of requirements, evaluation criteria and contract format. Your supplier list is valid for 2 working days from the date of creation. If you do not use your list within 2 working days you will need to create a new supplier list (follow steps 6 to 10). You can use our eSourcing tool to run a competition or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. read guidance for our eSourcing tool Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your needs. You should allow enough time for suppliers to review, prepare a response and ask clarification questions. Evaluate supplier responses. Award the contract. Put a notification of the award on Contracts Finder. Documents Updates Crown Commercial Service (CCS) became Government Commercial Agency (GCA) on 1 April 2026. Documents published before this date may still refer to CCS. All contract documents remain valid for existing and new contracts, and there are no changes to how you work with us. We shall procure a notification system that sends SMS, email and any voice messages to relevant recipients. The primary need is map based notification of inhabitants and entities during operational episodes. The notification shall be sent to those who have registered for national addresses, or operate business activities within a given area. Operational events can be planned measures that result in a break in the delivery for technical work on the pipeline network, or in the event of pipeline breaks, leaks and other non-planned situations. For such events Bergen vann needs to be able to gather data for later reporting and statistics. This applies to both event and notification, duration and number of persons affected. The system shall also be used for notifying other municipal departments than Bergen water.

sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.description: The DOE Office of Science (SC), Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), Office of Environmental Management (EM), Office of Nuclear Energy (NE), Office of Electricity (OE), and Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Office (HGEO) hereby announce interest in receiving applications from interdisciplinary teams addressing the Genesis Mission National Science and Technology Challenges to accelerate scientific discovery and research and development (R&D) workflows using novel artificial intelligence (AI) models and frameworks. By achieving AI advantage, these teams will advance the DOE's mission and ensure America’s security and prosperity by addressing energy, environmental, and nuclear challenges through science and technology. Teams are encouraged to leverage the extensive scientific and data resources of the DOE/National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), the National Laboratories, U.S. industry, and academia. The resulting AI models and workflows, if successful, may be integrated into the American Science Cloud. DOE is soliciting new FY26 Phase I small team and Phase II large team applications in the following topic areas: advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, critical materials, nuclear fission, nuclear fusion, quantum information science, semiconductors and microelectronics, discovery science, and energy (see specific focus areas in Section III Program Descriptions). In addition, this RFA will remain available to allow the recipients of FY26 Phase I awards to apply for larger team Phase II awards. In a few weeks, DOE plans to amend the RFA to clarify the LOI and application guidelines for FY26 Phase II awards. In FY27, DOE plans to amend the RFA or to issue an alternative funding opportunity to update the topic and focus areas to allow a second competition of Phase I small team applications and Phase II large team applications.
sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.title: The Genesis Mission: Transforming Science and Energy with AI

sig_16a777e75b86af434518.description: The Ministry of Defence (MOD), through the Defence AI Accelerator Task Force (TF RAID), intends to procure a secure, scalable capability to support operational planning across Defence. TF RAID exists to accelerate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-enabled capabilities in support of Defence outcomes, working with users, technical specialists and industry to identify, test and transition operationally relevant solutions. This requirement is expected to support operational planners by improving access to authorised planning information, enabling reusable machine-readable planning knowledge, orchestrating analytical services, and supporting the modelling, testing and comparison of alternative Courses of Action (COAs). The procurement will be structured as a single competition with 2 Lots: - Lot 1 will focus on planning data, knowledge and analytical orchestration services; and - Lot 2 will focus on COA testing, evaluation and adaptation services. Suppliers are invited to bid for 1 or both lots. Together, the Lots are intended to improve the speed, quality, traceability and robustness of operational planning while maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency, security and interoperability within Authority-approved environments, including those handling information up to SECRET UK EYES ONLY where required. MOD will be seeking to compete this requirement through the Government Commercial Agency Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS/RM6200). Participation in any subsequent competition will therefore be limited to suppliers appointed to the relevant Lots of the AIDPS Framework who pass the shortlist filter exercise. Lot 1: Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services (PDKAOS). The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the integration of planning data, machine-readable planning knowledge and advanced analytical services. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and scale of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. Requirement Summary: The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Discover, access and exploit authorised planning information from multiple sources. • Create and maintain reusable representations of planning knowledge, expertise, assumptions, dependencies and relationships. • Assemble, configure and reuse analytical services in support of operational planning tasks. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce dependency on fragmented information sources, manual processes and specialist knowledge bottlenecks. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application. Lot 2: COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning. The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the representation of operational environments, modelling of Courses of Action (COAs), evaluation of alternative scenarios and adversary responses, and generation of evidence-based insights to support planning and decision-making. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and robustness of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Represent operational environments, actors, assumptions, constraints and dependencies in reusable and machine-readable forms. • Model, test and compare alternative Courses of Action. • Explore multiple operational scenarios, environmental conditions, assumptions and adversary responses. • Generate evidence-based insights to support adaptation and refinement of operational plans. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce reliance on manual wargaming, fragmented information sources and time-intensive analytical processes. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application.
sig_16a777e75b86af434518.title: DDAITF/013 Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services & COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning

The following equipment is intended in particular: mobile device, e.g., tablet, for recording and transmitting vital data as well as with communication function (chat/video), connected medical measuring devices: at least pulse oximeter, blood pressure monitor, body scales, and thermometer, cloud- or web-based software platform with secure access to a demo environment, remote maintenance and device replacement in the event of a defect, German-speaking support during business hours, training or technical instruction of the team staff (online or in person), repeatable if necessary. A rental or managed service model (term until the end of the project duration on 30.11.2029) is preferred. This should include maintenance, repair, and device replacement as well as a provision for loss/damage. Also of interest is the possibility of exchanging technically outdated devices during the contract period and easily adding further medical measuring devices if required. The application and support should be available in German. In addition, a low-barrier or barrier-free user interface is desirable. The planned award will be made as a direct order, taking into account economic efficiency and economy. Interested companies that consider themselves capable of providing the service are called upon to submit an offer by 24.09.2026, 10:00 o'clock. Binding period of the offers until 31.10.2026. Interested companies are requested to contact vergabe@uk-halle.de by e-mail by 23.09.2026 to receive the tender documents. sig_176a5d3078f78a0949cf.description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-12 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-12-challenge-2-scaling-dynamically-service-management-capabilities

sig_18505bd007cfba2ea6ae.description: Following an analysis of existing systems that revealed functional gaps related to reporting, early warning and funding tracking, the contracting authority has determined that the complexity of the Merheim campus project and the requirements of the funding providers necessitate an effective and transparent controlling and communication system. For this purpose, the contracting authority wishes to commission the implementation of an IT-supported system for construction and project controlling for the compliant and auditable management of all projects and sub-projects of the new health campus at the Merheim site, whereby transparency, traceability and early warning in particular must be ensured on all levels via system support. It must be ensured that the integration of existing systems and the connection of relevant interfaces take place smoothly. This includes the transfer and exchange of cost and financial data, the transmission of procurement information and contract award statuses, as well as the provision of structured, role-based access to relevant project data, plans and approvals for external service providers and suppliers. Furthermore, internal audit must be enabled through read-based access rights to ensure the traceability and documentation of internal audits.
sig_18505bd007cfba2ea6ae.title: Software for project controlling at the Merheim Health Campus

Südwestrundfunk (SWR), as a public service broadcaster of the ARD, is strictly dependent on a functioning IT infrastructure to fulfil its tasks. In the age of digital communication, central elements are necessary for efficient process control in order to be able to plan, execute, and implement processes digitally, both internally and across the entire ARD. Different software solutions for network management are currently in use at Südwestrundfunk and the eligible state broadcasting corporations. The network management tool CheckMK is already in use across the board at a large number of the eligible entities and is deeply integrated into the system landscape. As part of the ARD structural reform, a holistic solution is to be established across the entire ARD. For this purpose, services for the Checkmk product are to be procured for Südwestrundfunk and other eligible state broadcasting corporations. Furthermore, the eligible entities require further services such as consulting and support in the area of network management and for the CheckMK product. Südwestrundfunk (SWR) as the contracting authority and the eligible broadcasting corporations therefore intended to procure in two lots: • Lot 1: Services for the Checkmk product incl. support • Lot 2: Development and consulting in the area of Checkmk The contracting authority (SWR) / eligible entities place the following essential requirements on the services to be provided by the contractor: Lot 1: - Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Delivery services Services of the Checkmk product incl. support for a limited period. - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Advance payment guarantee Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 17 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 1) The acceptance quantities for Lot 1 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 5.6 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Number of services in units for Checkmk incl. support: Minimum acceptance quantity: 1.000.000 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 1.400.000 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1.800.000 units Acceptance quantities Checkmk Synthetic Monitoring: Minimum acceptance quantity: 10 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 200 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 500 units Acceptance quantities virtual appliances: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1 units per licence scale up to 600.000 services Lot 2: - Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Services Consulting and support services for the Checkmk product from Lot 1 Development, migration, and integration services - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 21 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 2) The acceptance quantities for Lot 2 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 6.8 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Service in hours: Minimum acceptance quantity: 200 hours, Planned acceptance quantity: 400 hours, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 600 hours Acceptance quantities Flat rate for incidental costs (incl. travel times) per on-site deployment: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 hours, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 hours, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 10 hours The start of the framework agreement for each lot is planned for 01.03.2027. In addition to the SWR as the contracting authority, the following public service broadcasting corporations as well as their subsidiaries and affiliated companies, provided that the participation of the public service broadcasting corporations is at least 50%, are involved in this framework agreement as eligible entities: • Deutschlandradio (DR) • Hessischer Rundfunk (HR) • ARD-Sternpunkt (represented by HR) • Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk (MDR) • Norddeutscher Rundfunk (NDR) • Rundfunk Berlin Brandenburg (RBB) • ARD-POC + Text (represented by RBB) • IVZ (represented by RBB) • Saarländischer Rundfunk (SR) • Südwestrundfunk (SWR) • Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR) Joint facilities (GSEA) for which the respective eligible entity has the lead are also eligible. The framework agreements will be concluded with an initial basic term of 24 months and two extension options of a further 12 months each. sig_188e0976d8f1b026399f.description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Headquarters, Space Technology Mission Directorate (STMD) will be releasing an Umbrella NASA Research Announcement (NRA) titled “Space Technology Research, Development, Demonstration, and Infusion-2026 (SpaceTech-REDDI-2026)” on or about December 9, 2025. The solicitation is available by opening the NSPIRES homepage at https://nspires.nasaprs.com/ , selecting “Open” under "Solicitations," and searching "Space Technology Research, Development, Demonstration, and Infusion-2026 (SpaceTech-REDDI-2026)" un- der Solicitation #/Keyword(s). Proposals will be solicited through Appendices issued under this Umbrella SpaceTech-REDDI-2026 Solicitation, as technology topics are defined and funding is made available. See STMD Solicitations and Opportunities ( https://www.nasa.gov/stmd-solicitations-and-opportunities/ ) for anticipated releases. Once new Appendices are released, interested parties will be able to access the Appendices by selecting “Open” under "Solicitations," and searching “SpaceTech- REDDI-2026” in the “Solicitation #/ Keyword(s)” search area, and then selecting “List of Open Program Elements”. It is anticipated that this Umbrella NRA Solicitation (SpaceTech-REDDI-2026) will be open for one year and Umbrella SpaceTech-REDDI Solicitations will be issued annually. NASA STMD leads the development, demonstration, and infusion of transformational space technologies that solve critical stakeholder needs. As the tech base for civil space, STMD advances technology to sup- port future NASA, other government, and commercial missions. STMD investments aim to (1) advance U.S. space technology innovation and competitiveness in a global context, (2) encourage technology driven economic growth with an emphasis on the expanding space economy, and (3) inspire and develop a powerful U.S. aerospace technology community. STMD bolsters and funds ideas from entrepreneurs, researchers, and innovators across the country. Space technology research and development occurs at NASA centers, universi- ties, national labs, and small businesses. Interested proposers should monitor the NSPIRES website. NASA Headquarters maintains an electronic notification system to alert interested parties of program announcements, including solicitations and associated amendments. Subscription to this service is free to all registered users of NSPIRES at https://nspires.nasaprs.com . To add or change a subscription to the electronic notification system for a specific pro- gram or a NASA Mission Directorate, users should login to the database system and select “Account Management,” then “Email Subscriptions.” It is the responsibility of the prospective proposer to check this solicitation’s NSPIRES page for updates. Further questions concerning the Space Tech-REDDI-2026 solicitation may be sub- mitted to: HQ-STMD-SpaceTech-REDDI@nasaprs.com . Responses to inquiries will be answered by e-mail and may also be included in the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) document located on the NSPIRES page associated with the solicitation; anonymity of persons/institutions who submit questions will be preserved.
sig_188e0976d8f1b026399f.title: Space Technology Research, Development, Demonstration, and Infusion (SpaceTech REDDI-2026)

sig_191dde4691cc3e047c8d.description: The Norwegian Environment Agency shall enter into a framework agreement with a provider who can cater for the organisation's total need for the procurement, administration and management of Microsoft licences and subscriptions. The objective of the procurement is to ensure cost-effective, flexible and future-oriented access to software, cloud services, licence management and accompanying consulting services. The framework agreement shall cover the delivery and management of Microsoft's licence and contract programmes, including the Enterprise Agreement (EA), the Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) programme, Server and Cloud Enrollment (SCE) and any subsequent or equivalent forms of agreement. The agreement shall also provide access to the purchase of standard software licences (off-the-shelf) from Microsoft and other relevant software suppliers. The contract's value is estimated to NOK 55 million. The maximum value of the agreement is NOK 65 million. Contracting Authorities The Norwegian Environment Agency, the Arts Data Bank, the Norwegian Cultural Heritage Fund, the Norwegian Polar Institute and the Directorate for Cultural Heritage are all contracting authorities for this contract. The Norwegian Environment Agency is responsible for implementing the tender competition and following up the contract and is the contract owner and will act on behalf of the other agencies in following up the contract.

sig_1951d05192e6de448c03.description: CLARIFICATION: This is ONLY a market exploration procedure to determine whether and, if so, which companies can offer the service intended for procurement. This preliminary information does not serve the purposes of Section 38 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The Munich Fire Department is planning, in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany, to tender and introduce an interface management system (≠ interface modelling system, see below) named "RESQON". RESQON is intended to make it possible to network all Integrated Control Centres (ILS) nationwide with one another and exchange data amongst each other. In addition, the system is to be used to connect external services with partly proprietary protocols to the various computer-aided dispatch systems of the respective control centre. RESQON consists of local instances at the control centres, which are to be combined into a network. This network is referred to as RESQON Mesh. Participating control centres can exchange incident data via RESQON Mesh. Within the RESQON Mesh there is a central instance, the so-called RESQON Core. RESQON Core provides external connections to standardised services such as, for example, AML and the nora emergency call app. Furthermore, connections to statutory health insurance control centres, to TPS service providers for eCall and police control centres are to be possible in the future. An elementary component of RESQON is an interface modelling system which allows various protocols and data to be transformed and, if necessary, process logic to be mapped using it. The interface modelling system is a component of every local RESQON instance. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- PLEASE NOTE: The purpose of this market exploration is to evaluate the availability of such interface modelling systems. This is also in particular in preparation for a possible direct award - in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany - in accordance with Section 14 Paragraph 4 No. 2 letter b) of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV), since the objective absence of competition for technical reasons must be demonstrated and, if necessary, proven by the contracting authority. This market exploration is therefore an essential part of the required comprehensive market analysis at European level. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- See additionally the document "2025-11-25_Markterkundung_Schnittstellenmodellierungssystem.pdf". This can be requested from the contact point via the e-tendering system. ======================================================== PROCEDURE FOR INTERESTED COMPANIES: Interested companies that consider themselves in a position to offer a corresponding product are requested to contact the contact point by email at: info@mayburg.de (providing contact details, at least email and telephone) by no later than Thu., 08.01.2025. The LH Munich - Fire Department - will then be informed accordingly and will seek further contact for the continuation of the market exploration or the market exploration procedure.
sig_1951d05192e6de448c03.title: Interface modelling system for RESQON

sig_1a09837a3d46dc7fd567.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of test manager and teamlead within S/4HANA for a product team in project P1160 "Critical Upgrade of ERP". The consultant shall assist with test coordination for product teams, as well as follow-up of teams within logistics, for the purpose of removing obstacles and ensuring speed and flow. The consultant will work closely with the manager of Value Management Office, the solution architects and the various product teams. The role can involve cooperation with other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.
sig_1a09837a3d46dc7fd567.title: Procurement of Test and teamlead within S/4HANA

sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.description: Background Trøndelag county needs a modern and comprehensive system for electronic substance register, which can support the entity's work on health, safety and the environment. The procurement is being carried out in order to ensure easy access to updated chemical information, contribute to compliance with the current regulations and facilitate safe handling of chemical products throughout the entire organisation. The county has a compound entity with different user groups and work areas, including sixth form colleges, laboratories, operation and cleaning functions, workshops, dental health services, road operation, administration and teaching environments. This sets requirements for a system that is user friendly, accessible and suitable for both employees and pupils, while at the same time being managed in an efficient way across units and professional environments. The aim of the procurement is to establish a joint system that provides a better overview of chemicals, supports local needs and at the same time enables central management and follow-up. Tenderers must therefore understand that the system shall function in a large and varied organisation, with a need for both broad availability and appropriate administration. Description of the assignment Trøndelag county shall procure an electronic substance register that is delivered as a site license for approx. 5,000 employees and 20,000 students. The system shall cover the county ́s need for registration, disclosure and management of information on chemical products across the entity. The delivery includes a digital system with functionality for i.a. search and access to safety data sheets, an overview of chemicals, as well as support for the accompanying HSE work such as risk assessment, substitute and exposure register. The system shall be suitable for different types of users and it can be used in both teaching related and operational contexts. Furthermore, the system shall support secure and efficient access management, including log-on and user administration adapted to the county ́s established identity management. A system is requested that combines user friendliness for local units with the possibility for general administration and control across the organisation. The design of the tender Tenderers shall fill in and respond to all points in the ESPD form, requirement specifications and price form. Any documentation beyond replies directly to the requirement specification shall be uploaded as pdf files, unless otherwise specified. The following shall be completed and submitted with the tender: · Complete Annex 1 - Tender Form · Digital requirement specifications and price form with reference to any annexes. · Completed data processing agreement with annexes. · Censured version of the offer
sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.title: Electronic substance register

sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.description: This is not a procurement notice nor a call for tenders, but a request for information through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying system suppliers to register for a potential tendering procedure. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social welfare, healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 6 000 professionals from various fields. Our vision is to be a pioneering community where services are accessible, the wellbeing of our population is among the best in Finland, and the occupational wellbeing of our employees is high. Our mission is to increase the health, functional capacity and security of our residents throughout their lives. Our values are “Mie turvaan”, “Mie uskallan”, “Mie vastaan” and “Mie välitän”. Strategic priorities include investing in personnel, smooth processes and the gradation of services. The realisation of these requires efficient, safe and user-friendly digital solutions. The roster planning system plays a central role in supporting the smooth flow of everyday operations, the occupational wellbeing of the staff and cost-efficiency. The purpose of the market dialogue is to obtain a comprehensive overview of the roster planning systems and related services available on the market. The information obtained can be used to assess what kinds of solutions exist on the market, what benefits they generate and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on the market offering and various suppliers' solutions 2. Understand the functionalities and key use cases of the systems 3. Explore integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 4. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 5. Gain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 6. Survey delivery and service models 7. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer systems or services falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the concept stage is not desired on this occasion. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: • what ready-made solutions and services they offer • in what kinds of environments the solutions have been deployed (example descriptions, no mandatory references) • the key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue All participants are offered equal opportunities to obtain information regarding the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, nor are procurement decisions made on the basis of it. If there is a large number of registered suppliers, the wellbeing services county may hold both a joint information session and a limited number of individual meetings. The market dialogue focuses in particular on how solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but thematic areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: • User management and information security • Working hours and shift management • Consideration of collective agreements and local agreements • Competence, qualifications and occupational health management • Usability and multi-user support • Reporting and information-driven management • Integrations with other systems • Mobile usage and employee services • Main administration, maintenance and support services • Intelligence and automation Pricing models and lifecycle services Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions also through a demo or practical example scenarios. The wellbeing services county will provide a set of questions in advance to guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared on an equal basis. The market dialogue will be conducted as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 60 to 90 minutes. The supplier will have the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. The wellbeing services county will also ask pre-defined questions that support the equality and comparability of the discussion. Meetings will be held on the following days: 21.10., 22.10., 27.10., 28.10. and 29.10.2025. The exact time will be agreed with the registered suppliers based on the order of registration and schedule coordination. The language of potential presentations/meetings is Finnish. Registrations are requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12:00. This request for information / market survey does not request tenders to be submitted nor are tenders given in response to this request for information; it requests ONLY procurement-related information. Participating or refraining from participating in the market survey / request for information does not affect the tenderer's position in any potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (supplier) to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is responding to this notice a precondition for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Those participating in the market survey have no right to compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not undertake to carry out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The submitted material will be handled as confidential in accordance with section 24, subsection 1, point 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities.
sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.title: Request for Information/Market Survey: Work shift planning system and related services

sig_1ab06211e4c143eb8191.description: Hereon requires external support for the migration of its SAP ERP system to S/4. The brownfield approach is to be used. This is a technical migration; potential improvements or optimisations will be carried out subsequently, decoupled from the migration. The subject matter of Lot 1 is the provision of comprehensive consultancy services for the planning, execution and documentation of the migration of the existing SAP ERP system to SAP S/4HANA. The services shall be performed in close coordination with the client's specialist departments. The contractor shall assume the following tasks: 3.1. Project planning and design - Preparation of a project schedule and content plan in close coordination with Hereon - Development of a migration concept including test design, definition of responsibilities and accompanying documentation 3.2. System analysis and process evaluation - Review of the existing SAP ERP systems with regard to the S/4HANA migration - Identification and evaluation of correction requirements in the implemented business processes - Communication of correction requirements to the specialist departments and verification of implementation 3.3. Archiving and system preparation - Archiving of FI and MM documents from completed financial years 2014-2019 - Setup of a sandbox system - Execution of necessary system copies from production to test systems 3.4. Migration and customising - Execution of the necessary customising - Execution and testing of the S/4HANA migration on sandbox, test and production systems - Review and adjustment of structural authorisations in connection with the Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS) - Analysis of existing roles and authorisations in the SAP ERP system as well as evaluation and application of new authorisation objects in the context of S/4HANA - Execution of the H4S4 conversion - Review and migration of the personnel cost commitment processor, ensuring functionality and data integrity in personnel cost planning - Connection of the SAP Enterprise Portal and support for the connection of the above-mentioned non-SAP products 3.5. Documentation and quality assurance - Preparation of audit-compliant final documentation of the migration - Support in the review of non-SAP software - Support during an internal security check (SAP Basis) 3.6. Training and hypercare - Preparation of (delta) training materials - Conducting training sessions for participating employees and key users - Provision of live support (hypercare) after the migration 3.7. Cooperation with the client - All services shall be provided in close coordination with the responsible specialist departments - Tasks that can sensibly be carried out by Hereon itself (e.g. non-SAP software, authorisation roles) shall be processed internally accordingly 3.8. Period and scope - The consultancy service is to be provided over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027.; As part of an ongoing SAP migration project, an external service provider is commissioned with Lot 2 to technically accompany and evaluate the project phases of concept review, test preparation and test execution as well as the final documentation. The objective is quality assurance and risk minimisation in the migration process, as well as ensuring audit-compliant documentation. The contract specifically comprises the following services: 4.1. Review of the migration concept - Analysis of the migration concept for completeness, consistency and feasibility - with a particular focus on ensuring that the planned documentation meets the requirements of an audit - Identification of potential risks and vulnerabilities, particularly with regard to the traceability and audibility of the migration steps - Preparation of an evaluation with recommended actions to ensure audit-compliant documentation 4.2. Support for test preparation and test execution - Advice on the planning and organisation of test activities (e.g. system, integration and acceptance tests) - Support in the definition of test cases and test data so that traceability and audibility for an audit are guaranteed at all times - Quality assurance during test execution with a particular focus on complete and audit-compliant logging - Evaluation of test results and derivation of measures 4.3. Review of the final documentation - Evaluation of project documentation regarding traceability, completeness and conformity with project objectives - Support in the preparation of handover documents so that all necessary evidence for a subsequent audit is available 4.4. Conditions of participation - Demonstrable experience in supporting SAP migration projects - Specialist knowledge of SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA - Experience in test management and quality assurance - Knowledge of standard project management and IT service management standards (e.g. PRINCE2, ITIL) 4.5. Period and scope The consultancy service is to be provided alongside the project over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027. The exact scope will be agreed upon when the contract is awarded.
sig_1ab06211e4c143eb8191.title: Migration SAP S/4 HANA

sig_1bdfd165987155c7367f.description: The aim of this project is the development and validation of a practical test catalogue / test guideline for evaluating the cyber security of complex autonomous vehicles of level L4 according to SAE J3016. The focus will be on the novel properties of complex systems and their novel technologies. This includes systems such as AI systems for perception, planning or sensor fusion, for example, or end-to-end systems. The interaction between non-AI systems and AI systems will also be examined. At the end of the project, a test guideline or test catalogue will be obtained which describes how complex systems in autonomous vehicles can be tested. In addition, tools and methods will be developed to enable testing. Through an iterative approach, experiences gained with the test catalogue are to be incorporated into a new iteration of the test catalogue. In addition, practical evaluation and a lessons learned part are to ensure that the test catalogue can be used for type approval or can support type approval, as well as generally representing a reference. The positive feedback of relevant stakeholders (other authorities, in particular BMV, KBA and BASt, the automotive industry and technical services) is to ensure that the developed methods and concepts (test catalogue, test tools and test process) prove themselves in practice and that tests can be carried out with them. sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.description: Background and Objectives of the Pathfinder Project: The Public Sector AI (PSAI) Directorate within the Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) exists to help the government make brilliant public services that empower people in the UK. We work at the very centre of government to drive digital transformation focused on user needs and to reimagine how government uses AI to deliver public services and initiatives. The newly established Government Efficiency Accelerator (GEA) programme is a flagship initiative aimed at driving operational efficiencies across some of the government's key enabling functions (Finance, Policy, HR) through the safe and responsible adoption of AI. The GEA is working in collaboration with the GCF Commercial Innovation Hub (CIH) to better understand the availability of AI based solutions that can be used by teams across government departments to drive efficiency and increase productivity. The goal of this Pathfinder Project is to engage with the market to understand current capabilities, initially focusing on three core business areas: Finance, HR and policy (more details on a specific problem area below). Applicants should note that this engagement is not intended to lead to the procurement of a particular solution for DSIT or any other UK Government Department. Rather, we are looking to build a catalogue of tested and "kitemarked" products that will be made available to public sector organisations to consider procuring them in the knowledge that they have been tested and will meet requirements such as security, usability, transparency etc. We are interested in hearing from all types of suppliers and would particularly encourage SMEs and VCSEs to submit proposals. Challenge Summary: As noted above, the GEA and CIH are engaging with the market to build a deeper understanding of how AI based solutions and products can help make government departments more efficient and productive. We appreciate there are a multitude of potential use cases so for this initial engagement we have chosen to focus on problems relating to budgeting and workforce forecasting. We are inviting suppliers to submit proposals outlining how their products could be used by finance teams across UK government departments in a safe, transparent and unbiased way. We are keen to explore solutions which can reduce the level of repetitive tasks required specifically when budgeting and conducting workforce forecasting. Submissions should demonstrate how the solution can streamline tasks, improve accuracy, and shorten time spent on repetitive work in order to free colleagues up to complete higher-value work. There is no fixed scope, as we aim for platform-agnostic, AI driven and innovative tools that adapt to various organisational needs. Solution should be accessible to organisations of all sizes and is not dependent on any specific ERP platform.
sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.title: GEA Pathfinder

sig_1ce7e51c86c3539cc86c.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an information request with which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying comprehensive digital solutions for the administration and implementation of surrogate payment for the personal assistance employer model, as well as the management of informal care, foster care and other fee-based contracts, and the payment of fees, other expenses, etc., and statutory official contributions. The aim of the survey is to find out what kind of comprehensive solutions containing the functionalities described below are available on the Finnish market. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on market supply and different suppliers' solutions 2. Potential implementation of integrations into various platforms or systems 3. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 4. Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 5. Survey delivery and service models The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer comprehensive solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The dialogue will focus on solutions that are already in production. Suppliers are requested to present services that are available and in which the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the conceptual stage is not desired on this occasion. When registering, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: Intended use and environment The system must be suitable for use by the wellbeing services county to manage the following service forms: - Informal care support and contract management - Foster care assignment contracts - Surrogate payment for the personal assistance employer model - Management of contracts for support families and support persons - Other similar contractual relationships User groups are: - Wellbeing services county employees (contract management) - Informal and foster carers (data entry) - Personal assistants and their employers - Other persons in a contractual relationship Key functionalities Contract management: - Electronic drafting and maintenance of assignment contracts - Contract lifecycle management - Recording of care days and working hours - Management of statutory leave Fee and salary processing: - Calculation of fees in accordance with care intensity categories - Payroll processing for personal assistants - Statutory payments and deductions - Processing of substitute carers' fees - Automatic inclusion of index adjustments Payment transmission: - Payment transmission operations approved by the Financial Supervisory Authority - Automatic payment processing - Generation of payment data files Integrations: - Direct data transmission connection to the Tax Administration - Possibility of integration into the wellbeing services county's other systems, particularly an interface to the accounting system - Data export and reporting (Data lake) - User account management via Entra ID Technical requirements - Cloud-based SaaS solution - Information security-audited system - Finnish-language user interface - Implementation in accordance with the Accessibility Directive - Continuous maintenance and updates - User support in Finnish We kindly ask you to answer the following questions: General description of the solution - Do you offer a system solution containing the functionalities described above? - What is the name of your solution and a short description? - What are the key strengths of your solution? Functionalities - How does your solution meet the described contract management needs? - What kind of fee and salary calculation features does the system include? - Does your solution have a licence from the Financial Supervisory Authority for payment transmission? - How is the Tax Administration integration implemented? Technical features - What is the technical architecture of the solution? - How is information security ensured? - What language options does the system support? Experience and references - In which wellbeing services counties / municipalities is your solution in use? - How many users does the system have? - Can you provide reference information on similar deliveries? Additional information - What other essential features does your solution include? - How is the system implementation typically carried out? - What kind of support and training do you offer? Responses to the questions are requested to be sent by 1.12.2025 at 15:00. Responses should be brief and informative. Responses are requested to be sent to the address hankinnat@ekhva.fi. Subject of the message: "Markkinakartoitus - omais- ja perhehoidon sekä henkilökohtaisen avun hallintajärjestelmästä ja ym. palkkioperusteisten sopimusten hallinta ja maksatus" This information request / market survey does not request tenders to be submitted, nor are tenders submitted in response to it; it requests ONLY procurement-related information. Participation or non-participation in the market survey does not affect a tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (Supplier) to participate in a tendering procedure, and answering this notice is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure at a later stage. Participants in the market survey shall not be entitled to compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The supplied material will be treated as confidential in accordance with section 24, subsection 1, point 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities. Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue thanks you in advance for your responses. They are valuable in defining our system needs and preparing for a potential procurement.
sig_1ce7e51c86c3539cc86c.title: Information request / Market survey: Survey of a complete solution for a management and payment system for family care, foster care and personal assistance, as well as similar fee-based contracts
