sig_1e637cd62aa7b58e2ba3.description: The Authority intends to procure a modern Corporate Technology Platform (Ecosystem) to replace fragmented and ageing legacy corporate systems and provide an integrated digital platform supporting key enabling services across Police Scotland. The requirement is for an integrated Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Human Capital Management (HCM) Ecosystem, together with the associated hosting, integration, implementation, data migration, training, transition, support and professional services required to deliver and sustain the solution. The Contract is expected to be for a period of seven (7) years with options, exercisable solely at the Authority's discretion, to extend by up to three (3) further periods of twelve (12) months each, giving a maximum potential duration of ten (10) years. Lot 1: . The Authority intends to award a contract to a single service provider for the provision of a Corporate Technology Platform (EcoSystem). The requirement is for an integrated Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Human Capital Management (HCM) Ecosystem, together with the associated hosting, integration, implementation, data migration, training, transition, support, and professional services required to deliver and sustain the solution. The scope of the Ecosystem contract will cover the following elements: MVP / Minimum Commitment (This is the minimum the Authority will commit to purchase as part of this contract): - HR - Payroll - Duty Management - Common platform services Optional Requirements (May be procured as either: a) additional modules within the proposed Ecosystem that will replace the system/solution currently in place, or b) integrations between the Ecosystem and the existing system or service, enabling data exchange, reporting, workflow triggers, or other interoperability without necessarily replacing the existing system): - Estates - Fleet - Finance - Procurement Contract Duration & Value: The Contract is expected to be for an initial period of seven (7) years with options, exercisable solely at the Authority's discretion, to extend by up to three (3) further periods of twelve (12) months each, giving a maximum potential duration of ten (10) years (120 months). The estimated total value of the Contract is approximately 51,000,000 GBP over the maximum potential contract duration. This includes initial and ongoing software licensing, software support and maintenance, cloud hosting, implementation services, and system integration services. Procedure & Negotiation Parameters: This procurement is being conducted using the Competitive Procedure with Negotiation (CPN). The Authority intends to invite a minimum of 5 qualified candidates to participate in Stage 2 (Invitation to Tender), subject to a sufficient number of compliant Stage 1 SPD submissions being received. In order to identify the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT), the Authority reserves the right to either: 1. Evaluate all initial tenders and award the contract without entering into negotiations; or 2. Commence negotiations with Bidders who submit compliant initial tenders in order to improve tender content. Bidders should note that initial tenders should be fully compliant and capable of assessment on their own merits without relying on negotiation or clarification. The Authority also reserves the right to apply successive stages during negotiations to reduce the number of tenders to be negotiated. Note: The Authority's minimum requirements and final award criteria are non-negotiable. Candidates must refer to the Corporate Technology Platform (EcoSystem) Information and Instructions for Candidates document available on PCS-Tender for full procurement details and instructions.. Candidates must refer to the Corporate Technology Platform (EcoSystem) Information & Instructions for Candidates on PCS-Tender. Non-compliance may result in submission rejection. Economic operators may be excluded from this competition under Regulation 58 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015.

The system should be able to manage both catering and retail operations as well as having the capability to offer additional functionality detailed in the specification below, to help facilities manage their daily financial transactions with a key driver being to reduce costs, drive sales and deliver better customer service. sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.description: In the field of road safety, the Safe System approach, recognised internationally and included in the “European Union Road Safety Policy 2021-2030” and the European Commission’s “Strategic Action Plan on Road Safety”, suggests acquiring greater knowledge about the different variables that influence road accidents —beyond the usual indicators, such as the number of accidents, deaths and serious injuries—, recommending the acquisition of other indicators, called Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), directly related to the prevention of deaths and injuries in traffic accidents. Among these indicators are the use of seat belts and child restraint systems, the use of helmets, vehicles travelling within the speed limit, drivers travelling within the legal blood alcohol limit, driver distractions and vehicle safety. These indicators constitute the object of this tender. The object of this lot is the design of a sampling plan for lots 2 and 3 and for the alcohol indicator and EDAP Study, obtaining the KPIs (except for KPI 6, whose calculation work remains within the scope of lot 4), and preparation of the dashboard.; The objective of lot 2 consists of carrying out measurements of speed and other characteristics of vehicle flow in a sample of 150 sections of the Spanish road network, in order to serve as a basis for the preparation and acquisition of the KPI 1 indicator; Carrying out fieldwork for the collection of data on the use of seat belts, child restraint systems (CRS), helmets and driving using mobile devices, by conducting non-participatory surveys in a sample of urban and interurban road sections, which allow the successful bidder of lot 1 to obtain these indicators (KPI 2, 3 and 5).; The object of this lot is the acquisition of the vehicle safety indicator (KPI 6).; The object of this lot is the management and supervision of the work of lots 1,2,3 and 4.
sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.title: Service for the preparation of reports on key performance indicators in road safety. 5 lots.

sig_1f3a2b4a4dcc01e9576c.description: The Norwegian Correctional Service shall procure parallel framework agreements for consultancy services. Consultants with experience within strategic consultancy, but not limited to: a) Strategy: scenario methodology and foresight, outside world analyses and strategy development b) Change management: Structured approach to leading individuals, teams and organisations from a current condition to a desired future condition. c) Performance management – some key words (not limited to, but relevant topics: process improvement, management tool/management system, target and result management, risk analyses and internal control. d) Reviews, analyses and evaluations: evaluation methodology and effect analyses. The Norwegian Correctional Service shall be more data driven and it needs more advanced analyses, predictive models, risk profile, prognoses etc., therefore there is a need for competence in data modelling and advanced analyses. e) Socio-economic analysis: methods for assessing and comparing the total costs and benefits of a measure for society as a whole. f) Cost estimation and uncertainty analysis: The process of calculating what a measure or project will cost, as well as assessing how secure or uncertain these estimates are and what factors can affect them. g) Profit planning/follow-up: Identifying, planning and ensuring that the expected gains from a measure or project are actually realised and measured over time. h) Innovation, design and service development: Need for competence in system design/management design in addition to service design i) KI: this means competence in KI and how the organisation can use this in an appropriate way. This also includes competence and experience on prerequisites and other consequences connected to implementation, from the technical to the more organisational sides. Competence/certification within recognised methods will be relevant. The sub-area covers the business perspective, and in some cases may overlap sub-area 2A.; Consultants with experience within operative management and consultancy services. The consultants shall contribute to the execution of deliveries in the form of, but not limited to: a) Project management: planning, organising, implementing and following-up a project in order to achieve defined goals within given frameworks for time, cost and quality. b) Management of development projects - competence in flexible methodology c) Alteration projects: manage and coordinate activities that shall carry out a planned change, with a focus on both technical deliveries and human factors such as involvement, communication and anchoring. d) Implementation project: ensure new systems, systems or processes in an organisation and ensure that they are implemented, anchored and used as planned. e) Digitalisation projects - The Norwegian Correctional Service shall digitalise several internal work processes and externally between actors in the criminal case chain as well as management cooperation partners. f) Preliminary projects and concept reviews: reviews the needs, assesses alternative solutions and recommends the most appropriate concept before the main project starts. g) Test management: Planning, managing and following-up test activities to ensure that a system or product fulfils the requirements and functions as expected. The Norwegian Correctional Service has started extensive work of renewing the ICT system and as a result of this need, both top competence and the capacity to carry out small and large projects. Competence/certification within recognised project implementation methods (e.g. the Project Wizard, Prince2 and/or other methods/framework) and flexible methods will be relevant.; Consultants with technical and developer competence, including, but not limited to: a) Architecture (business, business, security, information, application architecture) b) Development, further development and maintenance c) Utilisation of large data, advanced analysis and KI/machine learning. d) Integrations, data exchange, machine interface, API e) Design and user friendliness f) Technical assistance for infrastructure g) IT security and privacy h) Skyreise - The Norwegian Correctional Service needs expertise in cloud architecture and specifically the Microsoft Cloud Technology platform It is important to ensure the correct architecture and sufficient security as an important part of the renewal of ICT systems in progress. sig_1f78a83939231b7ec8b5.description: Award of services for the implementation of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund. We are looking for a contractor to take over the central management of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund and the numerous associated tasks. Background: The Founders' Fund, operated by Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt on behalf of the City of Frankfurt, has been a cornerstone of Frankfurt's start-up support since its introduction in 2010. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund has since established itself and is now an integral part of the start-up activities of the City of Frankfurt am Main, Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt and the Frankfurt-Rhine-Main ecosystem. In 2009, the foundation stone for the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was laid. The microfinance study commissioned at that time revealed that young companies were facing a financing gap for credit requirements. On this basis, the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was launched. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund project is currently being operated by an external contractor (hereinafter referred to as the Contractor) and is the responsibility of Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt GmbH as the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the Contracting Authority). In addition, professional administration is necessary to ensure transparency, efficiency and sustainability. The Contractor, who is commissioned with the administration and implementation of the fund, must therefore have sound experience in the field of start-up financing, project and portfolio management and, ideally, in working with public institutions. Furthermore, knowledge of risk management, supporting founders and developing suitable monitoring and evaluation instruments is required. The Contractor will work closely with the Bürgschaftsbank Hessen and partner banks and offer founders a proven financing and coaching model. An essential part of the success model is not just the financial support for start-ups, for which Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt assumes 80 % of the guarantee, but also extensive support included in the Founders' Fund programme in the form of coaching by the Contractor throughout the entire loan term. In summary, the Contracting Authority expects the following services from the new Contractor: - Organisational services - Information and enquiry management - Review and processing of financing enquiries - Support/accompaniment of financing projects - Measures for loan defaults, early warning system - Debt collection and processing - Reporting and monitoring - Marketing/communication - Cooperation and community network maintenance

sig_214e7ee6c2bc7fe072c3.description: The City of Helsinki Urban Environment Division is establishing a dynamic purchasing system, within which equipment and goods procurements for snow management solutions will be tendered. During the duration of the dynamic purchasing system, all interested candidates may submit a request for participation. The operation and scope of the dynamic purchasing system are described in more detail in the invitation to participate and its attachments. According to the preliminary estimate, dozens of procurements will be carried out within the dynamic purchasing system over the coming years. The total value of the procurements is estimated to be a total of 19 500 000 euros during the entire duration of the DPS for comprehensive service procurements. The dynamic purchasing system is used to prepare for future procurement needs, which will be implemented in sufficient numbers to achieve the objectives. This is an estimate, and the contracting authority is not committed to any procurement quantities. The number of procurements may be significantly lower than estimated if the objectives of the snow management entity are met by other means. sig_22950ad748b46de96910.description: Forsvarsministeriets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse (”FMI) wishes to enter into a contract regarding the delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles. The existing system is intended to be replaced by a more modern, reliable and user-friendly solution that supports efficient booking, lending and return of pool vehicles as well as providing FMI with access to relevant operational and administrative data. The purpose of the contract is to ensure the Danish Defence a comprehensive solution that, with a minimum of resource consumption from FMI, enables secure, flexible and efficient management of pool vehicles across the organisation. The solution must support both open and closed vehicle pools, be able to handle a large number of users and vehicles, and contribute to high availability and continuity in the Danish Defence's transport solutions. The contract comprises the supplier's delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of the overall system, including both the application and the infrastructure necessary therefor, for use by the Danish Defence's pool vehicles, as well as the delivery, installation and operation of electronic car-sharing equipment in the vehicles. The contract includes a start-up period consisting of a development period and an implementation period, during which the system is adapted, developed and commissioned in accordance with FMI's requirements. The supplier is responsible for the delivery of the application and for the infrastructure necessary therefor, including hosting the system on servers located in Denmark. The system is delivered as an internet-based solution (SaaS), and the supplier is responsible for all operation of the underlying infrastructure. The supplier is responsible for the integration of existing data regarding users, pools, pool vehicles and bookings, as well as for any reuse of already installed electronic car-sharing equipment. The system must support self-service access for users, comprehensive administration and reporting functions for FMI, as well as technical support and a round-the-clock manned helpdesk. The contract runs for 72 months from signature. The contract may be extended on the same terms by up to 2 times 24 months. It is a requirement that the development period must have a maximum duration of 6 months and that the implementation period must have a maximum duration of 6 months. The current system handles approx. 25.000 users and 2.800 pool vehicles. During the contract period, the solution is as a starting point expected to be able to handle up to approx. 5.000 pool vehicles. In view of the uncertain international security policy situation, however, the Danish Defence has a need for an option to be able to scale the solution so that the application and the associated infrastructure can, upon the customer's request, be expanded to handle up to 10.000 pool vehicles without impairment of functionality, response times, availability or the other requirements and service levels set out in the contract. In addition, the contract includes an option regarding the choice of access technology for the pool vehicles, whereby the customer, instead of using the Danish Defence's existing access carriers (RFID etc.), can choose an access and locking system supplied by the supplier on the terms set out in the requirements specification and the contract.
sig_22950ad748b46de96910.title: Tender for a contract regarding the supply, operation, maintenance, support, and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles

sig_23103fc3ebc0597973b3.description: The project includes the supply and installation of equipment for the creation of a national electronic citizen authentication system compliant with the highest security standards and compatible with the European Regulation (eIDAS 2.0) and the European Digital Identity Regulation, which will offer an advanced set of authentication services. Additionally, it includes the creation of a central Citizen Identity Hub and the infrastructure for providing qualified electronic signature certificates to Greek citizens. Overall, the offered system must be able to successfully serve the entire production-issuance cycle (collection of supporting documents and biometric data, management of applications and data, personalisation of security documents, quality control of personalised documents) of security documents. The Contracting Authority considers the reasonable delivery deadline for the Integrated Security Documents Information System, its related implementation services, as well as the digital identity and authentication services (hereinafter “Main Project”), to be the period of 18 months. Within the framework of the Main Project, the Contractor must implement and deliver the following: Implementation Study, Delivery of Project Equipment and ready-to-use Software, Implementation services for development - operational environment and development, Integration Services, Trial migration and Acceptance Testing period, Training, Trial Operation Period. After the final delivery and acceptance of the Main Project, the operation and maintenance period of ten (10) years begins, during which the contractor will provide the following services: - Operation and maintenance of the system - On site support - Telecommunications services - Supply of other consumable materials (envelopes, barcode labels, cardboard boxes). - Supply and Personalisation of security documents. Specifically: Period A (3 years): During the first three (3) years from the final acceptance of the Main Project, the contracting authority will procure 6.420.000 security documents of type ID1 and 1.050.000 security documents of type ID3. Period B (7 years): During the remaining seven (7) years of the contract duration, the contracting authority will procure up to 32.580.000 security documents of type ID1 and up to 7.150.000 of type ID3, according to its needs. At the same time, it will be able to personalise other security documents (format ID-1, ID-3) in case it is required in the future. At any time during the operation and maintenance period, following a decision by the Contracting Authority, an option may be exercised with the object of: a) extending the provision of the operation and maintenance period services for an additional period of up to 5 years in total, from its original expiry date, and/or b) extending the duration of the supply and personalisation services for security documents until the quantities of the contract are exhausted and, in any case, not beyond five (5) years from the original expiry date of the operation and maintenance period. The option may be exercised by a unilateral declaration of the contracting authority to the contractor once or more times for a minimum period of one (1) year and a maximum of five (5) years.

sig_2366bcd26f0a92db294b.description: HUS (hereinafter also referred to as the Contracting Authority or Client) requests to participate in the procurement of imaging solution and related services. The procurement will be carried out through a competitive dialogue procedure (see Annex 1 Description of the Procedure). The object of the procurement is imaging solution and related services. This procurement concerns the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS), which is intended to be replaced with a new solution. The solution entity may also include functionalities of a Radiology Information System (RIS), an artificial intelligence (AI) platform designed to support the achievement of the objectives, and functionalities related to appointment booking/scheduling, as well as a speech recognition solution. The objective is to ensure that the service path between appointment booking system, the radiological information system (RIS), and the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) operates optimally. The aim is to develop customer experience based on a unified service model. The objective is to provide patients with more efficient diagnostics and good care also in the future. In addition, the objective is to reduce the manual and overlapping work. The imaging solution must enable smooth workflows for all user groups and support the development of processes to improve productivity. The deployment project may include the migration of images, image metadata, and RIS data from the Client’s current PACS system. The service includes support and maintenance activities and may also include 1 level support provided by the Supplier. The objective is also to explore solutions for scalability regarding a joint archiving solution for digital pathology and imaging. A more detailed description of the current state, the solution to be procured, and the services included in the procurement can be found in Annex 2 Current and target state description of imaging systems. Please also take into account the other annexes to the request to participate (Annexes 2.1–2.6, and 4), which provide additional information on the current and target state. These annexes are not binding on the Contracting Authority in the later stages of the procurement procedure and may be subject to change during the negotiations. If the documents have been drawn up in both Finnish and English, in the event of conflict of interpretation, the Finnish text shall prevail. The request for participation, along with all related documentation and any clarifying questions, must be submitted in Finnish or English in accordance with the instructions provided in the request to participate. sig_25691773fadd0d99dd05.description: Gloucestershire ICB and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) ICB are merging to form a single integrated body in April 2027. Both organisations currently rely on external providers for the delivery of their IT services. A new, unified service model is required; one that supports the merged organisation from day one, is commercially sustainable, and is capable of evolving as the ICS matures. Six principles shape the design of the future service: 1. Cloud-first and 'secure by design'. All new and renewed services will be cloud-based wherever possible. On-premises infrastructure will be exited as part of transition. This is both a strategic choice and a compliance requirement under the Government Cloud First Policy and Technology Code of Practice. 2. Outcome-focused. The service is defined by what it must deliver, not how it must be delivered. The supplier is expected to bring expertise, innovation and accountability for outcomes, not simply execute a prescriptive technical specification. 3. Single point of accountability. The preferred model is a single managed service provider with end-to-end accountability for operational delivery. This avoids the fragmentation and unclear ownership that characterises the current multi-supplier landscape and reduces the management overhead on the ICB digital team. 4. Lean governance. The ICB digital team will provide strategic oversight, roadmap ownership and supplier governance. It will not carry operational delivery responsibilities. This reflects the lean, strategically focused character of the merged organisation and the direction set by the Model ICB Blueprint. 5. Interoperable by design. The service must integrate cleanly with nationally contracted NHS platforms, in particular NHS.net Connect, the Health and Social Care Network (HSCN) and NHS Secure Boundary Service, as well as local platforms, such as the Gloucestershire ICS WAN and into UHBW and Crown Datacentres in Corsham. Service interfaces with these platforms should be clearly defined before the procurement specification is finalised. 6. Sustainable. The ICB's carbon neutral commitments should be reflected in technology choices, including energy-efficient end-user devices, PoE-powered monitors and cloud-based infrastructure in preference to on-premises data centre equipment. The following service stacks are in scope for the new managed service, reflecting services currently provided across both incumbents, consolidated and extended to support the merged organisation: - Service desk. The primary user-facing support channel, available 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday. - Desktop support. Onsite presence at both sites as and when required, including end-user support, moves, adds and changes to desktop arrangements, MFD, Audio Visual equipment, and Teams Room management. The onsite support model must include provision for routine physical tasks including WFH equipment management, peripheral replacement, cable and hardware swap-outs, and stock management. - End-user compute. Device lifecycle management including provisioning, refresh (five-year target cycle), configuration, and secure disposal. - Telephony and unified communications. Microsoft Teams Phone as the unified platform for the merged ICB. - Print. Cloud-managed secure print at both sites. - Meeting rooms. Physical teams Room management and audio-visual support at 2 locations with 15 meeting rooms at one and at Shire Hall, Gloucester and 9 at the second location. - Asset management. Asset tagging, recording, and lifecycle tracking for all ICB-owned IT equipment. - Supplier and procurement management. The supplier will assume management of all ongoing third-party technology relationships and will procure all IT equipment and recurring support contracts on behalf of the ICB. Licence management across the estate is required. - DSPT support. The supplier is expected to provide the ICB with the technical evidence and assurance data required to support annual DSPT submission, including patch management records, asset inventory, access control logs and incident reports. - Project, change and architecture. The supplier will own project and change management, problem management, and architecture design. - Digital signatures. Digital signature capability is required as part of the new service. Full details are provided in the service specification. The total maximum contract value for the initial 3-year Contract is £1,920,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable). At the end of the initial contract term the Commissioner will have two, separate, consecutive one-year extension option periods that can be exercised at the discretion of the Commissioner, giving a maximum possible contract value of £2,700,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable) over 5 years if the full contract term is fulfilled. The Commissioner is of the view that TUPE does not apply to this service. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to use the Direct Award procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 for any subsequent extensions or new contracts for similar requirements. The new contract will commence on 1st April 2027, although implementation of the services will start during January 2026. Lot 1: .

sig_26e1b91d8504330c38df.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information with which the contracting authority is conducting a market survey of potential tenderers and solutions available on the market for its procurement need. The information obtained through the market survey will be used in the preparation of the future procurement. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) has a need to procure technology to be taken home for the use of the wellbeing services county's residents, as well as an alarm system that receives the alarms produced by the aforementioned technology. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is assembling and launching as its own operation a so-called Safety Assistance Service, the goal of which is to enable and support customers' independent coping in their own homes around the clock. A central element in the Safety Assistance Service is the technology utilised in it that is taken to homes or home-like services, and the receiving system for the alarms produced by them. With this request for information, LUVN wants to survey the technology solutions available on the market that are suitable for social and health care, that ensure the customer's safety at home, and solutions suitable for receiving alarms related to these. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue estimates that the procurement entity according to its needs will consist of the following parts, but changes may occur in the entity: - Technology installed at home for the customer's safety (e.g. sensors, detectors, wristbands) as well as their maintenance and backup device services - Safety alarm centre system and mobile software possibly related to it - Service implementation project - Continuous services, support, maintenance and service of the technology and alarm centre system - Expert services related to the aforementioned technology and its utilisation and use during the contract period according to the subscriber's need. To support the specification of its procurement needs, the planning of the procurement and the preparation of the tendering documents, Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue wants to engage in a market dialogue with suppliers offering solutions corresponding to the procurement need. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county hopes to receive information generally about solutions on the market corresponding to the object of the procurement. We are interested in your solutions and services related to safety technology supporting living at home and how the solutions direct alarms to the safety alarm receiving system and what features the receiving system includes. We also want to know what kind of information your system produces to support the planning of services offered to the customer for the professional, in addition to alarm information. Suppliers are requested to register for the market dialogue by email to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi Registration is requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12. The registration should be titled as follows: “Kodin turvapalvelulaitteet ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä” (Home safety service devices and alarm receiving system). The content of the email message is sufficient to be the supplier's name and the contact details of the supplier's contact person. LUVN will be in contact with the contact persons of the suppliers who have registered to agree on the implementation of the market dialogue. According to the wellbeing services county's plans, the market dialogue should include both discussion sessions and the exchange of written material, but the exact schedule of the dialogue will be specified later. The subscriber reserves the possibility to organise one-to-one market dialogue discussions in addition to commenting on written material. The subscriber reserves the right to select a suitable number of Suppliers for one-to-one discussions based on the written responses. The times for the one-to-one discussions will be agreed separately with the Suppliers. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The description of the procurement and the estimated schedule of the procurement procedure as well as other information presented in the market survey notice are preliminary and indicative advance information. Responding or not responding by companies does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation is paid for participation. The contracting authority will treat the information provided by the registered companies confidentially, and the names of the companies or other information will not be published.

sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.description: NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The programme will support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes and/or those diagnosed with primary hypertension, through the delivery of evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising a Selection Stage and an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage. Suppliers will be shortlisted following evaluation of their suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience, with a maximum of five suppliers invited to submit a tender. Lot 1: . NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The Framework will support NHS Scotland's strategic objectives to improve population health outcomes, reduce health inequalities and support the prevention and management of long-term conditions through evidence-based, digitally enabled interventions. The requirement comprises a single integrated service with two pathways: - Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme (DDPP) for individuals identified as being at increased risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes; and - Primary Hypertension Programme (PHP) for individuals diagnosed with primary hypertension, supported through lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to improve health outcomes and reduce cardiovascular risk. The appointed Framework Participant will be required to deliver evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to support participants in achieving sustainable improvements in health behaviours and clinical outcomes. The service will utilise a digital platform/application supported by appropriately trained personnel, including health coaching and clinical governance arrangements, to facilitate participant engagement, self-management, education, monitoring and behaviour change. The service is expected to support a range of participant needs and will include, as appropriate, digital onboarding, risk assessment, lifestyle intervention, coaching support, educational resources, progress monitoring, outcome reporting and onward referral or escalation processes where clinically indicated. The Authority seeks a solution that is accessible, inclusive and capable of supporting diverse populations across Scotland, including individuals who may experience barriers to participation arising from geography, deprivation, language, disability or digital exclusion. The Framework Participant will be expected to work collaboratively with NHS Scotland, NHS Boards, Primary Care and other relevant stakeholders to support the promotion of the programme, participant recruitment and self-registration, service mobilisation, programme delivery, performance monitoring and continuous improvement. Current funding has been identified to support approximately 15,000 participants through the Diabetes Prevention pathway during the initial three-year term of the Framework Agreement. The Hypertension pathway is anticipated to support approximately 500 participants per annum. These figures are provided for information only and do not constitute a guarantee of volumes. The Authority reserves the right, subject to future funding availability and service requirements, to increase participant volumes and/or expand the scope of the Framework to include additional prevention cohorts, pathways, clinical indicators or service requirements that are closely aligned to the subject matter of the Framework Agreement. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure. Suppliers will first be assessed at Selection Stage through completion of the Single Procurement Document (SPD) and Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ), which will assess suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience. A maximum of five suppliers will be shortlisted and invited to participate in the Invitation to Tender stage.
sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.title: Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme

Lot LOT-0001: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Project Racoon. 2.1 NVIDIA Deep Learning System DGX B300 Cluster - Lot 1 Required procurement of four NVIDIA DGX B300 systems for the efficient processing of computationally intensive AI issues (e.g. medical imaging, digital pathology, omics, and NLP). The system serves as central infrastructure and enables the flexible provision of GPU workstation environments for university partners in the RACOON joint project via advanced virtualization with DGX OS / NVIDIA Enterprise AI. The new systems integrate seamlessly into the existing management infrastructure, which is based on the NVIDIA Base Command Manager and NVIDIA Mission Control. This ensures highly efficient, consistent administration without additional familiarisation or migration effort for the operations team. Since all algorithms and AI models are based on the proprietary NVIDIA CUDA architecture, the system has no technical alternative; a transition to other architectures or APIs would be associated with a disproportionately high and economically unjustifiable effort. In addition, the existing GPU cluster management is built natively on this software stack. The selected Blackwell generation (B300) offers the only adequate performance class with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs, 2304 GB total memory, and a 800 Gbit/s InfiniBand connection. Furthermore, the enormous power density (10 U in the rack at max. 15,1 kW per system) guarantees resource-saving integration into the capacity-limited data centre. Lot LOT-0002: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Projects Athene. 2.2 NVIDIA GPU servers, network, and Spark cluster - Lot 2 The procurement serves to expand and optimize the existing infrastructure of the Research Compute Cluster (RCC) to meet the growing demand for high-performance resources for AI and data-intensive research applications. The NVIDIA DGX Spark systems enable the development, testing, and inference of AI models in the same NVIDIA software environment as the central GPU servers of the RCC. As a result, developed applications can be transferred to the higher-performance RCC resources without fundamental adaptations. The additional GPU server expands the central computing capacity of the RCC and is used in particular for medical AI, image analysis, genomics/metagenomics, as well as the training and inference of large AI models. Integration takes place into the existing Slurm-based infrastructure. To connect the additional components, the existing management and BMC network infrastructure is also expanded by a technically identical SuperMicro SSE-G3748R-SONIC. This ensures a uniform and operationally consistent infrastructure without establishing a separate network solution.

sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.description: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (hereinafter referred to as RED) is designed to build upon previous efforts in engineering education research. Specifically, previous and ongoing evaluations of the NSF Engineering Education and Centers Division program and its predecessors, as well as those related programs in the Directorate for STEM Education, have shown that prior investments have significantly improved the first year of engineering students’ experiences, incorporating engineering material, active learning approaches, design instruction, and a broad introduction to professional skills and a sense of professional practice – giving students an idea of what it means to become an engineer. Similarly, the senior year has seen notable change through capstone design experiences, which ask students to synthesize the technical knowledge, skills, and abilities they have gained with professional capacities, using reflective judgment to make decisions and communicate these effectively. However, this ideal of the senior year has not yet been fully realized, because many of the competencies required in capstone design, or required of professional engineers, are only partially introduced in the first year and not carried forward with significant emphasis through the sophomore and junior years. The Directorates for Engineering (ENG) and STEM Education (EDU) are funding projects as part of the RED program, in alignment with the Improving Undergraduate STEM Education (IUSE) framework and Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) initiative. These projects are designing revolutionary new approaches to engineering education, ranging from changing the canon of engineering to fundamentally altering the way courses are structured to creating new departmental structures and educational collaborations with industry. A common thread across these projects is a focus on organizational and cultural change within the departments, involving students, faculty, staff, and industry in rethinking what it means to provide an engineering program. In order to continue to catalyze revolutionary approaches, while expanding the reach of those that have proved efficacious in particular contexts, the RED program supports four tracks: RED Planning (Track 1), RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2), RED Innovation (Track 3), and RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4). Two- and four-year institutions are encouraged to submit to any track as appropriate for their goals and context. RED Planning (Track 1) projects will support capacity-building activities at institutions of special interest to NSF’s mission, including two-year engineering-centered programs building transfer partnerships, two-year or four-year institutions in EPSCoR jurisdictions, Primarily Undergraduate Institutions (PUIs), and Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs) in order to create more opportunities in engineering for students in every part of the country. Planning projects should provide the support for such institutions to explore the development of a RED Projects in Tracks 2, 3, & 4. RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2) projects will adapt and implement evidence-based organizational change strategies and actions to the local context, which helps propagate this transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation (Track 3) projects will develop new, revolutionary approaches and change strategies that enable the transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4) projects will achieve the same goals as Track 3 projects across multiple institutions. Of particular interest to this track are projects partnering two-year institutions with other eligible institutions. Projects in tracks 2, 3, & 4 will include consideration of the cultural, organizational, structural, and pedagogical changes needed to transform one or more departments to ones in which students are engaged, develop their technical and professional skills, and establish identities as professional engineers or technologists. The focus of projects in these tracks should be on the department’s disciplinary courses and program. RED project initiatives are expected to be institutionalized at the end of the funding period. Proposals are especially encouraged that address areas of increased national interest including but not limited to advanced manufacturing, advanced wireless, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, microelectronics and semiconductors, net zero technologies, sustainability, systems engineering, and quantum engineering.
sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.title: IUSE / Professional Formation of Engineers: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (IUSE/PFE: RED)

sig_2a19c6e7c46b70946e86.description: Framework agreement iBS II Lot LOT-0001: Integrated Control System (iBS). The integrated control system (iBS) is a subsystem of the integrated control and operating system (iLBS) and includes, amongst other things, the central services of the iBS (iBS-Z), integrated operator terminals (iBP) in accordance with the redundancy regulation 2, the reference image function (RBF), iBS communication (iBS-Kom) as well as the iBS-Z console. The iBS subsystem is connected to other iLBS subsystems via standardised interfaces, thereby enabling the operation of integrated sub-centres (iUZ) with electronic interlocking / digital interlocking (ESTW/DSTW). Lot LOT-0002: Transfer network router. The transfer network is a component of the iLBS system and implements communication between all transfer network participants (e.g. iBS-Z, iLBS-ZE and central directory service) in the overall iLBS system up to the network layer (OSI layer 3). This does not include: VPN LST gateway modules, all components of the transport network, the time standard receiver (e.g. DCF-77) or the middleware broker. (including all system components for redundancies). The components are thus used both at the interlocking location (TSO or existing interlocking) and at the locations of the individual iBS, the BSO. Lot LOT-0003: Broker and directory service. A component of the iLBS is a network of broker servers via which the components and subsystems communicate with each other (via Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP)). (including all system components for redundancies). The brokers are thus used at the iBS and LMC locations. A broker pair (redundant design) is always required at each location. The brokers use the AMQP protocol or Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (JBoss EAP) as a platform. For the hardware, 2 HU per physical broker instance in the computer cabinet are provided in the 19 inch rack. The installation depth of 700 mm must not be exceeded. Cooling of the brokers must take place from the front. (see also system specifications requirements specification DiB-0454). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0004: Local routing plan management (LLPV). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0005: Operational management of the central directory service (ZVD) of the LMC and the transfer network of the iLBS . The operational management for the central directory service and the transfer network (transmission system consisting of transfer network router, broker, etc.) comprises organisational, technical and documenting activities required to keep the test systems usable for planned tests. The framework will cover population health management software solutions that enable analysis and management of health data from a variety of sources to improve healthcare delivery and decision-making. This will empower Approved Organisations and stakeholders to deliver proactive, personalised care while improving efficiency and supporting preventative health interventions. Also can support addressing health inequalities and the wider social determinants and support the decision-making process across the health and social care sector. The framework is divided into three lots: Lot 1: Population Health Management Digital Solutions Delivery of population health management systems that will support the NHS's and other public sector organisations desire to deliver population level health and care across whole, or large-scale areas of the population - for example, an integrated care system, a city or town, a health community, a large acute Trust or a local authority - or multiples of these. As part of securing and modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring Data Diode solutions to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centres (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre and an Option to extend the Contract and replace the Data Diode Hardware. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of certified Data Diode appliances, comprising dedicated Hardware and associated Software, certified in accordance with Common Criteria or EUCC at EAL4 or higher. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the Data Diode solutions as part of its trust service infrastructure. The Data Diode solutions must provide one way traffic from the Agency's isolated Root CA environment to other network zones, while preventing any data transfer in the reverse direction. The solutions must support integration with the Agency's existing infrastructure and the required protocols for transfer of files, time information, monitoring and logging data. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of four Data Diode appliances for deployment across the Agency's production and staging environments in two data centers, together with the required Standard Software and deployment in the Agency's test and development environments; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Standard Software and Hardware, security patching, product lifecycle management and hardware replacement; and (c)Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options; and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract.

sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.description: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a complex disease involving interactions among many different cell types, tissues, organs and biological processes. Genetics, the environment, and lifestyle all play a role in disease development and progression. Over the past two decades, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) has supported major T1D research consortia covering basic, translational, and clinical research. Each consortium has focused on different aspects of T1D, such as specific organs, stages of disease or clinical outcomes. Together, these consortia have collected large longitudinal and multimodal datasets using standardized protocols and coordinated studies. While individual consortia have improved our understanding of specific areas, combining their work offers a rare opportunity to see how different biological processes interact to drive T1D development and progression. This integrated view can answer fundamental questions about T1D biology that cannot be answered using individual datasets or studies alone. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) now make it possible to integrate these complementary datasets and study T1D across various tissues, disease stages, and biological levels. Building on these resources, NIDDK will support a coordinated, milestone-driven research project to answer fundamental questions about T1D biology and accelerate the development of personalized medicine. The project will combine multimodal human pancreas and clinical datasets to better understand how biological processes interact as T1D develops and progresses. The research will generate new insights into T1D biology, help us understand the different forms and stages of T1D, identify biomarkers, and inform new approaches for disease prevention, intervention, and treatment. To support the research, the project will develop and test advanced multimodal AI models. It will also develop AI-enabled research workflows, new methods to integrate data, and privacy-preserving synthetic datasets.
sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.title: Multimodal AI to Accelerate Precision Medicine for Type 1 Diabetes (U01- Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.description: This program will advance scientific community datasets to enable scientific discovery and innovation using artificial intelligence (AI) and other methods. Its goal is to increase the value that can be derived from existing scientific datasets by leveraging novel methods and artificial intelligence (AI). This will unlock new AI-driven insights. It can enable interdisciplinary research. It also enables investigations outside of the original motivation for data collection and analysis. The program seeks to 1) apply AI-based capabilities to feature extraction and metadata generation, and the integration of multiple datasets. 2) Develop robust data pipelines necessary for automated analysis of existing datasets and similar use-cases by AI tools and systems. 3) Augment and/or harmonize existing datasets to better enable use by AI data pipelines and automated analysis. Proposals should address dataset security and integrity. Governance and the process for scientific communities to contribute to the datasets should also be addressed. Proposals are encouraged to leverage existing resources. These may include NSF data platforms , the NSF Integrated Data Systems and Services program , the NSF-led National AI Research Resource , the Genesis Mission platform , or other national infrastructure. NSF is open to exploring partnerships with philanthropy, private industry, or the non-profit sector to support additional proposals or collaborative opportunities that will advance AI-driven scientific discovery through unlocking the value of high-impact scientific datasets. Expanding Participation in STEM, NSF Priorities, and Gold Standard Science: NSF prioritizes cutting-edge discovery science and engineering research, advancing technology and innovation, and creating opportunities for all Americans. NSF has established priorities set forth by Congress, the administration and the NSF director to promote NSF's mission . Proposers should review the list of NSF priorities and are encouraged to align their proposals with them, where appropriate. NSF also expects the highest standards of scientific rigor, integrity and adherence tenets of Gold Standard Science in proposals, as appropriate for the field of science and research modality.
sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.title: Unlocking Dataset Value for AI-Enabled Scientific Discovery (AI Datasets)

sig_2d9632169b86508efd34.description: Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) for Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust Lot 1: . Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to procure an Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) solution to support clinical documentation across a range of services and care settings. The solution should enable clinicians to capture consultations and generate structured clinical outputs including but not limited to documentation, clinical record notes, summaries, and correspondence, while integrating seamlessly into existing clinical workflows and digital systems. The aim is to reduce administrative burden and support more meaningful patient interactions, improving the overall patient experience through more engaged consultations, higher quality documentation, reduced errors, improved continuity of care, and shorter turnaround times for clinic letters and updates. It should also enable clinicians to spend more time focusing on the patient, while maintaining high standards of clinical safety, transparency, and documentation quality. The solution must support use across a range of real-world clinical environments, including inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, and community settings, where factors such as background noise, shared spaces, and variable connectivity may impact performance. The solution must also support consultations involving third parties (e.g. carers, family members, or interpreters), ensuring accurate capture, speaker differentiation, and appropriate inclusion within the output. The contract will be for 2 years with optional extensions for two more years. The procurement will be undertaken using the Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) RM6200. If you wish to register on this DPS you can find out how to do so here: https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6200?nav=0 Please note that all bidders for this requirement must be certified under NHS England's Ambient Voice Technology Self-Certified Supplier Registry. Details can be found here: https://digital.nhs.uk/services/ambient-scribing/ambient-voice-technology-self-certified-supplier-registry. Additional information: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust intends to create a DPS supplier shortlist on 13th October 2026 with the intention of issuing a capability assessment on 14th October 2026, to be returned by 21st October 2026. The intention is for the tender documents to be issued on 10th November 2026 to those bidders who have met the capability assessment requirements. Berkshire Healthcare reserves the right to amend these dates.

sig_30b8ea18f3ebeb9ed8d1.description: Lapin hyvinvointialue invites tenders for an entity comprising: 1. safety devices provided to the home Lapin hyvinvointialue for customers 2. alarm reception service 3. alarm reception system for producing the above-mentioned service as the wellbeing services county's own operation. In the procurement, safety devices refer to various safety devices provided to the home that can be used to improve the safety of a customer living at home. The safety devices to be procured are safety phones and their accessories, a positioning safety wristband and a solution for door monitoring in communal living. Alarm reception service refers to a service in which alarms coming through safety devices are received, an initial assessment of the need for assistance is made and the request is forwarded further to safety assistants. The service must operate around the clock every day of the year. Alarm reception system refers to a system with which the contracting entity can receive alarms from various safety devices and forward them as tasks to safety assistants. It is intended for Lapin hyvinvointialue to take over the alarm reception service as its own operation according to a preliminary schedule in spring 2028. The wellbeing services county procures the alarm reception service until the reception system has been put into use, after which the procurement of the reception service will end. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the tender invitation and its appendices, particularly in appendix 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". In the tender competition, one supplier is selected as the framework agreement supplier. Through the framework arrangement, the wellbeing services county procures safety devices and services from the selected supplier during the contract period as needed. The needs of the wellbeing services county may vary during the contract period, and the tender invitation does not commit to specific procurement quantities. The contract period of the framework agreement is fixed-term for two years, after which the agreement will continue until further notice. The contracting authority's intention is to conclude an agreement with the selected supplier as soon as the tender period has ended, the tenders have been compared, the procurement decision has been made and the appeal period has ended. According to the contracting authority's estimate, this time point will be during October 2026. The schedules for the implementation of device replacements and other measures related to commissioning will be agreed together with the selected supplier in a manner that takes into account the needs of both parties. In addition, an alarm reception system as a whole is procured from the selected supplier, which includes the delivery of the system and its ongoing service. The ongoing service agreement for the system is valid until further notice. The procurement has not been divided into lots because this is a unified entity formed of goods and services, the compatibility of all parts of which must be ensured. From the perspective of the safety of Lapin hyvinvointialue customers, it is important that one supplier is responsible for the functionality of the entire entity. The procurement notice has been published a second time because two previous procurement procedures had to be discontinued due to needs to modify the procurement documents.
sig_30b8ea18f3ebeb9ed8d1.title: Safety devices provided to the home, alarm reception service and alarm reception system

sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.description: The European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) is an independent intergovernmental organisation supported by 35 states. ECMWF is both a research institute and a 24/7 operational service, producing and disseminating numerical weather predictions to its Member States. This data is fully available to the national meteorological services in the Member States. The Centre also offers a catalogue of forecast data that can be purchased by businesses worldwide and other commercial customers. The supercomputer facility (and associated data archive) at ECMWF is one of the largest of its type in Europe and Member States can use 25% of its capacity for their own purposes. The organisation was established in 1975 and now employs around 500 staff from more than 30 countries. A description of ECMWF’s activities and infrastructure can be found at: https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/whatwedo. The purpose of this Prior Information Notice (PIN) is for ECMWF to provide advance notice that an Invitation to Tender (ITT) is being prepared for the future acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System. The ITT will seek proposals from Tenderers for licensing and support services for an advanced hierarchical data storage Management system and related consultancy services. The aim is to enter into a long-term contract for the procurement of these services, include commissioning, training of ECMWF staff and supporting the solution over the lifetime of the contract. At this stage neither expression of interest nor questions regarding the future ITT are possible and full and equal information will be published on ECMWF’s eProcurement Portal which will be accessible via https://procurement.ecmwf.int/. Further information for suppliers is available via https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/suppliers including information about registering for the Portal, where prospective tenderers can register free of charge and receive updates on procurement opportunities.
sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.title: Acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System

sig_325870b72bba15601c84.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A NOTICE OF THE COMMENCEMENT OF A MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is planning a tender process where the subject of the procurement is an HR system package for payroll, employment relationship management, personnel development, and travel and expense claim management, including an outsourced payroll service and a travel and expense claim service. The package also potentially includes a statutory archiving solution. The subject of the procurement also includes system implementation and commissioning, support and maintenance services, operational services, and further development services. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue’s payroll and travel and expense claim services are currently outsourced to Sarastia Oy. The services are managed in systems administered by the service provider, S365 HR and M2. S365 HR acts as the master data for personal information. Supervisors, employees and HR have access to the current HR system, which is currently used for employment lifecycle functions - HRD functions are not in use. The new system and service to be procured will support Länsi-Uusimaa’s desire to facilitate and lighten the administrative work of supervisors and to develop the HR system towards a more modern solution that includes HRD functions such as development discussions and the management of permits and qualifications. The goal is not only to select systems but also to build a functional and sustainable partnership with the supplier. The procurement tentatively includes, among other things, the following functionalities and features: - Outsourced payroll service, which will be implemented for all Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue personnel, excluding social benefits. sig_3302b5a39cb60ed79550.description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.
sig_3302b5a39cb60ed79550.title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?

sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) National Center for Injury Prevention and Control (NCIPC) is soliciting investigator-initiated gold standard research proposals to rigorously evaluate programs and policies for their impact on primary prevention of child sexual abuse (CSA) or problematic sexual behavior (PSB) among youth. For the purposes of this NOFO: CSA is defined as sexual victimization during childhood (younger than 18 years of age) perpetrated by an adult. PSB is defined as sexual behaviors among children (younger than 18 years of age) that are not developmentally appropriate and have the potential to cause harm to the child or children involved (including behaviors that are unintentionally harmful or inappropriate as well as behaviors intended to cause harm). Research funded under this announcement will strengthen the evidence base for primary prevention of CSA and PSB. Applicants must propose to rigorously evaluate a program or policy for primary prevention of CSA or PSB that addresses one of the following three research priorities: Programs or policies focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in digital spaces (e.g., downloading or possession of illegal images of children, nonconsensual image sharing, use of artificial intelligence to create fake explicit images of children); Programs or policies addressing the use of digital spaces for commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC) or sex trafficking (e.g., online recruitment of minors for sexual content creation, online advertisements soliciting minors for commercial sex acts, using technology to facilitate in-person meetings with minors for the purpose of sex); Organizational policy approaches focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in youth-serving organizations (e.g., community centers, youth development organizations, juvenile residential care facilities, faith-based organizations, group foster care).
sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.title: Rigorously Evaluating Approaches to Prevent Child Sexual Abuse and Problematic Sexual Behavior among Youth

sig_34cfb216a1e442309086.description: The Republic of Moldova is undergoing an accelerated and complex European Union accession process following the opening of accession negotiations with the EU in 2024. The accession process requires comprehensive alignment of Moldova's legal, institutional and policy framework with the EU acquis, as well as strengthened governance structures, institutional coordination mechanisms and implementation capacities at national and local level. In September 2025, Moldova successfully completed the screening process for all chapters of the EU acquis, enabling the transition to structured technical negotiations and implementation of opening benchmarks and subsequent requirements identified during the screening process. These developments generate increasing demand for specialised expertise, institutional capacity development and practical support for the implementation of EU-related reforms. Particular importance is attached to reforms related to rule of law, democratic governance, public administration, justice and internal security, especially under Cluster I "Fundamentals", including Chapter 23 (Judiciary and Fundamental Rights) and Chapter 24 (Justice, Freedom and Security). At the same time, Moldova's EU accession process also requires stronger local governance capacities, improved multi-level coordination and increased participation of civil society, diaspora organisations and other stakeholders in EU-related reform processes. In this context, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH implements the projects "EU Integration Support Project" (EUISP), financed by the German Federal Foreign Office (FFO), and "Facilitating the EU Accession process through Coordination and Engagement in Moldova" (FACE), financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). To support the implementation of these projects, GIZ foresees the establishment of a comprehensive Short-Term Expert Pool (STEP), enabling flexible and demand-driven mobilisation of national and international expertise. The STEP will support activities related to legislative and policy approximation to the EU acquis, negotiation preparation and benchmark fulfilment, institutional and organisational capacity development, strategic planning and coordination, strengthening local governance capacities, facilitation of international cooperation and peer-to-peer exchange, as well as structured stakeholder engagement and support for local initiatives. The contractor implementing the STEP will provide technical advisory services, analytical support, capacity development measures, international exchange formats and implementation support in close cooperation with GIZ and Moldovan partner institutions. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacities of national and local actors to effectively coordinate, implement and support Moldova's EU accession and alignment process. The procurement concerns the establishment and operation of a comprehensive Short-Term Expert Pool (STEP) supporting the implementation of activities under the GIZ projects "EU Integration Support Project" (EUISP) and "Facilitating the EU Accession process through Coordination and Engagement in Moldova" (FACE), both contributing to the Republic of Moldova's EU accession and alignment process. The contractor will provide flexible, demand-driven and results-oriented consultancy and implementation support services aimed at strengthening the capacities of national and local actors involved in Moldova's EU accession process. The services will combine technical advisory support, institutional and organisational capacity development, international experience exchange, stakeholder engagement and support for local initiatives. The contractor will be responsible for identifying, mobilising, coordinating and managing national and international experts and support measures in close cooperation with GIZ and Moldovan partner institutions. The assignment may include the following services and activities: - technical, legal and methodological advisory services related to EU acquis alignment, policy development and implementation of EU-related reforms; - preparation and revision of draft laws, regulations, strategies, methodologies, guidelines and analytical documents; - institutional, legislative and implementation gap analyses, including assessment of institutional capacities and implementation readiness; - support for negotiation process, fulfilment of opening and closing benchmarks and related monitoring and reporting processes; - development and strengthening of strategic planning, coordination, monitoring and reporting mechanisms related to EU accession and EU-aligned reforms; - provision of thematic expertise related to rule of law, democratic governance, justice, internal security, public administration reform and local governance; - design and delivery of trainings, workshops, mentoring, coaching and institutional learning activities for representatives of public institutions and other stakeholders; - organisation and facilitation of international peer-to-peer exchange, study visits, policy dialogues, expert discussions and cooperation formats involving EU Member States, accession countries and international experts; - support for strengthening coordination, cooperation and communication mechanisms between national institutions, local public authorities and other stakeholders involved in the accession process; - support for participatory and stakeholder engagement processes involving civil society organisations, diaspora representatives, women"s organisations and organisations representing vulnerable groups; - support for strengthening local governance capacities and practical application of EU-related planning, implementation and monitoring approaches at local level; - support for the conceptualisation, management and implementation of small-scale support initiatives and local contributions linked to EU accession-related objectives; - facilitation of innovative cooperation, consultation and policy development formats, including policy labs, simulation exercises and practical learning approaches; - monitoring, reporting, documentation and knowledge management activities related to the implementation of the assignment. The contractor will ensure process-oriented and implementation-oriented delivery of services, including quality assurance, operational coordination, backstopping and effective mobilisation of expertise throughout the contract period. Particular emphasis will be placed on ensuring the practical applicability of delivered support, strengthening institutional ownership and supporting sustainable implementation of EU-related reforms at both national and local level. Services will be implemented in close coordination with GIZ and relevant Moldovan partner institutions, including the Bureau for European Integration within the State Chancellery, line ministries, local public authorities, civil society organisations and other relevant stakeholders. Given the dynamic nature of the EU accession process, the assignment requires a high degree of flexibility and responsiveness in order to address evolving priorities, reform needs and operational requirements related to Moldova's EU accession and alignment process.
