sig_34d88c631a5b77984883.description:
In times of crisis, information, both correct and incorrect, spreads to an unprecedented extent. Social media in particular contribute to the spread of intentional disinformation and unintentional misinformation due to their high speed of dissemination and perceived anonymity. Furthermore, artificial intelligence opens up unprecedented possibilities in the generation and dissemination of disinformation. In radiological emergencies, this can lead to uncertainty and to citizens not adhering to protective measures. Furthermore, disinformation (e.g. about a necessary evacuation) can lead the population to potentially harmful behaviour and trigger chaotic conditions. While the spread of disinformation is problematic in many respects, the problem in a radiological emergency is that institutions and decision-makers have to identify and react to it under high time pressure. The BMUKN and BfS would also be confronted with the citizens' need for information and a flood of misinformation and disinformation, which makes the rapid and targeted dissemination of correct information very difficult. However, rapid and effective crisis communication is essential in a radiological emergency. The research project is intended to compile the current state of knowledge on disinformation and misinformation and to systematically analyse and prepare it for the purposes of crisis communication and radiological emergency protection for the BMUKN and BfS. The focus is on the following questions: - What disinformation and misinformation exist in the context of radiological emergencies or could arise? - What types of actors and motivations can be identified/categorised? - What strategic deductions for crisis communication already exist or can be drawn? - Which strategies against disinformation and misinformation are classified as promising in the context of radiological emergencies, and which are less so? The aim of the research project is to (1) identify tools and methods for the detection of disinformation that the BfS can use in a radiological emergency and (2) to develop concrete recommendations for the strategic handling of disinformation in crisis communication in a radiological emergency. It should become clear which findings on existing disinformation and misinformation in radiological emergencies and other crises relevant to the issue are available and which strategies can be used for communication in a radiological emergency as well as for the development of communication exercises to prepare for an actual situation. The project is not intended to comprise a general treatise on disinformation and misinformation in general, but rather to be specifically tailored to the needs of the BfS and BMUKN. At the end of the project, there will be an overview of concrete tools for detection and guidance on the strategic handling of disinformation in a radiological emergency. The present research project thus offers the BMUKN and BfS an important basis for informing the population both about a radiological situation and about precautionary or protective recommendations and thus serves the implementation of the Radiation Protection Act, in particular §105 and §112. The basis for the performance of tasks by the BMUKN/BfS is the current state of science and technology in accordance with atomic and radiation protection law. The investigations, studies and expert reports commissioned by the BMUKN/BfS must therefore be based on the current state of science and technology in the respective field of work. In this context, new findings and scientific-technical progress must be identified and evaluated with a view to the objectives of the project. The bidder must be in a position to carry out the required investigations on a scientifically sound basis in accordance with the requirements for scientific practice in the described areas of responsibility. The provision of services must be carried out in a data protection-friendly manner. All currently applicable legal requirements, such as the GDPR and BDSG, must be implemented. If personal data (Art. 4 No. 1 GDPR) or even certain categories of personal data, e.g. health data, political opinions, etc. (Art. 9 Para. 1 GDPR) are processed, a data processing agreement (DPA) or an agreement on joint processing may have to be concluded. The contractor must submit a data protection concept and comply with all obligations of the GDPR. The data must not leave the scope of the GDPR. sig_353a5497188f16ab5553.description: Stirling Council, as part of the Stirling and Clackmannanshire City Region Deal’s Digital Quarter, is soon to undertake a procurement exercise for the operation of new digital and coworking space being developed in Callander. This will be located in a newly extended and refurbished library building in Callander (on Church Street, a short distance from the Main Street in Callander). The proposal is for a flexible space where some rooms will be bookable in their entirety for meetings or other use, alongside desk space for individual rentals and access to other services. A feasibility previously commissioned highlighted the need for informal space for networking as well as the more formal space for desks and meetings. In addition there will be shared access to equipment such as a printer, and also a newly installed kitchen. Early consultation with the market as part of the feasibility stage has indicated that 24/7 access to the hub is essential, as is a welcoming and person-centric feel to the facility. A membership model could be considered. To support early market engagement and inform the development of the service specification, we are pleased to invite potential operators of the facility to attend an information session about the forthcoming business opportunity. The purpose of this session is to: - Share initial proposals regarding the scope of the procurement - Gather insights and feedback from potential service providers particularly in terms of possible design layouts before the design is finalised. - Understand market capabilities and any operational constraints - Explore innovative approaches to operating a coworking space. Session Details: Date: Wednesday 10 December 2025 Time: 3pm-4pm Location: Callander Library, South Church Street, Callander, FK17 8BN We welcome your participation and would be grateful for your input. Please confirm your attendance by 5pm on Tuesday 9 December by emailing investinstirling@stirling.gov.uk. We look forward to engaging with you at the session. Lot 1: . sig_35dff215c51ce3c4f509.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council has a requirement to progress the proposed 500km North Solway Coastal Path project to RIBA Stage 4 technical design. The project is part of the Solway Coast and Marine Project – landscape connections project, part funded through the National Lottery Heritage Fund (NLHF) Landscape Connections programme. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway Council has a requirement to progress the proposed 500km North Solway Coastal Path project to RIBA Stage 4 technical design. The project is part of the Solway Coast and Marine Project – landscape connections project, part funded through the National Lottery Heritage Fund (NLHF) Landscape Connections programme. The project has been awarded a stage 1 development and the timescale for this element of the project is expected to include tender requests being issued in December 2025/ January 2026 with a delivery phase for this stage of 11-12 months ending in December 2026. It is anticipated that the construction phase will commence in late 2027, dependent on a successful stage 2 application to the NLHF Landscape Connections programme, with an 8-year implementation period. Many sections of the route are already designated core paths however there are gaps in the coast network, and the existing access infrastructure is variable in quality. The deliverables from the design phase will be based on an agreed physical sub-division of the route provided which is based on an initial business case proposal and will include: · Creation of a GIS digital mapping information layer to an agreed format · Detailed information on land ownerships derived from SCOTLIS, investigations, existing records and local knowledge. · Survey of agreed routes and existing route infrastructure including an audit of existing Core Path sections for current condition, useability and signage · Recommendations for upgrading of existing path sections to an agreed standard for a promoted route · Identification of potential candidate fully accessible route sections suitable for all abilities to viewpoints/ places of interest from access points and linking to coastal gateway sites and car parks. · Directional signage strategy and detailed recommendations for implementation · Detailed design access infrastructure proposals for existing Core Path sections · Options appraisal for new path section and initial discussions with landowners · Detailed design proposals for new path route sections including access infrastructure and surfacing types · Detailed costings and designs for proposed works for each route section and sub divided into each individual landholding · A full project delivery plan based on sections and schedule in both electronic and hard copy format · Proposals and recommendations for a phased delivery.

sig_385fb26148b2325dfc3a.description: Open procedure, pursuant to Article 71 of Legislative Decree No 36/2023, for the award of development, maintenance and management services for the information system of Fondimpresa (FPF System). A contract concerning the following activities shall be concluded with the successful tenderer of this procedure: i) Software development and enhancement (MEV) ii) Corrective and adaptive maintenance (MAC/MAD) iii) Housing, operation and hardware/software maintenance iv) Helpdesk (hereinafter also referred to solely as "Service" or "Services"), as better defined, described and set out in the technical specification attached to the tender specifications. A handover period with the new successful tenderer taking over at the end of the contract must be guaranteed, lasting at least 2 (two) months. Regarding the procedures for executing the contractual relationship, please refer to the provisions in paragraph 9 of the technical specification, without prejudice to compliance with the service levels referred to in paragraph 10 of the technical specification, failing which the penalties established therein shall apply. In order to outline the background context, notwithstanding what is better established in the technical specification, it is specified that Fondimpresa has acquired an information system (named "FPF System") for managing the training plans of the Training Account and the System Account, for communication between Fondimpresa, its regional offices and the member companies, for acquiring and managing membership data and contributions transmitted by INPS, as well as monitoring information to be sent periodically to the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies and for registering state aid with the RNA. The development of the Fund's activities, the diversification of training financing measures made available to member companies (via public notices), the increase in financing granted and the number of training plans managed, the steady growth in memberships and the evolution of monitoring specifications required by the guidance and supervisory authority, entail the need to guarantee: • evolutionary maintenance (MEV) of the FPF system; • corrective and adaptive maintenance (MAC/MAD) of the FPF system; • management of housing and operation services with particular attention to system monitoring activities and security aspect verification (penetration tests, vulnerability assessments, etc.); • management of the first and second-level helpdesk service; • the development of new document flow management features with a view to continuous and progressive paperless operation of the Fund's activities; • the integration of new tools based on artificial intelligence to automate and optimise human operational workflows; • architectural developments and hardware/software infrastructure modernisation interventions to ensure appropriate levels of security, efficiency and service continuity; • application support for the disaster recovery system. The currently estimated user base is approximately 280.000 users against approximately 210.000 contributing positions affiliated with Fondimpresa. The contract shall have a duration of 60 natural and consecutive months, commencing from the start date of activities determined by the date of a specific record of commencement of activities. For all services described in the preceding article, no interfering risks are identifiable for which specific safety measures need to be adopted and, therefore, the preparation of the DUVRI is not required (pursuant to Article 26, paragraph 3-bis, of Legislative Decree No 81/2008). Consequently, there are no safety costs of an interfering nature, which are therefore quantified as € 0,00. Since the tender procedure has as its object services of an intellectual nature (as these primarily concern software development and the elaboration of customised solutions, functional analysis and governance of system evolution), tenderers are not required to indicate, pursuant to Article 108, paragraph 9, of the Code, the amount of labour costs and company costs for fulfilling provisions regarding health and safety in the workplace. Please refer to the Tender Specifications and its attached technical specification for tender particulars. The contract consists of a single lot as it is characterised by the functional unity of the service. Therefore, it is considered appropriate, both from the perspective of economic efficiency and optimal service execution, not to proceed with a division into lots. In any event, the tenderer's future bid shall be understood to refer overall to the entirety of the services forming the subject matter of the tender.

sig_38986fa46939d895c50f.description: For this project We have 6 modules. Each module is made up of 3 stages. These stages are (1) an x-y stage, (2) a tilt goniometric stage, and (3) rotational stage. The links to these stages and the control box can be seen in the attached supporting document. The difference between our stages and the COTS stages is that each stage has a different motor to the COTS item (integrated 485 bus-type closed-loop stepper driver, IRS42E-K02, manual available). All modules are controlled via a single controller box. The controller box has power and user instructions from control software (via RS232 to USB cable) as inputs and has six output cables, each connected to one of the modules (RS232 to RS232). Each output cable is limited to 2m length. The cable from the controller connects to the bottom most stage of the module, that is the x-stage. The x-stage is then connected to the y-stage via a RS232 cable. The y-stage is connected to the goniometric stage via a RS232 cable. Finally, the goniometric stage is connected to the rotational stage via a RS232 cable. In this way, a controller with 6 outputs controls 6x4=24 motors. This setup is shown in the diagram and a picture of a single module is also provided on the attached supporting document. The control signal is sent via the control box to the desired module. If the control signal is not for the x-stage, the control signal is passed up the chain, and so on. We need the control software to interface with our existing hardware to control the 6 modules. The solution could interface with the existing control box, or alternatively provide a new controller to interface with the 6 modules. The requirements above are for the software/control of the 6 modules. Lot LOT-0000: . None

sig_3a48dd21108b2e189500.description: In line with technological evolution and the principles established in the Digitalisation Plan for Public Administrations and the National Cybersecurity Strategy, the trend in public sector corporate networks is moving towards architectures based on separate and isolated networks, using protocols running over Layer-3, such as SD-WAN, to create convergent communications services that enable: - Operational efficiency to be increased and management costs to be reduced. - Intelligent and proactive traffic management to be incorporated, particularly through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence techniques. - Native integration with perimeter security systems and operations centres (SOC) to be facilitated. - The use of hybrid links (fibre, 4G/5G, Internet, etc.) to be permitted, guaranteeing high availability of services. - Scalability and flexibility to be ensured when opening new offices or launching new municipal services. In the field of office interconnection, the City Council of Ávila aims for an even more advanced and robust approach, replacing SD-WAN-based networks with Layer-2 networks capable of transporting VLANs based on the 802.1Q protocol. One of the fundamentals of this requirement is not to lose performance, such as the extremely low latency currently enjoyed, which is characteristic of campus networks or metropolitan area networks, constituted by point-to-point circuits. The City Council of Ávila is promoting an evolution towards a communications model based on the principles of robustness, agility, security, integration and scalability, in order to guarantee a modern, efficient and resilient infrastructure that supports the institution's digital transformation and continuous improvement in the provision of services to citizens. Based on this, the telecommunications services of the City Council of Ávila are being tendered, covering the areas of fixed and mobile telephony, broadband Internet access, data transmission between offices and associated services, as well as the maintenance of the infrastructures necessary for their correct provision. The contract seeks the provision of the related services and the comprehensive maintenance of the equipment and infrastructures necessary to guarantee the correct provision of the services throughout their validity, including the essential LAN equipment to provide the VoIP service, understanding that these are essential services for the proper functioning of the City Council.
sig_3a48dd21108b2e189500.title: Telecommunications service for the City Council of Ávila (fixed telephony, mobile, data, internet and associated services) distributed in 3 lots

sig_3a776fefa39e632dc03f.description: The Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites results-oriented proposals for programs that foster economic opportunities for U.S. businesses and investors, innovation collaboration, showcase American leadership and excellence in science, technology, culture, the arts, sports, education, and English language, and strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous as we commemorate the 250 th anniversary of U.S. independence (2026) and 230 years of U.S.-Tunisian friendship (2027). All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: • Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. • Programs that connect U.S. companies with Tunisian partners, suppliers, and market opportunities, facilitate business-to-business networking and investment matchmaking, prepare Tunisian startups and established businesses to meet U.S. market standards, enter U.S. markets, and partner with U.S. investors. • Sports diplomacy, culinary diplomacy, art exhibitions, film festivals, theater, musical theater, musical performances and master classes. • Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programs, including through use of new and immersive technologies, such as virtual reality (VR) or augmented reality (AR) technology. • U.S.-Tunisian University-industry partnerships, including with research or technology parks, that generate mutually beneficial commercialization projects or that create opportunities for U.S. companies in STEM fields and emerging technologies and innovation. • Hackathons, STEM or Maker Space camps/competitions, or other related hands-on activities that showcase American leadership and excellence in innovation and STEM fields, including but not limited to space exploration, technologies with beneficial applications to daily life developed as a result of NASA initiatives, or that foster target audiences’ artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and readiness. • University and cultural institution linkages programs that include but are not limited to development and implementation of a course, joint PhD advising, or joint degree program, or the design and teaching of a jointly-led course that includes virtual or in-person instruction from a U.S. professor/expert in fields outlined under Excellence in Education and English Teaching priority outlined in this APS. • English language programs, including but not limited to teacher training and programs that share innovative American English teaching methodologies, specialized English courses to improve business opportunities and innovation collaboration with U.S. companies, investors, U.S.-Tunisian university-industry partnerships, and foster economic self-reliance among target audiences. • Podcasts. • Professional and academic exchanges and programs. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must focus on one of the five priority areas outlined below: ECONOMIC PROSPERITY AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP: Initiatives that expand U.S. commercial and investment opportunities; strengthen U.S. ties with Tunisia’s entrepreneurship ecosystem; promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices; and/or share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of creating economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. CELEBRATING AMERICA’S 250thANNIVERSARY AND U.S.-TUNISIAN ENDURING PARTNERSHIP: Initiatives, including innovative, small-scale programming and programming at our American Corners, that: 1) celebrate U.S. scientific breakthroughs, innovation, economic dynamism, sport prowess, agricultural strength, national parks, tourism, public service, freedom of speech or press, and other ideas and partnerships that shaped America’s development during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence (2026) and in honor of the 230th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia (2027); 2) showcase and share American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, theater, film, and cultural heritage protection, including through artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities, including community service initiatives that bring together Americans and Tunisians during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence (2026) and the 230th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia (2027); 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase the Tunisian public’s awareness and understanding of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation. INNOVATION AND COLLABORATION IN SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY: Initiatives that encourage artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and readiness in Tunisia through use of U.S. AI platforms and technologies; raise awareness and promote collaboration on projects related to the 2027 solar eclipse; and expand U.S. ties to Tunisia’s innovation ecosystem through research collaboration and university-industry partnerships, including research and technology parks, to generate mutually beneficial commercialization projects that create opportunities for U.S. companies in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including but not limited to cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and AI. MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Initiatives that leverage the U.S.-hosted 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics, and 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values, and demonstrate U.S. economic strength, infrastructure, and excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. Excellence in EDUCATION AND ENGLISH TEACHING : Initiatives that showcase American leadership and excellence in education and English teaching in public or private institutions; provide specialized English courses to improve opportunities with U.S. companies/investors for target audiences; and foster innovative collaboration between U.S. and Tunisian higher education institutions to enhance Tunisian participants’ understanding of U.S. culture, values, history, and policies, including in American studies, culture, and literature, freedom of speech, the arts and creative industries (film, music, design thinking, and cultural entrepreneurship), cultural heritage preservation, tourism and hospitality, municipal management, water and/or waste management, urban design, and STEM fields. Program and application details are available in the TUNIS APS FY2026 Questions should be addressed to PASTunisSmallGrants@state.gov

sig_3bf58af309ef4560a9f9.description: The Burgenlandkreis acting as the client intends to construct a new school campus on the "Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße" site, consisting of a school building and a 3-field sports hall. The Centre for the Vocational Preparation Year (BVJ), which is also planned on the site, is not the subject of this tender. The construction site for the planned new campus building is located east of the Naumburg centre within the scope of a legally binding development plan (B-Plan No. 62 "Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße"). The former buildings and surface pavings have already been dismantled. The school property itself is situated on Schönburger Straße running to the south and on Dr-Wilhelm-Kniest-Straße, newly planned and constructed in the course of the development plan procedure, between Schönburger Straße and Grochlitzer Straße to the east. The campus also includes the plot with the plot number 692. The street quarter between Schönburger Straße, Rosa-Luxemburg-Straße and Grochlitzer Straße is characterised by largely homogeneous buildings consisting mostly of three-storey residential buildings. The plot is largely flat and covers an area of 25.196 m2. The structures of the new school campus are distributed across three building areas. In the invitation to tender, the building parts of the construction project are designated as follows: Sub-project A School building The building, which houses the school rooms of the special needs school, the secondary school and parts of the BVJ, forms the centre of the facility as the largest building mass and is itself structured into three "building cubes", staggered in height between two and four upper floors. The three building section areas are each structured around an inner courtyard core. The buildings are constructed using solid construction methods with load-bearing walls and columns made of reinforced concrete as well as reinforced concrete ceilings with a flat roof. The foundation is laid on reinforced concrete floor slabs. The middle building section (A 1) has a basement, while the northern and southern building sections (A2 and A3) do not have basements. Sub-project B Sports hall The three-field sports hall is arranged to the north adjacent to the school building. A two-storey functional wing adjoins the southern longitudinal side of the large hall room with DIN dimensions (4 5 x 2 7 m). The building foundation for the social wing is constructed as a slab foundation with reinforced concrete floor slabs, while the hall is founded on individual foundations and strip foundations beneath the external walls. The load-bearing walls, columns and floor slabs in the social wing are constructed in reinforced concrete. The hall roof is designed with glued laminated timber girders and a load-bearing shell made of trapezoidal profiled steel sheeting. Workshop building of the BVJ (building component C) not the subject of this tender Lot LOT-0000: Naumburg Education Campus, Schönburger Straße, 06618 Naumburg, lot 4-09 building automation. School building: - 12 automation stations with network connection and building management system - connected components: AHU unit, electrical alarms, heating control, sanitary. - approx. 1500 hardware data points - approx. 17.000 m new installation of energy and control cables - approx. 50.000 m new installation of alarm and measuring cables to be supplied: - 2 pieces central HRU unit, approx. 22.500 m3/h - 1 pieces central HRU unit, approx. 5.000 m3/h - 5 pieces roof fan polluted exhaust air - approx. 120 pieces fire dampers with actuator - central heating distribution system - approx. 300 underfloor heating actuators Sports hall: - 2 automation stations with network connection and building management system - connected components: AHU unit, electrical alarms, heating control, sanitary. - approx. 500 hardware data points - approx. 4.000 m new installation of energy and control cables - approx. 15.000 m new installation of alarm and measuring cables to be supplied: - 1 pieces central HRU unit, approx. 8.500 m3/h - approx. 20 pieces fire dampers with actuator - 4 heat pumps and central heating components - approx. 70 underfloor heating actuators

Renewal of the Software Assurance (SA) Programme for the Ministry's Microsoft software licences 3. Renewal and extension of support licences (Firmware Updates, Enhanced Support and Phone Support) for the FortiAuthenticator system of the Secure Transmission System (STS) infrastructure, with a total estimated value of 140.300,00€ excluding (without) VAT 24% or 173.972,00€ including VAT 24%. Lot 1 : Supply of SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR). The requested supply concerns the need to adopt modern security solutions for the Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports. In this context, it is necessary to procure a SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR), which will detect threats and automate the response to them, supplementing the technical measures already maintained by the Agency. In detail, a SIEM/SOAR system allows for the centralised collection and analysis of logs from multiple sources, facilitating the timely detection of and immediate response to security incidents. At the same time, it strengthens compliance with regulatory frameworks and supports effective risk management. sig_3c6906217ed34d1b7a09.description:
Väylävirasto is preparing a procurement, the subject of which is the operating services for the road information systems of Väylävirasto, which suppliers will produce with the help of expert teams. The expert service to be procured includes operator services for six different information systems of Väylävirasto. The procurement is divided into the following four sub-areas. - Sub-area 1 Operation of Tievelho; - Sub-area 2 Operation of the Structural Register; - Sub-area 3 Operation of maintenance and - Sub-area 4 Location reference operation. The goal of the procurement is to ensure the smooth use of information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating, and to support the development of information systems. The expert teams will consist of road data experts, structural experts, operators, and technical experts. The roles include both senior and junior-level professionals. The length of the contract has been tentatively set at three years, plus an option of up to two years. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register for the market survey in accordance with the registration instructions presented below. In the call for tenders, the tenderer may submit a tender for one or more sub-areas. A tender may be submitted independently, together with subcontractors, or as a consortium. Companies interested in the market survey are requested to notify as soon as possible, but no later than 30.9.2026 at 23.00 by filling out the electronic registration form: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ErRyRq6yXZ The market survey consists of the opportunity to comment on the draft material of the tender before the publication of the call for tenders. Please note that this is a market survey notice and this notice does not yet request tenders. Failure to respond to the market survey notice does not prevent participation in a potential call for tenders. The information presented in this market survey notice and the estimated publication date of the call for tenders are preliminary and indicative advance information, which does not bind Väylävirasto to any kind of decision. The preliminary goal of Väylävirasto is to publish the contract notice in January 2027. The market survey notice does not oblige Väylävirasto to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The procurement will form an expert team to support system development, maintenance, and specification, which will be responsible for user support, training, supporting data production processes, data processing and updating, quality management, information services, and documentation and communication related to operation. The experts will identify development needs that arise during operation and convey them to the client and to the separately procured development task specification service. The experts will act at the interface between Väylävirasto, system users, data producers, and maintenance, specification, and further development suppliers. The planned expert team will consist of road data experts, operating service experts, technical data management experts, and project data management experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Basic data repository for road information (Tievelho): Basic data repository for road network infrastructure, condition and measurement data, restrictions, decisions, and classification data.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include, among others, quality assurance of the Structural Register data, checking and updating data, checking data to correspond to prevailing guidelines, checking data content and quality assurance, checking and updating process diagrams, and specifying data content. The planned expert team will consist of structural experts who have experience in using the Structural Register. A security clearance will be conducted on the experts. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Structural Register: The Structural Register is a basic data repository for structures and an asset management system. In addition to administrative and structural data, it contains, for example, damage and condition data on structures such as bridges, tunnels, and fixed sea marks. In addition to objects owned by Väylävirasto, the register also contains data on structures owned by municipalities and cities. The Structural Register serves, for example, the experts and service providers of Väylävirasto, Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, as well as municipalities and cities. The system is being developed and the data content is being expanded continuously.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include ensuring the smooth use of maintenance information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating. A key goal is to ensure that maintenance information systems contain and are provided with up-to-date, high-quality, and structurally uniform data. The background is an identified need to: • Develop and implement quality control of data in maintenance information systems. • Maintain data in maintenance systems. • Produce data and materials for the needs of experts. • Develop and implement a uniform way of data management • Support data production processes in the production and utilisation of road data and maintenance data. • Develop, support, and supervise the data management related to road maintenance of Väylävirasto and Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment • Develop and maintain instructions and documentation related to the utilisation and updating of maintenance data • Support Väylävirasto in development projects related to maintenance and road data management. The planned expert team will consist of operating service experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. Short descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: YHA: Repair management system YHA (formerly

maintenance management system) is used for programming repair sites (selection, prioritisation and timing of sites and measures), calculating the impact of the planned programme, reporting and monitoring condition data, and exporting contracts to the Harja system. The system is used to manage repair measures for existing paved roads, walking and cycling routes, and gravel roads. Harja: The Harja system is used to monitor, supervise and report on the financial, qualitative, temporal and quantitative execution of highway maintenance contracts, surfacing and road marking contracts, lighting contracts and waterway canalisation contracts. The content of different contract types varies. Harja is one of väylävirasto's largest information systems.; The procurement establishes an expert team whose tasks include supporting the operation, testing and definition of systems related to the Väylävirasto location referencing framework. Tasks include, among others, road addressing of roads related to the creation of the road address network in conjunction with the Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, work related to the maintenance of Suravage geometry, support for the testing and definition of Viite (Road Address System) and the Framework Converter, and tasks related to the maintenance of the road address network. The expert team will consist of road data experts. Brief descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: Viite: Road address system maintenance application. There is a need to make changes to road addresses due to the completion of road projects or administrative decisions. There are three tasks in the maintenance of the road address system: Maintenance of road addresses (including carriageway data (but not lane data)), maintenance of road names, and maintenance of nodes and junctions. In Viite, road addresses are linked to the frozen road link geometry of the Centre Line Geometry Repository, and road address maintenance takes place in a map user interface based on road link geometry. When maintaining road addresses, road address history is also preserved in Viite. Road addresses are used to record the locations of data related to highways. The most significant system utilising road addresses is Tievelho. Framework Converter (Viitekehysmuunnin): A REST-type interface application used to convert road locations from one location referencing framework to another, for example to obtain coordinates for a road address. The data to be converted is sent to the Framework Converter using a GET/POST request, the application processes the data and returns the converted data to the calling application as a response. The interface service is publicly available on the internet. In addition, there are separate authorised interface addresses for the service.
sig_3c6906217ed34d1b7a09.title: Procurement of operating services for road information systems

sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.description: The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), with other NIH Institutes and Centers (ICs), intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to investigate the mechanisms of action of therapeutic medical devices with the overall goal of improving clinical outcomes with device-based approaches. Medical devices are essential in managing health conditions, complementing drugs and behavioral interventions, and often offer unique benefits. Despite the commercial availability of numerous medical devices and ongoing development of new technologies, many have shown inconsistent results in preclinical studies, failed translation to humans, and exhibit varied patient outcomes. To overcome these challenges, it is crucial to understand the mechanisms by which medical devices produce a therapeutic effect, to identify physiological markers of neurological conditions, and to assess how device-based therapies influence these markers. Advancing this knowledge will improve device-based interventions, inspire new device designs, and optimize current clinical approaches. Applications will be invited from interdisciplinary teams pursuing innovative research on how medical devices produce a therapeutic effect. Applicant teams will likely exhibit expertise in areas such as engineering, biology, pathophysiology, surgery, clinical care, healthcare delivery, biostatistics, software development, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, regulatory science, and clinical trials. This program will accept projects on investigational devices and those already FDA-approved and in clinical use. Applications are expected to include strategies for developing or optimizing therapies that could significantly improve patient care. Supported research may include mechanistic clinical trials, animal studies, and computational modeling or simulation. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.title: HEAL Initiative: Optimization of Therapeutic Medical Devices through Team Science Mechanistic Research (RM1)

sig_3ee832445041b66999b9.description: The Kölner Verkehrs-Betriebe AG (KVB) intends to publish one or, where applicable, several procurement procedures for the procurement of validators including a background system and relevant software interfaces, likely from the year 2026. In order to improve KVB's level of knowledge regarding the technical and commercial aspects of such a procedure, KVB is conducting a market consultation pursuant to Section 26 of the Sectoral Procurement Ordinance (SektVO) ("industry dialogue"). As part of the industry dialogue, KVB will inform itself about, inter alia, 1. Functionalities of validators (hardware, software) and background systems 2. implementation options for KVB 3. commercial aspects (pricing models, price range, cost factors). Subject of the industry dialogue: KVB intends to replace the mobile ticket vending machines in the trains and buses with validators. These are intended to function without paper and cash based on contactless EMV transactions and to be embedded in an ABT/IDBT-capable system. Travel entitlements are to be stored as encrypted tokens in a cloud-based background system, whereby both providers and cloud storage must at least have the necessary ISO 27001 certification. The operation of the background system in a cloud environment must be subject to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The validators must make it possible to purchase a specific, independently configurable range of tickets (pre-selection) and additionally support an interoperable check-in/check-out procedure with integrated best-price calculation for the customer. All physical and virtual payment instruments that comply with the EMV standard (EC card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, etc.) must be accepted; in addition, payment via a prepaid card (closed-loop) must be possible. KVB reserves the right to commission a financial/payment service provider with the processing of payments. Corresponding software interfaces/APIs must therefore be supported/addressed. The payment options are to be expandable in the future. The customer must be able to view and manage their travel entitlements (ABT) independently via an online portal (web portal). The web/online portal is to be provided in KVB's corporate design. In addition, further software interfaces to a central customer account, which is set up internally by KVB, are to be provided. It must be possible to use a token that is linked to another person's payment medium. The control of the issued travel entitlements must be ensured across transport associations (at least throughout NRW) and made possible by corresponding software interfaces from the provider. A control option must also be possible when the validator is offline. The regular processing of blacklists is supported. Current and future developments of VDV-KA and (((eTiCore must be taken into account. The background system must contain at least the following software interfaces: - Ticketing back office with payment gateway and connection to payment service provider - Device management - Key management - Customer management - Enterprise asset management system - Fault notification software interface The background system should promote interoperability and must be able to be integrated into an overarching system landscape. The accounting data from the validators must be able to be integrated from there into the sales accounting system PATRIS (LHIND). Participation in the industry dialogue / qualification criteria: If potential bidders are interested in participating in the industry dialogue, KVB requests notification by email by no later than 23.9.2025, 10:00 hours, to the contact point daniela.lehnert@kvb.koeln. The references must be submitted in full by this time. When expressing interest in participating in the industry dialogue, the following qualification criteria / capabilities of the bidders must be proven and submitted. KVB reserves the right to exclude bidders whose qualification is not proven or is not sufficient based on proven references / documents from the industry dialogue and not allow them to participate in the industry dialogue. Submission of 2 references regarding previously executed contracts / services that are comparable to the advertised service in terms of subject matter and scope. The comparability of a reference requires that the subject matter of the reference contract includes at least the successful implementation / introduction of an ABT/IDBT system including mobile validators and a background system in public transport. In one of the reference contracts, the system must have been implemented on the basis of contactless EMV transactions. The reference contracts must not date back more than 5 years. The reference projects must have been implemented in Europe. The relevant factor in this regard is the date of acceptance or complete performance of the service. The following details must be provided in the reference: a) Name and address of the respective reference client b) Brief description of the reference project c) Contractual role of one's own company in the reference project d) Meaningful description of the nature and scope of the service provided (by oneself) e) Details of any (own) subcontractors f) Description of the comparability of the project (essential overlaps / parallels to the present industry dialogue) g) Duration of the project h) Contact person (naming a contact person who can confirm the reference and is authorized to provide information to KVB regarding the quality of service provision)

sig_3f443255f38bcabd6daa.buyer_original: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik
sig_3f443255f38bcabd6daa.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods demonstrate astonishing performance in many application areas and are increasingly used in areas that affect daily life. The field of cybersecurity has not remained untouched by AI either. New AI tools are published almost daily in this context, and large AI language models (LLMs) in particular are already being used today for various application purposes. At the same time, the threat landscape is changing significantly as benignly intended models are misused for attack purposes (dual use). As a consequence, it must sometimes be assumed that vulnerabilities will be discovered and exploited ever faster in future with the increasing capabilities of AI. Against this background, the defensive side must also take action, which is why this project is intended to investigate how AI can be used profitably in the SSDLC and what effects ongoing developments have on the security of software. For this purpose, the project is divided into three parts, with related but distinct services: In work package 1-4 [HM1.1], a study on the current state of the art and science in the field of AI in the Secure Software Development Life Cycle is to be drawn up. In addition, best practices for the use of identified AI tools are to be developed. The results are to be published. In work package 5-6 [HM2.1], based on the study and in cooperation with the BSI, the contractor shall review the evaluation criteria for AVA scoring in Common Criteria certification and update them in view of new circumstances. In addition, an implementation plan for the use of AI tools for conformity assessment bodies is to be created. In work package 7, a reference architecture is created for the Open CoDE platform, which illustrates how AI tools can be integrated into the Secure Software Development Life Cycle and the software environment of Open CoDE. Suitable tools are to be proposed in this regard. Lot LOT-0000: KI im Secure Software Development Life Cycle (KISDL). sig_3f48acbeeee6adfeb946.description: The aim of the procurement is to establish a framework agreement for the delivery of equipment, consumables and production services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør-Øst. The procurement shall support the implementation and use of uniform physical and digital identification of locations and equipment based on international GS1 standards. Locations shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GLN and the equipment shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GIAI, in the form of GS1 Digital Link and other standardised GS1 syntaxes. Through the use of international standards, marks shall be able to be used by digital systems in Helse Sør-Øst, e.g. systems for Facility Management (FM)/property management, clinical logistics, medical engineering, ERP, etc. The procurement shall result in: - Standardised types of brands for locations and equipment. - Support for multiple information carriers on brands - Support for local production of brands - Support for production of large volumes of brands as external services. - Standardised production basis. - Secure management of business critical information. The procurement includes systems for both local production of brands in the health companies, and production of large volumes of brands. The system for local production can include production equipment, necessary software and/or integration components, consumables, equipment for encoding/programming NFC and UHF RFID, training, support, maintenance and documentation. The contracting authority will, together with the chosen supplier, establish a set of standardised brand types that will be used for the production of labels for locations and equipment. A tag type is a documented specification that specifies how a brand should be designed and produced.
sig_3f48acbeeee6adfeb946.title: Products and services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør-Øst

sig_4109de053106f368a495.description: Further to the UK1 Pipeline Notice published on 19th November 2025 by BlueLight Commercial Limited (ref: 2025/S 000-077692) in relation to a Victim & Citizen Engagement Technology Solution which will be used by UK law enforcement agencies, this UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is issued to inform the market of a potential future opportunity. This Pre-Market Engagement Notice is issued solely for the purposes of information gathering and engagement with the market. It does not constitute a call for competition and create any obligation on the Authority to proceed with a procurement exercise, or enter into any commercial arrangement. Please note the procurement route and anticipated publication date for this opportunity are yet to be determined. These elements will be confirmed following completion of the market engagement process and development of the Authority’s commercial strategy. Any future procurement will be subject to separate formal notice and the publication of full procurement documentation via the Find a Tender Service (FTS). BlueLight Commercial Limited (BLC) are conducting Preliminary Market Engagement to gain a better understanding of the market, supplier appetite, capacity, and capability, as well as perceived risks and opportunities. Any learnings will be used to formulate the associated procurement strategy. BLC work in collaboration with blue light organisations to maximise commercial benefit to UK emergency services. The focus of this solution will be improving Victim & Citizen Engagement, building trust and confidence, reducing demand within control rooms, and reducing the costs of serving the public by using innovative software to keep both victims and citizens more engaged. The aim is to ensure all forces have access to the most effective, reliable, and innovative solutions available in the market. This Solution needs to facilitate the force contact engagement from first contact with a police force to final closure of the contact, and via integration with police systems, e.g. Command and Control, Records Management Systems providing contact and updates throughout the journey without the need to call the force contact centre. It seeks to further drive standardisation and consistency, whilst helping forces to develop capability and invest in technology which will not only improve the service at first point of contact but will improve the overall contact experience. This Solution must facilitate Victim & Citizen engagement to reduce failure demand whilst proactively engaging to ensure high levels of customer (internal and external) trust and confidence. The delivery of the desired solution may be considered to follow the same customer service path as an online application or ordering process. For example, acknowledgement of the initial contact, time appropriate follow up contacts at defined points within the communication journey, and a closure contact at the end of the process. All communication will be auditable and align with the Victims code as appropriate. We are looking for solutions that can meet individual force needs and achieve the following: *Improve experience of members of the public accessing the policing service *Provide the public with consistent updates in a timely manner, *Improve public trust, confidence, and satisfaction, *Reduce Contact Management demand, *Improve force's overall Contact Management performance. Lot 1: .

sig_418d8d9a6769dfce9ec2.description: As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS). The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. sig_42f77bcf1d26787817ad.description: GeodatenProxy-System [GeoProxy] Fraport AG, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is a leading global airport operator. The company was founded 1924 and operates Frankfurt Airport, one of the world's most important aviation hubs. In addition, Fraport is involved in the administration and operation of several other airports worldwide. Fraport currently operates the ELDIS III software (SW) from eurofunk at the Frankfurt am Main site as a system relevant to KRITIS (Critical Infrastructure) and LuftSIG (Aviation Security Act) in the security control centre with the service areas works fire brigade, rescue service, and security as an operational control system, and in the integrated passenger flow control centre as a workflow system. The system currently in use is predictably reaching its technical limits, making a replacement necessary. The functions to be replaced by new systems comprise operational control and force dispatch, hazard reporting management, and the provision of geo-information in the form of a geoproxy. Maintenance, upkeep, service, and support are also required for all new systems. Applicants must sign a confidentiality agreement provided by Fraport (see informative documents) and submit it together with the application to participate. Following the procurement competition, an indicative tender round will initially be held as part of the tender phase, which will then be followed by one or more binding tender rounds. Within the indicative tender round, bidders may submit proposed amendments to the contract, specification of services, and annexes. Fraport decides on their acceptance or rejection. The contracting authority points out even at this stage that, in the event of being invited to submit a binding tender, the tenderer must mandatorily provide the following proofs: 1. All persons deployed in the project and in all maintenance, service, and support services are German-speaking at least at level B2 in accordance with the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) and are provided from a time zone of UTC +0 to +3. 2. Proof of full access to the control of development resources and unrestricted authority to modify and expand the offered software and hardware. Due to the critical path schedule that must be strictly adhered to given the importance of the overall system to be procured here for the maintenance of flight operations, Fraport may withdraw from the entire contract if the contractor culpably fails to provide services designated as "already available" within the meaning of hardware and software functions after contract award, or fails to provide them in accordance with the contract. The scope comprises delivery, agile (additional) development, commissioning with migration of legacy systems of a new geoproxy system, training of Fraport AG employees, as well as maintenance, service, and support services. The geoproxy takes over supplied consolidated geo-data from a geographic information system provided by Fraport AG and makes this available to the new operational control and hazard management system at a required high availability and performance. In this context, additional external geo-data relevant only to the security control centre must also be connected.
sig_42f77bcf1d26787817ad.title: GeodatenProxy-System [GeoProxy]

sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.description: Høje-Taastrup Kommune is considering procuring the purchase and support of AV equipment as well as devices (PCs and tablets) for the schools sector as operational leasing. This means a solution where the supplier undertakes the delivery, assembly, operation, maintenance and support of equipment as a solution where the supplier owns the equipment and the municipality obtains the right of use via payment of an annual fee. Therefore, the municipality wishes to enter into a dialogue with 2 - 3 suppliers of such types of IT equipment to discuss what the municipality should pay attention to in connection with procurement. Some documents are enclosed that describe some of the intended content in a procurement (requirements, wishes, etc.). The dialogue will be based on these documents. Initially, the municipality wishes an indication of whether you will enter into a dialogue with the municipality regarding such a procurement, as well as a response with some initial thoughts that you as a supplier have regarding a procurement of this type of operational leasing. As inspiration for this, here are some initial questions: Is the best way to procure the goods and services via 2 procurement or can both types of services (AV and PC/tablets) advantageously be combined in one procurement? Is there anything we should be aware of that a contract must contain and/or absolutely not contain: e.g. breach of contract, penalty - how do we handle defects in the equipment? Will the fact that the supplier owns, assembles and services e.g. AV equipment provide an advantage e.g. via the supplier's strict control of drivers/software as well as versioning of these components in relation to a more stable, well-functioning and cohesive AV solution across the municipality? Are there other things we should be aware of? Here, consideration is given to advantages the municipality can achieve and the disadvantages that may lie in such a solution. The intention is that equipment is to be replaced in an ongoing process. This means the supplier will take over support on e.g. existing AV equipment. The dialogue is intended as an informal discussion of advantages and disadvantages/risks of establishing such solutions. It is not immediately intended that actual transfer of employees should take place; the intention is to establish another and more efficient way to operate and support the mentioned solution areas.
sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.title: Consultation regarding the procurement of leasing for AV equipment and devices for the schools sector in Høje-Taastrup Kommune

sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.description: Provision, implementation and operation of a cloud-based, SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud) of the Stadtwerke Düsseldorf AG including affiliated companies. The aim of the procurement is to create transparency regarding data stocks, access authorizations and security-relevant activities, as well as to support measures to increase information security and comply with regulatory requirements in the KRITIS environment. In addition to the provision of the platform, the service also includes supportive services for the analysis, evaluation and prioritisation of security-relevant events as well as for the derivation of suitable measures. The processing of all data shall take place exclusively within the scope of the EU GDPR. An uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations must be ensured. The aim is to conclude a contract for the provision, implementation and operation of a scalable, cloud-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud). The solution must cover the following functions and services in particular: - Analysis and evaluation of data stocks, data access and permission structures, including the identification of potential security and data protection risks, - The solution should have integrated functions for detecting anomalies in user and system behaviour (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) - Creation of transparency regarding effective accesses and permissions, - Detection and evaluation of conspicuous, risk-prone or security-relevant activities, - Provision of monitoring, reporting and verification functions to support audit, compliance and security requirements, particularly in the regulated KRITIS environment, - Support in deriving and implementing suitable measures for risk reduction (e.g. adjustment of permissions or restriction of access rights), - Integration into the client's existing hybrid system landscape (in particular identity services, file and cloud storage as well as collaboration platforms) via standardised interfaces, - Provision and operation of the solution including maintenance, ongoing development, updates and technical documentation in a SaaS model. In addition, services are to be provided that support continuous evaluation, assessment and prioritisation (managed detection and response) of security-relevant events and provide recommendations for action. If configured accordingly, these services may also include operational support services. Continued operation requirements: - Ensuring an uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations, including a suitable migration and transition concept, - Taking over existing configurations, evaluations and settings as far as technically possible, - Guaranteeing compatibility with existing system landscapes, role and permission models, - Minimising migration, integration and training efforts while taking cost-effectiveness over the entire life cycle into account, - Ensuring continuous operational capability during the transition phase. All services relating to the client's data or metadata must be provided exclusively within the scope of the EU GDPR.
sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.title: Provision and operation of a SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions

sig_44927bea86389180d737.description: The tender aims to achieve and promote the stable and future-proof operation of the "Schleupen.CS" ERP system on a highly available and secure infrastructure for use by the client's employees and external service providers, including migration, SaaS operation, interfaces, administration, and support. The SWH is tendering for the provision of a highly available cloud infrastructure in the contractor's data centre. The service consists not only of providing data centre capacity but, due to the intended role as a solution provider, encompasses holistic responsibility for the stable and future-proof operation of Schleupen.CS. The services to be provided include, in particular: - the provision of the necessary hardware and data centre infrastructure, - the provision of software necessary for the operation of the systems (including current versions of Microsoft Windows Server, Microsoft SQL Server, Remote Desktop Services, and Citrix if applicable for the publication of remote apps, as approved by Schleupen SE), - the takeover or migration of the existing system (including the sub-systems necessary for operation) into the data centre environment, - the takeover of existing interfaces to third-party service providers (mandatory requirements: SMGWA, ticket system, customer portal), - the operation of the Schleupen.CS system (including sub-systems) in the data centre: production and test systems with the existing tenants, - the sufficiently performant - at least with symmetrical 200 Mbit/s - internet connection of the client to the contractor's data centre. Connection must be established via an encrypted VPN tunnel or by providing the service provider's own hardware, which is integrated into the contractor's internal network, - the takeover of support services within the scope of data centre operations, - the takeover of support services for the Schleupen.CS system, in particular holistic, independent communication with Schleupen SE in the event of application and problem cases, - the provision and maintenance of current hardware and software (operating system software, database software, application software), which are operated with active maintenance contracts / software assurance, - the monitoring of systems and applications, - immediate error detection, communication to the client in the event of an error, and error rectification, - the maintenance of highly available system operation (24 h/ 7 days a week) throughout the entire contract term. It is mandatory that strict, logical isolation from the contractor's other customers is maintained. The precise details regarding the subject matter of the contract can be found in the specifications (Annex B of the procedural letter).

sig_44988596b4418aad1d58.description: A total of three lots in the area of support - technical system administration are sought. Lot 1: SAP Basis Support, Lot 2: Software Development Support and Lot 3: Software Development Support Risk/Cont Lot LOT-0001: SAP Basis. SAP Basis administration is responsible, taking into account that LfA has outsourced the SAP operations of its ERP and BW systems to the SAP Cloud, for the smooth operation of our SAP systems in close cooperation with SAP. The core tasks in the SAP Basis environment include daily monitoring of the SAP landscape to ensure high-performance and error-free operation. Standard Basis transactions are regularly checked for error messages - both directly in the relevant SAP transactions and on the basis of incoming system messages via email, or via active evaluation of reports in SAP for Me. Another essential component is the importation of hotfixes as well as SAP and LfA specialist releases in order to keep the systems constantly up-to-date and secure. This also includes the analysis, assessment and processing of vulnerabilities in the Baramundi system to ensure IT security on a sustained basis. Tasks in SAP Basis also include operation and maintenance of SAP Solution Manager (e.g. importing security patches, creating new change cycles, analysing transport problems). New incoming tickets (incident, problem and change management) are processed continuously. Quarterly system and client copies are carried out jointly with SAP, with the focus of activities at LfA being, on the one hand, on the coordination of individual work packages, including the involvement of SAP peripheral systems, and, on the other hand, on follow-up work in the SAP systems. Lot LOT-0002: Software Development Support. - Analyses of requirements - Support of productive operations / support (error analysis and remediation) - Preparation of IT concepts and test concepts - Implementation / execution of customer-developed solutions o Open Text Team Developer development o ABAP development o Pl/Sql developments o C# developments o Interfaces - Maintenance of the data model - Test Lot LOT-0003: Risk Software Development Support. - Software development for the RISK/CONT system - Interface programming for data supply to RISK/CONT from operational systems and data delivery from RISK/CONT to other disposition systems - Preparation of functional, computer science and test concepts - Clarification and coordination of functional requirements with the specialist department - Effort estimation for implementations from functional requirements - Test - Support of productive operations / support (error analysis and remediation) in the RISK/CONT system. - Preparation and maintenance of documentation of technical systems and processes for the RISK/CONT system.

sig_45c985c19003ef2cd69f.description: 1. Contracting Authority The EWE Group, headquartered in Oldenburg, is one of the large regional energy supply companies in Germany. EWE is active in various business areas, including energy (gas/electricity), telecommunications, information technology, mobility and hydrogen. With over 10.000 employees and a turnover of around 8,7 billion euros in the 2024 financial year, EWE is one of the significant players in the German energy industry. EWE pursues a clear strategy towards a sustainable, innovative and future-oriented energy supply - including through projects in the field of wind energy and the hydrogen economy. The EWE Group is predominantly in municipal hands and supplies around one million households in the electricity segment alone. 2. Subject of the tender The EWE Group as the contracting authority (CA) intends to procure a software solution for Business Process Management (BPM) that meets the company's specific professional and technical requirements. The subject of the tender is the acquisition, implementation and operation of BPM software, including initial user training and the migration of existing data and process models from the legacy system to the new system. The software should enable intuitive modelling of processes - with a focus on Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN). For this purpose, user-friendly drag-and-drop editors are required for the simple creation, adaptation and maintenance of process models. In addition, the following functionalities are required: - Independently configurable workflows, e.g. for the approval of process models - Extensive commenting and collaboration options for all user groups - Versioning of process models and the possibility to manage several variants of a process - Comprehensive reporting and analysis functions Also desired are: - A flexibly configurable authorisation and role concept - Interfaces to other IT systems to support import and export processes, in particular: * Import of data from IT systems (e.g. organisational units) * Export of data to third-party systems, such as analysis platforms like SAP Datasphere, Snowflake or Azure OneLake
