sig_46d1eb55ab861ad2d53b.description:
Background and problem: The DEHSt has been operating end-to-end digitised specialist procedures for approx. 20 years. Central components of the IT landscape used by the DEHSt are in a phase of renewal. The number of software artefacts to be developed by the DEHSt is growing continuously – schedules are therefore becoming increasingly tight and parallelisation and complexity are increasing. Several legacy systems must also be completely replaced. To remedy this, the DEHSt has developed a Software Development Kit (SDK), which consists of software and extensive documentation, for example for commissioning a test and integration environment. The aim of the SDK is, on the one hand, to carry out a technological renewal and, on the other, to significantly increase development speed while maintaining standards. The SDK provides documentation, software libraries, several independent services for the centralised control (workflow control) of the specialist applications, as well as a base and an example application that integrates into the existing software and process landscape of the DEHSt (i.e. addresses existing central services, the so-called 'DEHSt platform'). The SDK and the DEHSt platform are based on a separation of frontend (AngularJS, NgRx, Material), backend (Spring-Boot), distributed web services and a build pipeline in GitLab as well as scalable operation on a container basis (Docker images on RedHat OKD). . Aim and subject of the project: This procurement measure is for a framework agreement with a term of 4 years. The framework agreement can be extended twice by one year each. The project is to include the development and maintenance of the entire Software Development Kit (SDK) as well as the development of specialist applications based on it. We distinguish between three related but parallel task areas: 1) Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management 2) Lot 2: New development of specialist applications 3) Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems For the SDK team, the goal is to increase the benefit for the administrative staff but also to positively influence the development time of the developer teams. For the developer teams, it must be a goal to develop a high-quality application in the shortest possible time based on an elaborated specification. Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 2.560 person-days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 640 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we see a demand of approximately 960 PD in the first year and an average of 500 PD per subsequent year. It is assumed that the workload can be distributed relatively evenly over the months so that a constant utilisation of a development team can be achieved.; Lot 2: New development of specialist applications . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 3.056 person-days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 764 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally see a demand of 500 PD per year, but in 2028 and 2029 an increased demand of about 1.000 PD. The utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. In most cases, the provision of the specialist applications must take place by fixed legal deadlines. This means that several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g. two to four development resources work on one specialist application, at the same time up to four specialist application projects must be processed). The legal deadline can unfortunately generally not be influenced by the contracting authority.; Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 4.472 (person-days) PD in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 1.118 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally see a demand of 650 PD per year, but in particular from mid 2028 until the change of the trading period in 2030 an increased demand of about 1.450 PD annually. The utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. The provision of the specialist applications must in most cases take place by fixed legal deadlines. This means that several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g.

two to four development resources work on one specialist application, at the same time up to four specialist application projects must be processed). The legal deadline can unfortunately generally not be influenced by the contracting authority.

sig_47117cc1f7e8df31d55e.buyer_name: South Karelia Wellbeing Services County; Päijät-Häme Wellbeing Services County
sig_47117cc1f7e8df31d55e.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information (RFI) whereby the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme invite system suppliers to register their interest for a potential procurement procedure. This is an RFI/market dialogue through which the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme are exploring potential system suppliers for an income and wealth assessment service to determine client fees in social welfare home care and housing services (community-based and round-the-clock living), as well as for compiling maintenance calculations in family law services and potentially for utilisation in other social welfare calculations. With this RFI, the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme are exploring digital solutions for compiling income and wealth assessments for client fee decisions using robotics. The client fee decision is made in connection with the client's service decision, and this has an impact on the management of the client process as well as on invoicing interruptions and terminations. The aim of the market survey is to find out what kind of product solutions containing the functionalities described below are available on the Finnish market. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services counties aim to: 1 Obtain information on market supply and different suppliers' solutions 2 Potential implementation of integrations into various platforms or systems 3 Evaluate the implementation of information security and data protection 4 Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 5 Explore delivery and service models The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer product solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions based on the automated compilation of income and wealth assessments to support client fee decisions. Suppliers are requested to present services that are under development or ready-made solutions. Suppliers participating in the dialogue are expected to present functionality to be put into production and information on how cooperation with the necessary actors to implement integrations has been taken into account in the preparation of the income and wealth assessment service. There is no need for a system solution based on process control, as this would result in additional recording requirements due to system changes. The core data contents consist of, inter alia, the Incomes Register and tax decisions of the Finnish Tax Administration, and benefit data from Kela. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: Purpose of use and environment The system must be suitable for the wellbeing services county's use for managing the following service forms: - income and wealth assessment for home care - income and wealth assessment for community-based housing, - income and wealth assessment for round-the-clock living - maintenance calculation for family law services, which forms part of a maintenance agreement concluded by parents. The maintenance calculation requires the data of both parents. - In all fees, the income data of spouses must be taken into account where necessary User groups include - children's supervisors - makers of client fee decisions in wellbeing services counties Key functionalities - produce, as part of the determination of client fees, income and wealth data on the basis of which a proposal for the amount of the client fee or solvency is formed - the calculation must not be saved in the income and wealth assessment service, meaning it does not create an archiving obligation. However, it must be possible to generate a PDF/PDF-A document from the document, which the wellbeing services county can attach as part of the decision and archive in a manner it deems fit. Integrations - Data transfer connection to the Finnish Tax Administration via the LIPA service bus (Incomes Register and tax data) - Data transfer connection to Kela's benefit data service via the LIPA service bus Technical requirements - The system must meet DPIA information security requirements - Data flow diagram and architecture description - User authentication and access control - Generation and management of log data Additional information - What other essential features does your solution include? - How is the implementation of the system typically carried out? - What kind of support and training do you offer? - Estimate from decision to implementation - The wellbeing services county's resource requirement Responses to the questions are requested to be sent by 14.9.2026 at 15:00. Responses are requested to be brief and informative. Responses are requested to be sent to hankinnat@ekhva.fi and hankinnat@paijatha.fi Message subject: "Market survey - Income and wealth assessment service system" This RFI/market survey does not request tenders nor are tenders submitted in response to this RFI; it requests ONLY information related to the procurement. Participation or non-participation in the market survey/RFI does not affect the tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (Supplier) to participate in a tendering procedure, nor is responding to this notice a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Those participating in the market survey are not entitled to receive compensation for their participation. The contracting authority does not undertake to carry out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The submitted material will be treated as confidential in accordance with section 24 subsection 1 paragraph 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities. The wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme thank you in advance for your responses. They are valuable in defining our system needs and preparing for a potential procurement.

sig_473df8db9ba357f2ba51.description: The Universitätsklinikum Münster (UKM) is conducting a market exploration for the introduction of a digital mailroom. The aim is to obtain information on available solutions, technical procedures, price levels and supplier structures. The survey is conducted in a technology- and process-open manner. The processing of incoming and outgoing mail is currently largely manual. External mail is sorted centrally, distributed and then re-sorted within the buildings. This process is time- and resource-intensive. Outgoing mail comprises both bulk and individual mailings. Providers who can already demonstrate successfully implemented solutions and present them as part of a system presentation are invited. Particular areas of focus are: - OCR/AI-supported text recognition in the scanning process - Handling of mail marked personal/confidential - Integration of the special electronic authority mailbox (beBPo) - Digitalisation of internal mail distribution The market exploration serves exclusively to gather information. This is not associated with a procurement decision. Interested providers are requested to submit proposed solutions and references for comparable projects to Universitätsklinikum Münster. Subsequently, the University Hospital will contact applicants it deems suitable.
sig_473df8db9ba357f2ba51.title: Digital mailroom - Market exploration

sig_475872817e19da0f367f.description:
Delivery/provision of a cloud-based software system for time recording (time management - ZWS) & personnel deployment planning (PEP) for medical services, nursing services & other service types. The subject of the procurement procedure is the provision of a cloud-based software solution (Software as a Service) for time recording (time management – ZWS) and personnel deployment planning (PEP) for the medical service (approx. 720 employees), the nursing service (approx. 2.180 employees) and other service types (approx. 1.372 employees – medical-technical service, functional service, administrative service, personnel of the training centres). In addition, approx. 500 internal and approx. 300 external students must also be managed in the system. A market-available standard solution is expressly being tendered, which can be adapted to the client's requirements through parameterisation. Individual solutions or in-house developments are excluded. This applies in particular to the bidirectional interface to the existing SAP ERP R/3 HCM infrastructure as well as to the new SAP S/4HANA environment. Further requirements for implementation, parameterisation, training and process standardisation are part of the tender documents or the specifications. The software must cover the following task areas in particular and must be provided as an integrated overall solution: -Personnel deployment planning incl. holiday and absence management (PEP) -Time management (ZWS) -Preparatory payroll accounting through the creation of collective agreement-relevant wage types in hourly or € values -Employee Self Service (ESS) -Manager Self Service (MSS) -Reporting and statistics. The interaction of these task areas is indispensable for efficient and modern personnel deployment planning, control and accounting. For this reason, these tasks must be closely linked and should appear as a single unit from a technological and user perspective. The solution must be able to be integrated without problems into the IT infrastructure available at the KC (SAP ERP R/3 HCM & SAP S/4HANA HCM & SAP IS-H/i.s.h.med) and must necessarily communicate with the software solutions already in use via standardised interfaces (state of the art). Both master data as well as attendance, absence and wage data must flow uni- and bidirectionally (depending on the data type) via the interfaces. The interface must necessarily work with change data records (data records to be changed in SAP are deleted and newly created or overwritten with new data records) in order to ensure the highest degree of automation and to minimise the need for manual intervention as far as possible. To map smooth processes, the PEP solution must ensure a consistent, secure and media-break-free data exchange. This is essential, especially for employee payroll accounting, and if it were to fail, it would have a lasting negative impact on the operation of the KC. The most automated transfer possible of required data from the legacy systems must be ensured. The new PEP solution must be able to import data from the IS-H/i.s.h.med, convert it into personnel requirements and integrate it into the deployment planning. With the help of the PEP solution, the wage types currently required at the Klinikum Chemnitz for the correct payroll accounting of all service types must be generated in accordance with the collective agreement regulations and transferred to the SAP HCM payroll and salary system in a time-controlled manner. In the medical collective agreement, 39 different wage types must currently be mapped, and in the non-medical collective agreement, 32 wage types. In some cases, wage types are created on an individual employee basis and depend on different conditions such as department, employee qualification, individual agreement. Especially with on-call duties, it happens that within a department, on-call duties are remunerated according to a fixed flat rate or according to the collective agreement regulations. The software solution must be able to map these constellations even within a month (see also the specifications). The connection of employees to the new PEP software solution is to take place in pre-defined waves. Accordingly, it must be ensured that some of the employees continue to be managed on the SAP PEP and other employees on the new PEP solution. The contractor must ensure that both systems function productively in parallel for the duration of the implementation and rollout and do not influence each other. The S/4HANA migration of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM planned in 2026 (Unicode conversion, database migration and S/4 application) must be taken into account. This concerns both project management and the function (bidirectional integration with the legacy systems HCM and ERP and the migration target, no PEP function maintenance after S/4HANA migration in the HCM). In addition, integration with the parallel project S/4HANA migration is required. The PEP solution is to be introduced on the current SAP HCM version ECC 8. Starting 2026, the transition of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM to SAP S/4HANA HCM is to take place, and with it the migration of the PEP software to the new system. Accordingly, it is assumed that the contractor has already successfully migrated the interfaces of their software solution from SAP ECC to S/4HANA and that all required functions are also fully available in the integration with an S/4HANA system (HCM and ERP). A project-specific EVB-IT cloud contract & service contract will be concluded for the procurement. The draft contract is part of this publication as well as the tender documents for the initial offer and can be further specified by the client within the framework of the procurement negotiations. The procurement is for a minimum contract term of 36 months after operational readiness has been established.

Thereafter, the contract shall be extended by one year at a time, unless it is terminated by one of the parties six months before the end of the contract. Details on this can also be found in the tender documents of the subsequent offer phase or offer phases.

The company was established in 2023 and, at the beginning of 2024, operations were transferred from the City of Tampere's municipal enterprise to a corporate form. Tampereen Vesi Oy provides water utility services in its operating area. The operating area mainly covers the zoned area of the City of Tampere. Tampereen Vesi Oy is inviting tenders for total payroll services, a time and attendance system and an HR system. OPTION IN PROCUREMENT PART A: Travel management services (incl. travel ledger and travel and expense claim system). PROCUREMENT PART B: HR system (incl. personal data system and HRD system). In both procurement parts, the systems used will process personal data extensively, so data protection requirements must be taken into account. The systems must also have the possibility to restrict access rights on a role-based basis. Both procurement parts also include the commissioning of services and systems, related advisory and expert services, and system support services. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in Annex 1 Preliminary service description. Information may be clarified during the procurement procedure. sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.
sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?

The scope of services further includes the delivery and assignment of the required software licences or usage rights, setup and parameterisation, data migration from legacy systems, connection of legacy systems, training and documentation, as well as subsequent software maintenance and support. The contractual basis for the supplies and services to be provided will be an EVB-IT framework agreement, which consists in particular of elements of the EVB-IT System, the EVB-IT Assignment Agreement Type A, the EVB-IT Cloud Contract, and the EVB-IT Maintenance S Contract, each with the corresponding EVB-IT general terms and conditions

sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure with the publication of the request for information; instead, any potential procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a precondition for participation in any subsequent tendering procedure that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information or for participating in the market dialogue. The responses provided to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of a personnel planning system. The subject of the procurement is a personnel planning system which: - supports strategic personnel planning and takes into account the qualitative (incl. staff competency structure) and quantitative planning of personnel required for organising service operations - enables the planning of personnel resources at the supervisory level - operates in accordance with processes defined by labour legislation (takes into account the starts, changes, terminations, etc., of employment relationships) - takes into account that the volume of personnel resources is guided by the level of service operations (increases / decreases / remains the same), care intensity and the budget, rather than a static, administrative vacancy system - can be integrated into HUS's other systems - scales to HUS's current personnel and organisational structure and its potential future changes - is a ready-made overall solution / service package. Personnel planning has a close connection to financial planning / the planning system (personnel costs). BACKGROUND TO THE PROCUREMENT Personnel planning is based on HUS's strategy and objectives. Personnel planning is carried out in both the short and long term. Strategic personnel planning is the organisation's long-term personnel planning. It can be used to anticipate changes in the operating environment and evaluate cost impacts. Personnel planning supports the organisation in achieving its objectives by ensuring access to the right capabilities, in the right place and at the right time. The objectives of planning are: - To identify the required number and structure of personnel as well as competence - To define the measures needed to ensure the personnel in accordance with the objective. These may include: • structural solutions related to the organisation of work and divisions of labour • development of personnel competence • renewal of processes • utilisation of digitalisation / new technologies The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service ranges. The purpose is to ascertain technical solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for the budget. HUS-yhtymä requests your written comments in particular on the following questions: - What kind of system / service package are you offering (description of implementation) and with what functionalities does the solution meet the needs of the contracting authority described in this request for information? - What are the integration possibilities of the solution you are offering? - What is the pricing model of the solution you are offering (e.g. licences, maintenance and support)? - Is the system / service package you are offering in use in other similar organisations (wellbeing services counties, health and social services operators)? Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will process your responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, suppliers may be offered an opportunity to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may be given preliminary call for tenders documents for comment. We kindly ask you to submit your responses to the request for information and notify us of your interest no later than 11.12.2025 by 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must state "HUS 495-2025 - Request for information: Personnel planning system".
sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.title: Request for Information: Human Resources Planning System

sig_4a270e1f30b203ded6d0.description: Framework Agreement for the Call-Off Provision of Associate Trainers: Digital Skills, Management Skills, Marketing including digital marketing and social media, Communication and Soft Skills, Health and Safety, Construction and Trade, Training and Assessment, Care, Mindfulness and Wellbeing, HR Training, Procurement, Tendering and bid writing, Accountancy systems, Visual Merchandising, Customer Service and Retail Optimisation Lot 1: Digital Skills. Digital skills, Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills, data literacy and data management, digital transformation and innovation capability, cybersecurity skills, digital marketing and e-commerce. With the acceleration of digital, the following are also subject areas that are in high demand: Digital skills focus on strong digital communication and collaboration abilities alongside cloud and productivity fundamentals. Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills centre on understanding foundational and responsible AI principles as well as applying process automation tools. Data literacy and data management priorities include the ability to interpret and visualise data effectively and uphold good data governance and ethics. Digital transformation and innovation capability requires skills in digital strategy and change leadership, paired with service design and user centred design approaches. Cybersecurity skills focus on building strong cyber hygiene and user awareness, supported by basic risk management and incident response knowledge. Digital marketing and e commerce emphasise SEO and analytics, combined with content creation and digital advertising to drive engagement and growth. Accredited and non-accredited opportunities ranging from SCQF5 and above requested. Training in widely used, industry standard digital tools- such as Microsoft Teams, OneNote for collaborative working, and digital bookkeeping platforms - is also in high demand. Lot 2: Management Skills. Strategic leadership & future planning, workforce development & talent management, change management and digital adoption, people, leadership & wellbeing management, operational & performance management. Businesses require managers who can demonstrate strong strategic leadership and future planning, workforce development and talent management, change management and digital adoption, people focused leadership and wellbeing management, and effective operational and performance management. Building these capabilities ensures leaders can respond to rapid technological change, manage skills gaps, and support resilient, high performing teams. Training should develop practical management capabilities including project management, change management, managing through crisis situations, supervising hybrid or home based teams, leading and motivating others, and building strong supervisory skills. Programmes should also strengthen interpersonal and developmental capabilities such as assertiveness, change and recovery management, coaching skills, developing individuals, and Insights Discovery profiling to support self awareness and team effectiveness. These subject areas are designed for new supervisors, emerging managers, and those seeking to upskill for career progression. Both accredited and non accredited options should be available. Non accredited workshops can be delivered as half day or full day sessions and should be contextualised to the specific needs of the business, particularly for bespoke contracts or sector specific requirements. Lot 3: Marketing. Businesses require marketing training across a wide range of evolving subject areas, including AI enhanced marketing skills, agile and adaptive marketing capability, data driven marketing and analytics, search engine optimisation SEO, content strategy and digital advertising, customer engagement and trust building, omnichannel and customer experience design, and advanced digital platforms and mobile first technologies. Alongside these, there is growing demand for brand creation and management, communications and PR, marketing strategy development, crisis communications, and video production, as well as understanding the difference between amplification and publication as businesses seek growth, explore new markets, or reposition for new audiences. Practical creative skills such as graphic design — particularly 2D/3D animation and Photoshop/Illustrator upskilling to enhance in house capability and deliver more impactful digital content. Digital marketing and social media skills are increasingly essential, enabling businesses to build visibility, engage target audiences, and compete effectively across fast moving online platforms. Lot 4: Communication and Soft Skills. Communication & interpersonal skills, teamwork and collaboration, adaptability & resilience, emotional intelligence & people skills, leadership & soft aligned skills, customer focused skills. Strong communication and soft skill capabilities to help teams adapt to rapid technological, economic and workforce change, clear and confident workplace communication, active listening, teamwork, collaboration, resilience, adaptability and emotional intelligence, as well as core interpersonal skills such as delivering effective presentations, problem solving, assertiveness and customer service communication. Training to mitigate the widening internal skills gaps and meet the growing importance of adaptability, creativity and strong communication. Seeking non accredited, introductory to intermediate level training, typically delivered in half day or full day formats, allowing staff to quickly upskill in essential, business ready soft skills that support productivity and workforce effectiveness. Lot 5: Health and Safety. Practical, compliance focused health and safety training that ensures staff are competent, up to date and able to manage modern workplace risks. Address gaps in documentation, risk assessments and ongoing training. COSHH Awareness, Human Factors in Health and Safety, IOSH Managing Safely, IOSH Working Safely, IOSH SHECW, NEBOSH qualifications, and broader Occupational Health and Safety training, support with legal duties around safe working environments. Fire risk awareness, mental health and wellbeing, and maintaining workforce competency through regular refresher learning. Alongside accredited options, non accredited, short format courses to provide flexible, cost effective, introductory or refresher training tailored to SME’s operational needs. Lot 6: Construction and Trades. Essential electrical safety and compliance training, including the City & Guilds 18th Edition Electrical Wiring Regulations (full qualification and industry update) and PAT Testing and Inspection & Testing Upskilling for renewable energy systems, EV charging installation, battery storage safety, Lock Out–Tag Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical diagnostics. Ensuring staff remain competent, compliant and able to work safely with modern technologies. These may be delivered through accredited qualifications or short, non accredited practical courses to support flexible, cost effective workforce development. Lot 7: Training and Assessing. Workforce development training that strengthens internal capability, particularly through Assessor and Verifier qualifications, Coaching and Mentoring, and Train the Trainer programmes, enabling businesses to build in house expertise, support staff progression and maintain quality assurance across learning and development activities. Delivered as accredited or non accredited options, offering flexible, cost effective pathways that allow organisations to choose between formal qualification routes or shorter, practical sessions tailored to operational needs. Lot 8: Care, Mindfulness and Wellbeing. Safeguarding, Child Protection and Adult Protection training to ensure staff can recognise, respond to and escalate concerns in line with current legislation and best practice. Autism training, including delivery aligned to D&A certificated programmes and SQA certificated courses, supporting organisations to work confidently and inclusively with neurodiverse individuals. Trauma Informed Practice, Mental Health First Aid, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) awareness, De escalation and Behaviour Support, and Professional Boundaries & Safer Working Practices, reflecting an increased emphasis on safe, ethical and inclusive service delivery. All programmes can be offered as accredited or non accredited options, providing flexible, practical learning tailored to organisational and sector requirements. Lot 9: HR Training, Procurement, Tendering and Bid Writing. HR training to strengthens effective people management, support compliance and improve workplace capability. HR focused training in areas such as employment practice, performance management and fair work aligned people processes. Procurement training to help understand and navigate Scotland’s public procurement system, the Scottish Government’s SME and Third Sector Procurement Action Plan (2024–2026), improve supplier readiness and expand SME participation in public contracts. Training for procurement rules, compliance expectations, sustainable procurement requirements and effective use of Public Contracts Scotland. Tendering and bid writing: practical support to build confidence and competence in preparing competitive bids. Training to facilitate understanding of evaluation criteria and improved tender preparation directly and to win contracts. Training in tender structure, evidence development and persuasive, compliant bid writing. Lot 10: Accountancy Systems. Cloud accounting training, including tools to report major internal and external cost savings while simplifying invoicing, reconciliation and reporting. Software including but not limited to: Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage Business Cloud. Training for real time reporting & dashboard use, automated reconciliation & digital invoicing, integration of cloud accounting with payroll, inventory & CRM. Automation & Digital Bookkeeping Skills, including AI assisted bookkeeping & categorisation, Automated VAT and payroll workflows Cybersecurity in Financial Systems, including secure logins & multi factor authentication, data backup & GDPR compliant data handling, fraud prevention & financial system risk awareness Digital Taxation & Compliance, including making Tax Digital (MTD) for VAT & self assessment, digital record keeping, submission of returns via cloud platforms. Data Driven Finance & Business Partnering Skills, including training for financial dashboards & data visualisation, forecasting & scenario modelling, KPI development & management reporting, business partnering & commercial analysis. Lot 11: Visual Merchandising, Customer Service and Retail Optimisation. Creative and strategic visual merchandising, high quality customer service and communication and operational retail skills for efficient and profitable store management Visual Merchandising Skills including window display design & in store presentation - creating eye catching, brand aligned displays, store layout planning & product placement - designing customer flow, optimising lighting, and using fixtures effectively to guide purchasing decisions. Understanding customer behaviour & retail psychology. Customer Service Skills for retail, including high quality customer interaction skills- effective communication, problem solving, and managing queries or complaints. Service excellence & personalisation- delivering tailored shopping experiences, a key differentiator in modern retail. Retail Optimisation Skills to improve store performance and operational efficiency, including retail operations management- record keeping, staffing, stock control and security procedures. Maximising retail profitability, including evaluating sales data, identifying improvement opportunities, and applying merchandising strategies. Marketing products effectively - basic retail marketing skills to support promotions, product visibility and brand positioning.

sig_4a280c8be1ebf32a6150.description: The Finnish National Agency for Education is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS), which covers the provision of expertise and technical support in the education sector, with a particular focus on services related to developing countries and emerging markets. The assignments tendered through this DPS may include, for example: • expert advice and support to EDUFI and to developing country ministries and organizations in development of education, • conducting analytical studies, reviews and evaluations • drafting and updating policy guidelines and other documentation, • designing and supporting the developing of action/project plans, • organizing and delivering training and capacity building sessions. Below is a list of the major work that included in the DPS, but not limited to: • externally funded projects of the Finnish National Agency for Education, such as Team Europe Initiatives - The Regional Teachers Initiative for Africa (RTIA) which supports teacher education and teacher professional development in Sub-Saharan Africa, including providing Technical Assistance to ministries of education. - Opportunity-Driven Skills and Vocational Education and Training in Africa (TEI OP-VET) which provides targeted support to (re)orient existing or planned sector-specific skills and VET interventions in partner countries across Sub-Saharan Africa, including Technical Assistance. • and other similar work of the Finnish National Agency for Education The scope and subject-matter of the DPS is described in more detail particularly in annex 1 "Subject-matter of the DPS". The DPS covers implementation of project work during 2025-2030 period. TOTAL VALUE The estimated total value of the Dynamic Procurement System is up to 8 000 000 euros (excluding VAT).

sig_4d2c5259822d64148bd2.description: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Biological Research has the potential to pave the way for breakthroughs in biotechnology and bio-system design that will create innovations, new industries, and jobs. To capitalize on this promise, the Directorate for Biological Sciences (BIO) will make awards for Postdoctoral Research Fellowships in Biology (PRFB) to recent doctoral degree recipients, for proposals with a research and training focus at the Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Biological Sciences to Strengthen and Safeguard Biotechnology Innovations. Applying AI to highly complex biological systems will reveal unknown mechanisms in the natural world that hold promise for technological developments. Candidates with AI and/or biology experience will develop deep expertise in both by proposing additional training in both areas. These combinations of current expertise and new cross-training will produce scientists who work seamlessly at the intersection of AI and biology. The fellows are expected to become field leaders who use AI capabilities to extrapolate from biological data to technological advances. Proposers are encouraged to consider how to leverage the nation’s diversity of existing biological data, and biological infrastructure, such as Biofoundries, Programmable Cloud Labs, Manufacturing USA Institutes, and NEON, to accelerate discovery, innovation and the biotechnology that improves human lives, promotes the U.S. economy, and benefits the nation.
sig_4d2c5259822d64148bd2.title: Postdoctoral Research Fellowships in Biology

sig_4d6289655769a44b06b9.description: Crown Estate Scotland (CES) is seeking a contractor to lead the survey and reporting of our tenant groups on the Scottish Crown Estate. CES has been surveying its tenants since 2017, with survey providing important feedback on CES performance, the service we provide and the relationship we have with our tenants Lot 1: . Crown Estate Scotland (CES) is seeking a contractor to lead the survey and reporting of our tenant groups on the Scottish Crown Estate. CES has been surveying its tenants since 2017, with survey providing important feedback on CES performance, the service we provide and the relationship we have with our tenants. There has been a break in survey while we have been developing our new corporate plan, with the last surveys carried out in 2023. This contract will align with our new corporate plan timeframe 2026-2031 with two surveys required – one in the first year of the Corporate Plan, scheduled for August this year (2026). And a second survey in year four of the corporate plan in FY 2029/30. Surveys are of our three main tenant groups – Property, Energy and Infrastructure, and Aquaculture, with reporting against a number of sub-groups under these. Previously different tenant groups were surveyed separately, with a rolling programme of surveys across a three-year cycle. For this contract we will survey all tenant groups together, requiring only one survey and reporting cycle in 2026 and again in 2029/30. Key to this survey will be reporting against the new corporate plan KPI on customer satisfaction ‘Customer satisfaction is increased by 10% over the plan period from the 2026 baseline’. Some support will be required on survey development and framing. All previous tenant surveys have been led by a contractor, adding transparency, objectivity and impartiality to the survey, helping to engender tenant trust and confidence in the process. Please note that the first survey must be completed in August 2026.

sig_4dad3150d64ada67da42.description: Transparency notice within the meaning of § 135 para. 3 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB) Measure: Acquisition of the software OK.Verkehr for vehicle registration and operation in the data centre for vehicle registration and driving licences Information on review periods: Regarding the deadlines for filing legal remedies, reference is made to § 160 para. 3 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB). § 160 GWB reads as follows: (1) The Public Procurement Chamber shall initiate a review procedure only upon application. (2) Any undertaking that has an interest in the public contract or concession and claims an infringement of its rights under § 97 para. 6 due to non-compliance with procurement regulations is entitled to file an application. In doing so, it must be demonstrated that the undertaking has suffered or is threatened with damage as a result of the alleged infringement of procurement regulations. (3) The application is inadmissible if: 1) the applicant has recognised the alleged infringement of procurement regulations before submitting the application for review and has not complained about it to the contracting authority within a period of 10 calendar days; the expiry of the period according to § 134 paragraph 2 remains unaffected, 2) infringements of procurement regulations that are recognisable from the notice are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders specified in the notice, 3) infringements of procurement regulations that only become recognisable in the procurement documents are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders, 4) more than 15 calendar days have passed since receipt of the notification from the contracting authority that it does not intend to remedy a complaint. Sentence 1 does not apply to an application for a declaration of the ineffectiveness of the contract pursuant to § 135 para. 1 no. 2. § 134 para. 1 sentence 2 remains unaffected. The contract can only be executed by a specific economic operator, as here, pursuant to § 14 para. 4 no. 2b of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV), only one company can be considered for the contract for technical reasons.
sig_4dad3150d64ada67da42.title: Transparency notice pursuant to § 135 para. 3 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB) for software procurement and maintenance for the vehicle registration and driving licence authority

sig_4e0f3a5f7e829612a581.description: The Piedmont Region, within the scope of the Electronic Health Record (EHR), manages radiological images through local and regional PACS systems, but the current architecture is fragmented and poorly standardised across the various Healthcare Authorities. This situation generates inefficiencies, difficulties with updates and suboptimal access to images, especially in clinical contexts where timeliness is crucial. Furthermore, viewing functionalities are limited and not fully integrated with regional digital services and telemedicine. To respond to the new requirements of interoperability, continuity of care and telemedicine, it is necessary to evolve towards a federated, scalable and user-centred platform capable of guaranteeing immediate, secure and integrated access to radiological images. With this market sounding, CSI-Piemonte therefore intends to verify the presence on the market of solutions that meet the aforementioned technical-functional and organisational requirements.

sig_4e2be62957b3ffaefa98.description: Puolustusvoimien logistiikkalaitos (hereinafter the contracting authority) invites you to submit a request to participate in the Haapajärvi charging plant production line development project for the Finnish Defence Forces in accordance with this call for requests to participate and its annexes. Subject of the procurement: Planning and development site located in the production area of the Haapajärvi unit of the explosives centre. The main tasks are: The contracting authority wishes to develop the production line using automation and robotics. The aim is simultaneously to minimise the number of personnel. The candidate must state the number of personnel required for the modernised line at the stated capacities. The contracting authority has selected the following objects for automation: Renewal of the existing lower conveyor, including automation of the existing laboratory work (includes thread cleaning and inspection, attaching / installing the intermediate piece, and loading the upper conveyor), automation of the attachment of the existing cavity base and automation of the existing weighing operation. The procurement includes all necessary design work, dismantling of obsolete technology, and delivery and installation of new technology in the explosive premises (IP54 T4) as a turnkey delivery in accordance with the procurement documents. The selected supplier must design all possible operations of the procurement object to be automated and to operate automatically. Likewise, the machines and equipment to be modernised must be designed to function as independent parts of the rest of the existing production equipment. The modernised line must meet the ergonomics requirements and capacity needs with 81 VRTKR, 120 VRTKR and 155 TKR products. There are various versions of these products, and these versions are specified in separately delivered drawings. The main tasks included in the delivery are listed as follows: 1) Production capacity in accordance with requirements and minimisation of the number of personnel 2) Renewal of the existing lower conveyor 3) Automation of the operations of the existing laboratory work (including thread cleaning and inspection, installation of the detonator, attaching / installing the intermediate piece, and loading the upper conveyor) 4) Automation of the operations of the existing cavity base attachment 5) Automation of the existing weighing operation. Items 2 to 5 include design, dismantling of the existing redundant part, and necessary equipment deliveries and installations. The objective is to carry out the procurement (including the design phase) during the years 2026 to 2027, such that the timing of the installation of the new technology would be as follows: Working hours at the site are possible 19.07.2027 to 15.10.2027 (weeks 29 to 41). The delivery must be ready by 15.10.2027. Working on site is permitted during installations around the clock every day of the week, if necessary. Before starting the installations, the selected supplier must carry out all necessary design. The selected supplier must present (in written and oral form) the entire implementation proposal for the procurement (including necessary plans and capacity calculations) to the Customer in good time, i.e. when the necessary plans are, in the supplier's opinion, ready for presentation. The final implementation documentation is included in the delivery scope of the procurement. The contracting parties shall agree on the more precise installation schedule within the aforementioned delivery schedule in accordance with the terms of the procurement contract to be signed after the selection of the supplier. The final acceptance is preceded by trial runs (cold run / hot run), capacity runs, training, delivery of final documentation and official inspections. The new equipment must be fully ready for use and production by 15.10.2027. The contracting authority will send the invitation to tender and its annexes (incl. technical specification) on the basis of this call for requests to participate to the tenderers approved by the contracting authority.

sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.description: Aarhus Vand is a utility group that manages water and wastewater activities. In this context, Aarhus Vand owns, operates, and maintains many kilometres of water and wastewater pipes distributed across the supply area. To ensure efficient operation of the pipes, Aarhus Vand requires accurate, updated, and accessible registration of the pipe network. For this purpose, Aarhus Vand needs a pipe registration system. Aarhus Vand wishes for a collective agreement comprising both the licences for the pipe registration system itself and consultancy services for ongoing development and maintenance of the system. Aarhus Vand hereby invites to a market dialogue regarding the above. The purpose of the market dialogue includes determining which systems are on the market that can fulfil Aarhus Vand's factual and objective needs. Aarhus Vand has identified the following requirements as being important in relation to a future pipe registration system. It is important to Aarhus Vand that these requirements can already be fulfilled now. The list is not considered exhaustive: 1. Full support for DANVA's latest models, currently: Dandas 3.1.2, TV inspection and manhole report 3.1.2, Danvand 2.1.2, cables, third-party pipes, and areas 1.1, burst registration 1.1.1. For all models, this applies to all concepts, attributes, codes, relations, and interfaces as well as DANVA's guidelines and data manuals. The system is configurable so that it can be easily and quickly adapted to changes in both the models and the user interface 2. All registrations are saved / data resides in one and the same database 3. The system must support data exchange in XML format. There must be an option for direct updating via e.g. SQL. There must be direct access to data, as well as the possibility of making direct integrations with other systems. 4. Quality assurance. XSD validation, predefined validations, etc., which support pipe registration and work with data, and thus ensure and maintain good data quality. 5. Possibility to work in "jobs" in connection with the digitalisation of an area / project / subject, which can subsequently be upgraded to be the master. That is, so that one does not work in the master until changes have been upgraded to the master. 6. The language in the system must be Danish. To a minor extent, it can be in English. 7. User interface. An intuitive and user-friendly user interface. Workflows must be supported by configurable templates/flows. Must contain a tool for replacing, splitting, and merging objects, e.g. pipes. Must have various construction tools. Must have 3D support. 8. User management via AD integration. Users must be able to have different roles/rights. 9. The solution must have stable and high performance 10. There must be an auto-save feature, or recovery of unsaved work or similar. All market operators who believe they can meet the above requirements are encouraged to register for the market dialogue. FRAMEWORK AND PARTICIPATION OF THE DIALOGUE As a general rule, the market dialogue will take place physically at Aarhus Vand, Hasselager Allé 29, 8260 Viby J. The dialogue is held individually per market operator. Interest in the market dialogue must be reported to Christoffer Larsen at christoffer.larsen@aarhusvand.dk or indkob@aarhusvand.dk no later than 20.10.2025. The dialogue meetings are held in the period from 21.10.2025 to 31.10.2025.
sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding IT system for utility registration in connection with water, wastewater, etc.

sig_500928eb240e422aaf60.description: This Market Engagement seeks to identify options to enable procurement of a dedicated backup collection tool for Operational Technology (OT) environments. The solution will ensure that the complete data state of critical OT assets is consistently captured and securely stored across multiple sites, serving as the organisation's data of last resort. The tool must collect the full backup state of OT assets including configurations, control logic, firmware, hardware metadata, and associated files. It must support both automated, policy-driven backup collection and authorised manual backup initiation, operating through secure and non-intrusive protocols that do not interact with OT control or programming interfaces and have no impact on live operations or safety-critical systems. The solution must be vendor-agnostic, deployable fully on-premise or within a private cloud, and capable of operating in air-gapped environments, with full audit trails and compliance reporting. IMPORTANT: Please read this section before deciding whether you wish to register for this event. This section provides you with information regarding the scope of this procurement and details some of the key requirements that a successful applicant MUST be able to deliver.
sig_500928eb240e422aaf60.title: Data of Last Resort Data Collection

sig_500a51ad0d67fead7aef.description: This notice is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, and its publication does not initiate a tendering competition. This is a market survey and a request for information related to a preliminary study directed at potential suppliers. The purpose of the request for information is to survey the solutions available on the market and to obtain comprehensive information regarding them so that the procurement in preparation can be carried out as appropriately as possible. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in the competition and does not affect the tenderer's position in it. The matters presented in the request for information are preliminary and may change as the preparation of the procurement progresses. The feedback received in the request for information will potentially be utilised in the preparation of the call for tenders. The subject of the request for information is a document management and archiving service at various information security levels (SaaS and On-Premise) including electronic signature, the possibility of integrations and the utilisation of automation, as well as customer support. The customer support service hours are fundamentally during office hours 8-16.15, but it must be expandable according to customer needs (possibly also at weekends). Customer support is available in Finnish and Swedish, with good oral and written skills in Finnish as a requirement. The anticipated scope of the procurement in the initial phase is approximately 20 central government organisations of varying sizes, a small proportion of which require the On-Premise service. We kindly ask you to register for the market dialogue by responding to this request for information in Tarjouspalvelu by the deadline. The market dialogue is divided into two phases: 1. Written responses to the request for information electronically by 17.10.2025 2. Supplier meetings: a review of the supplier's solution and open questions concerning the subject of the procurement. The meetings will be held in weeks 45 and 46. We reserve the right to present additional questions to suppliers if it is deemed necessary for the advancement of the competition. Any additional questions will be presented electronically to those who have participated in the market dialogue. The contracting authority will select a maximum of 5 potential tenderers for the market dialogue that have the capability to produce the service in accordance with the subject of the procurement in its planned scope. The capability of potential tenderers will be assessed based on the responses given to the questions presented later in this request for information. An invitation to the meeting will be sent to the suppliers selected for the market dialogue by the end of week 43. Those who have responded to the request for information or participated in the market dialogue will not be paid any compensation for responding to the request for information or for costs arising from participation in the market dialogue. The information provided by suppliers will be treated confidentially.

sig_50dbbeb33ff1ae694cb9.description: The aim of this tender is to conclude several framework agreements on the evaluation of communication measures by the Federal Government, federal ministries and subordinate or associated authorities ("Federal Government Alliance"). These framework agreements comprise in particular the advice, development, conception, implementation and evaluation of evaluations. For this purpose, future contractors shall propose and implement suitable evaluations in accordance with the topics, issues, objectives and target groups specified by the demand bearers. The awarding of these services takes place in two lots. A detailed description of the service to be provided can be found in the contracts and the specifications. Lot 1 of the framework agreement tendered here primarily comprises the evaluation of press and public relations (PR) measures of the Federal Government, the respective federal ministries and federal authorities including subordinate or associated authorities ("Federal Government Alliance"). In addition to the evaluation of this external communication, this lot also enables the evaluation of internal products of the demand bearers (e.g. intranet, newscenter, etc.) as well as internal processes by surveying the employees of the demand bearers (internal communication). It includes qualitative methods such as group discussions, qualitative workshops, insight communities, in-depth interviews as well as quantitative methods such as computer-assisted surveys (CATI, CAPI, CASI, CAWI), written postal interviews/push-to-web surveys, mixed-mode surveys, embedding questions in an omnibus survey and on-site surveys. In addition, usability tests are also possible (using qualitative or quantitative methods). A detailed description of the service to be provided can be found in the contract and the specification; Lot 2 of the framework agreement tendered here comprises media resonance analysis and the analysis of public relations in social media for the Federal Government, the respective federal ministries and federal authorities including subordinate or associated authorities ("Federal Government Alliance"). A detailed description of the service to be provided can be found in the contract and the specification.
sig_50dbbeb33ff1ae694cb9.title: Evaluation of Federal Government communication measures ('Evaluation 2026')

sig_51dd928abedab57fcef9.description: The U.S. Military Academy at West Point's mission is "to educate, train, and inspire the Corps of Cadets so that each graduate is a commissioned leader of character committed to the values of Duty, Honor, Country and prepared for a career of professional excellence and service to the Nation as an officer in the United States Army." The United States Military Academy is located at West Point, New York. USMA executes research to enhance the education of cadets, develop the faculty professionally, and address important issues facing the Army and the Nation. In addition, the Academy conducts research and analysis in emerging fields that may realize novel or vastly improved Army capabilities. At West Point, research is organized and administered through centers and institutes, most of which reside within academic departments. These centers and institutes, affiliated with each other through the Academy Research Council (ARC), coordinated and supported by the Academic Research Division (ARD), provide the infrastructure necessary to tackle the nation’s and the world’s most challenging problems. Our research centers and institutes bring context to the classroom, are central to our vibrant and pioneering faculty, and are one way West Point connects to the Army and to the Nation. Our students are driven, our faculty is world-class, and through our centers, scholars and scientists thrive and produce their best work. Cadets regularly win Best Paper Awards at national and international graduate-level conferences, our faculty hold fellowships and chairmanships in their discipline's national organizations and our products are deployed to the soldier. In addition to applied research, there are centers and institutes at West Point that focus on other aspects of the USMA mission. The USMA BAA identifies topics of interest to the USMA departments, directorates, and research centers and institutes. These groups focus on executing in-house research programs, with a significant emphasis on collaborative research with other organizations. The groups fund a modest amount of extramural research in certain specific areas, and those areas are described in this BAA. The USMA BAA seeks proposals from institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, state and local governments, foreign organizations, foreign public entities, and for-profit organizations (i.e., large and small businesses) for research based on the following campaigns: Socio-Cultural; Information Technology; Ballistics, Weapons, and Protections; Energy and Sustainability; Materials, Measurements, and Facilities; Unmanned Systems and Space; Human Support Systems; and Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Quantum Technologies. Proposals are sought for cutting-edge innovative research that could produce discoveries with a significant impact to enable new and improved Army technologies and related operational capabilities and related technologies. The specific research areas and topics of interest described in this document should be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting.
sig_51dd928abedab57fcef9.title: UNITED STATES MILITARY ACADEMY Broad Agency Announcement

sig_520c3a78e4d7855a5f4a.description: Mobile operational data collection in road maintenance operations at Hessen Mobil for the East Hesse and West Hesse departments As part of this tender, road maintenance operations at Hessen Mobil for the 8 road maintenance depots of the Operations and Traffic Department East Hesse and the 8 road maintenance depots of the Operations and Traffic Department West Hesse are to be optimised through the deployment of a mobile operational management system (EMS). The main objectives of the new operational management system (EMS) in winter maintenance are legally secure verification of the operations carried out in the context of the duty to maintain road safety, operational evaluations, performance billing with external contractors and other road construction authorities, as well as efficient operational control using real-time monitoring. Furthermore, drivers are to be relieved of workload during winter maintenance by means of route guidance functions. The contracting authority intends to conclude an EVB-IT service contract (with a system delivery contract) with up to 3 extension options of 12 months each.

The subject matter of the contract is the design, implementation, quality assurance and support during commissioning and operation of the new reporting platform of WIBank (Wirtschafts- und Infrastrukturbank Hessen), an institution within an institution (Anstalt in der Anstalt - AIDA) within Landesbank Hessen-Thüringen (Helaba). In addition, this includes the ongoing further development of the platform created as part of the project. The existing info portal currently forms the central data warehouse and reporting system of WIBank. It consolidates data from various source systems and provides reports based on this as well as returns for funding programmes of the European Union, the Federal Government and the State of Hesse. The subject matter of the project is the provision of a new reporting platform for the finance and accounting, risk management and treasury departments. This includes in particular the connection of SAP WIBank as the initial operational source system, the setup of the "Regulatory Reporting" data mart, the transfer of historical data from the existing info portal and the implementation of the defined target reports. Upon completion of the project, the developed platform will be expanded as part of continuous further development. This includes in particular the connection of further source systems, the setup of additional data marts and the migration of further reports from the existing info portal. In the long term, the existing info portal is to be completely replaced and decommissioned. All services are to be provided on the basis of a framework agreement and therefore only upon separate call-off/individual order. The upper limit for call-offs from the framework agreement amounts to a total of EUR 6,5 million (gross). For further details, reference is made to Appendix I 02 - Appendix 0_Specification of Services.

sig_52f1d358a2b23a5a2733.description: NRW.BANK is the largest state promotional bank in Germany. It employs approximately 1650 members of staff and, with a total assets of approximately 162 billion euros, ranks 11 among all banks in Germany. It consists of 19 divisions with a total of 250 organisational units and 232 managers, of which 5 are dual leadership roles. Since 2022, a cultural change initiative has been underway within the bank, the results of which include the design of a mission statement with strong requirement criteria for collaboration, initiative, efficiency and personal responsibility. Culture pilots support implementation in the 19 divisions of the bank. In parallel with this, alongside the traditional run organisation for ongoing business processes, an agile delivery organisation has been and is currently being established in which larger change projects are bundled into agile-working teams. The organisational structure has not been changed in this context, i.e. the members of staff seconded wholly or partly to the agile delivery organisation also remain attached to managers in the existing organisational structure. The scope of the contract includes the preparation, execution and follow-up of an annual staff survey. The contractor shall conduct the surveys using an online survey instrument. The first survey shall be conducted in September 2026. The notification of all managers regarding the survey results for their areas of responsibility must have taken place by November 2026 at the latest. The workshops for processing the survey results shall follow immediately after the first survey and take place on demand. Following the first survey, the cycle for subsequent surveys shall be determined: this can be 12, 18 or 24 months. Further details can be found in the specification of requirements (Annex 1) or the framework agreement.
sig_52f1d358a2b23a5a2733.title: Employee survey at NRW.BANK

sig_53859266daf39dfe09a0.description: 2M-IT Oy (hereinafter also the "Contracting Authority" or "Client") is establishing a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for data-driven management and artificial intelligence services. Organisations providing services under the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) may submit requests to participate in the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All candidates who have submitted a request to participate and who meet the suitability requirements set for candidates will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. The internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system to be established will cover data-driven management and AI platforms, solutions and services, licences, and expert services, as well as various combinations thereof. The aforementioned are to be procured for services produced for social and healthcare organisations, which will be specified in more detail in the call for tenders for the DPS internal competition. Solutions may be procured for use in specialised medical care, primary healthcare, and social services, as well as in support activities related to these tasks. They may be implemented in the service production of 2M-IT Oy as part of the services for one or more clients. In addition, 2M-IT Oy may also procure solutions for the needs of its own business operations. The actual procurements will be made on the basis of separate calls for tenders as internal competitions within the DPS, in which the contracting authority will specify and describe its detailed procurement need. The subject of the procurement of platforms and licences may be, for example, a solution based on commercial off-the-shelf software for data-driven management or AI, software usage rights, licences, and/or an open-source software solution. The subject may also include, among other things, tools for data-driven management, data warehouse automation, integration, analytics and reporting, and visualisation. The solutions and services to be procured may consist of the supplier's own services and products or services and products licensed by a subcontractor provided through the supplier. In service production, either the Client's existing own operating service and other capacity can be utilised, or this can be included in the subject of the procurement. The subject of expert services can be specified in areas such as: • Data-driven management and AI consulting • Planning and management of data management and governance projects • Concept, data, and interface modelling and architecture definition • Development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data pipelines (ETL) and integrations • Knowledge of open interfaces and standards and integrating AI as part of applications • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data warehouses, data cubes, and data lakes • Development of analytics, advanced analytics, machine learning, and robotics • Development of AI algorithms into finished products in various technologies • Implementation expertise in various technologies (e.g. Google AI, AWS Cloud computing, Microsoft AI) • User interface and application development (Chatbot etc.) • Definition and development of cost accounting • Definition of services, processes, and governance models • Selection, consulting, and training of tools used in development • Machine training, converting original material into a processable format, and teaching artificial intelligence
sig_53859266daf39dfe09a0.title: Knowledge management and artificial intelligence (AI) services

sig_53930fa9072f523f79cf.description: The Rheumazentrum Mittelhessen has decided to tender for a complete hospital information system for the site, which fulfils the KHZG funding requirements 3- 6 and which, furthermore, maps all administrative and clinical processes of an acute, AHB and (DRV) rehabilitation clinic. At the site in Bad Endbach, an acute clinic with 80 beds and an Anschlussheilbehandlung (AHB) and rehabilitation clinic with 36 beds are available for the holistic therapy of acute and chronic rheumatic diseases. The clinic complex also includes two practices with medical rheumatology consultations and an outpatient therapy facility for physiotherapy, physical therapy and occupational therapy. Over the years, the clinic area has been constantly modernised and the infrastructure expanded. The Rheumazentrum Mittelhessen has decided to tender for a complete hospital information system for the site, which fulfils the KHZG funding requirements 3- 6 and which, furthermore, maps all administrative and clinical processes of an acute, AHB and (DRV) rehabilitation clinic. The future HIS is to be set up in such a way that it is the patient-leading system in interaction with other subsystems/modules. The HIS is to be introduced on the basis of a "best practice" approach within the framework of joint project work. The contractor is accordingly expected to provide a consultative and optimising process approach within the framework of the software implementation. The software to be supplied must have the capabilities and instruments that, for example, enable users to manage the patient's treatment progress as efficiently as possible, as well as to document and bill services quickly, in a revenue-secure manner and in compliance with the KHZG (FTB 3-6). The providers are therefore requested to submit a tender for a complete KHZG-compliant HIS including all necessary services for implementation and maintenance/service, which fulfils the mandatory criteria of the KHZG funding requirements 2 - 6 (the mandatory criteria for the admission and treatment management of the FTB 2 are fulfilled via the portal solution of the company Samedi, the discharge and transfer management via the solution of the company Verbund Pflegehilfe (see "Interfaces" tab of Annex 1), the contractor only owes the connection in this area in accordance with the technical requirements and interoperability standards of the KHZG). The new HIS is intended to significantly support the digitalisation and efficiency of hospital processes and thus optimise patient care.
sig_53930fa9072f523f79cf.title: Hospital information system
