sig_5406453d5e3ac9e2fa53.description: The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) established a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) to procure Work Focused Activities for Jobcentre Plus Districts in England, Scotland and Wales via the previous DWP eProcurement Solution (ePS). DWP has now migrated to a new ePS, Atamis and DWP are therefore reissuing this notice via the Atamis portal. However, please note that 'online' applications to join the FSF DPS 2 via the Atamis Portal are currently suspended and a temporary 'offline' process is in place, further details are below. The DPS is for the procurement of social and other services referred to in Regulation 74 of the Public Contracts Regulations (2015) and as such, the intention is to use a light touch regime, rather than the full regime described in Regulation 34 (Dynamic Purchasing System). The DPS is for the sole use of DWP. The Flexible Support Fund Dynamic Purchasing System 2 - For the Provision of Work Focused Activities (FSF DPS 2) is the replacement for the DWP Dynamic Purchasing System for provision of work-focused activities known as the Flexible Support Fund DPS (FSF DPS). The FSF DPS expired on 31 October 2021 and was replaced by the FSF DPS 2 with effect from 1 November 2021. Currently the 'online' application process is suspended, and a temporary 'offline' process is in operation. Any new supplier wishing to apply to join the FSF DPS 2 should send an email to cdfsf.adhocprocurement@dwp.gov.uk requesting to apply to join the FSF DPS 2, and the relevant information will be sent to you via email. Although DWP are currently operating an 'offline' process to join the FSF DPS 2, suppliers will still be required to create an account on Atamis. Suppliers can do this via the link below, which will take you to the DWP Atamis landing page. To ensure that the page functions correctly, you must accept browser cookies https://dwp2.my.site.com/s/Welcome From this landing page, new suppliers will be able to create an Atamis account by selecting the "Supplier Registration Here" button and following the on screen instructions. The landing page also has a link to the Supplier Portal Help page, where you will find an article to help with registering for an account https://suppliersupport.atamis.co.uk/hc/en-gb/articles/4613254620319-Registering-with-a-Supplier-Portal Estimated overall value of this DPS will be £250,000,000.00

This is a negotiated procedure with a call for competition pursuant to Section 11 Paragraph 1 Sentence 1 Alt. 2 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VSVgV). The subject matter of the contract to be awarded is the procurement for the delivery and setup of software as an overall system a) for the analysis, IT-supported comparison, and research of mass data in a stock of several partly federated source databases as well as ad-hoc imported data, in particular from the backups of digital evidence by the police of Schleswig-Holstein, b) for the technical integration of existing data sources in a central data integration platform (data integration component). The license requirement initially comprises 30 concurrent users; the license quantity required for this is to be procured. Optionally, there shall be the possibility to expand the number to up to 75 concurrent users. This option must be included in the tender, but the actual uptake is optional. The contracting authority provides for a staggering of the additional licenses to be acquired optionally. The additional licenses are offered in stages: Option 1 enables the procurement of 20 additional licenses (a total of 50 users), Option 2 another 25 licenses each, so that a maximum number of users of 75 can be reached. The term of the license is three years from the award of contract. The contracting authority has the right to extend the term up to three times by twelve months each time. Licenses acquired within the framework of options 1 and 2 have a term of three years from their provision, which can also be extended three times by twelve months each time, but the licenses procured by exercising options shall end at the latest simultaneously with the term of the licenses initially procured as a base. The contracting authority uses an EVB-IT Transfer Agreement Type B, an EVB-IT Maintenance Agreement, and an EVB-IT Service Agreement as the basis for the contractual agreement. These will be made available together with the other documents in the bidding phase. The procurement essentially comprises the following services: The rental of an overall system consisting of • an analysis software for cross-cutting analysis, IT-supported comparison, and research of mass data in the inventory of several partly federated source databases as well as ad-hoc imported data, in particular from the backups of digital evidence by the police of Schleswig-Holstein and • a central data integration platform (data integration component) for the integration of existing data sources, which can be installed in the computer centre of Dataport - on-premise. This includes a productive, development, and test system which is to be integrated into the existing IT infrastructure of the police of Schleswig-Holstein. With regard to the demarcation of data integration from IT-supported comparison and automated data analysis, reference is made to the attached document "Definition of Terms Analysis and Data Integration". Further details can be found in the document "Part A - General Part Call for Competition". The procedure concerns a classified contract pursuant to Section 104 Paragraph 3 No. 2 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB) or Art. 2 lit. b and d of Directive 2009/81/EC and is conducted in accordance with the VSVgV. According to the decision of the contracting authority, only economic operators established in an EU Member State or Iceland or Norway are authorised to participate (by application and tenders) ("authorised participants"). Applicants and tenderers may not provide subcontractors in their application and tenders who are established in a state other than those mentioned in the previous sentence ("third country"). This also applies to any other reliance on the capacities of such undertakings. For the determination of establishment, the definition of origin in Art. 3 Paragraph 1 of Regulation (EU) 2022/1031 shall apply mutatis mutandis, for economic operators as groups Art. 3 Paragraph 2 of the aforementioned regulation. sig_5485d4092ed80bdeff22.description: This is not a call for competition. The London Borough of Croydon is undertaking preliminary market engagement in relation to the potential commissioning of an Erasmus+ teacher/educator training and international mobility programme for Croydon schools. The Council is seeking expressions of interest only from organisations with demonstrable previous experience of managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects and international education mobility programmes on behalf of schools or public-sector organisations. The appointed provider would be expected to provide end-to-end programme management, including: • Previous experience of successfully managing and delivering Erasmus+ projects, including details of the number and type of projects delivered • Management and coordination of international teacher training, CPD and school visits across European destinations, with destinations to be confirmed • Organisation and management of participant travel, accommodation, and associated logistics • Support with participant recruitment and selection, including ensuring appropriate eligibility and allocation processes • Management of Erasmus+ grant administration, financial monitoring, evidence, and reporting requirements • Support for safeguarding, risk management and participant welfare throughout the programme • Delivery or commissioning of high-quality teacher CPD and training aligned to the agreed programme objectives • Development and implementation of programme evaluation, impact measurement, and outcomes reporting • Monitoring and reporting on participant outcomes and the wider impact of the programme on participating schools; and • Effective stakeholder management and communication with the Council, schools, training providers, and international partners. The programme is intended to support Croydon schools in developing practice in areas including inclusion and SEND, digital and AI-enabled education, wellbeing, sustainability, innovation, and oracy/communication-rich learning, aligned with relevant Erasmus+ priorities. Providers should only register an interest where they can demonstrate the relevant specialist experience, capacity, international networks and organisational infrastructure required to manage an Erasmus+ mobility programme from participant selection through to final evaluation and grant reporting. Registering your interest Providers wishing to participate must register their interest through the correspondence area no later than 21 September 2026 Please complete the sections provided in the document attached and return via the messaging area on the inTend Portal: Following the registration deadline, the Council will review responses and may engage with organisations whose experience and capabilities align with the requirements. This market engagement exercise is intended to inform the Council's understanding of the market and potential future commissioning arrangements. It does not constitute a procurement process, and participation does not provide any advantage in any future procurement activity. Organisation name Main contact name and job title Contact email address A brief response confirming: • the number of Erasmus+ projects your organisation has previously managed • your experience of managing international school/teacher mobility programmes • your experience of grant administration and reporting • your ability to manage travel, accommodation, participant selection, safeguarding, CPD and evaluation; and • a brief example of a comparable programme successfully delivered. Word Limit: 250 words The London Borough of Croydon use the Intend portal to manage supplier records and to run procurement activities. If you do not yet have an account, please register, if you do have an account, It is essential that your company information on Intend matches the details held by Companies House, please do log in and check this. Intend Portal: https://in-tendhost.co.uk/croydontenders/aspx/Home Register on the Central Digital Platform If you haven’t already, please register your organisation on the Central Digital Platform. This is a government-wide initiative to streamline supplier engagement and improve transparency. Again please do ensure your information matches your Companies House details. Central Digital Platform Registration: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/procurement-act-2023-short-guides/suppliers-how-to-register-your-organisation-and-first-administrator-on-find-a-tender-in-three-easy-steps-html We appreciate your cooperation and look forward to working together. sig_559688f76cf5b25e25a5.description: INVITATION TO MARKET DIALOGUE With this RFI Yle invites interested suppliers to participate in the market dialogue held prior publishing the call for tenders (RFP). With this RFI Yle gathers insights and proposals for solutions that will help us achieve a system (or systems), which meets all Yle's requirements as well as both the current and future production needs. The system and all of its components should create an environment, which workflows are easy for users, and which communicates flawlessly with other systems that Yle has. Yle is looking for either a) a single vendor system with all the features or; b) a modular solution from different vendors. The description and object of the RFI, as well as the schedule of the procurement process, are preliminary and Yle will specify the needs and objectives of the procurement in the final RFP. It may also be that no invitation to tender is published in case Yle decides not to proceed with the renewal. At this point Yle is looking to identify the solutions available in the market that could meet Yle’s needs. It is possible that there will be round 2 of RFI before publishing the final request for proposals (RFP). In case, at this point, Yle feels it is needed, we will schedule meetings with the few chosen suppliers. Please see the appendix of this RFI for further information. INTERESTED? Interested suppliers are invited to take part in the market dialogue by sending a request to participate by email to tarjoukset.yle(at)yle.fi at latest by 15th of November 2025. In case you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to contact us. Please include a description or additional appendices covering the following topics in your email: - Description of the solution you provide, including a description of which key features are included in your solution - A short company presentation, including the size of the company in terms of revenue and number of employees. - Your previous experience and few appropriate reference cases. - Reference architecture view - Description of your licence and pricing model - Description of your cyber security policies and continuity planning - Description of your GDPR policies - Your general agreement terms and conditions and description of SLA terms if possible We will review the answers as soon as they are received.

sig_57834ae89fbcdf435cb5.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 through a merger of railway and postal omnibus services. Its transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, the Euskirchen district, and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brúhl, and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban population centres with sparsely populated, rural areas. With capacity, competence, and years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region travel reliably and safely – in an environmentally friendly, sustainable, and innovative manner. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated independently and some on behalf of RVK. The transport network encompasses 132 routes with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 routes are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a transport performance of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. In order to successfully drive forward the vision of sustainable, clean mobility in the service area in the future and thus sustainably reduce local pollutant emissions, Regionalverkehr Köln GmbH (RVK) is implementing extensive measures for digitalisation and networking, and thereby more attractive public transport to reduce NOx and other pollutant emissions, as part of its internal "Null Emission" project (https://www.rvk.de/projekt-null-emission). Based on successful projects in the field of sales backend systems with electronic tickets, subscription online (Abo-Online), and digital timetable information, a stable basis for central customer management has already been established. The planned measure of developing a mobility app within the framework of the "Mobility App and Platform" project builds upon these existing structures and must be seamlessly integrated into the existing sales landscape. As part of this new measure, which is particularly tailored to rural areas, a multitude of previously analogue or isolated mobility offerings are to be bundled into an integrated, intermodal mobility app. Both regional and interregional transport services will be integrated to give users seamless access to various forms of mobility. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV). The approval period is fixed until 31.12.2026 and cannot be extended. Encompasses the programming of frontend, backend, and interfaces as well as the integration of the application into the existing system landscape.; Development of a user-centred design concept including UX design, design system, wireframes, prototyping, and accessible design. The results serve as the basis for technical implementation in Lot 1. Both lots are closely related from a technical perspective and will be implemented in parallel or sequentially. The contracting authority coordinates the cooperation between the contractors of both lots to ensure a smooth exchange. In particular, regular coordination and joint review meetings are planned.
sig_57834ae89fbcdf435cb5.title: Digitisation of municipal transport systems for sustainable mobility solutions in rural and urban areas - mobility app and platform

sig_57ee5d561469897c12b5.description: The purpose of this Notice is to invite market operators to a Market Engagement Event for the potential future exercise to procure services supporting the development of an innovative obesity pathway in North East and North Cumbria on Thursday 8th January at 10:45 via Teams Integrated Care Board (NENC ICB) is developing a new, community-first obesity pathway as part of the Obesity Pathway Innovation Programme (OPIP). The pathway will support adults with obesity who are waiting lists or at risk of economic activity due to obesity and related long-term conditions. To enable this at scale, NENC ICB is exploring options to procure a digital partner to provide an integrated platform that will act as the digital "spine" for the pathway. The intended service is expected to support the following: 1. Identification and invitation of eligible patients (for example via population-health tools and waiting-list data) 2. Digital referral, consent and triage 3. Patient-facing tools for self-assessment, remote monitoring and behavioural support (including AI meal planning) 4. Role based portals for community pharmacies, specialist teams and programme staff. The platform will need to integrate with existing NHS systems (for example NHS App, GP clinical systems and provider electronic patient records), support high standards of clinical safety, information governance and cybersecurity, and generate data and dashboards required for independent evaluation of outcomes, equity and value for money. This Market Engagement Event is intended to help NENC ICB understand the capabilities, innovations and constraints within the digital health market, and to test our emerging requirements and delivery approach. Feedback from suppliers will be used to refine any future specification and procurement strategy for these services. Additional information: To attend this event please register on Eventbrite using this link: https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/market-engagement-event-innovative-obesity-pathway-nenc-tickets-1978132080302?aff=oddtdtcreator This notice is for information and engaging with the supply market only. It is not a binding statement of intent or call for competition. HI NENC reserves the right not to enter a formal process and not award a contract. The information contained in this notice, including information relating to the nature and scope of the requirements, the service classification of this requirement from the list of CPV codes, is only indicative of the HI NENC's current thinking and is neither exhaustive nor binding. HI NENC reserves the right at its absolute discretion to amend it at the time of issue of any further notices or at any other time. The aim is to gather information on available systems, understand the market ́s capacity and gain insight into current and future systems connected to this area. The electronic maternity journal is used in the health service to document and follow-up information related to pregnancy, birth and childcare. The electronic maternity journal is currently in use at 8 health authorities in Helse Sør-Øst RHF. The system is closely integrated with the central electronic patient journal system (EPJ) and supports the entire patient pathway connected to pregnancy, birth and childcare. The system also meets the requirements for obligatory reports to national authorities, including the Medical Birth Register and The Norwegian Tax Administration.The current system serves approx. 3,500 users divided in 2,700 PCs and covers 8 health trusts and 18 maternity wards. sig_59fd16c23a30647b6211.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a Request for Information directed at potential Suppliers. Therefore, no tenders are requested or to be submitted in response to this request for information. No comments or questions received via the request for information will be answered. One of the tasks of the Finnish National Agency for Education is the publishing of learning materials and publications. Customers include both private individuals and organisations, in particular schools and educational institutions. Products are delivered to the customer either physically (e.g. textbooks) or digitally (e.g. electronic learning materials). We request up-to-date information on a comprehensive service encompassing product logistics, licensing, and online shop services. The service to be procured includes • a SaaS online shop solution where customers can purchase non-fiction books, textbooks, publications, and licences for digital learning materials published by the Finnish National Agency for Education, as well as downloadable files, using commonly used payment methods • a logistics and distribution service for textbooks and publications, including distribution to key resellers such as Library Service, bookshops, and learning material intermediaries • a digital product licence management service, and • a sales settlement service, including inventory value reporting. Service requirements • The online shop must serve our customers in Finnish, Swedish, and English. • The service must meet the accessibility requirements of the Act on the Provision of Digital Services. • It shall be possible to integrate the service with the Finnish National Agency for Education's digital learning platform (licence management) and product register. • The online shop solution must provide the capability for the Finnish National Agency for Education to edit the layout, texts, and settings of the online shop. In addition, it must be possible to add sample pages, reading samples, and promotional videos to the online shop. We request the following information 1. Does the Supplier have a comprehensive service meeting the above description to offer? 2. What pricing model does the Supplier use? 3. Based on the above description, does the Supplier have any comments on the potential requirement specification for the procurement? 4. Optional additional question: The Finnish National Agency for Education is exploring alternatives to replace its self-developed product information system and royalty register. Is it possible to tailor a product and royalty register into the Supplier's service that includes the necessary databases and user interface? The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to implement it in the manner described in the request for information. The contracting authority is not obliged to take account of responses received to the request for information when drawing up the call for tenders. Responding to the request for information does not bind the tenderer or affect the tenderer's position in any potential procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information or for any product demonstration.
sig_59fd16c23a30647b6211.title: Request for information: The Finnish National Agency for Education's logistics and user licence service for fee-charging products as well as an online shop

sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.description: Verkehrsgesellschaft Landkreis Gifhorn mbH (VLG) intends to gradually convert its bus fleet to electromobility within the framework of the requirements of the Clean Vehicles Procurement Act. For this purpose, electric buses and the charging infrastructure required for their operation are to be procured and integrated into operational processes. VLG plans to initially provide charging infrastructure for initially 11 vehicles by the year 2027. A charging and load management system is to be introduced for the centralised control and monitoring of charging processes, for limiting grid load as well as for supporting operational vehicle dispatching and vehicle stabling. With the introduction of electromobility, additional requirements arise for the planning and control of vehicle deployment, charging processes and available electrical power. Vehicle availability, battery charge state, energy demand, planned departure times, charging point occupancy and available grid capacity must in future be brought together and taken into account in a system-supported manner. The initial expansion stage comprises the charging infrastructure for 11 vehicles. The exact number and design of the charging points, their technical properties as well as the operational systems and data sources to be integrated are described in a binding manner in the quantity framework, in the interface descriptions and in the appendices to this specification. The increasing requirements in the course of the progressive electrification of the bus fleet as well as the expansion of the charging infrastructure require a high-performance charging, load and energy management system. With the introduction of an LMS, charging processes are to be controlled taking into account the boundary conditions from charging infrastructure, vehicle data, battery charge states and range requirements. The LMS must control the charging processes in such a way that the charge states required for the planned vehicle deployment are reached in good time. The charging infrastructure is to be integrated into the LMS so that the status of the charging units can be centrally monitored and controlled.
sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.title: Procurement and introduction of a charging management system for VLG

sig_5bd60a64138ad98ac5e2.description: The Scottish Government is pursuing a comprehensive programme to reform and modernise Scotland’s compulsory purchase system. Lot 1: . The overall aim of this research is to provide information about the compensation received by those whose land is acquired under compulsory purchase powers. The evidence generated through the research is intended to inform decisions on potential future legislation by the Scottish Government and scrutiny of any such legislation by the Scottish Parliament. The objectives of the project are to address the following questions: a. How frequently and to what extent are compensation payments affected by the prospect of future planning permission (“hope value”)? b. In cases where hope value is a factor, to what extent are payments affected by the timing, costs and risks of implementing any such prospective planning permission? c. To what extent does the current condition of property affect the market value calculated for the purpose of compensation?
sig_5bd60a64138ad98ac5e2.title: Compulsory Purchase Compensation Research

sig_5c570f68fc4d8b9d2297.description: Our Workplace Innovation Leadership Academy supports the ongoing development of business leaders at all levels and stages of experience. The Leadership Academy delivers programmes under a framework agreement with multiple suppliers across the Scottish Enterprise area, the programme plays a key role in cultivating leadership capability and innovation within businesses. The current framework expires early April 2026 and we anticipate commencing a new procurement process in December 2025. To inform this process, we are seeking to engage with the market to better understand current capabilities and approaches to delivering high-impact leadership development. We welcome expressions of interest from suppliers who possess specialist knowledge, proven experience, and the capacity to deliver innovative and effective leadership programmes tailored to diverse business needs. The Workplace Innovation Leadership Development Framework will consist of a series of one-day workshops, one-to-one coaching sessions, and topic specific diagnostic tools, delivered over a period of 2 - 6 months, depending on the Lot. Delivery will follow a hybrid model, combining online and face-to-face formats to maximise accessibility and impact. The Framework will deliver programmes across the Scottish Enterprise area, responding to demand. Where appropriate, programmes may also be delivered in collaboration with other enterprise agencies across Scotland. Lot 1: Transformational Leadership Programme. A cohesive leadership programme designed for both emerging and established leaders, with consistent core themes and tailored content to reflect each group's unique needs and experiences. Lot 2: Innovating Leadership: AI, Data & Emerging Tech. To empower leaders to embed AI, data, and emerging tech into strategy, foster ethical leadership, and drive internal innovation in a tech-enabled world. Lot 3: Growth Through Risk & Ambition. To support leaders in evaluating growth strategies, embracing risk as a catalyst for innovation, and exploring strategic options like investment, mergers, and ESG-aligned finance. Encourages a culture of learning through experimentation. Lot 4: Leadership in Times of Geopolitical & Economic Volatility. Helps leaders build resilience, agility, change capability and foresight to lead through uncertainty, global disruption, and change—while staying focused on long-term sustainability and stakeholder trust.
sig_5c570f68fc4d8b9d2297.title: Workplace Innovation Leadership Development Programme (P26-0006)

sig_5cb6de6c4d3736be684f.description: Description: The State of Saxony-Anhalt has its own state data network, which is currently operated technically by an IT service provider. The state data network was set up by this IT service provider. The intention now is to retender the operation of the state data network as a high-performance and integrated state data network (LAN/WAN) as well as all measures and services necessary for this. The operation of the operations centre with, among other things, network-related services, the operation of components and systems within a data centre and necessary operational and technical tools are also to be awarded. To prepare for this retender, the MID as the responsible authority for the State of Saxony-Anhalt is conducting a market exploration in accordance with § 28 of the VgV. The aim is in particular to explore what organisational, technical and economic solutions are available on the market to ensure operation on a permanent, secure, reliable and scalable basis, as well as the conditions that may be necessary for this and the general time schedule. This is expressly not a call for competition or any other bidding procedure, but rather a non-binding market analysis for orientation and as a basis for decision-making for the preparation of any subsequent procurement procedure. Companies that wish to participate in the market exploration will be provided with further documents in the market exploration procedure. In order to gain access to these documents, an expression of interest and the submission of a non-disclosure agreement are required to protect sensitive data regarding critical infrastructure. Interested parties are therefore requested to express their interest in participating in the present market exploration procedure by 28.11.2025 at the latest by sending an email with the subject 'Market exploration procedure state data network' to the following email address: lnstender@sachsen-anhalt.de and stating the necessary contact details (name of the company, registered office of the company, address of the company and email address). You will then receive a draft non-disclosure agreement, which must then be completed and returned signed. Upon receipt of the non-disclosure agreement, the further documents for the market exploration will be sent to the interested parties concerned. These contain further information and documents. It is planned to conduct online market exploration discussions with the interested parties. These are expected to be scheduled in the four calendar weeks following the above-mentioned deadline. To prepare for the discussions, participants are asked to complete and submit a prepared questionnaire. Further information on this can be found in the market exploration documents, which will be made available after the submission of the non-disclosure agreement.
sig_5cb6de6c4d3736be684f.title: Market consultation on the operation of the state data network

sig_5ddac62cdd050fb6ea26.description: LapIT Oy is an IT company owned by the municipalities, joint municipal authorities, and municipal limited companies of Lapland and Koillismaa, which provides comprehensive information management and IT services. Our company's head office is located in Rovaniemi. LapIT is considering putting the financial management system out to tender and offering it to its owner-customers. Currently, there are 10 municipal customers interested in the procurement. According to preliminary plans, the procurement would cover the following processes: - from financial planning to forecasting - from procurement to payment - from sales to debt collection - from bookkeeping to financial statements - authority reporting (municipal reporting) Based on preliminary information, the procurement would cover the financial management solution as a comprehensive service, including implementation and user training, migrations from old systems, and integrations. LapIT requests willing potential tenderers to participate in a dialogue. In principle, we will accept into the market dialogue those tenderers who meet at least the following criteria: - The supplier must have at least 2 references for the solution for municipal customers. The systems reported as references must have been in production use for at least 2 years. - The solution must comply with high data security and the data must be located in the EU/EEA area. - The tenderer must offer implementation support and continuous service support in the Finnish language. The tenderer must attach to their registration: - A description of their service in Finnish. - Presentations of at least two reference deliveries as stated above. - The description should show the lifecycle status and development roadmap of the system. Willing participants can register for the dialogue by notifying us by email at jasmine.suopanki@lapit.fi by 5.11.2025. The intention is to start the market dialogues as soon as possible. LapIT will select the suppliers it chooses for the market dialogue based on the descriptions. LapIT reserves the right to limit the number of those who have participated in the market dialogue. The implementation method of the market dialogue will be decided later (written/meetings). Participation in the market dialogue does not in any way affect the tenderer's position in a possible future tendering process. The market dialogue will be carried out in the Finnish language. Everything presented in the market dialogue and the discussions held during it are preliminary and do not bind LapIT Oy or the tenderer. No compensation will be paid to those who have participated in the market dialogue for their participation. This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders but a request for information/invitation to a market dialogue. This preliminary information notice does not bind the client to the procurement; the actual procurement notice will possibly be published later. The decision on launching a possible procurement process will be made later.

sig_5ee014d4aebe9663afd1.description: Project reason TenneT requires a portfolio management system (PMS) to support electricity trading in the short-term market (day-ahead and intraday) in Germany. Objective of the tender The objective is the procurement of a high-performance PMS to support electricity trading. In accordance with TenneT's architectural guidelines, the solution is to be cloud-based, preferably operated in the tenderer's cloud. In coordination with TenneT, deployment in a third-party provider's cloud (e.g. Azure) or at TenneT is also possible. The system must enable the management of multiple portfolios and support the processes for participating in day-ahead and intraday auctions as well as continuous intraday trading. The system will be used in the electricity trading sector and must cover the following main functions: - Portfolio management - Connection to power exchanges - Trading overviews & GUI - Algo-trader / trading support in continuous intraday trading - Data management - Reporting & analysis - Settlement - Schedule management Scope of services - Provision of a COTS software solution (licences) - Support & maintenance of this solution (maintenance) - Hosting of the solution - Application management services - Consulting and training services Procedural notice A detailed specification of services as well as other procedural-relevant documents will be provided after signing a non-disclosure agreement. Please send this to us completed and signed via the Mercell messaging function. The tender is being conducted in accordance with the SektVO (Sectoral Procurement Ordinance) via a negotiated procedure with a call for competition. Accordingly, TenneT is already bound to confidentiality pursuant to Section 15 SektVO. As things stand, the value of the tender cannot be reliably estimated.

sig_5fce472d03558e520413.description: The Tribal Colleges and Universities Program (TCUP) provides awards to federally recognized 1 Tribal Colleges and Universities, Alaska Native-serving institutions, and Native Hawaiian-serving institutions to promote high quality science (including sociology, psychology, anthropology, linguistics, economics and bioeconomics, statistics, and other social and behavioral sciences; natural sciences; computer science, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and cybersecurity), technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), STEM education, research, and outreach. Support is available to TCUP-eligible institutions (see the Additional Eligibility subsection of Section IV of this solicitation) for transformative capacity-building or community engagement projects through Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) , Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) , TCUP for Secondary and Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) , TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) , Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) , and Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) . Collaborations led by TCUP institutions that involve non-TCUP institutions of higher education are supported through TCUP Partnerships , with the participation of other NSF programs to support the work of non-TCUP institutions. Finally, research studies that further the scholarly activity of individual faculty members are supported through Small Grants for Research (SGR) . Through the opportunities highlighted above, as well as collaborations with other National Science Foundation (NSF) divisions and directorates, and other organizations, TCUP aims to increase Native individuals' participation in STEM careers, improve the quality of STEM programs at TCUP-eligible institutions, and facilitate the development of a strong STEM enterprise in TCUP institutions' service areas. TCUP supports transformative capacity-building, community engagement, or research projects at TCUP-eligible institutions through the following funding tracks: Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) projects provide support to design, implement, and assess comprehensive institutional improvements in STEM education and research capacity at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education. By strengthening STEM education and STEM education research, successful projects will increase the number of STEM students and improve the quality of their preparation. ICE-TI projects create and/or adapt and assess innovative models and materials for teaching and learning in STEM, embody knowledge about how students learn most effectively in STEM teaching and learning activities, and bring STEM disciplinary advances into the undergraduate or graduate experience. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees offered by TCUP-eligible institutions or significantly enhance instructional approaches. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) support the attainment of a short-term, well-defined goal to improve the quality of STEM education at an eligible institution. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects could, for example, enhance academic infrastructure by systematically adding traditional knowledge to the scope or content of a STEM course, updating curricula, modernizing laboratory research equipment, developing and delivering professional development for K-12 STEM educators, or improving the computational infrastructure. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees or significantly enhance instructional approaches. TCUP for Secondary & Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) supports in-service professional development in STEM disciplinary or STEM education content and/or research for K-12 STEM teachers in the relevant service area. Examples of project activities include, but are not limited to, professional development involving seminar series and engagement in STEM instruction and content during the academic year, structured series of summer intensive workshops and trainings, and summer research opportunities. The objective of this strand is to broaden the instructional capacity for STEM in the K-12 workforce and thereby to the entire community, and to build the capacity for STEM disciplinary or education research among participating educational professionals. TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) coalesce the STEM and/or STEM education expertise into a team, designed to support and promote the STEM goals, needs, aspirations, or interests of the chartering reservation or tribe(s). TEA Centers may address a critical tribal or community need or focus on a realm of research or design that is beyond the scope of individual research grants or that is of interest to multiple tribes. The objective of this strand is to build on the capacity developed through prior TCUP support and apply expertise to collaborations with communities in the institution’s service area, or nationally. The Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) strand supports projects at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education to upgrade the cyberinfrastructure necessary to conduct, expand, manage and administer STEM programs of study, including research. The objective of this strand is to equip TCUP institutions to meet the demands of virtual instruction, advanced computing, and data science opportunities. Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) provides support for activities that prepare an institution for Implementation-level projects. Consequently, they are available only to TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education that have never received TCUP support, have not received TCUP support within the previous five years, or are embarking on a significantly novel STEM strategic plan. Examples of supported activities include completing an institutional assessment of its current STEM instructional capacity, or engaging in conversations necessary to formulate a shared vision of what that capacity should be and how to achieve it. Pre-TI awards can support staff and faculty release time, travel, stakeholder gatherings, and associated administrative costs. The objective of this strand is to conduct self-studies and formulate strategic plans for the development of STEM instructional programs of study. The TCUP Partnerships strand provides support for collaborations that will improve TCUP institutions' instructional and research capacity in STEM fields supported by NSF; attract, retain, and support TCUP students in internships and research endeavors deemed to be necessary for a complete curriculum offering; and engage partner universities to provide an academic grounding and a successful transition for students who wish to study or attain degrees in STEM fields supported by NSF. TCUP Partnerships broaden the number of scientific disciplines available to students at TCUP institution through collaborations with non-TCUP institutions. Active Pre-Engineering Education Collaboratives or Partnerships in Geoscience Education awards are not affected by this revision. The objective of this strand is the development, through instructional and research capacity-building, of academic and career pathways for TCUP students through supporting collaborative projects between and among TCUP and non-TCUP institutions. Interested teams of collaborators for which a TCUP institution serves as lead should contact the TCUP program directors. Support for non-TCUP partners must be obtained from other NSF programs, which follows the procedures of the prior Partnership strands. Small Grants for Research (SGR) strand support STEM or STEM Education faculty members at TCUP-eligible institutions to initiate or pursue research projects or programs that may include undergraduate or graduate student engagement. Awards are intended to help further the faculty member's research capability and effectiveness; improve research and teaching at his or her home institution and create and study new models and innovations in STEM teaching and learning. International research or collaborations are strongly encouraged. TCUP students may seek support for international research opportunities under the guidance of a TCUP STEM or STEM education faculty member and an international research collaborator. These awards are particularly appropriate as a means of recruiting and retaining highly qualified scientists, engineers, and educators at TCUP-eligible institutions. The objective of this strand is to support faculty research and professional development that build research capacity at TCUP institutions. [1] Executive Order 13021 defines Tribal Colleges and Universities ("tribal colleges") as those institutions cited in section 532 of the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 301 note), and other institutions that qualify for funding under the Tribally Controlled Community College Assistance Act of 1978, (25 U.S.C. 1801 et seq.), as well as Navajo Community College as authorized in the Navajo Community College Assistance Act of 1978, Public Law 95-471, Title II (25 U.S.C. 640a note). The term "Alaska Native-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 20 percent Alaska Native students. The term "Native Hawaiian-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 10 percent Native Hawaiian students. Most TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education are two-year or community colleges. See the Who May Submit Proposals section in this solicitation for further details.

sig_5ffa3471f05cf4c9fb5c.description: The Authority is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced and compliant Bidder to provide a secure, efficient and fully compliant electronic bulk ("e‐Bulk") solution for the end-to-end administration of DBS applications. The solution must support the Authority's Registered Body status and provide a fully hosted, cloud-based platform that enables the secure processing, tracking and management of DBS applications across multiple Council services and user groups. The Successful Provider must be an approved DBS e-Broker, authorised to submit applications on behalf of Registered Bodies. The Authority requires an accessible, bilingual in Welsh and English, compliant with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WGAC) 2.2 AA accessibility standards, and capable of supporting multiple Council service areas and user roles. An optional Digital Identity Verification service may also be awarded as part of the contract, subject to the Authority's assessment of the Provider's data protection, information governance and security arrangements. The procurement process will be conducted in four (4) stages. Bidders must successfully meet the requirements of each stage before progressing to the next stage of evaluation. Where a stage is assessed on a pass/fail basis, bidders must achieve a "Pass" outcome in order to proceed. Where a stage is subject to scored evaluation, bidders must achieve the minimum threshold score specified within the tender documentation. Any bidder that fails a pass/fail requirement, receives a score below the minimum required threshold, or otherwise fails to satisfy the requirements of a stage, will be excluded from further consideration and their tender submission will not be evaluated in subsequent stages. The Council reserves the right to reject any tender that fails to meet the mandatory requirements of this procurement exercise. Full details can be found in the ITT.

The Legal AI Workspace software to be procured must serve as a specialised working environment to support legal professional work within the KfW Group using generative artificial intelligence. The software will be used in particular for legal research, analysis and the preparation of legal content, as well as for the (partially) automated creation, revision and structuring of documents and other legal work results. Users are personnel from the Legal department as well as other specialist departments and subsidiaries within the KfW Group. A Legal AI Workspace connects large language models with specialised processing layers that are optimised for working with legal content. It differs from general AI assistants in that it brings together legal professional processes in a unified working environment and employs mechanisms that are indispensable for professional legal practice. These include, in particular: the traceable anchoring of generated statements in verifiable sources, the structured processing of complex documents, and the rule-based review of contract content. The software must provide the following core functions. Legal research: The software must be able to answer complex legal questions based on relevant legal sources. Every generated statement must be traced back to concrete, verifiable sources (in particular statutes, case law, commentary literature) and made transparent for the users. KfW considers integrated access to curated legal databases to be a quality-enhancing feature. Furthermore, the software must be able to work with documents and internal knowledge databases provided by KfW. Document analysis and contract evaluation: The software must be able to process and evaluate the content of documents, including complexly structured contracts, tabular content and scanned documents, without essential structural information being lost. This includes the ability to systematically and completely compare contract content against specified review standards. Text creation and drafting support: The software must support the creation and revision of legal texts, in particular contract drafts, memoranda and opinions. Proposed changes must be able to be tracked directly in the document; the mere provision of generated text for manual adoption by the users does not meet the requirements. The software complements a general AI software already in use at KfW. The new software will be operated as an independent tool and will use a model infrastructure provided by the contractor. It is expected that the software will achieve significant increases in efficiency and quality in daily legal advice, document creation and review, and recurring standard legal tasks. Without prejudice to the provision of the software as a Service (SaaS) described in this document and the usage rights granted in connection therewith, the provision of the software must be carried out in such a way that it at least satisfies the intended purpose. KfW is entitled to at least the usage rights required to fulfil the intended purpose. The contractor is therefore liable for the following services: (a) provision of software with the functional scope, (b) execution of a project for the implementation of the software, (c) operation as SaaS, (d) provision of additional services as required, (e) termination support. Further details can be found in the 'Service Description' and in particular the mandatory criteria in accordance with the annex to the Service Description 'Mandatory and Optional Criteria'. sig_6147e73e78c8ff9c06ad.description: Consultants from COWI are currently conducting a feasibility study for Sporveien in Oslo. The purpose of this study is to define technology-independent and supplier-independent functional requirements for the future signalling system of the Oslo tram network, which consists of more than 130km of tracks with almost 100 stopping points. The tram infrastructure in Oslo has a history stretching back over 150 years, and has recently seen significant investment in modern rolling stock. This provides a unique opportunity to assess future solutions for a modern signalling system, and Sporveien has expressed a desire to invest in a future signalling system for the trams. As part of this project, we wish to gather information from suppliers of signalling and light rail systems. We therefore invite relevant suppliers to share information about your solutions, technologies, and experiences. We are particularly interested in systems that support safe, modern operation and that are adaptable to both the current and future needs of the Oslo tram network. Additionally, Sporveien AS and COWI AS are planning a dialogue conference with suppliers in Oslo on November 13th. This conference will provide an opportunity to discuss future collaborations and explore new opportunities for growth and development. We hope to see you at this conference. Once we have established contact with your organization and received your company’s contact information we will send you a letter of invitation with the complete aganda. Please see https://www.sporveien.no/for-leverandorer/trikkens-fremtidige-signalsystem/dialogue-conference/ for more information.
sig_6147e73e78c8ff9c06ad.title: Request for Information from Signalling System Suppliers

sig_615a7ad8699f790a495c.description: The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) seeks to commission an external consultant to undertake an independent programme level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan 2025-2030. The evaluation will assess the design, implementation, and impact of a complex, multi-strand programme delivered between August 2025 and March 2030. This will include directly funded activities, wider activities mobilised through the programme and selected aligned activities where appropriate and supported by the available evidence. The commissioned evaluation is intended as a cross-cutting programme-level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan as a whole. It is recognised that individual projects, interventions and delivery activity within the wider programme will be subject to separate monitoring, evaluation and research activity commissioned by the North East MSA or undertaken by delivery partners. The evaluation will synthesise evidence generated through proportionate project level evaluations (including light touch monitoring and in depth project deep dives) to provide a coherent, programme wide assessment and will not be responsible for conducting primary project-level evaluations, except where explicitly agreed. This will support strategic assurance, learning and decision making, and inform future iterations of the Action Plan and wider North East MSA and regional policy and investment decisions. The programme-level evaluation will therefore consider both the evidence relating to individual interventions and the combined contribution of the wider programme towards the intended outcomes of the Child Poverty Action Plan. The programme‐level evaluation will also seek to determine the degree to which reducing child poverty has been embedded as a cross-cutting theme across North East MSA activity, and that of partners. This will include examining how the Child Poverty Reduction Unit and the regional Child Poverty Action Plan have influenced strategic priorities, programme and project design, funding and delivery decisions, and whether they have contributed to changes in policies, practices and activities beyond those directly funded through the programme. Lot 1: .
sig_615a7ad8699f790a495c.title: Child Poverty Action Plan - Programme Evaluation

Nordværk I/S is inviting tenders for the procurement, implementation, and subsequent operation and maintenance of a new specialised system for the administration and support of waste collection, hereinafter referred to as the Solution. The procurement is carried out with the aim of replacing the current system support for Nordværk's waste management area and establishing a comprehensive, modern and future-proof Solution that can support the business processes associated with the administration, planning, case processing, execution, registration, follow-up and documentation of waste collection. The procurement includes the delivery and implementation of the Solution as well as the services necessary to establish and commission the Solution. This includes, among other things, clarification and configuration, migration and establishment of relevant data, establishment and adaptation of integrations, testing, training, documentation, commissioning, as well as subsequent operation, support, maintenance and further development in accordance with the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution must support Nordværk's entire value chain in the waste management area from a citizen's or customer's scheme, enquiry or order to the planning and execution of the specific waste management task, as well as subsequent registration, case processing, follow-up, controlling, documentation and the basis for billing. The procurement is part of Nordværk's work to ensure efficient, cohesive and data-driven administration and operation of waste collection. The Solution must support standardised and verifiable workflows, high data quality, a reduced need for manual processes and better opportunities for management, follow-up and ongoing development of the waste management area. At the same time, the Solution must be able to integrate appropriately into Nordværk's other system landscape and support organisational, operational and technological changes over the term of the Contract. The overall purpose of the Solution is in particular: i) to support cohesive and efficient workflows within customer administration, case processing, operational planning, task execution, registration, controlling and follow-up, ii) to support operational waste collection for both Nordværk's own and external waste collectors, including planning, routes, navigation, registration of completed tasks, handling of deviations and operational follow-up, and iii) to establish a flexible and future-proof system foundation with high data quality and good opportunities for integration, configuration, automation, reporting and ongoing further development. The business processes and functionality applicable to the Solution are described in more detail in Appendix 3 of the tender documents – Delivery Description. The Solution is expected to support several different internal and external user groups. This includes, among others, approx. 186-200 internal waste management employees, 55-65 administrative employees, 10-20 administrators/superusers, 40-50 administrative users at external waste collectors and 100-110 waste management employees at external waste collectors. The user groups will have different roles and access needs in the Solution. The Solution must be established on a technical platform that supports the requirements for availability, security, integration, scalability, operation and further development set out in the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The more detailed technical requirements for the Solution and its establishment appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The Solution must have an open, transparent and well-documented architecture and must be able to be integrated into Nordværk's overall system landscape. The Supplier must deliver and maintain the documentation necessary for, inter alia, operation, administration, integrations, configuration, troubleshooting and further development of the Solution, in accordance with the requirements of the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution supports business-critical processes in connection with the daily administration and execution of waste collection. Requirements are therefore set for, among other things, the Solution's availability, stability, security, traceability and data integrity, so that data and registrations can be used reliably in operational management, customer service, case processing, controlling, documentation and as a basis for billing. The Solution must be integrated with a number of Nordværk's other systems and technical solutions. This includes, among other things, relevant interfaces to the billing system, GIS and data basis, self-service solutions, registration equipment, weighing systems and other third-party solutions where data exchange is necessary to support cohesive workflows. The specific requirements for integrations and interfaces appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The tender also contains a number of options for additional functionality and deliveries that Nordværk may choose to use in accordance with the Contract. The specific options and the terms thereof appear in the Contract and the Contract's appendices, including Appendix 3 – Delivery Description. Commissioning of the Solution must take place after the completion of the agreed activities regarding, among other things, clarification, configuration, data migration, integrations, testing, training and approval. The detailed procedure and schedule for implementation and commissioning are determined in accordance with the Contract and the relevant appendices. The Contract thus contains an implementation period of up to 12 months as well as, after commissioning, an operating period of 6 years with the possibility of extension by 2 times 12 months. sig_626e0fe9980779c88162.description: Digitalisation of invoice processing in relation to billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The AOK Baden-Württemberg (hereinafter: AOK BW or contracting authority) is a body governed by public law with joint self-administration by insured persons and employer representatives. It is divided into 14 district directorates and the head office in Stuttgart and insures over 4,6 million people in the state of Baden-Württemberg. To further increase efficiency in the processes, invoice processing is to be digitalised. Specifically, this concerns the billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The currently practised workflows differ according to the type of documents transmitted. In around 80-85 % of cases, a data record with a collective invoice is transmitted. In this case, invoice verification by the staff of the AOK Baden-Württemberg is difficult, as the invoice receipts cannot be directly assigned to a file. Around 10 % of cases are purely paper-based. The remaining cases are transmitted with a structured data set and an image. The postal recipients are filled in automatically. The task of the future service provider will be to scan the paper documents and generate a single invoice together with the associated documents. The requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue must be strictly adhered to. Participation in the initiated competition requires that the requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue are met and that the future contractor either proves certification in accordance with the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue with the tender or undertakes to submit the application in relation to the services covered by the contract within two months of the award of the contract. If the certificate is not submitted within twelve months of the award of the contract, the contracting authority is entitled to immediate extraordinary termination. Details are set out in the service description.

sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.description: This PIN provides early information about the expected starting date and purchase volume for a pre-commercial procurement (PCP) carried out by the THERESA PCP project and about the open market consultation (OMC) that is organised in preparation of this pre-commercial procurement (PCP). The THERESA Buyers Group of healthcare providers have identified a shared need for innovative and sustainable solutions to treat hospital wastewater (HWW) at the source, before it reaches the municipal network, to reduce environmental and health risks linked to pharmaceutical residues, antimicrobial-resistant microorganisms and genes, and other hazardous contaminants. The THERESA PCP aims to stimulate the development of environmentally sustainable, cost-effective, and scalable on-site HWW treatment systems capable of efficiently removing cytostatic drugs, X-ray contrast agents, antibiotics, antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and genes (ARG), while minimising energy consumption, chemical use, and carbon footprint. The contract notice is expected to be published in May-2026 and phase 1 to be started in January 2027, following the PCP timeline. The procurement will take the form of a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) awarding R&D service contracts to several providers in parallel, through a phased and competitive process comprising three stages: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products in real hospital environments. After each phase, intermediate evaluations will down-select the best-performing and most innovative solutions. The contractors with the best-value-for-money solutions will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. The PCP is a joint cross-border initiative coordinated by Fundación Miguel Servet (Spain) as Lead Procurer, on behalf of a Buyers Group of hospitals and public health institutions from Spain, Estonia, Poland, Belgium and the Netherlands, supported by technical and innovation partners. Testing is expected to take place in Spain, Estonia, Poland and the Netherlands to ensure adaptability. Price is not the only award criterion, and all criteria are stated only in the procurement documents. The selected contractors will retain ownership of the Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) generated during the PCP and will be able to commercially exploit the developed solutions beyond the scope of the procurement. The R&D services will be carried out primarily within the European Union and/or countries associated with the Horizon Europe Programme. At least 50% of the total value of R&D activities will take place within the EU or associated countries. In addition, contractors must ensure that none of the contracted services are performed in countries nor by entities that are subject to EU restrictive measures under Article 29 of the Treaty on the European Union (TEU) and Article 215 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (TFEU)23 (sanctions). They must ensure that none of the goods procured or used for the procurement were developed, produced or supplied in countries or by entities that are subject to such restrictive measures. Duration of the contract in months: 30 months (January 27 to June 29). The duration covers all three PCP phases: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products. The PCP is expected to start after the publication of the Contract Notice and to end upon completion of the validation phase. This contract is not subject to renewal.
sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.title: Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) of innovative and sustainable solutions to treat Hospital and Healthcare System Wastewater – THERESA PCP

sig_63f9927b01416df1f55c.description: VR software development and purchase of VR headsets The subject of the tender is the design, development, implementation, testing and operational handover of a modular virtual reality (VR) learning module to promote the resilience and action competence of children and young people aged 7 to 14 years in crisis and hazard situations, as well as the procurement of the corresponding hardware (15 pieces of VR headsets + accessories). The learning module is intended to convey real everyday situations from the field of civil protection in a safe virtual environment. The aim is to impart age-appropriate basic knowledge and action competences for extraordinary events to children and young people and to strengthen their self-efficacy in dealing with crisis situations. Module 1 - Fire Safety Education The application teaches, among other things: • Recognition of a hazardous situation, • Behaviour in the event of smoke development, • Correct evacuation of a building, • Use of escape routes, • Behaviour at assembly points, • Making an emergency call, • Cooperation with adults and emergency services. The focus is on correct behaviour and not on the depiction of a fire event. Module 2 - Blackout The application teaches, among other things: • Recognition of a power outage, • Orientation without electrical aids, • Calm behaviour, • Communication within the family, • Handling of flashlights, • Significance of emergency supplies, • Information acquisition, • Energy-saving behaviour, • Cohesion and mutual support. The application is intended for use in schools, extracurricular educational institutions as well as at public information and prevention events. The solution is to be developed in such a way that it can be expanded in the future with further scenarios without fundamental changes to the software architecture
sig_63f9927b01416df1f55c.title: VR software development and purchase of VR headsets

sig_64047b64fb36c444a620.description: The Contracting Authority has launched the METKA project, which aims to replace the automatic train protection system of the Helsinki Metro with a radio-based Automatic Train Control (ATC) and Radio Network (RN) system. As part of the METKA project, the Contracting Authority is considering a procurement of “Work Train ATC Common Interface”, entailing the installation, testing and commissioning of the ATC and RN equipment on the Work Trains. The scope of the procurement is described in more detail in Annex 1 (Procurement description). This Request for Information must not be considered as a call for tenders. At this stage, the Contracting Authority requests information for preliminary market consultation prior to the official procurement procedure. The Contracting Authority will decide separately whether to proceed with the procurement. The purpose of the market consultation is to receive feedback on the intended scope of the procurement from potential service providers interested in the provision of the services and gather information on potential service providers, on their resources and capabilities. The information gathered through this Request for Information may be used to prepare the contract notice. The Respondent can participate in this market consultation by responding to the questions set out in the question form of this Request for Information (Annex 2 Question Form). Respondents are requested to answer as many questions as possible. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to request additional information and to discuss the Respondent’s response, if deemed necessary. The Contracting Authority welcomes all interested companies to actively participate in this Request for Information and to provide their feedback and proposals for ensuring the efficiency of the procurement process and for enhancing the service providers’ interest in participating in the procurement. The Contracting Authority will open the submitted answers and review the information at 11 December 2025, 12.01 pm. The contract notice is scheduled to be published in December 2025. Please note that taking part in the market discussion does not affect the participation of interested parties in the actual procurement procedure or the selection of the supplier. No compensation will be paid for responding to this Request for Information.

sig_6512f77e4da294323564.description: This notice is not an official launch of our procurement(s), it is to alert the market to future opportunities and allow us to begin conversations that will shape plans for multiple future requirements. The Cabinet Office (Government Skills Group) is transforming the way learning and development (L&D) is designed, procured, and delivered across the Civil Service. Following the announcement by the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, the government is establishing the new National School of Government and Public Services (hereon The National School). The National School is tasked with delivering high-quality, targeted training to approximately 558,000 civil servants, developing executive leadership in the wider public sector, and to partner with public sector training bodies. The strategic goal of the National School is to shift away from the historically outsourced prime-supplier managed-service model. In its place, the Cabinet Office is building an insourced, hybrid capability. Under this new Future Operating Model (FOM), the Cabinet Office will directly manage core operations, standard curricula, and stakeholder engagement. However, expert external provision will remain a critical element of the programme. The National School transformation programme relies on three core, interdependent pillars to transition Civil Service training away from fully outsourced prime-supplier models toward an in-house, hybrid operating model by April 2028. Together, these pillars work to build direct relationships with suppliers, provide a modern digital learning infrastructure, and establish robust in-house operational workflows. Pillar 1: Future Supplier Partnerships (FSP) The FSP project serves as the commercial enabler of the new operating model, building the in-house capability required to buy learning services and manage supply chains directly. We aim to establish direct, value-driven contractual relationships with UK-based SMEs, universities, business schools, and niche providers. The project team have identified an indicative Three-Stage Roadmap to enable this delivery: Stage 1 (Immediate - April 2027): Procuring urgent digital and specialist training needs that cannot be fulfilled through existing frameworks. Stage 2 (April 2027-March 2028): Phased procurement for core, National School-sponsored curriculum, coaching, and talent programmes. Stage 3 (March 2028 onwards): On-going phased procurements falling out of Stages 1 and 2, depending on the length of contracts identified. The scope of the requirements will cover several key procurement categories, including, but not limited to, specialised coaching pools (including for neuro-diverse leaders), blended training delivery, learning design (retaining Crown Intellectual Property), access to subject matter experts including within academia, independent research and evaluation, helpdesk/admin surge, and off-the-shelf qualifications. Pillar 2: Future Technologies (FT) The Future Technologies project focuses on designing and implementing the digital architecture required to run a personalised training operation for approximately 558,000 civil servants. The core objective here is the setting up and integration of platforms to manage the access, booking, payments, and evaluation of learning materials. This involves transitioning away from heavy manual processes to maximise technological efficiencies. At this stage the project team has identified the central deliverable as a unified online portal allowing learners to access the full National School offering. Key technologies in scope for procurement include, but are not limited to, a new Learning Management System (LMS)/ Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems to centralise stakeholder engagement, and design/delivery tools. Pillar 3: Future Learning Operations (FLO) The Learning Operations project is responsible for building the actual systems, processes, and internal capabilities required to run the day-to-day training operations in-house. Their core objective is establishing an integrated operational function by April 2028 that supports over 558,000 civil servants in completing their learning journeys. It is highly dependent on the digital and commercial pillars to develop the underlying platforms that support operations. Market Involvement As part of the initial phases of the programme, the project teams are keen to connect with the market and gain insight into current trends, operations and barriers.
