sig_654e236c4fe1c73fa01a.description: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding a common Operating Platform for the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio. After Transition In, where the Support Systems are transitioned to the Operating Platform, the Supplier shall be responsible for operation, including Data Centre operation/Hybrid Cloud Custom Services/Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Infrastructure operation, as well as Support and maintenance of the Operating Platform. Furthermore, after Transition In, the Supplier must ensure Subsequent Transitions to and Transformations of the Operating Platform. The purpose of the common Operating Platform is, among other things, to obtain secure and stable operation with high availability as well as a modern technological platform with a high degree of scalability that supports the needs of the Customer and the municipalities. It is the Contracting Authority's business need that all Services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the Supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In addition to the focus on secure and stable operation, the Supplier must ensure a successful Transition In of the Support Systems with the least possible disruption to the Contracting Authority's business, as well as Subsequent Transitions and ongoing Transformation, including a gradual transition to Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and, to the extent that it supports the needs of the Contracting Authority and the municipalities, Managed Public Cloud Services. In connection with Transition In, a high level of information security must be established, which must be continuously maintained and improved throughout the Contract. The contract has the following 4 main services: I. Transition In, where the Contracting Authority initially wishes for the establishment of and secure and stable transfer to an Operating Platform for the Support Systems, based on Hybrid Cloud Services, with the implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of Environments and data, and takeover of knowledge from the Outgoing Supplier. Subsequently, the Contracting Authority wishes to carry out successive Subsequent Transitions for a number of the Contracting Authority's other IT systems from the current operating models to the Operating Platform, based on Hybrid Cloud Services. II. Ongoing Services for the Operating Platform, including; a. Support; b. Hybrid Cloud Services, including Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Hybrid Cloud Custom Services; c. Tools for supporting Application Suppliers; d. Governance, Operational Processes, security services, Documentation, and operational reporting. III. Service catalogue with the use of standardised methods, technologies, and services, through which the Contracting Authority wishes to be able to provision services on a cloud platform that; a) Offers a wide range of services; b) Is accessible via the public internet; c) Has a publicly available price structure with settlement of services according to consumption on subscription terms. IV. Methods and tools for supporting collaboration with the Contracting Authority and the Contracting Authority's application suppliers, where the Contracting Authority wishes for the delivery of the future operating platform to be supported by proactive collaboration across the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio.

sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.description: With this notice, Istekki announces the organisation of market dialogues for a service voucher and purchased service system. The purpose of the dialogue is to ensure that those preparing the procurement have access to as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. The subject of the procurement is the service voucher and purchased service system entity and its interfaces with other systems, the delivery project (including e.g. migrations, conversions), maintenance and support of off-the-shelf software, support services, separately ordered expert services, as well as customer service. Further development may be carried out on the procured system during the contract period. The service voucher and purchased service system is used for granting service vouchers and payment commitments and for purchasing services from private service providers or other public actors. Through the system, it is necessary to centralise the creation and use of service vouchers and purchased service orders (payment commitment) and the settlement of accounts for rendered services to private service providers or other public actors. The service voucher and purchased service system must take into account needs from the perspectives of the service organiser, the service producer and the customer using the service. Through the system, the service organiser must have the option to manage service provider agreements, plan service provision, grant service vouchers and payment commitments, allocate payments, handle correction requests and monitor various report views. The service provider must have the option to apply to become a service provider through the system. In addition, the service provider must be able to record the service received by the customer in the system and thereby handle settlement based on approved transaction entries. The customer must receive the granted service voucher / payment commitment for use via the system. The service voucher customer must have the option to compare or view service providers, monitor the execution of the service from the system and provide feedback on the service. The contracting authority will organise the market dialogues either as remote meetings or in writing, or utilising both methods. The market dialogues will be held in Finnish. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the dialogue of more detailed schedules and instructions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this notice are merely preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as preparation progresses. If you are interested in participating in the market dialogue, please notify us of your interest no later than 11.09.2026 at 14.00 to hankinnat@istekki.fi. If you wish, you can also attach Finnish-language brochures or other material regarding your own service. It is worth noting that this notice does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tendering procedure may also be omitted. No separate remuneration is paid for responding to the dialogue or participating in any presentation events. We would like to mention again that this is not a contract notice or call for tenders. The purpose is to familiarise oneself with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the request for information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering procedure or bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate suppliers' participation, as it helps us build the upcoming tendering procedure into as functional and clear an entity as possible.
sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.title: Service voucher and purchased service system, market dialogue

sig_67e3dab12e5ff6eb83aa.description: The subject of the procurement is a rostering and time and attendance system (hereinafter also "the System") procured as SaaS off-the-shelf software for use by the Kainuu Wellbeing Services County. Kainuu HVA is putting out to tender SaaS off-the-shelf software that is easy to deploy and meets the contracting authority's needs without software development work. By procuring SaaS off-the-shelf software, the contracting authority ensures that the System can be put into production use reliably and that, with its ready-made functionalities, it supports the contracting authority's processes and operating models. The system is configured with the system's existing functionalities for the contracting authority's needs in the deployment project. The system must support the working hour forms in accordance with the various collective agreements (hereinafter VES/TES) (HYVTES, SOTE agreement, LS) applicable to the contracting authority, as well as the various ways of organising work, i.e. fixed and flexible working hours. The subject of the procurement includes the functionalities described in the tender request and the system modules required by them, as well as any new rostering and time and attendance features and functions coming to the System during the contract period. In the initial phase, the System will not be introduced in rescue services or emergency care, but the contracting authority's objective is for them to become System users later during the contract period. The contract period is estimated to begin in November 2026 and be indefinite.
sig_67e3dab12e5ff6eb83aa.title: Rostering and time and attendance system as an off-the-shelf software, Kainuu wellbeing services county

sig_67fd93d3a6cfc9935732.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of solution expert SAP Basis in project P1160 'Critical Upgrading of ERP'. The consultant will be a part of the enabling team SAP-Basis in CIT DRIV AGM and shall take care of the role within the discipline SAP Basis. The role can involve cooperation with any other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.
sig_67fd93d3a6cfc9935732.title: Procurement of an SAP Basis Solution Expert

sig_68225bdb357591370d7b.description: Technical renewal and digital expansion of the parking system for Smart Parking Lot LOT-0000: Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe municipal area, Smart Parking - parking system for Smart Parking. The subject is the technical renewal and digital expansion of the existing parking systems at 5 locations of Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe, as well as the complete renewal of the parking system in the Karstadt multi-storey car park. The goal is a modern, service-oriented and functionally uniform parking infrastructure. The existing facilities are to be supplemented in such a way that modern digital parking processes based on number plate recognition, QR code functions, cashless web payment, digital discounting and self-service functions for short-term and long-term parkers can be used consistently and across all locations. The intention is not an isolated replacement of individual devices, but the functional expansion of an already existing overall system. Scope of services: delivery, installation, integration, commissioning and acceptance of the components at all locations; provision and setup of the central software and control computer components. Technical requirements and integration: - All components must be centrally manageable via the existing control computer/cell computer topology. - A continuous parking process (entry - identification via ticket, number plate or QR code - payment at machines/web service/discount point - exit - audit-proof accounting) must be guaranteed across the entire system. - Interfaces, firmware/backend versions and data models must be provided by the manufacturer in a coordinated manner. Installation, commissioning and acceptance: - Installation and commissioning during ongoing operation while minimising downtime; coordination with the project manager. - Acceptance criteria and partial acceptances: partial acceptance per location after successful functional/integration test; formal final acceptance after complete system integration. Other services: - Complete technical documentation in German. - Instruction/training of personnel: instruction of operating personnel per location as well as administrator training for the control computer system. A maintenance contract must be concluded for the maintenance of the systems, which covers the following areas: software, control/cell computer, availability of a technical service centre reachable 24/7, on-call service for on-site maintenance & repair.
sig_68225bdb357591370d7b.title: Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe municipal area, Smart Parking - parking system for Smart Parking

sig_6824e87e6a593ea0459a.description: Kansaneläkelaitos (Kela) invites tenderers to a market dialogue concerning the payment commitment concept developed by Kela to ensure national impact. The objective of the market dialogue is to understand how the concept could be utilised to meet the needs of various public administration actors. This is therefore an invitation to a market dialogue (not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders). The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey suppliers on the market and hear the views of potential tenderers. Participation in the market dialogue does not bind any party. Participation in the market dialogue is not a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent tendering procedure. Participation does not in any way affect a tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. No remuneration is paid for participation in the market dialogue. Interested parties are requested to register for the market dialogue by email at myntti-tuki@kela.fi no later than 23.9.2026 at 16.00. The market dialogue will be carried out in two stages. First as a written procedure, in which the materials and related questions will be sent by email to those who have registered for the market dialogue 24.9.2026. Answers to the market dialogue must be provided by 5.10.2026. In the second stage, based on the responses, we will invite organisations to Teams discussions. Information provided in the market dialogue will be treated confidentially. The names of companies involved in the market dialogue or other information concerning companies will not be published in connection with the responses. Information provided in the market dialogue does not bind any party. The market dialogue will be conducted in the Finnish language.

Reasoning Background With the entry into force of the amended Federal Nature Conservation Act (BNatSchG) on 01.03.2010, monitoring in accordance with EU Directive 2009/147/EC ("Birds Directive") was incorporated into Section 6 of the BNatSchG. This includes, in particular, the observation of the conservation status of European bird species and their habitats. In accordance with Section 7 ( 2) no. 12 of the BNatSchG, all bird species occurring naturally in Europe are considered "European bird species". According to Article 9 of the Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC), the EU Commission assesses at regular intervals the contribution of Natura 2000 to the realisation of the objectives of the Habitats and Birds Directives. This requires the content of the standard data forms (SDF) to be updated at regular intervals based on information available for each site in the network (Commission Implementing Decision 2011/484/EU). For this purpose, information on populations, population trends and habitats of the species relevant according to Article 4 paragraphs (1) and (2) of EU Directive 2009/147/EC is required. Monitoring in EU Special Protection Areas (SPAs) as part of the European Natura 2000 network is part of the monitoring of European bird species and their habitats in accordance with Section 6 of the BNatSchG. As a sub-programme, it serves (in accordance with Directives or Regulations 92/43/EEC, 2009/147/EC and 2019/1010) - the determination of populations of relevant bird species at least once in the six-year reporting cycle for each SPA, - the continuous determination of population trends and site-related conservation statuses of significant breeding bird species, - the continuous determination of population trends and site-related conservation statuses of significant migratory and wintering bird species, and - the standardised recording of habitat information, impairments and threats across the entire area of the SPAs for a comprehensive assessment of the conservation status of relevant bird species and their habitats. Standardised monitoring in the SPAs in Rhineland-Palatinate began with a pilot project 2025/2026 in ten selected SPAs (in accordance with the coalition agreement for Rhineland-Palatinate in the period 2021-2026). Therefore, the site-specific data foundations and qualities are currently often still unsatisfactory, and the state data do not allow for the determination of statistically robust population trends and conservation statuses for the significant bird species in the Rhineland-Palatinate SPAs. This prevents, in particular, appropriate priority and target planning by nature conservation authorities for measures to achieve good conservation status for the relevant species, where this is not already the case. The task package tendered here serves the supplementary recording in further SPAs with a view to the next bird protection report in the year 2031 (data period 2023-2028). The expected data serve to fulfil the reporting obligations to the EU under Article 12 of Directive 2009/147/EC and Regulation 2019/1010. Prospectively (ideally from 2029), all Rhineland-Palatinate SPAs are to be recorded in a six-year reporting cycle in accordance with a standardised monitoring concept (not part of this contract). Monitoring in EU Special Protection Areas 2011 the State Working Group of Bird Protection Stations (LAG VSW), together with the Umbrella Organisation of German Avifaunists (DDA) and the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation (BfN), has presented recommendations for the monitoring of European bird species and their habitats (LAG VSW et al., 2011). These pursue the goal of formulating a nationwide uniform standard for data collection. In this context, the principles mentioned for monitoring in SPAs leave sufficient room for state-specific adjustments. The results of the monitoring form the basis for site management against the background of the respective conservation objectives and for the reporting obligation under Art. 12 of Directive 2009/147/EC. Furthermore, they serve as a reference for decisions in preliminary and compatibility assessments. For the purpose of collecting baseline data in EU Special Protection Areas to improve data quality for the next bird protection report (reporting period 2023-2028) and for the efficient planning of future SPA monitoring, the implementation of the "Greece ruling" (ECJ in a request for a preliminary ruling from a Greek court under Art. 267 TFEU, 12.9.2024 - C-66/23) as well as the implementation of the "Nature Restoration Regulation" (EU Regulation 2024/1991), this procurement procedure is intended to provide baseline data on the occurrence and distribution of relevant species in accordance with Article 4 paragraphs (1) and (2) of EU Directive 2009/147/EC in as many Rhineland-Palatinate SPAs as possible. sig_6858bb78cc291b25b1ab.description: The project is aimed at potential international travellers and describes the possibility of active travel in Germany (focusing on hiking, cycling, and canoeing where applicable). The experience does not present individual destinations or tourism products, but rather conveys the characteristic qualities of Germany as a diverse active travel destination. The focus is on typical travel experiences and the combination of nature, physical activity, culture, culinary enjoyment, and relaxation that characterise active holidays in Germany. The project serves not only to impart knowledge, but the guest should be addressed, "taken by the hand", complete simple tasks, and be emotionally engaged. This has at least the same priority as the information. Objective: Extension of the length of stay. The project is to be developed for the output channels virtual reality (including inflight entertainment on aircraft with VR headsets), mobile, and web in order to generate the widest possible reach. This pilot project concerns a new type of destination marketing in which combinations of user engagement, user guidance, and content presentation from gaming, VR, artificial (AI-supported) content generation, and real content are combined. The bidder must combine these different skills and create an appealing, interactive product that fascinates customers with Germany as a travel destination. In addition to virtual environments, scenarios, and avatars (or digital entities/objects), the project should also incorporate existing media from the GNTB (photos, films, drone footage, 360-degree panoramas, etc.) and present them in an impressive, interactive form. Depending on the concept, further media may need to be digitally created, purchased, or shot. In addition, the use of (a few) Gaussian splats is planned for the first time, provided it makes sense in terms of content and technology. To our knowledge, the planned mix of (partially photorealistic) digitally created content and real images, panoramas, videos, and avatars is unprecedented in tourism marketing. Further information can be found in the service description in the tender document. Lot LOT-0000: Active travel in Germany. sig_68e9e3c7d8bb768a7d86.description: The employee survey in The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is carried out annually, usually at the end of January/February. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency has had a very high response percentage in recent years, between 82 % and 87%. In 2025, the survey was sent out to just over 2,000 respondents. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency currently uses Rambøll as its supplier and they are responsible for the entire process - from dispatching and administration to analysing the results. The results will be presented in an insight report that will be presented to the management team. With new competence in the HR department, including HR analyst competence, Forsvarsbygg is now considering taking a greater degree of ownership of the survey. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is looking at an option to administer the survey itself and get access to raw data, so that own analyses can be carried out, etc. Practical if the market dialogue: There is a form (excel sheet) that can be answered and the deadline is set at 12:00 1 December 2025.Input and form is submitted by using the communication model in Mercell.Based on received responses, the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency will make an assessment and possibly call in some suppliers for 1:1 conversations - if the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency deems it appropriate. These 1:1 meetings are likely to take place via Teams (possibly physically at The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency at Grev Wedels plass 5).
sig_68e9e3c7d8bb768a7d86.title: The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency invites tenderers to a market dialogue - Tool (SaaS) for handling employee surveys.

sig_6a1c3dbeafff2d320ec8.description: Dundee City Council intends to procure a construction consultant resource and project management system to improve the planning, allocation and monitoring of architectural, engineering and specialist consultancy resources across its capital and housing programmes. The system will complement existing corporate and client-side systems, including Civica, by providing enhanced resource planning, capacity forecasting, workload visibility, timesheet reporting and management information. The objective is to improve service efficiency, strengthen forward planning, support evidence-based resource decisions and provide greater assurance over programme delivery, capacity utilisation and value for money. Lot 1: . Dundee City Council is undertaking this Prior Information Notice (PIN) and market engagement exercise to better understand the solutions currently available within the market for construction consultant resource and project management software. The information gathered will assist the Council in developing its procurement strategy, refining its requirements and determining the most appropriate route to market. As part of this exercise, the Council intends to invite selected suppliers to participate in product demonstrations, currently anticipated to take place during early October 2026 (please note, these dates are indicative only). These demonstrations will provide an opportunity for the Council to gain a greater understanding of available solutions, functionality, implementation approaches and delivery models. Suppliers wishing to be considered for participation in the demonstration stage are requested to complete and return the attached questionnaire. The information provided will be used solely for market engagement purposes and to assist the Council in identifying suppliers whose solutions appear capable of meeting the Council's requirements. Completed questionnaires should be submitted by 12 Noon on 25 September 2026 to trina.forbes@dundeecity.gov.uk. Suppliers who do not submit a completed questionnaire will not be considered for participation in the demonstration stage. The Council reserves the right to limit the number of demonstrations undertaken and participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. Additional information: This PIN is issued for market engagement purposes only and will not be used to evaluate, select or exclude suppliers in any future procurement process. Information received will help Dundee City Council understand the market, develop its requirements and determine the most appropriate procurement approach. Participation is voluntary and does not commit the Council to proceed.

sig_6b692a82e072d7a22034.description: The National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) is CDC's state-based surveillance system for violent deaths and suicides. NVDRS combines information from death certificates, coroner or medical examiner reports, including toxicology reports, and law enforcement reports to provide comprehensive, incident-level data on the circumstances surrounding violent deaths. Through this Notice of Funding Opportunity, CDC will support eligible state, territorial, and local government entities, or their bona fide agents, in operating and modernizing NVDRS. Recipients will conduct statewide or territory-wide surveillance by collecting, linking, managing, analyzing, and submitting high-quality data on violent deaths and suicides. A central focus of this NOFO is timely and complete data reporting through two coordinated reporting processes: quarterly provisional data pulls and annual data closeout. Beginning in Year 1, recipients will prepare data for CDC's quarterly provisional data pulls to support earlier access to preliminary, actionable information. Recipients will progressively update case records as additional source documents and information become available. Annual data closeout is the primary process for producing the complete, finalized, and validated NVDRS dataset for each data year. Recipients must ensure that all eligible cases are fully abstracted, updated, validated, and completed using all required and available data sources by the annual closeout deadline. The finalized annual dataset supports national reporting, analysis, dissemination, and public health action. This NOFO also emphasizes modernization of data systems and workflows to increase efficiency, reduce reporting burden, improve data quality and timeliness, and enhance data usability. All recipients will complete a modernization readiness assessment within six months of award and implement at least one modernization pilot during the period of performance. Pilot activities may include automated data import and extraction, electronic data exchange and interoperability, workflow automation, data-quality tools, and enhanced data analysis and visualization. With CDC approval, recipients may also participate in optional activities that link NVDRS data with other relevant data systems to improve surveillance and expand public health insights. The intended outcome is a sustainable, modernized national surveillance system that produces timely provisional data and complete, reliable, high-quality annual data to inform violence and suicide prevention and support public health action.
sig_6b692a82e072d7a22034.title: Modernizing Violent Death and Suicide Surveillance Using the National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS)

sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.description: Die BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. Lot LOT-0000: Service Portal/Digital Customer Management, V0470/2026. The BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. The future system is intended to serve as a central platform for managing customers, contracts, access media, billing and communication with customers. The planned scope of services comprises in particular the provision, setup, customisation and operation of an integrated service portal with the following components: End Customer Portal (EKP): A digital portal through which customers can independently use services provided by BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular registration, management of customer data, conclusion and management of contracts, viewing of parking operations and invoices, as well as communication with BREPARK GmbH. Employee Portal (MA Portal): A central work surface for employees of BREPARK GmbH for managing and processing customer transactions. This comprises in particular the maintenance of customer data, processing of contract enquiries, management of contracts and access media, execution of checking and approval processes, and support for internal administrative processes. Business Customer Portal (GKP): The solution must provide a business customer portal through which authorised business customers can independently manage their contract-related data and access permissions. BREPARK manages various parking facilities on behalf of third parties and manages long-term parking permissions for business customers, amongst other things. Around 7.000 access media for business customers are currently managed. The aim is to provide business customers with a digital option for independently managing their permissions and access media, thereby simplifying administrative processes. The service portal is to be integrated into the existing system landscape of BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular connection to SAP Business ByDesign as the leading ERP system and the required interfaces to existing parking management and access systems. The contractor must provide an operational overall system which fulfils the requirements of this specification of services and enables the further development of the digital customer processes of BREPARK GmbH. In addition to the provision of the software, the scope of services also includes the required configuration, customising, integration into the existing system landscape, data migration, execution of tests, commissioning, and the required training, maintenance and support services for ongoing operations. Implementation takes place as an overall system. The contractor bears responsibility for the total technical and functional integration of all required components and interfaces.
sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.title: Service portal/Digital Customer Management, V0470/2026

sig_6dabd753c32e71f5ef91.description: Description of the procurement: The Danish Agency for Digital Government (Digitaliseringsstyrelsen) operates on behalf of the Danish State a national qualified trust service for the management of qualified electronic signature creation devices under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS2). As part of modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring a Qualified Signature Creation Devices (QSCD) to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centers (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to upgrade the throughput capacity of the QSCD and an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of the certified QSCD in accordance with eIDAS2. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the QSCD as part of its qualified trust service. The QSCD must integrate with the Agency's existing infrastructure, including the Agency's certificate authority, authorisation server, and signing components. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of certified QSCD Hardware sized and configured for operation across two data centres with redundant active/active configurations with a defined minimum production throughput per second, measured in RSA 4K operations equivalent; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Hardware, security patching, and up to two replacements of Hardware during the contract term to maintain valid certifications; (c) Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options; and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract.
sig_6dabd753c32e71f5ef91.title: Qualified Signature Creation Device (QSCD)

sig_6ded036e88f2a8424bb6.description: Invitation to market dialogue. Sykehusinnkjøp HF hereby invites tenderers to a market dialogue for the procurement of a laboratory information system for the health companies in Helse Nord. The market dialogue is a part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out because the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from potential suppliers, possibly also from other interested parties. As a part of this process, suppliers are invited to provide input to the procurement prior to the announcement. The feedback makes it possible to make a decision about the type of procurement and procurement procedure. Based on input from the market dialogue, the Contracting Authority will, as needed, open to a closer dialogue with some of the suppliers for further details and discussions. The contracting authority would like input on the following points: Short presentation of the supplier/tendererWhich the specialist areas the system is meant to cover (see further information on all disciplines within the laboratory service in annex "Invitation to market dialogue") About the solution, including brief information on functionality, possibilities and limitations, and: Describe how the system is built up in the tender documentation. modules, and which advantages this provides. How the system is deployed to clients; web based and/or sw deployed on clients. By the latter; whether there are specific requirements for clients. How the system will be deployed back-end. Describe how the system supports portable devices (tablets etc.). References to customers where the system is in use (and possibly which parts of the system they use). The tenderer ́s thoughts on how the system will support future development within the disciplines, e.g. within AI, integrations (i.a. FHIR), personalised medicine, etc. Input for the procurement as regards the expected functionality described in chapter 5 (see annex "Invitation to Market Dialogue"):How does the system ensure user friendliness, intuitive user interface and training? How does the system cover the overall description and for each of the disciplines covered by the solution? If there is functionality that cannot be offered we would like to know this. Which disciplines the solution covers and whether it covers all disciplines within the laboratory service (note possible exceptions for transfusion medicine/blood bank). How the system supports decision support functionality. How the solution supports artificial intelligence. How the system supports personalised medicine. How does the system support different integration mechanisms with other systems (FHIR, message exchange in accordance with Norwegian requirements, etc.?) Delivery. Which factors affect delivery time and how do you handle risk? All the functionalities are ready developed and can be delivered. If there is functionality that needs to be developed, it is desirable to know. Delivery model: cloud and/or local installation. If the system is cloud compatible; about Norwegian requirements are complied with. Whether there are specific requirements for HW and underlying SW-platform for customers. Short proposals as to how the system will be implemented at Customer Provisions that the Customer is expected to fulfil. Frequency of release bicycles and response to new functionality and error recovery. Integrations: does this require assistance from customers? Describe the pricing model and what factors affect the total cost of ownership (TCO) Licenses Maintenance/support price driven factors. And input that the tenderer deems important. Deadline for written feedback on the above mentioned points from interested parties: 28.11.2025. This is only a prior information notice in order to get information on the market and to have a dialogue with relevant suppliers. The actual competition may be announced at a later date. Feedback on or questions to the market survey is done in the Mercell communication module. After this market survey, the contracting authority will assess the need to hold meetings(s) with relevant interested parties.

sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications to develop, operate, and sustain a cloud-based data storage and computing platform that democratizes access to large-scale Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) genetic and genomic data. The platform must be secure, scalable, and interoperable. The platform will support the NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), the primary NIA-supported repository for the archiving and distribution of human genetic data related to AD/ADRD. The purpose of the platform will be to: Enable efficient ingestion, curation, harmonization, and analysis of multi-ancestry, large population-scale datasets; Provide robust analysis, visualization, and artificial intelligence -ready resources within secure cloud workspaces; Ensure compliance with federal security and data-sharing policies; Promote interoperability with other NIH- and NIA-supported repositories; and Provide user support, training, and community engagement. The NOFO aims to foster collaboration, accelerate discovery, and maximize the scientific value and impact of AD/ADRD genetics research for the broader research community. By improving data accessibility, interoperability, reporting, reproducibility, and scalable computational systems that enable rigorous, reproducible, and transparent research, the NOFO seeks to align with the NIH’s plan for Gold Standard Science and the AD/ADRD Research Implementation Milestones . Additionally, the NOFO seeks to address the Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's recommendation of ensuring broad, secure access to high-value datasets and enhancing data usability to maximize the return on research investments and support future discoveries in AD/ADRD. Moreover, the NOFO intends to directly advance NIA’s Strategic Directions , particularly Goal G to support the infrastructure and resources necessary for high-quality research, by strengthening data sharing, computational infrastructure, and research rigor across the AD/ADRD community. The NOFO intends to utilize the U24 activity code. Applications are not being solicited at this time. This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.title: The NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS)

sig_6ed7cd14dea6dc521d15.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to create a Logistics Center for the PRIMED-AI Program to facilitate and coordinate PRIMED-AI activities to maximize impact for the PRIMED-AI community. Within the Logistics Center, three integrated Cores will serve the functions of Administration, Evaluation, and Outreach for the PRIMED-AI Consortium. It is expected that the Logistics Center will work closely with other PRIMED-AI consortium members to collect, curate and disseminate information regarding tools developed by the PRIMED-AI award recipients, and will facilitate widespread access and awareness across the relevant scientific, patient, and clinical communities.
sig_6ed7cd14dea6dc521d15.title: Logistics Center for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U24 Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

This Request for Information (RFI) is a preliminary market engagement exercise under the Procurement Act 2023, intended to inform and shape the emerging vision ahead of any procurement. Through it, Southern Water is seeking to: • Understand the capability, capacity and appetite of the market to deliver a programme of this nature; • Test the feasibility and realism of the emerging vision, and in particular the delivery timescale; • Gather delivery approaches, technical options, innovations, case studies and indicative commercial models; • Understand how the market would best package (Lot) the requirement; and • Inform Southern Water's business case, sourcing strategy and eventual procurement approach.

sig_6fcb6f1f758a9219b3e3.description: This invitation to tender ('ITT') relates to Lake District National Park Authority's (the 'Authority') procurement for a Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework Agreement, for our Ranger Services Team and others. Successful Tenderers will be appointed onto a multi-supplier Framework Agreement divided into Lots. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Authority and by other bodies in the Authority's network by prior agreement. The Authority is seeking a mix of contractors to bid for a place on the Framework Agreement, including companies, consultants, sole traders, and Small and Medium Sized Enterprises. This procurement is divided into Lots (and sub-lots in the case of Lot 4). Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots/sub-lots provided that you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in the Lot Specification at Table A. Please note that you do not need to be able to provide all of the services listed in the Lot specification, provided you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in that Lot you may submit a tender. All Prices should be submitted as a maximum for provision of your goods/services and will be a commitment for the duration of the Framework Agreement, subject to the allowed increase in price annually. This Framework Agreement will allow for Direct Award and Further Competition of Call-off Contracts. Tenderers should read the instructions contained in this ITT carefully before submitting a response. Failure to comply with the requirements set out in this ITT may result in the rejection of the Tender. Tenderers are advised to acquaint themselves fully with the extent and nature of the goods and/or services in the Statement of Requirement and with the Terms and Conditions. Participation in this procurement automatically signals that the Tenderer accepts the Terms and Conditions contained in this ITT. If a Tenderer is awarded a place on any Lot of the Framework, a draft Framework Agreement will be provided after all awards have taken place (est. February - March 2027). Any award is not legally binding and subject-to-contract until the final Framework Agreement between the Authority and the Tenderer is signed. The Lake District National Park Authority looks after the Lake District National Park, encouraging people to enjoy and understand its beauty and supporting those who live and work here. Further information about the LDNPA, including our statutory functions, is available on our website. We are working towards making the Lake District an inspirational example of sustainable development in action. We want its prosperous economy, world class visitor experiences and vibrant communities to come together in sustaining the spectacular landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage here. Details of how we are doing this are outlined in our Vision: Our purpose and vision - Lake District National Park Our Ranger Services Team at LDNPA has a focus on maintaining and improving the Rights of Way and other access in the Lake District National Park, while encouraging and educating users in responsible outdoor recreation on accessible land and navigable lakes. They support visitor management and nature recovery initiatives, and the enhancement and maintenance of our rural properties, in line with our strategic priorities. They work closely with communities to help them meet their needs in ways that contribute to our Vision. The Ranger Team's workload includes project work, such as the Coast-to-Coast and Fix the Fells. The Historic Environment Team commissions specialist consultancy support to inform the conservation, management and enhancement of the National Park's historic environment. This may include heritage impact assessments, conservation area appraisals, historic building recording, conditions surveys, archaeological investigations, landscape and townscape character assessments, design advice, and other specialist heritage and built environment studies to support planning, conservation and place-shaping objectives. Our needs are specific and will vary. We are looking for Suppliers who understand the work we do and not only can provide exceptional services, but who can contribute to our wider Vision for the Lake District. Please note that the Lot Descriptions in section 2 are included to provide some background information on the work of the Authority. The following are examples of types of services which may be required by our Ranger Service. This is not exhaustive but is intended to demonstrate the breadth of the services which will be required: Providing services on a recurring and annual basis, such as our bridge maintenance responsibilities and sourcing of materials for daily use; Providing advice and practical work on specific public sector funded projects, such as the Coast-to-Coast project. Providing specific advice to our internal team of individuals and organisations with whom we operate, for internal projects involving our own land and property, and also to our partner organisations such as Fix the Fells. Lot 1: Bridges Supply, Repair and Maintenance. The Authority supplies, installs and maintains bridges on public rights of way throughout the National Park including bridleways and footpaths for use by horse riders, cyclists, mobility scooters and pedestrians. We are seeking suppliers who can assist with the following: • Supply bridge materials as component parts and/or complete structures in a variety of materials including recycled plastic, metal, timber, concrete, stone. These bridges will need to be to our specification or bespoke design in some cases. • Using the materials listed above, build and install those bridges in a wide variety of locations, including some remote and difficult to get to. This can include machine work, working with helicopter delivery companies, working with hand tools, demolition and construction of abutments. • To repair existing bridge structures in situ, including replacement of handrails, decking boards, beams, abutments e.g. stonework. • To provide designs to structural engineers' standards to meet the supplied specifications for a wide range of bridge types, including footbridges, bridleway bridges and those suitable for road traffic in some instances. This might include reviewing and revising our existing designs and specifications, to producing bespoke designs for individual unique locations and bridge types. • For structural engineers to inspect the current condition of bridges and abutments to check they meet the standards for the required user groups and to sign off newly installed bridges to verify that they meet the required specification and standards. • To provide, erect and use scaffolding, including in remote locations, to complex designs, to enable the team to carry out maintenance and construction work on the bridges and other rights of way work in a safe and secure manner, following current industry and health and safety standards. Services required: • Supply of prefabricated bridge kits • Provision of materials e.g. timber/ plastic/ metal • Bespoke design of bridges • Installation of bridges • Repair of bridges • Engineer surveys on bridges • Scaffolding on bridges to support safe installation or repair Lot 2: Supply of Materials. The Authority requires qualified suppliers for the supply, delivery and installation of materials and services to support our countryside construction and maintenance projects. It aims to ensure high-quality, timely, and cost-effective delivery of materials and services while complying with health, safety, and environmental standards. It also aims to facilitate the provision of locally sourced materials to reduce transport mileage, to support the economic wellbeing of the National Park, and to showcase local products. Suppliers under this framework must demonstrate relevant experience, proven quality standards and the capacity to meet delivery schedules. Services and materials will be provided according to defined specifications, with monitoring of performance through key indicators such as timeliness, quality, and responsiveness. Suppliers must ensure that all materials supplied meet relevant British Standards or industry-recognised equivalents. Goods required: • Pipes/drains • Grass seed • Treated and some graded timber for fencing and the construction of timber boardwalks • Gates • Waymark roundels for Public Footpaths, Bridleways, Byways and permitted routes • Local stone (from the Lake District) for construction of unbound surface paths, stone for drainage works and dry-stone walling and bridge revetments • Plastic boardwalks from 1m to 3m width with non-slip finish • Metalwork (gate springs, gate hinges, catches screws, nuts, etc.) • Screened (inert) topsoil • Fingerposts and Waymarkers • Benches • Fencing wire • Metal fencing (i.e. Clipex) • Native tree species grown from seeds sourced in seed zone 301, or if unavailable, 302. Lot 3: Minor Practical works under £50,000. The Authority requires a range of qualified suppliers for delivery of practical works and services supporting our countryside access and nature conservation projects across the National Park. This often requires working in remote locations with challenging access. All work standards and specifications will be set out in relevant documents. All work will need to be carried out to all relevant legislative requirements by appropriately trained and qualified staff. Examples of the types of work the Authority requires are: construction, repair and maintenance of structures, furniture and surfaces forming part of Public Rights of Way work (PROW) such as footpaths, bridleways and byways. Surfacing -The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Un-bound, bound, crushed stone or tarmac paths. • Machine construction of profile inversion (subsoil) paths • Supply and delivery and laying of stone flags • Construction and repair of pitched stone paths using local stone. Drainage works - The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Plastic drainage of all sizes. • Stone culverts • Drainage ditches. Fencing, Walling and hedgerows- The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • All forms of fencing including Post and rail, post and wire, metal estate style • Drystone and bound (mortared) walling in local vernacular style. • Hedgerows planted and maintained in the local vernacular style. Vegetation management • Mechanical and chemical control of vegetation on public rights of way, open land and formal sites including control of Invasive Non-Native Species (INNS). Countryside Furniture - The supply, construction, repair, and maintenance of; • Wooden and metal fingerposts, signs, benches, gates stiles, boardwalks and other countryside furniture. Tree Works • Surveying, planting, felling, maintaining and high access rope work relating to tree management. • Supply of native tree and plant species. Transportation • Transportation of plant, machinery, materials to accessible parts of the National Park. Habitat Restoration Works • Restore peatland areas by hand and or machine. • Planting of native species Traffic Management Supply and management of traffic control systems on public highways up to 'A' road standards. Please see our Rights of Way Specification Resource Pack at Appendix 1. Services required: • Surfacing • Drainage installation and maintenance • Sub soiling • Installation of stone flags • Pitching to create paths • Fencing • Walling • Vegetation control and clearance • Installation of countryside furniture (e.g. fingerposts/benches) • Tree works • Planting (trees and hedgerows) • Spraying (herbicides) • Hedge trimming • Salting and gritting paths • Trail sweeping • Mooring works (Ullswater/servicing) • Graffiti removal • Woodland management through thinning, coppicing, halo thinning, girdling, and processing of timber • Bracken management through mowing, rolling, or chemical application • Scrub management • Hedge laying • Grassland restoration and management activities; mowing, baling, weed wiping, harrowing, seeding, plug planting • Chemical control of invasive, non-native species Please also see Appendix 1 of the ITT. Lot 4: Consultancy and Specialist Services. The Authority requires a range of consultancy services to assist it in carrying out its statutory duties and project work. Our work is incredibly varied, and consultancy is required in relation to all stages of a project from feasibility, design, planning, and surveying. We require specialist advice in relation to Rights of Way, and lake/water works. Other areas of the Authority's work include historic buildings and environment, planning and architectural surveying so we welcome consultants from a range of specialist practice areas. Advice sought could be, for example, in the form of written reports, design drawings to agreed standards, survey datasets (in agreed formats) or overseeing the delivery of defined projects around nature recovery or access and recreation related works. This Lot is divided into three individual sub-lots based on the type of consultancy required. Lot 4a: Access and Recreation services required: • Traffic management e.g. traffic lights • Planning consultancy • Structural engineering design • Construction Design and Management works • Electronic counting surveys - people, horses, vehicles, bikes etc • Rights of Way consultants • Project managers • Visitor monitoring and data • Property management and consulting Lot 4b: Natural Environment: • Ecological surveys (e.g. habitat surveys using NVC, UKHAB frameworks/Habitat condition monitoring using BNG or CSM methods/specialist surveys for taxonomical groups i.e Bryophytes, Lichens, protected species groups, insects) • Baseline surveys • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat Management and Monitoring Plans • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat bank monitoring survey and reporting • Habitat and property management and monitoring planning • Drone Surveys • Geospatial surveys Lot 4c: Historic Environment: • Historic Structure Surveys (e.g. condition surveys, archaeological and structural assessments and repair schedules) • Archaeological surverys (e.g condition surveys, fieldwork, heritage assessments) • Contract administration services for Historic Structure Construction Projects Lot 5: Training and Development. he Authority requires qualified companies to provide essential training to ensure that individuals working in various roles are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to work safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements and legislation. The training requirements cover a range of topics, including first aid, manual handling, chainsaw, plant and equipment operation (to name a few - please see Appendix 2 for a full concise list), which are required to minimise risks and ensure a safe working environment. Courses will need to be accredited by recognised bodies, providing learners with the necessary qualifications to meet industry standards. • First aid • Manual handling • Practical countryside management training e.g.: walling, fencing • Plant and machinery operations e.g.: 4WD training, chainsaws, quad bikes, strimmers; • Species management training (e.g tree conditions surveys) • Please see Appendix 2 of the ITT for a list of all training requirements. Lot 6: Supply and repairs of Equipment, Plant and Machinery. The Authority has an internal fleet of various machinery, equipment and plant. We require services for maintenance and servicing of all types of equipment, plant, and machinery. We also require suppliers who can source and provide new equipment, plant and machinery as required. For example, current categories include: • Plant: diggers, dumpers, tracked power barrows, remote flails, chippers. • Vehicles: land rovers, pick-ups, 4x4s, electric vans and cars. • Power tools: compressors, jet washes, cement mixers, drills, stone saws, angle grinders chop saws etc. • Hand tools: spades, panel saws, shovelers, tampers, steel bars etc. • PPE: chainsaw trousers, hard hats, eye protection, hearing protection etc. • Fuel (Aspen, diesel, petrol, LPG etc.) • Servicing and safety inspections (e.g. LOLA checks on lifting strops and chains, and general servicing of tools like compressors) • Bi-annual service of outboard motors for patrol boats • Servicing of patrol boat trailers • Annual servicing of life jackets, patrol boat radar systems and CCTV systems. We require maintenance and servicing of all machinery and vehicles. Services required: • Servicing • Repairs • Maintenance (boats, outboard engines, trailers, lifejackets, diggers, dumpers, radar, CAT scanners, generator calibration) • Inspection of kit/ equipment • LOLER items checks • Supply of new machinery as required Lot 7: Helicopter Operations. Provide helicopter operations for the transportation of stone and other materials to remote locations throughout the Lake District: movement of prebagged fell stone in one-ton bags to high altitude worksites on popular mountain paths. Stropping, bunding and prepping materials such as flagstones, fence posts or bridge materials prior to flying. Providing specialist safety advice to officers involved in helicopter operations - before during and after any operations. Provide experienced ground crew for hooking on and assessing loads, receiving loads where necessary and ensuring specialist kit or equipment such as signage strops and radio headsets are available. To provide an indication of volume, in 2025 LDNPA flew over 400 tonnes of stone to high altitude sites. Suppliers must hold all relevant Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approvals, USL Licensing and operate in accordance with UK aviation regulations. Services required: • Transport of materials and equipment within the Lake District National Park using helicopters • Airlift operations • Load preparation (stropping, bunding) • Ground crew provision • Flight planning and risk assessment Lot 8: Higher Value Practical Works - £50,000 and over. The Authority secures frequent bids for grant money provided by national, regional and local government as well as charitable organisations and private funding organisations. This funding enables the Authority to undertake larger scale and usually multi-facetted projects or programmes of work varying in value from the high tens of thousands of pounds to the low millions of pounds. Such projects may involve delivery of one type of product or service across a range of sites throughout the park or a multi-facetted project including access, nature conservation, interpretation, and conservation of the heritage-built environment. We are looking for suppliers who can provide work at scale and across a range of areas, either directly or by acting as Primary Contractors and providing project management and delivering work through co-ordinating multiple suppliers and contractors. Examples of such work packages include the establishment of the Coast-to-Coast National Trail, barn restoration through the Farming in Protected Landscapes programme and Access for All projects. The type of work is similar to that contained in Lots 1, 2, and 3 but at large scale. Services required: • General construction project work (see description) • Sub soiling • Stone flags • Pitching • Construction Design and Management work • Supply and construction of bridges • Public path works • Securing relevant consents, assents and planning permissions • Woodland Management • Grassland restoration • Riverbank Stabilization

sig_6fd419bd4cdb323d6a29.description: The object of the procurement is the testing equipment for the ETCS subsystems of the Digirail testing laboratory, the related software, and the installation, maintenance, development, support and training services related to the entity. The main objective of the Digirail testing laboratory is to ensure that the systems procured in the Digirail project meet all technical and operational requirements, support the integration and interoperability of the ETCS system, and are ready for the SIT and SAT testing phases. The laboratory is used especially for the testing of interoperability (IOP/ESC) between ETCS trackside equipment and ETCS on-board subsystems, but more broadly also for the verification of requirements and other integration and interoperability testing, covering the entire chain from track equipment to rolling stock. The client states that the selected service provider must be impartial in relation to the companies acting as current or future equipment suppliers in the Digirail project as a whole, and the client's view is that the selected service provider cannot act as such an equipment supplier or be selected as such an equipment supplier. The details of the request for participate and the request for tender can be found in the appendix documents in Finnish and English.
sig_6fd419bd4cdb323d6a29.title: ETCS test equipment for interoperability testing between Trackside and On-board Subsystems

The contribution service of ARD, ZDF, Deutschlandradio (hereinafter referred to as "Contribution Service" or "Client" or "AG") intends to replace the existing Db2-z/OS platform with a modern, open target platform based on PostgreSQL in on-premises operation. The subject matter is the technical migration of the existing database and application components without functional changes. The objective is the complete, high-performing and secure executability of all affected applications on PostgreSQL. The eight work packages to be performed by the contractor (AN) within the scope of the overall project are described below. The tasks are to be performed in close cooperation and coordination with the project team of the Contribution Service. 1. Migration of the Db2 database to PostgreSQL - Analysis of the database and development of a migration plan with the aim of transferring the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Migration of the database structure including all relevant database objects incl. tables, indexes, views, triggers. The management of schema changes under PostgreSQL is to be supported by a Liquibase model. Stored procedures are not part of the migration, as their replacement has already taken place. - Migration of data from the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Verification of the correctness of the migration by suitable test procedures. 2. Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements - Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements. - Support of the Client in proving the correct functionality of the applications. - If application errors occur, solution concepts must be developed, coordinated with the Client and implemented to ensure the correct functionality of the applications. In doing so, an adaptation of the application code (e.g., Java in RUBIN) should be avoided if possible. 3. Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database and sizing of the hardware required for on-premises operation - Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database through suitable tuning measures, so that the performance requirements of the Client are met. - Elaboration of a hardware sizing on the basis of which the Contribution Service can procure the hardware required for on-premises operation for the operation of the applications without further conceptual preliminary work. - Proof of compliance with the performance requirements of the Contribution Service by means of suitable test procedures on the hardware procured by the Contribution Service (this is carried out according to the sizing specifications of the AN). 4. Setup of the required system environments and infrastructure as well as design of the required operational processes - Setup of the server infrastructure and the associated system software (operating system, database) using the Ansible Automation Platform. - Setup (installation, integration, establishment of operational readiness) and operation of the required system environments (development, reference, training, test, production) for the individual applications in cooperation with the team of the Contribution Service. - Management of test environments and test data - Documentation of the corresponding procedure and operational processes. - Design and testing of the required operational processes (backup and recovery, system monitoring, etc.). - Transfer of responsibility for these tasks to the Contribution Service team by the milestone "Trial Operation". 5. Development of a tool for pseudonymisation / anonymisation and test data generation - Development or integration of a commercial tool for pseudonymisation/anonymisation of data in accordance with the functional requirements of the Contribution Service. - Development or integration of a commercial tool for the generation of consistent test data (subsets of production data) for development and test environments as well as for performance measurements 6. Qualification of users - Transfer of the necessary integration and operational know-how to the Contribution Service team. - Support and assistance of Contribution Service experts in taking over operational tasks. - Conducting training courses and other qualification measures in the areas of PostgreSQL, operational tools and others. 7. Go-live and support during the start-up phase - Preparation of the go-live of the applications. - Go-live fine planning - Conducting dress rehearsals for the go-live of the applications. - Support of the go-live, standby - hypercare for a period of nine months. 8. Project and release management - The project is organised with project and sub-project management as well as a steering committee. The AN ensures professional project planning, project control and project reporting and establishes risk management appropriate to the risk. - At the project and sub-project level, dual staffing with representatives of the Contribution Service and the AN is planned. - All necessary deadline meetings, workshops, etc. are to be prepared, moderated and documented by the AN. - All results and in particular decisions made are to be documented properly, in detail and comprehensively by the AN. - Templates and models are to be agreed between the Contribution Service and the AN. - The Confluence system or another system provided by the Client is to be used as the project repository. - The AN shall provide for the establishment of a project office (PMO) (however, an on-site establishment at the Contribution Service is not required). The description of the tendered services is continued under section 5.1 of this notice. Continuation of the description of the tendered services from section 2.1 of this notice.

- The project office supports project management on both the Contribution Service and contractor sides for administrative tasks (recording and administrative tasks, information preparation and distribution, planning tasks, report preparation, etc.). - The AN provides release management to coordinate the further development of the applications by the Contribution Service and the migration activities over the course of the approx. three-year project duration. The following services are not the subject of this tender: - Provision of the PostgreSQL database software, operating system software - Procurement of the hardware and system technology required for operation. - Procurements of tools and software tools required by the Client for the operation of the systems beyond the end of the project or permanently. It is intended, provided that a sufficient number of applications to participate by suitable tenderers is received, to limit the number of tenderers who will be invited to submit tenders in the subsequent negotiation procedure to three suitable tenderers. Unsuccessful tenderers will be informed in writing of their elimination. The restriction of the circle of tenderers is based on objective, non-discriminatory criteria (cf. this notice and Part A. Conditions of Participation of the Participation Brochure) The Contribution Service will suspend the negotiation procedure for a period of 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation over the turn of the year. The selected bidders will receive information before the suspension of the procedure that they belong to the limited circle of bidders. In addition, the Contribution Service will inform them via the communication function of the dtvp procurement marketplace about the resumption of the negotiation procedure and the provision of the tender documents as well as the invitation to submit initial tenders on the dtvp procurement marketplace. The procurement procedure will be continued with at least one negotiation round for 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the previously described suspension of the procedure. The awarding authority will only invite the three selected suitable bidders to submit an initial tender based on the detailed tender documents including a detailed description of services. In addition, for quality assurance purposes, the implementation of a 2-month pitch is planned. Bidders will receive technical documents, test data without production reference as well as selected SQLs and code snippets, carry out an exemplary trial migration, analyse risks and outline (partial) solution concepts including procedures for hardware sizing. The pitch fee is 20.000 euros net. The pitch results feed into the quality evaluation. Further details on the pitch as well as the concrete schedule for the implementation of the pitch and the parallel preparation of the initial tenders can be found in the tender documents, which will be made available to the bidders belonging to the limited circle of bidders after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the 2-month procedure suspension via the invitation to submit the initial tender on the dtvp procurement marketplace. SELECTION OF THE LIMITED CIRCLE OF BIDDERS The Contribution Service will select a maximum of 3 bidders for the negotiation procedure. If more than 3 applicants are suitable after checking the applications to participate, the selection will be made on the basis of the following objective criteria: The Contribution Service will award a maximum of 200 points for the reference list submitted by the applicant. Within the framework of awarding the maximum 100 points per specified migration reference, the Contribution Service will exclusively base its decision on the two reference contracts of the applicant that were confirmed by the reference client during the reference check, meet the specified minimum requirements and achieved the highest score during the evaluation. In the event that more than three applicants belong to the restricted circle of applicants due to an equal number of points, all these applicants with the same score will also be invited to submit a tender. In detail, the awarding of points is based on the following criteria: a) Comparability of the source system in the reference project (15 points) - Replacement of a DB2 database from a mainframe system: 15 points b) Data volume of the reference project related to structured data (max. 30 points) - > 2 TB (minimum requirement) to 5 TB: 10 points - > 5 TB to 10 TB: 20 points - > 10 TB: 30 points c) Technical complexity of the data model and application logic (max. 40 points) - High data integrity: The migration included a data model with high referential integrity with foreign keys: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using triggers: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using views: 5 points - High application binding: The migration included the adaptation of embedded SQL: 5 points - Combined technical complexity: In addition, it is evaluated whether the migration required a combination of the above-mentioned techniques. Full points will be awarded if the migration included the cumulative application of foreign keys and triggers and views: 20 points d) Scope of operational responsibility in the reference project (max. 10 points) - Operational responsibility for 3 (minimum requirement) to 6 months: 5 points - Operational responsibility for > 6 months to 12 months: 10 points e) Type of client in the reference project (max. 5 points) - Client from the private sector: 0 points - Public sector client: 5 points Further details on the competition for participation can be found in the participation brochure provided on the dtvp procurement marketplace.
