sig_71b044f6ea8a0fde2b93.description: The U.S. Embassy Athens Public Diplomacy Section (PDS Athens) of the U.S. Department of State is pleased to announce funding is available through its Public Diplomacy Grants Program in fiscal year 2025. This is an Annual Program Statement, outlining our funding priorities, the strategic themes we focus on, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Please carefully follow all instructions below. The deadline for grant applications is July 11, 2025. Funding decisions will be made on these applications on a rolling basis after this deadline, with a goal of informing all applicants of the final funding decision by September 30, 2025. Applicants may apply for funding between $25,000 and $100,000 . Please use the grant application documents and budget template found on the Embassy website https://gr.usembassy.gov/education/ . Purpose of Grants program: PDS Athens invites proposals for projects that strengthen ties between the United States and Greece through concrete demonstrations of cooperation between our two peoples, aiming at making America safer, stronger and more prosperous . All grant proposals must convey an element of American history, culture, or shared values. Competitive proposals should support a priority program area (see below). They should also include a connection with American expert/s, organization/s, or institution/s that will promote increased cooperation between the people of the United States and Greece even after the program has finished. Priority Program Areas: The Public Diplomacy Section is focused on the following priorities in the form of programs, exchanges, and media opportunities that: Promote American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Celebrate 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership Promoting American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Greek students and professionals in emerging technologies have demonstrated a strong technical foundation that can be strategically leveraged to benefit U.S. technology firms and bolster American leadership in critical industries. By channeling this talent to serve the needs of American companies, we can reinforce U.S. technological dominance, strengthen innovation pipelines, and ensure that international engagement directly supports American economic and strategic priorities. We invite proposals aimed at enhancing U.S.-Greece technological cooperation in ways that clearly advance U.S. national interests. Proposals must focus on initiatives (not conferences) that help U.S. firms address critical workforce and skill shortages, expand the reach of American products and innovation standards, and create structured pathways for Greek talent to contribute to U.S.-driven innovation. Prioritized activities include, but are not limited to: Public-private partnerships that connect U.S. technology firms with high-potential Greek talent through American-led career readiness programs, skills development, and reskilling/upskilling initiatives tailored to U.S. industry standards and needs. Training modules designed for integration into Greek higher education or vocational curricula that: Align directly with the needs of U.S. employers; and Target high-demand fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology, cybersecurity, data analytics, and cloud computing—strengthening the global competitiveness of U.S. firms. Innovation bootcamps that feature U.S. technologies, platforms, and products, familiarizing international talent with high-quality American tools and practices. Collaborative projects between U.S. technology companies and Greek educational institutions to promote the adoption and use of American-developed AI and other emerging technologies, reinforcing the global footprint of U.S. innovation. All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American commercial and strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy. Celebrating 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership On July 4, 2026, the United States will commemorate the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. This historic milestone presents a powerful opportunity to celebrate American excellence, leverage people-to-people ties, and highlight our achievements, legacies, and contributions as part of America’s story of excellence. We invite proposals that underscore American excellence and contribute to the celebration of America250 , highlighting this momentous occasion through impactful and engaging programs. We welcome submissions that promote U.S.-Greece bilateral engagement and spotlight American achievements, innovation, leadership, and the role of faith and religion in democratic societies. Proposals should feature initiatives (not conferences), and include activities such as (but not limited to): Podcasts and/or public lectures on U.S. history, its ties to Greece, democracy, and its global impact Roadshows showcasing 250 years of American innovation and U.S.-Greek cooperation Sports activities or themed games/events Secondary educational modules that will reach Greek classrooms and help to enhance Greek students’ and educators’ positive understanding of America All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy.

sig_721640b036162c17fbaa.description: Dumfries & Galloway Council are seeking a suitably qualified and experienced organisation ideally with an engineering background to undertake a comprehensive crane condition / reliability survey. Dumfries and Galloway Council operate a Mechanical Biological Waste Treatment facility located in Dumfries. The plant operates with 2 overhead gantry cranes which are used to lift and transfer waste around the fully automated waste treatment facility which has been in situ since 2006. The completed survey is intended to inform the Council of the cranes current condition, any immediate remedial action necessary and set out the requirements for future annual maintenance and servicing. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway Council operate a Mechanical Biological Waste Treatment facility located in Dumfries. Construction on the site started in 2004 and was completed in 2006. The plant operates with 2 overhead gantry cranes which are used to lift and transfer waste around the fully automated waste treatment facility The plant was designed and constructed by Italian company Systema Ecodeco and operates with 2 Demag waste handling cranes, overhead electric top-running crane with a single hoist trolley unit. Technical specification document can be provided, however, overview of the cranes is: Manufacturing year 2006 Date of commissioning 2006 Serial number GS1442 & GS1443 Customer’s crane identification CP1 & CP2 Rated load 6.3 t Span 20.05 m Length of the runway ?? m Lifting height 11.8 m Type of the crane - Double girder EOT with one trolley Location in the customer’s process - Waste Hall Type of control - Automated Operating method - VFD Hoist - VFD Trolley - VFD Bridge Weights Trolley weight - 4.0 t No. of trolleys -1 Bridge weight - 20.0 t Non-fixed LLA weight - 0 t Fixed LLA weight - 3.5 t Design standards, classifications and speeds Crane structures - FEM 1.001 -1987 Trolley structures - A8 Movements - A8 Hoisting - 30 m/min / 1.0 m/min – M8 Trolley - 70 m/min / 1.0 m/min – M8 Bridge - 120 m/min / 1.0 m/min – M7 We are seeking to engage with a suitably qualified engineering company to undertake a comprehensive crane reliability study for both cranes currently in operation. The scope of works should include, but not be limited to, the following: - Internal endoscopic inspection and vibration analysis of the hoist gearboxes. - Vibration analysis of the rope drum, trolley wheels, hoist motor, trolley motor/gearbox, bridge motors/gearboxes and bridge wheels to determine the level of internal component degradation. - Measurement of the bridge and trolley wheels and compare to OEM specification. - Insulation and winding resistance measurements on all motors. - Rope drum inspection using specialist tools to measure the amount of wear present in the contact surfaces. - Disassembly, thorough cleaning and measurement of the internal components of the hoist, trolley and bridge brake units and compare to OEM specification. - General crane control panel electrical component condition analysis to include thorough examination of the trolley festoon mechanics, power and control flatform cables and hoist encoder cable. - Carry out thermal imaging surveys in addition to the component condition analysis to further determine problematic areas prior to potential failure. - Provide a comprehensive Crane Reliability Study structured report detailing all recommendations, corrective actions and remedial repairs. - All/Any supporting documentation. - A Geometric Survey or equivalent to provide accurate information detailing the alignment and the square of a crane. The scope of the survey should include wheels, guide rollers, end trucks, girders, and other components of the crane. - A 3D Runway Survey or equivalent to deliver accurate information on the alignment of the crane runway and expert recommendations for any needed corrective actions.. The Council requests that only organisations with the relevant capability, experience and qualifications register interest in this notice. Any feedback that can be offered is welcomed.

sig_729b45308c6d2eb6e263.description: Background Arendal municipality has an ongoing need for graphical services connected to information material and visual communication aimed at inhabitants and internal target groups. The municipality produces some material itself, but needs external assistance for assignments that are more complex, time consuming or require special professional competence. The procurement shall ensure access to capacity and relevant competence within graphical design, at the same time as the municipality takes care of the need for uniform visual communication and clear identity. The municipality shall be one sender. It is also important to ensure that material and visual deliveries fulfil the requirements for universal design and ensure accessible and understandable communication for different user groups. The municipality therefore needs to establish a new framework agreement that provides predictable access to graphical assistance as needed, both for smaller ongoing assignments and for major or more strategic deliveries. Description of the assignment The procurement is for graphic services for Arendal municipality. The delivery shall cover the development and production of various types of graphical material and visual elements, including information material, reports, presentations, templates, graphics for digital surfaces, infographics, illustrations and professional design consultancy services. The assignments will vary in extent and complexity. The municipality needs a tenderer who can assist with both smaller, limited assignments and large deliveries that require more planning and close cooperation with the contracting authority. Minor assignments means limited deliveries such as, for example, an ad, poster, presentation or simple illustration. Larger deliveries means assignments that include planning, coordination and multiple sub-services, such as a report or campaign material. The deliveries shall be able to be used further in the municipality ́s own channels and tools, and it is important that the deliveries can be further developed and adapted internally. The framework agreement shall also include the design of profile material and profile articles, as well as graphic materials connected to the use of, among other things, vehicles, buildings and work clothes. Web design for arendal.kommune.no is not included in the procurement. It is important to have clear contact points, effective clarifications and a good understanding of the municipality ́s graphical profile, communication needs and targets for clear, available and recognisable communication.

sig_72fc7eb88055e268874c.description: Government and the nation face a talent shortfall in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity. The CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service ( CyberAI SFS ) program welcomes proposals that address AI and cybersecurity education and workforce development. CyberAI refers to using AI in cybersecurity as well as providing security and resilience for AI systems. The Scholarship Track provides funding to establish, or to continue, scholarship for service programs with integrated AI and cybersecurity components (CyberAI). Scholarship recipients must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents and work after graduation in the AI or cybersecurity mission of a government organization for a period of at least the length of the scholarship. The Innovation Track supports projects that enhance preparation of AI and/or cybersecurity professionals. Projects may expand existing educational opportunities, curricula, degree programs, educational pathways, methods and interventions, and partnerships among institutions of higher education, government, and employers. Two statutes authorize this program: 15 USC §7442 (cybersecurity) and 42 USC §18993 (AI). CyberAI SFS aligns with the Executive Order 14277 to prioritize AI within scholarship for service programs. sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) invites exploratory grant applications, hereafter referred to as the Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual learning Hubs or NExT AI Hubs (formerly Learning Disabilities Innovation Hubs), to address the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies on developmental outcomes in children diagnosed with or at risk for developing a specific learning disability (SLD) impacting reading, writing, and mathematics. NExT AI Hubs include a single Research Project and a Leadership Core that support the goals and aims of the Hub. This NOFO seeks to serve as a catalyst to 1) speed the maturation of nascent/novel, high-impact, high-risk research that advances understanding of the role AI technology plays in supporting, improving, or limiting the learning, cognitive, and socio-emotional needs of children at risk for or diagnosed with SLDs, 2) build an evidence base for the SLD community to inform policy or practice, and 3) provide project-embedded, career-enhancing research and professional development opportunities to support the next generation of transdisciplinary SLD scientists. This initiative provides opportunities to support planning and building a body of research and corresponding intellectual infrastructure to enable NExT AI investigators to compete for large research and program project opportunities in the future.This NOFO aims to integrate research topics that are of relevance to various research programs at the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) and align with the NICHD Strategic Plan. The NOFO intends to build cross-programmatic, transdisciplinary and cross-cutting scientific research, and critically nurture the development of early career investigators capable of conducting this research.
sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.title: Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual Learning (NExT AI) Hubs (P20 Clinical Trial Optional)

sig_76efaff15002776a3b58.description: Banedanmark expects to publish the tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnosing railway telecommunications and signalling systems in Spring 2026. To be sure that the process for tender and the contract is aligned with the capabilities of the market, Banedanmark wishes to invite potential vendors for a written market dialogue and verbal hearing regarding the upcoming tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnose railway telecommunications and signalling systems. The purpose of the market dialogue is to get the markets feedback on the scope and if it is aligned with the market regarding the composition of the products/services, the commercial conditions, the price structure, market conditions, risks, and the partnership after having entered the contract etc. In that way Banedanmark will be able to optimize the tender material accordingly to how the market is today before making the tender public. The market dialogue process is the following: Banedanmark has attached an appendix to this document, which Banedanmark request the potential vendors to answer and return via EU-Supply. - Appendix 1 Questionnaire and answers (Potential vendors must fill out this document). The potential vendors must return their answers through EU-Supply not later than 05.12.2025 Depending on the answer’s Banedanmark will have the option to invite potential vendors to a digital meeting via Microsoft Teams. The selection of potential vendors to the meeting will be done through the criteria, to secure a representative of the market, to discuss the answers and possible implications. The topics in Appendix 1 will provide the initial questions for the market dialogue. If the potential vendors are invited for a meeting and find it relevant, they are welcome to send any suggestions for other topics that should be discussed during the market dialogue. The digital meeting will be held, if relevant, 11.12.2025 and 12.12.2025. Banedanmark will, with the invite to the digital meeting, send a Teams link. The duration of the meeting is approx. 1,5 hours (CET+1) in the span of 8-16 Thursday (11.12.2025) and 8-12 Friday (12.12.2025). If the potential vendor suggests meeting times/dates, Banedanmark will try to accommodate those requests.

Framework agreement for the supply of conference, presentation and media technology including the provision of lot-related associated services for the purpose of holding video conferences as part of hybrid committee meetings of municipal call-off authorised entities in Schleswig-Holstein Lot LOT-0001: On-site advice Region North. Region North: District of Nordfriesland, District of Schleswig-Flensburg, City of Flensburg Lot LOT-0002: On-site advice Region Centre. Region Centre: District of Dithmarschen, District of Plön, District of Rendsburg-Eckernförde, District of Steinburg, City of Kiel, City of Neumünster Lot LOT-0003: On-site advice Region South. Region South: District of Ostholstein, District of Segeberg, District of Pinneberg, District of Stormarn, District of Herzogtum-Lauenburg, City of Lübeck Lot LOT-0004: Fixed projection screens. The subject matter of this lot is the delivery, assembly, commissioning and documentation of permanently installed projection screens for municipal meeting rooms (meeting rooms, conference rooms or similar) and service. The services comprise in particular: • On-site measurement • Delivery of the screens including all fastening materials • Dismantling and disposal of old screens (in individual cases) • Assembly and ready-for-operation installation • electrical connection for motor control • Functional testing • Instruction of the client (for retractable screens) • Handover of documentation • Disposal of packaging material Installation is generally carried out in existing buildings during ongoing operation. In individual cases, installation takes place as part of the redesign of a meeting or conference room. Lot LOT-0005: Mobile projection screens. The subject matter of this lot is the delivery of mobile projection screens including transport bags for flexible use in municipal meeting, conference and event rooms. The screens are used for changing locations within municipal properties and must be able to be transported, set up and operated by one person. The delivery includes: • Mobile projection screen • Stand or carrying system • Transport and protective bag • Operating instructions • Warranty certificates • Delivery to the place of performance Lot LOT-0006: Ultra-mobile media and presentation systems. The subject matter of this lot is the delivery of a fully integrated, ultra-mobile media trolley for the implementation of: • Council meetings • Committee meetings • Hybrid committee meetings • Hybrid citizen assemblies Operation is carried out by changing users without special media technology knowledge. The solution must be designed as a compact all-in-one unit and contain all components for image, sound and voice transmission. Lot LOT-0007: Permanently installed ceiling projectors (beamers). The subject matter of this lot is all services for the operational handover of a permanently installed projection system consisting of ceiling projector(s), ceiling mount(s), signal transmission, control technology, cabling and all accessories required for operation including planning, assembly, cabling, configuration, instruction and documentation as well as service. The system is used to display presentations, meeting documents, video conferences, live streams and other media content in council, committee, meeting and conference rooms. Lot LOT-0008: Mobile projectors (beamers). The subject matter of this lot is the delivery, setup and operational handover of mobile projection systems (beamers) including transport accessories, connection cables and all components required for operation as well as service. The devices are used for flexible use in council, committee, meeting, training and event rooms for displaying presentations, meeting documents, video conferences and multimedia content. The projectors must be usable at different locations within the administration without permanent installation. Lot LOT-0009: Smartboards (Interactive All-in-one Collaboration Boards). The subject matter of this lot is the delivery, assembly, commissioning and operational handover of interactive all-in-one collaboration boards with an integrated touch display, whiteboard function, video conferencing technology, loudspeaker system, microphone array and screen sharing as well as service. The systems are used to hold in-person, hybrid and video conferences as well as for the joint processing of documents, presentations and meeting documents. The contractor takes over delivery, assembly, configuration, commissioning, documentation, training and support. Lot LOT-0010: Permanently installed sound reinforcement. The subject matter of this lot is the delivery, assembly, commissioning and calibration of a permanently installed sound reinforcement system for voice transmission in committee, board and meeting rooms as well as service. The system is used to support in-person, hybrid and video conferences and is designed for continuous operation in municipal meeting rooms. The contractor assumes all services required for operational handover including an on-site appointment for inventory assessment, specialist planning, cabling, assembly, configuration, documentation, instruction and service. Lot LOT-0011: Mobile conference speakers. The subject matter of this lot is the delivery of mobile conference speakers (speakerphones/soundbars) for use in meeting, conference and committee rooms as well as service. The devices are used to hold in-person, hybrid and video conferences with multiple participants and must be compatible with common conference platforms. Lot LOT-0012: Conference microphones. The subject matter of this lot is the delivery, setup, commissioning and operational handover of a wireless digital conference microphone system for council, committee, advisory board and committee meetings.

The system consists of member and presiding committee microphone stations including gooseneck microphones, integrated loudspeakers, battery systems, charging infrastructure, control unit, accessories and all components required for operation. The system must be suitable for face-to-face meetings, hybrid meetings, live streams, recordings and connection to video conferencing systems. The contractor shall undertake planning, delivery, configuration, commissioning, instruction, documentation and service. Lot LOT-0013: Handheld microphones with stand. The subject of this lot is the delivery, assembly, commissioning and operational handover of a professional wireless handheld microphone system including microphone stands, charging facilities, radio receivers, accessories and all components required for use. The system is used for speech transmission at council, committee, advisory board, meeting and hybrid events as well as public sessions. The contractor shall undertake all services required for operational handover including delivery, assembly, configuration, frequency planning, acoustic measurement, documentation and instruction as well as service. Lot LOT-0014: PTZ room camera systems. The subject of this lot is the delivery, installation, setup, commissioning and operational handover of professional PTZ room cameras (pan-tilt-zoom) for use in meeting, conference, committee and council halls. The cameras are used for high-quality video capture of sessions, meetings, video conferences, live streams and hybrid events. The contractor shall undertake all services including planning, on-site measurements, delivery, installation, cabling, configuration, commissioning, documentation and instruction as well as service. Lot LOT-0015: Mobile 360-degree conference camera systems. The subject of this lot is the delivery, setup and operational handover of mobile intelligent conference camera systems for council, committee, meeting, training and conference rooms as well as service. The systems must enable comprehensive audio and video capture of in-person participants and be suitable for hybrid meetings and video conferences. The systems shall consist at least of: • Camera system • Microphone array • Loudspeaker system • Power supply unit • Connection cables • Transport accessories (transport bag or transport case) • Required software Lot LOT-0016: Frontal video conference camera systems (videobars). The subject of this lot is the delivery, installation, setup, commissioning and operational handover of frontal video conference camera systems (videobars) for meeting, conference, committee, training and body rooms as well as service. The systems must integrate camera, microphone array and loudspeaker system into a single device and be suitable for hybrid meetings, video conferences, digital collaboration and presentations. The systems are intended in particular for mounting on or beneath interactive displays, smartboards or large screens. The contractor shall undertake delivery, documentation and support. Lot LOT-0017: Accessories for media, presentation and conference technology. The subject of this lot is the delivery, setup and operational handover of accessory components for media, presentation and conference technology as well as service. The components are used for signal transmission, connection of mobile terminal devices, expansion of presentation systems and management of multiple signal sources within meeting, training, conference and body rooms. The contractor shall supply all accessory components including necessary adapters, connecting cables and documentation.

sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.description:
The project comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions in the area of information security to maintain the information network of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin, which is certified based on BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001. The ISO 27001 certification is proof of the Union law eligibility criterion of "security of information systems" of the EU paying agency (Article 1 in conjunction with Annex I point 3 letter B of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2022/127) and requires the regular execution of internal audits and security revisions in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Internal personnel resources and competencies for carrying out internal audits are not available, which is why, in accordance with chapter 8.3, BSI standard 200-1, it has been decided to award the execution of the audits to external experts. The previously awarded project with the same project content expires in the year 2026, which is why a multi-year follow-up project is being awarded to ensure continuous and long-term internal auditing until 2030. The subject matter of the project shall be flexibly retrievable auditing services for the information network of the EU paying agency, which consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which as outsourcing partners or the components outsourced to them, shall represent the essential audit subjects of the audits. Based on an jointly prepared audit schedule, four audits per year are planned. The project is to be awarded to demonstrably experienced experts in the field of information security revision or ISMS auditing in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Lot LOT-0001: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV. The contract subject matter comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions for an information network certified on the basis of BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001 and its participating outsourcing partners. The information network to be audited "Operational running of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin" consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection of the State of Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), which perform the professional tasks of approval, control, disbursement, accounting and administration of arrears of subsidy funds of the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF), the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which are treated as outsourcing partners. The essential audit activities are to be carried out for the outsourced components of the information network at the outsourcing partners. With these institutions, a transfer of paying agency tasks has been agreed on the basis of responsibilities ordinances, transfer ordinances or other regulations. Based on a federal-state interface model for EU paying agencies coordinated with the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI for short), the outsourcing relationships are essentially differentiated into: 1. Organisational interfaces (S-O): Institutions that perform transferred tasks of approval and control within the business processes of the paying agency and use central paying agency specialist applications within the information network to fulfil tasks, as they do not provide central paying agency specialist applications themselves and do not operate any specific application environments. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - 14 approval offices (offices for agriculture) in the districts, - the State Forestry Enterprise (LFB), - the Investment Bank of the State of Brandenburg (ILB). 2. Technical interfaces (S-T): Institutions of the technical operation of the central paying agency specialist applications and systems as well as data storage. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - the central Brandenburg IT service provider (ZIT-BB), - Land Surveying and Basic Geographic Information Brandenburg (LGB) - init AG for the operation of an application procedure. A medium three-digit number of persons work in the information network. Every year, several million euros in a three-digit amount of EU, federal and state funds are administered. The paying agency specialist applications essentially comprise client/server and web applications, for which an IT system landscape consisting of terminal, web, application and database servers is deployed. Use is made by administrative units using virtual clients via the state administration network of the State of Brandenburg. Applicants access the online application systems operated in a demilitarised zone (DMZ) via the internet. In coordination with the client and based on the documentation of the ISMS, the contractor shall draw up and carry out a multi-year audit schedule. The planning and execution of the audits takes place with the participation of the information security officer of the EU paying agency. Based on empirical values, four audits per year are to be carried out with different procedure participants respectively, which should be flexibly retrievable.

Per audit, the workload in person-days (PD) is estimated at approx. 10 PD. The contract subject matter comprises the audits for the years 2027 up to and including 2030. The client reserves the right, with the award of optional services, if contractor capacities are available, to commission further audits in accordance with the schedule of services for the year 2026. Accordingly, the following scope of work is expected - 2026: 2 audits - 20 PD (optional, upon availability) - 2027: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2028: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2029: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2030: 4 audits - 40 PD - Total: 18 audits - 180 PD The execution of the audits should take place along the relevant standards for audits and security revisions according to the BSI IT-Grundschutz methodology (BSI auditing scheme or the guideline for IS revisions based on IT-Grundschutz). The client reserves the right to optionally commission the contractor in the year 2026 with up to two (2) further audits for two (2) audit subjects in accordance with the schedule of services.
sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.title: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV

sig_78c5b72c81dbabda0bf0.description: Industrial biotechnology offers enormous potential for sustainable growth by replacing fossil raw materials with renewable biological resources, achieving climate targets and strengthening competitiveness. Germany is well positioned in the research and development of bioeconomic products and processes. Previous funding measures by other departments and the federal states show that bioeconomic products and processes can be implemented on a laboratory scale. However, there is a lack of broad implementation of bioeconomic products and processes on an industrial scale. Therefore, to support the transformation of the economy into a sustainable, climate-neutral economic model, the funding programme "Industrial Bioeconomy" was initiated, which started with the entry into force of the "Directive for funding the use and construction of demonstration plants for industrial biotechnology" of 16 December 2020 on 29 December 2020 (BAnz AT 28.12.2020 B2). This funding guideline was superseded by the "Funding guideline for the establishment of an industrial bioeconomy through the further development and scaling of bio-based processes and the establishment of regional innovation clusters" (BAnz AT 27.09.2024 B1), published in the Federal Law Gazette on 27 September 2024. The aim of the programme is to unlock the potential of new bio-based processes for industry and to transfer sustainable products into broad application. In order to reduce the economic and technical risks of development and market launch, the funding is intended to demonstrate the potential of bio-based products and processes at an early stage. Projects are funded that have a high potential for industrial application, the creation of new value creation and new jobs, strengthen the market position of the participating companies and make a relevant contribution to sustainability. sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.description: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) seeks to advance its mission by supporting multidisciplinary, consortium-based research using precision systems biology approaches to uncover links among chronic illnesses, infectious diseases and microbiomes. There is an urgent scientific and clinical need to understand the pathways by which infections lead to chronic lifelong health issues or alternatively, how long-term illnesses might predispose or exacerbate acute infections. The objective is to harness cutting-edge technologies along with longitudinal patient cohorts and biobank data for comprehensive analysis of genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors leading to advances in prevention and treatment strategies for both chronic and infectious diseases. The cutting-edge technologies may include multi-omics, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, organoid-based validation systems, and integration of real-world data, alongside improved access to digital health records and advanced clinical informatics tools. The goal is to generate meaningful insights into disease progression and host-pathogen interactions. Grant authorities that allow NIAID to forecast this opportunity are as follows: Sections 301 and 405 of the Public Health Service Act as amended (42 USC 241 and 284) and under Federal Regulations 42 CFR Part 52 and 2 CFR Part 200.
sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.title: Precision and Systems Biology to Uncover the Link Between Chronic and Infectious Diseases

sig_7922b435cef825e3fe8f.description: This is a request for information, which is not a prior information notice, a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to survey the market and collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for a future tendering process. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in the tendering process. To ensure the success of the future tendering process, it is important that tenderers provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. This request for information is used to clarify the supply available on the market regarding substitute management systems and suppliers. A substitute management system enables a single centralised service channel for the sudden substitute needs of professionals. With the help of a substitute management system, we want to streamline substitute management processes. The need is to find a modern and user-friendly, off-the-shelf SaaS system intended for the management and coordination of substitutes, as well as for the notification and booking of temporary work shifts. In addition, we want to improve and modernise the user experience of our substitute management systems so that the applicant experience and communication are improved. The systems must be integrable via standard interfaces with, among other things, the client organisation's user information and access rights management service. The objectives of the services are equal accessibility, timeliness and continuity. The goal of the procurement is to move from heavy services to proactive and preventive services, whereby the effectiveness of the services can be improved. We offer system solutions to our clients in the social and health care sector as well as the municipal sector. The scope of the future procurement, the procurement method and the parties will be specified as the preparation of the call for tenders progresses. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The goal of the procurement is to find a system: - that is an easy-to-use, off-the-shelf SaaS solution - that can be integrated into the client organisation's AD and reporting environment via open interfaces - that is information secure and takes data protection into account - whose supplier has a clear implementation model that includes extensive documentation and guidance for the client and contracting organisation - that can be used on mobile devices and via a browser. In addition to the system procurement, the procurement includes connection interfaces to other systems, licences, a delivery project, maintenance and support for off-the-shelf software, as well as other separately ordered expert services, for example, the planning and implementation of system change and development needs and development projects. The solution must scale to the organisational structures of social and health service organisations and the municipal sector. The implementation of the solution must be based on generally used standards and system-independent interfaces. The solution to be procured must function as part of the existing technical and functional environment. The solution includes at least two separate environments in terms of its functions; production and test/training environments, which are identical in their basic structure. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT The following are descriptions of the operating environments of the organisations related to the request for information, which are requested to be used in describing the functionality and pricing model. Users of the data transmission system are, for example, users from wellbeing services counties and municipal organisations. Users of the information systems are also stakeholders and external users. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The request for information must be answered by 25.9.2025 at 12:00. Responding takes place by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. Please head your message as follows: "Markkinavuoropuhelu: Sijaisvälitysjärjestelmä" (Market dialogue: Substitute management system). Responses to the Questions attachment of the request for information must also be submitted with the response. You may also attach, for example, brochures to the response. Based on the responses received, Istekki Oy will select 3–5 suppliers to present their solutions in one-hour Teams meetings. The meeting between the selected respondent, Istekki and the representatives of the clients will be recorded. The information provided at the request for information stage will be treated as confidential. Please indicate in your request for information response which of the times below suit you best: Mon 29.9. at 10 – 11 Mon 29.9. at 13 – 14 Mon 29.9. at 14 – 15 Tue 30.9. at 11 – 12 Tue 30.9. at 12 – 13 Tue 30.9. at 13 – 14 The times will be confirmed supplier-specifically after the response time for the request for information. The tendering service automatically creates deadlines for submitting questions and responding to the request for information. Instead of these deadlines, the deadlines in the request for information document shall be followed.

sig_7a64ef18d7dd087476c3.description: The subject of the contract is the temporary provision of the IdentityManager standard software with the specified modules. This includes: - Right to use the functions of the applications, including the specified modules for individual users in accordance with the total quantity defined further below - Costs incurred by the operation of the software at the manufacturer's site, under the requirement that the software, together with the specified modules and including all data storage, must run on systems that are protected within the EU by the requirements of the GDPR - Costs incurred by the operation of the software at the manufacturer's site, under the requirement that a dedicated, separate virtual/logical infrastructure is used by the manufacturer for the execution of the software, which ensures a strict separation of the software instance used by the ILB, including data storage, from other customers who use the same functions at the manufacturer's site. - Standard support from the product manufacturer - Right to use various connectors within the timeframe acquired by the right to use the software. - Separate instances for productive systems ("production instance") as well as development and test systems ("test instance") Further information on the nature and functionality of the software in question can be found in Part B, Service Description. One Identity Manager from OneIdentity Base Engine: One Identity Manager is a market-leading standard software for Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), which centrally controls user accounts, access rights and the associated risks in complex IT landscapes. The software enables seamless, transparent and audit-proof management of identities across on-premises, hybrid and cloud environments. One Identity Safeguard PASM: The core module secures the entire lifecycle of privileged access credentials; passwords and SSH keys are stored in a hardened vault (appliance or SaaS) and rotated automatically. Access credentials are released exclusively via a policy-based workflow with optional approval levels (e.g. four-eyes principle, time-limited access). In addition, this module acts as a proxy and records all administrative sessions (e.g. via RDP and SSH) without gaps. The recordings include video, keystrokes and metadata. The entire data traffic is monitored in real time, with predefined rules enabling the immediate blocking of suspicious or unwanted actions. This ensures complete, audit-proof traceability. Connectors: Licences must be offered for the items in Chapter 1.1 - Application list for interface integration. Note: a different, varying duration is required for each connector here.
sig_7a64ef18d7dd087476c3.title: Provision of IdentityManager standard software with the One Identity Safeguard PASM module and connectors

The assignment comprises the provision of system support for the management of wellness allowances for monthly-paid employees and an option for hourly-paid employees (hereinafter referred to as the Service). The Service shall support the entire process for managing wellness allowances and function as a digital tool for both employees and administrators at the Municipality. The assignment includes a comprehensive commitment for the Service, which encompasses the system support that forms part of the Service as well as associated services required for the Service to be introduced, used and function over time. The Service also comprises the following options: Option 1 Management of wellness allowances for hourly-paid employees. Price for Option 1 is included in the evaluation of bids. The tenderer shall state the price for Option 1 in the Price Schedule Appendix. If such price is not stated, the bid may be rejected. The Municipality has the right, but not the obligation, to exercise this option during the contract period. Option 2 Administering the management of expense receipts and supporting the disbursement of reimbursement from the Municipality to the employee for purchases of wellness services from wellness suppliers affiliated with the Service. (voluntary) Price for Option 2 is not included in the evaluation of bids. The Municipality has the right, but not the obligation, to exercise this option during the contract period. If the Supplier can provide this functionality, the price for Option 2 shall be submitted in the Price Schedule Appendix. Option 3 Benefit bicycles (voluntary) The option concerns the Supplier being able to offer support through the Service for the administration and management of benefit bicycles for the Municipality's employees for private use. The solution may be provided through a third-party supplier affiliated with the Service. The Municipality has not currently made a decision on the introduction of benefit bicycles and no requirements regarding such functionality are therefore set within the framework of this procurement. The option is not covered by the evaluation and the Tenderer shall therefore not submit any price for the option. The Municipality decides unilaterally if, when and to what extent the option is to be utilised during the contract period. The Municipality reserves the right to refrain from utilising the option and to, in whole or in part, procure a corresponding service or functionality through a separate procurement. sig_7c81fa0efc36e2e2f76b.description: The ekom21 - Kommunales Gebietsrechenzentrum Hessen (hereinafter: ekom21) is a body governed by public law pursuant to the Hessian Data Processing Association Act (DV-VerbundG). It is the central IT service provider for Hessian municipalities and their institutions. From locations in Giessen, Darmstadt, Kassel and Fulda, it comprehensively supplies its end customers with modern information and communication services (ICT) of all kinds. The approximately 500 members in Hesse and other customers nationwide include approx. 29.000 end users from local authorities and other public institutions, such as districts, cities, municipalities, municipal eigenbetriebs, special-purpose associations, institutions, hospitals and residential homes. In the governmental sector, ekom21 serves numerous state associations, ministries and regional administrative offices. In total, ekom21 thus provides services for six million citizens. The range of tasks of ekom21 is growing and changing continuously, which goes hand in hand with a steady expansion of the customer base. In order to accommodate the requests of our customers for a data protection management system (DPMS), a corresponding partner must be commissioned. For this reason, ekom21 is tendering a DPMS for its customers. Primarily, a cloud-based data protection management system (SaaS) is to be procured that supports, documents and controls all processing activities pursuant to Art. 5 30 General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) as well as the Hessian Data Protection and Freedom of Information Act (HDSIG). The aim is to reduce the effort for risk and impact assessments, the register of processing activities (RoPA), data subject requests, contract and sales management as well as audit evidence, while simultaneously increasing compliance quality. Lot LOT-0000: Data protection management system. The procurement procedure aims at the conclusion of a framework agreement with an economic operator. The framework agreement is intended - without establishing an obligation to purchase - to enable the demand-driven provision, introduction and long-term support of a "data protection management system" as well as associated services for customers of ekom21. The maximum value of the framework agreement amounts to 1.000.000,00 million € (net). Further details can be found in the procurement documents.
sig_7c81fa0efc36e2e2f76b.title: Data protection management system

sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.description: The NSF State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program aims to expand access to the compute required for AI-enabled scientific discovery and to transform the research, education, and training opportunities offered by institutions of higher education. AI Infrastructure Hubs will connect researchers to new compute infrastructure that leverages contributions from state governments, research institutions, industry, and philanthropy, accelerating AI-enabled discovery across science and engineering and developing a skilled technical workforce for AI use in the scientific enterprise. The program responds to a core tenet of Science: A New Golden Age to renew America’s research and development (R&D) for changes in today’s scientific enterprise, including the role of AI in laying the foundation for a new era of scientific discovery and the growing role of industry and philanthropy in funding R&D. In response, the Administration’s FY28 R&D Priorities Memorandum called for investing in AI for science as a national mission and expanding the scale of, and flexible access to, advanced compute and data infrastructure that researchers now require for frontier scientific discovery. Each AI Infrastructure Hub will be organized as a flexible state or regional consortium of state and local governments, research institutions, philanthropies, and the private sector. Consortia will be responsible for all funding for new or expanded computing, data, and AI resources, whether on-premises or cloud-based. NSF will fund each Hub’s consortium coordination, AI infrastructure workforce development, and faculty training and coursework development in leveraging AI for science.
sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.title: U.S. National Science Foundation State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs:

sig_7dc5517446b4836f18dd.description: Work package "UDP Migration Support" as part of the Urban Data Management (UDM) project In September 2024, the implementation phase began in the project "Establishment of Urban Data Platform (UDP) and Migration of Geographic Information System (GIS)". The Federal City of Bonn is relying on the open source project Civitas Core for the establishment of the UDP. With the Universal Urban Data App addon, the basics are in place that allow applications from the old GIS to be migrated to the UDP. In the conception phase of the project, approx. 300 applications to be migrated were identified. 80 percent of these applications support the enforcement of statutory services. Since the previous GIS can no longer be operated, the migration must be completed as quickly as possible. A valid estimate determines a total effort of 5197 person-days (PD) here. This effort will mainly be provided by internal employees in the 3 areas of requirement clarification, development and support. Support services amounting to roughly 650 PD up to the year 2028 are to be procured in the tender. Due to advancing support by AI, the contracting authority assumes that the migration duration can be decisively reduced. The focus of the procurement is on support services to be provided using the existing platform tools of the UDP. The migration is to be provided in accordance with the respective trades' existing Bonn guidelines such as data modelling, Geoserver configuration, Universal Urban Data Addon configuration, Masterportal configuration. Independent development work on the tools of the platform itself is not planned within the scope of the contract, or only to a very small extent and after prior consultation.
sig_7dc5517446b4836f18dd.title: Federal City of Bonn, work package "UDP Migration Support" as part of the Urban Data Management (UDM) project

sig_8227979e95ca042cc209.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) invites a single cooperative agreement application for the Resource Center for the Cardiovascular Repository for Type 1 Diabetes (CaRe-T1D). The purpose of CaRe-T1D is to support innovative, discovery and mechanistic research through the study of human cardiovascular (CV) tissue. This research seeks to better understand cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 1 diabetes, highlight differences compared to type 2 diabetes, and ultimately guide the development of therapies to treat this major cause of morbidity and mortality for individuals with type 1 diabetes. To achieve these goals, the Resource Center will expand the CaRe-T1D biorepository of human CV tissue, further develop the data commons for data sharing and for artificial intelligence (AI) tools, coordinate the research activities of the investigative teams in the CaRe-T1D consortium, and make CaRe-T1D resources accessible to the broader research community. This NOFO is associated with the Special Diabetes Program (https://www.niddk.nih.gov/about-niddk/research-areas/diabetes/type-1-diabetes-special-statutory-funding-program/about-special-diabetes-program) which funds research on the prevention, treatment, and cure of type 1 diabetes and its complications, including unique, innovative, and collaborative research consortia and clinical trials networks.This is a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for a Single Source that will invite application(s) from eligible organization(s) to apply. Please see Section III. Eligibility for additional information. In accordance with NIH standard peer-review processes, the application(s) will be peer-reviewed, and only meritorious application(s) will be considered for funding.
sig_8227979e95ca042cc209.title: Single Source Competition: Continuation of the Cardiovascular Repository for Type 1 Diabetes (CaRe-T1D) - Resource Center (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_85675749643cdece19fd.description: Smart Applications Management Limited (SAM) is the trading name of South West Smart Applications Limited, a Membership based central purchasing body, which owns and runs the National Mobilities Procurement Hub for its Members. The Goods and Services will be supplied via Award Without Competition and by Competitive Selection Process. Lot 1 of this Framework is seeking the provision of On Vehicle Digital Technology (AVL, CCTV, APC, TLP, Comms, On Bus Destination, AVA, Bridge Strike Systems & Vehicle Compute Capability). Lot 1 - has 9 parts: Lot 1 - Part 1 - Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) Solution Provision of an integrated Automated Vehicle Location solution capable of accurately determining and communicating vehicle location in real time. The solution shall support route, journey and stop association, estimated arrival/departure information and integration with other onboard and back-office systems. Requirements include resilient positioning, industry-standard data interfaces, remote configuration, monitoring, diagnostics, reporting, security and ongoing support throughout the solution lifecycle. Lot 1 - Part 2 - Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Solution Provision of a comprehensive onboard CCTV solution providing appropriate internal and external vehicle coverage for passenger safety, operational management and incident investigation. The solution shall support continuous high-quality recording, secure storage and retrieval, authorised access and evidential integrity. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, equipment health monitoring, remote diagnostics, secure communications, configurable camera arrangements and enhanced analytics where required. Lot 1 - Part 3 - Automatic Passenger Counting (APC) Solution Provision of an Automatic Passenger Counting solution capable of accurately recording passenger boarding and alighting and determining vehicle occupancy without driver intervention. The solution shall provide reliable passenger-count data for operational, planning and passenger-information purposes and integrate with onboard and central systems. Requirements include appropriate counting accuracy, standardised interfaces, secure data transfer, reporting, monitoring, diagnostics, remote management and resilient operation. Lot 1 - Part 4 - Traffic Light Priority (TLP) Solution Provision of a Traffic Light Priority solution enabling suitably equipped vehicles to request priority at traffic signals based on vehicle location, route and operational circumstances. The solution shall support configurable and conditional priority strategies and integration with vehicle, roadside and central systems. Requirements include secure, low-latency communications, monitoring and reporting, remote configuration, interoperability, performance analysis, testing, cybersecurity and ongoing technical support. Lot 1 - Part 5 - Comms Tool (Radio) Solution Provision of an onboard communications solution enabling reliable and secure voice and data communication between drivers, vehicles and operational control functions. The solution shall support operational messaging, service information, alerts and emergency communications through an appropriate driver interface. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, secure communications, operational logging, remote configuration, equipment monitoring, diagnostics and resilient operation across the vehicle fleet. Lot 1 - Part 6 - On-Bus Destination Solution Provision of integrated on-bus destination equipment capable of clearly displaying route and destination information to passengers and intending passengers. Solutions shall support appropriate front, side and rear displays, accessibility and visibility requirements and integration with onboard systems to automate displayed information. Requirements include remote configuration, operational overrides, equipment monitoring, diagnostics, secure communications, robust vehicle-grade equipment and ongoing maintenance and support. Lot 1 - Part 7 - Audio Visual Passenger Information (AVA) Solution Provision of an accessible onboard Audio Visual Passenger Information solution delivering automated visual and audible information concerning routes, destinations, next stops, disruptions and other relevant passenger messages. The solution shall integrate with vehicle location and onboard systems to trigger information accurately. Requirements include accessible presentation, remote and priority messaging, configurable content, secure communications, monitoring, diagnostics, resilient operation and ongoing system support. Lot 1 - Part 8 - Bridge Strike Prevention Solution Provision of an onboard Bridge Strike Prevention solution designed to reduce the risk of vehicles approaching or striking structures with insufficient clearance. The solution shall use vehicle dimensions together with accurate location, mapping and detection information to provide timely audible and visual driver warnings. Requirements include reliable hazard identification, minimisation of false alerts, offline resilience, secure updates, event logging, diagnostics and onboard-system integration. Lot 1 - Part 9 - Vehicle Compute Capability (VCC) Solution Provision of a robust onboard Vehicle Compute Capability providing a shared computing platform for hosting, integrating and managing multiple vehicle applications and data services. The solution shall provide sufficient processing capacity, storage and future scalability while supporting secure application separation and interoperability. Requirements include edge processing, secure communications, remote software management, monitoring and diagnostics, onboard-system integration and future expansion throughout its operational lifecycle. Lot 2 is for Franchising and Wider Transport Ticketing & Payment Consultancy Services. It has 6 Parts: Lot 2 - Part 1 - Franchised Bus Scheme Development and Implementation Support The provision of specialist consultancy services to support the development, assessment and implementation of bus franchising schemes. Services may include business cases, network and commercial design, financial modelling, consultation, procurement, mobilisation, integrated fares and ticketing, assets and technology, contract management, service permits, independent assurance and stakeholder engagement. Lot 2 - Part 2 - Transport Ticketing Management Policy Advice The provision of strategic, policy and management consultancy relating to transport ticketing and payment systems. Services may encompass ITSO, Stored Value, contactless EMV, barcode and QR ticketing, Account Based and Multi-Token Ticketing, Mobility as a Service, and wider ticketing initiatives across public-sector authorities, transport operators and national organisations. Lot 2 - Part 3 - Transport Ticketing Technical & Revenue Scheme Delivery The provision of technical consultancy and delivery support for transport ticketing schemes, including development of technical specifications, implementation and integration of ITSO and other ticketing technologies, Electronic Ticket Machines and ticketing readers. Services may also include management of multi-platform implementations and development of technical solutions through engagement with relevant stakeholders. Lot 2 - Part 4 - Transport Ticketing Governance, Research and Competitive Bidding Services The provision of specialist support relating to transport ticketing governance, research, procurement and competitive funding or bidding activities. Services may include governance advice for public and commercial organisations, preparation of grant, tender and franchise submissions, support for public procurement exercises, and research activities contributing to sustainable transport policy and delivery. Lot 2 - Part 5 - Entitlement (Concessionary) Travel Management Services The provision of management, policy and project support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, with particular emphasis on revenue reimbursement and apportionment. Services may include multi-operator and multimodal schemes, multiple ITSO HOPS and Customer Management Systems, and schemes operating across multiple ticketing channels, technologies and participating organisations. Lot 2 - Part 6 - Technical Entitlement (Concessionary) Support Services The provision of specialist technical support for entitlement and concessionary travel schemes, including reimbursement implementation, revenue modelling and apportionment, ETM data analysis, national reimbursement guidance and alternative allocation methodologies. Services may also encompass auditable datasets, payment reporting, stakeholder-led revenue solutions and expert technical evidence supporting appeals, tribunals or legal proceedings. sig_85bec1a283e55de29bb2.description: Vantaan kaupunki is planning the procurement of a new cultural heritage system to replace the current collection management system (Kirsti), which was implemented in 2014. The current system is technically obsolete, slow, and difficult to develop. The goal is a modern, easy-to-use, and efficient solution that supports museum operations, cultural heritage management, and digital transition. The system must support, among other things, object, image, AV, paper, and cultural environment archives, a reference library, actor information, and press clippings. Integrations are required for Finna, Finto, MapInfo, Matti, the Finnish Heritage Agency's spatial data, and the PAS service. Key features: efficient search, clarity, ease of use, and compliance with GDPR requirements. Users: Museum staff, consultants, authorities, collection service customers, and the public via Finna. Targeted benefits: Better availability of information, increased work efficiency, reduction of unnecessary work, and improvement of processes. Strategic importance: supports the digital transition, has a broad impact, and generates value for over 10 000 residents.
sig_85bec1a283e55de29bb2.title: Procurement of a cultural heritage system

sig_86162daacf1775ecac5d.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of solution expert in Project P1160 'Critical Upgrade of ERP' and DRIV. The consultant shall take care of the role within the discipline SAP Defense and Security (D&S). The role can involve cooperation with other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.
sig_86162daacf1775ecac5d.title: Procurement of a SAP Defence and Security Solution Expert

sig_8619e337dca715e1a15c.description: The subject of the procurement is an appointment booking and video conferencing system (hereinafter also the "System") for use by the City of Mikkeli's customer services. The System to be procured must enable the management of customer service appointments for the City of Mikkeli's employment services and customer meetings via video conferencing through a single system. The objective is to procure a SaaS ready-made solution that is easy to use, meets data protection and other legislative requirements, and can be implemented on a rapid schedule. The procurement seeks a comprehensive appointment booking and video conferencing system as a ready-made solution that offers pre-built functions for managing appointments and conducting video conferences. A ready-made solution refers to a finished end product that can be configured for the Subscriber's use without the procurement involving the development of a completely bespoke system. In the initial phase, the System will be for the use of the City of Mikkeli's employment services. Later, the City of Mikkeli must have the option to expand the use of the System to other units. The procurement seeks one (1) party with overall responsibility to supply the System as a SaaS service. The overall service must include the necessary software interfaces, programs, firmware, licences, and maintenance and support services in accordance with the call for tenders and its appendices. The contract period is estimated to begin in November 2026 and the contract is valid until further notice.
sig_8619e337dca715e1a15c.title: Booking and video conferencing system as off-the-shelf software, City of Mikkeli

sig_86a204079f2c82c65933.description:
WISTA stands for Wissenschafts- und Wirtschaftsstandort Adlershof and is a state-of-the-art technology park in the Adlershof district of Berlin (Treptow-Köpenick borough). It is considered one of the most advanced high-tech parks in Europe and is a central hub for science, business, and start-ups. WISTA Adlershof is a location with an area of approx. 4,2 km2, approx. 1.300 companies, research institutions, and university institutes with 28.000 employees. The WISTA Management GmbH acts as a site developer, service provider, and economic promoter. It supports companies, research institutions, and start-ups at the site and fosters innovation and growth in the region. In addition to its real estate portfolio, WISTA possesses its own campus network, which consists of a high-performance cable network as well as a 5G infrastructure. The network has been continuously expanded and technologically developed since 1998 – from classic telephony and data services to Gigabit and 10G connections, cloud and UCC integration, campus-wide Wi-Fi and IoT applications, through to local 5G and current network 4.0 topics. It thus forms an essential digital infrastructure of the campus and is the subject of the expression of interest procedure. The attractiveness of the campus network stems from its established telecommunications infrastructure at a dynamically growing high-tech location. The network has an existing customer base, established line routes and network nodes, as well as redundant carrier connections. Additional development prospects arise from the continuous expansion of the campus through new buildings, the expansion potential for cloud, security, and UCC services, as well as the addition of a local 5G campus network. The campus network thus offers a resilient infrastructural foundation with further economic and technological growth potential. The reasons for the sale by WISTA are a strategic further development of the campus network by a specialised provider with qualified personnel and the necessary expertise. Subject of sale: Passive infrastructure (fibre optic, copper, conduits, manholes, cable distribution cabinets, building connections) Active infrastructure (switches, routers, servers, telecommunications system) Customer contracts (insofar as transferable, consent/transfers still to be checked) Frequency allocation 5G (not alienable, subsequent use/transfer still to be checked from a regulatory perspective, application for own allocation required) Land/line rights (insofar as transferable, easements/permissions still to be checked) Software/licences (insofar as transferable, licence terms still to be checked) Cable network: The WISTA campus network at the science and business location Adlershof forms the central communication infrastructure for voice and data services in the core area of the technology park. It currently serves around 400 customers as well as approx. 4.400 participants in the voice sector and is therefore an essential location factor for Germany's largest science and technology park. The existing infrastructure includes a high-performance cable duct system, a line network based on copper and fibre optics with a total length of almost 20 kilometres, as well as a Gigabit Ethernet backbone. Technically, fibre optic backbone connections, single-mode and multi-mode fibre optic cables, copper cables, copper cross-cables, and FM cables with 100 double cores are used in particular. At the active network and services level, the campus network includes transmission and switching equipment for voice and data communication, routing/switching components, data core and access areas, network gateways to wide area networks, as well as a communication network consisting of communication systems from the manufacturer Unify. The users' existing voice and data infrastructure is connected to the network; some users are connected via LAN ports under 100 Mbit/s or VDSL, while other users have connections from 100 Mbit/s. The WAN connection is designed to be redundant with at least two external carriers and has two redundant gateways with 100 Gbit/s. The campus network is particularly interesting as an established, operator-capable infrastructure with an existing customer base, available line routes, documented network gateways, and development potential. The future operator is to operate, maintain, further develop, and actively market the network to users on their own responsibility. In addition to the existing copper, fibre optic, and fibre infrastructure, the existing customers, the available telecommunications and data network components, the expansion potential at the growing Adlershof location, and the possibility of introducing new cloud, security, VoIP, and UCC services are of value. 5G network: The WISTA 5G campus network is designed as a local private 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof. It serves as a supplement to the existing cable infrastructure and is to be gradually expanded at outdoor and indoor locations. Initial expansion has been carried out in the area of Albert-Einstein-Straße 16 (central outdoor location) as well as in the showroom/a:head context (indoor location). The regulatory basis for the 5G infrastructure is a local frequency allocation by the Federal Network Agency for the frequency range 3.700–3.800 MHz. The allocation holder is WISTA Management GmbH. The allocated bandwidth is 100 MHz; the frequency allocation is limited until 20.02.2030. The allocation area covers an area of approx. 0,873273 km2. Technologically, the 5G infrastructure is based on a Nokia DAC/NDAC Medium+ environment with 5G standalone architecture, Edge Core, NDAC manager, Nokia AirScale components, HPE Edge servers, router and switching components, and SIM kit. WISTA Management GmbH intends to sell its cable network and 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof.

Only 99 years were stated as the duration because the announcement platform mandates the specification of a limited period. The sale is permanent and is not intended to be reversed after 99 years.
sig_86a204079f2c82c65933.title: Sale of campus network

sig_88fe649111a131b35915.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The aim of the tender is to provide a future-proof and demand-oriented expandable central backup solution that enables reliable backup as well as fast and reliable recovery of the business-critical and medically relevant data and IT systems arising at Magdeburg University Hospital. The solution to be procured must take into account the requirements for secure, highly available and permanently available operation in a KRITIS-relevant environment and thus make a significant contribution to the operational safety, fail-safe operation and resilience of the IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. The overall solution to be procured is to consist of four coordinated system components: • a high-performance all-flash backup appliance for processing large amounts of data and a high number of parallel backup and restore processes, • a highly available backup storage system as the primary backup target with integrated deduplication function, • a high-performance enterprise rack server as a Veeam backup server as well as • two appropriately dimensioned enterprise rack servers as Veeam backup proxies. The backup infrastructure is to be designed in such a way that it takes into account the existing and foreseeable future requirements of Magdeburg University Hospital. In addition to the delivery of the required hardware and software, including all components and licences required for intended operation, the scope of services also includes the professional installation, configuration and integration of the overall solution into the existing IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. Furthermore, the scope of services includes the commissioning of the overall solution as well as the execution of the required functional, performance and acceptance tests. The contractor must provide a fully functional and ready-for-operation overall solution that complies with the requirements laid down in the specification of services and the schedule of services. All services are to be provided in compliance with the legal, regulatory and technical requirements applicable at the time of service provision as well as the relevant norms and standards. Lot LOT-0000: Central backup system. Procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The specific functional requirements result from the schedule of services.
