sig_89acec772031c0972bea.description: The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable specialist application for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin NUM GmbH (NUM). The scope of services comprises in particular software provision, hosting, and technical operation by the contractor, setup and customising, data migration, interfaces, and exports including system-neutral transfer to the financial software selected at a later date, a documented API, support, maintenance, training, and documentation. The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable software solution for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin GmbH (NUM). The solution must digitally map the funding processes from application through review, approval, contract creation, payment request, and interim and final reports. NUM is in an organisational transition phase. Previous processes are partially connected to existing structures of Charité, external project management agency processes, SharePoint or file shares, Excel tables, PDF documents, and easyOnline/XML data. In future, the office is to establish its own structures for processing, reviewing, and documenting funding processes. The software must support both administrative processing and review (currently the Administration, Finance, and Controlling team) and specialist processing and review (currently the Science Management team). The respective reviews take place in parallel, sequentially, or consecutively depending on the process. Input masks, checklists, review notes, task lists, and status logic must therefore be able to traceably depict both review perspectives. The software does not execute the actual payment order, bank execution, or direct retrieval from the Federal Treasury. However, it must provide the data required for forwarding the funds in a structured and system-independent manner. Since the client's financial software will only be selected after this procurement, the technical transfer must be possible via at least a documented, configurable exchange format. The concrete target format and field assignment will be agreed upon in the implementation project after the financial software is selected. The actual retrieval of financial funds from the Federal Treasury and the bank execution take place outside the software. The provision of the retrieval data package and the technical implementation of the agreed data exchange are part of the scope of services. The subject of the tender is an integrated specialist application for funding management with which administrative and specialist review, processing, and decision-making processes can be fully digitally mapped. Document management is a central component of this specialist application and must ensure the process-related linking, structured storage, versioning, management, and retrievability of documents. What is being sought is therefore neither a pure document repository nor an isolated form system, but an end-to-end funding management solution. Insofar as products, procedures, or manufacturers are named in this specification of services, this is done exclusively to describe the required scope of services; equivalent solutions are permitted. Existing target systems of the client determined before publication, or those determined prior to publication, are clearly named in the procurement documents, including the required integration scope.

sig_8a2ff45572d92c9c256c.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject matter of the market dialogue is the expert services in information security and data protection under preparation as well as the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security for the needs of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Väylävirasto is putting out to tender the following two expert service procurements: Expert services in information security and data protection This tender procures experts to support the safeguarding and development of information and cyber security, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto has several different administrative or technical projects and undertakings underway in which operations are developed and existing information systems are renewed or new ones are ordered. What all these projects and undertakings have in common is that they must implement information security and the fulfilment of central government information security requirements in a manner suitable for the organisation. The subject matter of the procurement is information and cybersecurity consulting and auditing services. The work takes place largely in a multi-supplier environment, but also as internal consulting for individual projects or undertakings. Information security audits are also carried out regularly in the supplier environment. In addition, an assessment is made of, among other things, the impact of information security instructions directed at central government on the projects and operations of Väylävirasto. In addition to the office environment, the subject matter of the procurement is the infrastructures managed by Väylävirasto (Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency), i.e. state-owned road, rail and waterways. Each transport mode has its own cyber security development needs, which in certain respects may differ significantly from each other. The aim of the procurement is to obtain a partner for Väylävirasto with which the organisation's and the various transport modes' information and cybersecurity development can be carried out. Assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security This tender procures conformity assessment body services to support the safeguarding of the information and cybersecurity, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Within the scope of this contract, conformity assessment bodies will produce assessment services in the role of an information security conformity assessment body approved by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency (Traficom). When offering and producing assessment services, the information security conformity assessment bodies must comply with the current legislation, official regulations, recommendations, guidelines and other obligations directed at conformity assessment bodies by the authorities concerning conformity assessment body activities. Particular attention must be paid to the instruction issued to conformity assessment bodies by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency for information security conformity assessment bodies 210/2016 O. During the course of the dialogue, the contracting entity will separately assess the need for a market dialogue regarding the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security. The following dynamic purchasing systems (DPS) of Hansel Oy will be used as the procurement procedure for both tenders: Expert services in cyber security and data protection 2025 Assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security 2021–2028 Hansel Oy's dynamic purchasing systems are open to all, and all companies meeting the suitability requirements may join them. sig_8b4bf10de5e76b471c05.description: South Lanarkshire Council seeks a Creative Consultancy to deliver a Market Assessment, Branding Strategy, Website Development, Content Library and Wayfinding Strategy for the Douglas Valley Outdoor Recreation and Adventure Tourism initiative within the Hagshaw Energy Cluster. 1. Market Assessment Review existing project documentation and identify implications for branding, marketing and website development. Analyse visitor data, market trends and audience segmentation, including visitor case studies. Benchmark comparable projects and destinations. Provide recommendations to inform branding, website design, content and future marketing activity. 2. Branding Development Develop and consult on three branding concepts before producing a final identity. Create brand assets including logo, name, tagline, colours, fonts and digital/print applications. Produce brand guidelines covering signage, interpretation, promotional materials and integration with existing site branding. Include recommendations for social media and future marketing activity. 3. Website Design, Build and Launch Create a branded website promoting Douglas Valley as a destination to live, work, visit and enjoy, supporting ambitions to attract up to 100,000 annual visits by 2036. Develop a scalable, content-led website with a planned lifespan of ten years. Include six core pages: Home, About, Explore, See & Stay, News and Contact. The Explore section will feature an interactive map highlighting key recreational and active travel routes, points of interest and route information including distance, elevation, difficulty and duration. Build the site on an accessible CMS suitable for community and council users. Host on a secure UK-based platform with maintenance and support arrangements. Ensure accessibility compliance and provide flexible management of route information and temporary diversions. 4. Photography and Video Library Establish a copyright-cleared library of photography and short-form video content for web, social media and print use. Source content through community engagement, youth-focused workshops and professional photography where required. Content will reflect identified visitor segments and feature strong people-focused imagery. Coverage will include renewable energy, local communities, nature, heritage and identity, local economy and outdoor recreation. Key locations include Coalburn, Douglas, Glenbuck, Glespin, Lesmahagow, Mainshill, Muirkirk, Poneil, Rigside, Douglas Water and Spireslack, alongside significant natural, heritage and recreation assets. 5. Wayfinding Strategy and Design Guidance Develop a first-phase wayfinding strategy focused on Coalburn, Douglas, Glespin, Douglasdale Community Woodland and connecting active travel routes. Establish a hierarchy of signage including gateway signs, orientation panels, interpretation boards, directional signage and waymarkers. Produce a spatial strategy identifying suitable signage locations. Develop design guidance covering dimensions, materials, specification, siting and future rollout. Prepare detailed proposals for priority installations to support future procurement. Work with Community Action Lanarkshire on implementation of information signs, directional signage and waymarkers along the NCN-Coalburn-Douglas route. Ensure all strategy, design and implementation follow inclusive design principles. Lot 1: . sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.description: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is the world's largest organisation for the international exchange of students and researchers as well as the internationalisation of German universities. Since its foundation in the year 1925, the DAAD has supported over 2,9 million academics at home and abroad. As an association, it is supported by German universities and student bodies. In addition to awarding scholarships, the DAAD promotes the internationalisation of German universities, strengthens German studies and the German language abroad, supports developing countries in building efficient universities and advises decision-makers in cultural, educational and development policy. To this end, it maintains an external network with regional offices, information centres and information points in more than 60 countries. Worldwide, more than 1.200 committed employees in Bonn, Berlin and regional offices work towards the goals of the DAAD. The DAAD is financed predominantly from federal funds from the Federal Foreign Office, the Federal Ministry of Education and Research, the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and the European Union. Other sponsors include foreign governments, companies, foundations and the Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft. The DAAD is inviting tenders for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement. A contractor (AN) is sought with specific competence and experience in the areas of usability, user experience, conducting user acceptance tests, continuous success measurement, optimisation and requirements analysis. The AN designs and conducts user-centred studies (e.g. usability tests, acceptance tests, user surveys, target group interviews), continuously measures the success of existing and new features, analyses information architecture, navigation and interaction design and derives concrete optimisation proposals from this. In addition, it supports the DAAD in requirements analysis and prioritisation of further development needs and documents the results in compact, decision-oriented reports for the product managers. The services mentioned below can be commissioned in combinations adapted to the respective project, both in individual studies and in long-term projects. Corresponding tasks may also have to be carried out for mobile apps under Android and/or iOS, possibly also accompanying development. So far, however, no development is specifically planned. The DAAD expects the following services from the contractor: a) Usability and user acceptance tests (in-person or remote) b) User surveys and target group interviews (in-person or remote) c) Laboratory use or rental for in-person tests d) Conception of customised UX monitoring systems for continuous success measurement e) Creation of personas and user structure analyses f) Workshops and design thinking (in-person or remote) g) Consulting, continuous optimisation support, content review and expert analysis h) Result documentation and presentation i) Web analysis and user tracking For further information, please refer to the service description in Annex 02.
sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.title: Framework agreement for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement

sig_8d0615bc5a9d1269f25b.description: Framework Agreement for Procurement Consultancy and Procurement Services for Vehicles and Equipment for Civil Protection Baden-Württemberg. The services are tendered as a framework agreement. The client is looking for a service provider to support it in the procurement of vehicles and equipment for civil protection. The contractor must in particular provide the following predominantly technical services, while the legal assessment and decision remain with the client: - Carrying out market surveys on the vehicles and equipment to be procured for civil protection, in particular with regard to the current state of the art and technical possibilities - Drawing up specifications taking into account technical specifications and the special needs of civil protection - Developing proposals for suitability and award criteria, including technical evaluation criteria - Processing technical applicant/tenderer questions - Processing complaints, in particular preparing complaint response letters - Evaluating requests to participate or tenders as well as developing award proposals for the contract award - Preparing prior information notices - Preparing procurement records - Advising in review procedures In addition, the contractor must optionally support and accompany the client upon respective call-off after the respective award in the procurement process, for example at construction meetings, prototype inspections, quality inspections and acceptances and, where applicable, also regarding the warranty phase after acceptance. Legal advice services are not covered by the contract. The services are tendered in the form of a framework agreement. The client determines the specific services to be provided and their deadlines individually in each individual contract. The contractor has no entitlement to the call-off of services from the framework agreement. There is no entitlement to further commissioning. The type and scope of the individual commissioning can vary per individual project. The client is entitled to an ordinary right of termination at any time for each individual contract issued on the basis of the framework agreement. The client reserves the right to commission any further special services. The framework agreement has a maximum duration of four years from the start of the services with regard to the non-optional services pursuant to Section 21 Paragraph 6 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV). Insofar as the client calls off the optional services, the conditions of the framework agreement for the individual contracts issued until the maximum duration is reached shall continue to apply until their final processing by the contractor even after termination of this framework agreement. The maximum quantity of services expected under the framework agreement amounts to up to a total of 500 vehicles and equipment, which the client can call off bundled in individual contracts for each individual contract.
sig_8d0615bc5a9d1269f25b.title: Framework Agreement for Procurement Consultancy and Procurement Services for Vehicles and Equipment for Civil Protection of the State of Baden-Württemberg

sig_8e275a5238ed1ec42ade.description: BIM Berliner Immobilienmanagement GmbH (BIM) intends to procure and introduce a new document management system (DMS) for company-wide use. The aim of the project is to provide a central, secure and audit-proof platform for managing, processing and archiving documents and files. The DMS is intended to support cross-departmental collaboration, reduce existing media discontinuity and ensure compliance with statutory, data protection and organisational requirements. Operation will initially take place on-premises in the BIM data centre. In the long term, the solution is intended to technically support hybrid and cloud-based operating models respectively. The scope of services comprises in particular: - Provision, implementation and introduction of the DMS software including installation, configuration and training, - Integration into existing systems, in particular SAP S/4HANA, email and office environments, - Migration of existing documents and metadata, - Design and implementation of defined workflows, archiving and authorisation structures, - Ensuring information security, digital accessibility and GDPR compliance, - Operation, maintenance and software support (support S) including service level management. The project is part of BIM's digitalisation strategy and is closely linked to the parallel projects "BIM SAP 2028" and "BitX", in which core business processes and specialist procedures are modernised and integrated. The contract term is 48 months with the option for a one-time extension of up to 24 months. The basis for the provision of services is the EVB-IT system contract in its currently valid version.
sig_8e275a5238ed1ec42ade.title: Software package and information systems, document management system

sig_8e6aa294f87c09cd46f5.description: Danmarks Nationalbank (the Customer) seeks to establish a framework agreement with one Supplier for the provision of specialized cybersecurity advisory and assessment services. As the operator and overseer of critical financial infrastructure in Denmark, Danmarks Nationalbank supports essential processes and systems that require a high level of security, resilience, and trust. The Customer continuously introduces new technologies, vendors, services and architectural changes that may impact its security posture. To ensure informed decision-making and maintain an appropriate level of cyber resilience, the Customer seeks access to independent technical experts capable of evaluating cybersecurity risks from an adversarial perspective. The purpose of the agreement is to provide the Customer with on-demand access to highly skilled technical cybersecurity experts with offensive security backgrounds, capable of delivering rapid, pragmatic and risk-based assessments of new technologies, systems, solutions, architectures and security-related questions. The service shall complement the Customer's internal cybersecurity capabilities by providing independent expert judgement, specialized technical expertise and threat-informed analysis to support secure decision-making, risk management and operational resilience. The Supplier shall provide access to cybersecurity specialists with relevant expertise across infrastructure, cloud, applications, identity and access management, emerging technologies, adversarial techniques and offensive security methodologies.
sig_8e6aa294f87c09cd46f5.title: Tender for a framework agreement on the delivery of Cybersecurity advisory and assessment services

sig_90116dd5159cffb33fea.description: The Student Loans company (SLC) have an agreement for Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service expiring April 2028. In order to provision for a retender of the agreement SLC are undertaking pre-market engagement with regards to the provision of the following: • Requirement A: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service (2026-TR-0109a) • Requirement B: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management (VM) Service (2026-TR-0109b) • Requirement C: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) Service (2026-TR-0109c) • Requirement D: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Service (2026-TR-0109d) • Requirement E: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Retainer Service (2026-TR-0109e) • Requirement F: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture and Engineering Support Services (2026-TR-0109f) SLC is considering an approach to the market to give the suppliers an option to bid for one or ALL of the contractual requirements. Requirement A Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service The Supplier will provide a Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) capability operating on a hybrid customer/supplier model. MXDR Service The Supplier will provide: • 24x7x365 monitoring of SLC security telemetry. • L1 and L2 Security Operations Centre capability (SLC retain L3). • Incident identification, triage and investigation. • Security use-case monitoring and tuning. • Management of Microsoft Sentinel detections. • SOAR playbook execution and optimisation. • Escalation management. • Alert enrichment. • Threat hunting capability. • Malicious activity investigation. • Service governance and performance management. • Security reporting at operational, tactical and strategic levels. Security Engineering (Operational) The Supplier shall provide: • L3 Engineering support for Sentinel. • Analytics rule development and tuning. • SOAR playbook management. • Connector maintenance and health monitoring. • Logging optimisation. • Onboarding and validation of agreed log sources. • Detection engineering support. • Detection gap analysis and monitoring coverage reviews. • Security use case development and continuous improvement. • Monitoring health checks. • Monitoring and remediation of ingestion issues. • Security platform optimisation. • Proactive automation support and development. • Threat intelligence-led detection improvements. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) & Phishing The Supplier shall: • Monitoring, triage and investigation of DLP, phishing, business email compromise (BEC), malicious email, malicious attachment and malicious URL alerts. • Investigation of suspected data loss, data exfiltration and policy breach events. • Support for user reported phishing submissions. • Escalation and coordination of confirmed incidents in accordance with agreed response procedures. • Identification and analysis of phishing campaigns, attacker infrastructure, indicators of compromise and emerging attack trends. • Recommendations for improvements to DLP policies, email security controls, detections and response processes. • Monthly reporting, trend analysis and security improvement recommendations. Reporting The Supplier shall provide: • Weekly operational reports. • Monthly service reports. • Quarterly service reviews. • KPI and SLA reporting. • Security metrics and trend analysis. Requirement B Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management Service The Supplier shall provide Vulnerability Management services Monday to Friday, UK Core Hours (09:00-17:00). Vulnerability Management The Supplier shall: • Monitor vulnerability management queues. • Investigate vulnerability notifications. • Manage vulnerability triage. • Validate vulnerability findings. • Perform exploitability assessments. • Provide remediation recommendations. • Support exposure management activities. • Support CTEM activities. Stakeholder Engagement The Supplier shall: • Conduct monthly technical review meetings. • Support resolver teams. • Assist remediation planning. • Review remediation performance. • Provide vulnerability prioritisation guidance. Dashboarding & Reporting The Supplier shall: • Maintain executive dashboards. • Enhance Power BI reporting. • Produce technical reports. • Produce executive reports. • Produce PCI compliance reports. • Produce risk trending reports. Tooling The Supplier shall support: • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. • Rapid7. • SLC PCI ASV Scanning tooling. • Jira. • Power BI. Requirement C Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation Service The Supplier shall provide a Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) capability, currently using AttackIQ or similar. BAS Service The Supplier shall: • Operate and maintain the BAS platform. • Deploy and maintain BAS agents. • Configure integrations. • Execute scheduled simulations. • Execute customer-specific simulations. • Execute retests following remediation activities. Adversary Simulation Testing scenarios shall include: • Initial Access. • Execution. • Persistence. • Privilege Escalation. • Credential Access. • Lateral Movement. • Command and Control. • Exfiltration. • Malware. • Ransomware. • Advanced Persistent Threat activity. Security Validation The Supplier shall assess: • Security control effectiveness. • Security monitoring effectiveness. • Detection coverage. • Response capability. • Incident handling. • Use-case effectiveness. Reporting The Supplier shall produce: • Monthly BAS reports. • Executive summaries. • Technical findings. • Remediation recommendations. • Retest outcomes. Requirement D Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence Service The Supplier shall provide strategic, operational and tactical Cyber Threat Intelligence services. Threat Intelligence Managed Service The Supplier shall provide: • Threat Intelligence reporting. • Integration into Microsoft Sentinel. • Indicator of Compromise feeds. • Threat actor intelligence. Operational Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat alerts. • Vulnerability intelligence. • Emerging threat notifications. • Campaign tracking. • Industry specific intelligence. Strategic Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat landscape assessments. • Quarterly threat reports. • Executive intelligence briefings. • Board level threat summaries. • Sector specific threat reporting. Security Operations Support The Supplier shall provide: • Intelligence support during incidents. • Threat hunting support. • Intelligence driven use-case creation. • Intelligence enrichment services. Requirement E Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics & Incident Response Retainer Service The Supplier shall provide a DFIR Retainer available 24x7x365. Cyber Incident Response The Supplier shall provide: • Incident investigation. • Malware analysis. • Threat containment. • Threat eradication. • Recovery support. • Crisis management support. • Regulator support. • On-site support Digital Forensics The Supplier shall provide: • Evidence acquisition. • Chain of custody management. • Endpoint forensics. • Server forensics. • Network forensics. • Cloud forensics. • Forensic reporting. Readiness Services The Supplier shall provide access to: • Tabletop exercises. • Incident simulations. • Executive workshops. • CSIRT training. • Lessons learned reviews. Retained Consultancy The Supplier shall provide specialist support including: • Security strategy input. • Audit support. • Major incident reviews. • Regulatory engagement support. • Ransomware negotiation services. Requirement F Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture & Engineering Support Services The Supplier shall provide specialist Security Architecture and Engineering services on a call-off basis. Security Architecture The Supplier shall provide: • Security architecture reviews. • Security design authority support. • Secure by Design reviews. • Solution security reviews. • Threat modelling. • Architecture governance. • Security requirements definition. • Architectural risk assessments. Security Engineering The Supplier shall provide: • Technical security engineering. • Security tool implementation. • Security configuration reviews. • Security hardening activities. • Technical control implementation. Strategy & Transformation The Supplier shall provide: • Security roadmap development. • Target operating model development. • Control framework assessments. • Security maturity reviews. • Improvement planning. Governance & Assurance The Supplier shall provide: • Security assessments. • Risk management support. • Audit support. • KPI development. • Board reporting support. • Security governance support. • Independent design and control assurance. • Security exception and risk acceptance reviews. • Third party and supplier security assessments. sig_92caf0427995304453c5.description: The Universität Hamburg (hereinafter 'UHH'), as a university of excellence with more than 43.000 students and approx. 6.000 employees, is one of the most research-intensive universities in Germany and at the same time one of the largest training institutions in Northern Germany. With its 'Flagship University' concept in the Hamburg metropolitan region, it maintains innovative and cooperative links with scientific and non-scientific partners. It produces future-oriented social goods for the location – but also nationally and internationally – namely education, knowledge and the exchange of knowledge, under the guiding principle of sustainability. The executive boards of the 6 Hamburg universities signed a Letter of Intent in April 2024 regarding the joint IT operation of the Hamburg universities. The aim here is to establish a joint organisation that is controlled by the universities and understands, bundles, and implements their needs, and provides high-quality IT services specifically for scientific institutions across the entire service spectrum. A service centre is to be built and established with the goal of creating synergies and thus providing digital services more efficiently, in a more targeted and user-centred manner, more comprehensively, and at the same time with better quality and protection against cyberattacks. In the course of this joint IT operation, it is necessary to create a joint, federated Identity and Access Management (IAM) structure for the Hamburg universities. The overarching goal is the provision of services for all Hamburg universities based on established federation technologies. Each university is to be equipped with a local IAM system, and the then technology-compatible systems are to be integrated into a joint, federated state identity and access infrastructure. The authoritative management of identities remains decentralised at the individual institutions. A central master directory is to be set up to hold the personal attributes necessary for joint operation. Such a federated infrastructure enables the universities to participate in jointly or centrally provided services (e.g. cloud, collaboration and e-learning services) and at the same time significantly increases the security of access, as modern, open standards such as SAML, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SCIM and FIDO2 are to be implemented throughout. For an organisation-independent, uniform and permanent identification of users, e.g. also when changing between universities, the nationwide federation service of the German National Research and Education Network (DFN-AAI), including the eduID service, is to be used as a basis. The joint state federation is intended as a sub-federation within the DFN-AAI in order to enable cross-university coordination beyond a uniform attribute set. The project aims to design, build and transfer this joint federated state IAM infrastructure into regular operation. A later inclusion of further scientific institutions in Hamburg is not excluded.
sig_92caf0427995304453c5.title: Establishment of a joint federated identity and access management infrastructure for Hamburg universities

sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.description: The Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE) program supports the translation of open-source science and engineering-focused research products into safe and sustainable ecosystems that address national and societal challenges. Open-source tools such as software, hardware, machine learning models, languages, and data platforms are designed to be shared as they are publicly-accessible and modifiable. These tools spark innovation in critical fields as varied as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing, banking, healthcare, research, education, next-gen manufacturing, mobility, and National security (including cybersecurity). PESOSE supports the creation of managing organizations for these ecosystems, ensuring strong governance, distributed development, and broad user communities across academia, industry, and government. PESOSE also supports enhancements to the safety, security, and privacy of Open-Source Ecosystems (OSE) by addressing significant vulnerabilities, both technical and socio-technical, to improve the resistance of the ecosystem against threats. This solicitation seeks three types of proposals, allowing teams to propose specific activities to: 1) scope and plan the establishment of an OSE, 2) establish and expand a sustainable OSE based on a robust, promising open-source product that meets an emergent societal or national need, and 3) improve the safety, security, and privacy of an existing OSE and its products.
sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.title: Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)

sig_94329553e52c261ebc1a.description: The client's IT encompasses a very wide range of services from merchandise management and billing systems such as SAP through control centre systems to apps, such as MVGO. IT demand sometimes grows faster than internal staff can be built up and should it decrease, reducing internal staff is sluggish. This scaling requirement is addressed by awarding services to external parties. One form of this is the external takeover of testing of software applications in a scope appropriate for each application (test concept, test management, test case definition, execution of functional and non-functional tests (e.g. L&P tests, regression tests, exploratory tests, ...), test automation). This support takes place in both traditional and agile environments. The client currently has 3 candidate groups of applications for which they wish to outsource testing. The known support effort is approx. 3 to 5 FTE. During the contract term, applications may be added, removed, or the annual effort for them may fluctuate. A framework agreement is being tendered. The individual applications are commissioned via call-off (possibly also with multiple call-offs). The client's experience shows that domain knowledge is essential for service delivery, especially when testing. The tender covers the following domains: • Public transport sales: Sales processes (app- and web-based sales channels, mass customer billing) • Purchasing and logistics (SAP MM/SD/CS) • Finance (SAP FI/CO) • Maintenance including mobile maintenance (SAP PM, app applications) There is no obligation for the client to exhaust the contract under this framework agreement. Services are fundamentally to be provided remotely. Exceptions that require on-site service delivery are workshops and, where applicable, tests in connection with hardware that is only available on-site at the client (e.g. a ticket vending machine). Other special conditions for contract performance: Contract execution in German, written and oral; within EU GDPR

sig_94d4002af06384a9cbb9.description: Above-threshold open electronic tender entitled "Procurement and installation of underground temporary waste storage systems for the pilot implementation of PAY AS YOU THROW (PAYT) programmes in the Municipality of Florina", with an estimated expenditure of 1.331.120,16€ including VAT of 24%, with sealed bids and with the award criterion being the most economically advantageous tender based on the best price-quality ratio Procurement and installation of fifty (50) "smart" underground waste collection bins (with a capacity of approximately 3m3 each), which will replace in volume approximately three (3) existing plastic bins. The bins shall be equipped with: 1) Access control and user identification system. 2) Weighing system for the discarded waste in each use.; In order for the Municipality to be able to monitor the conditions of use of the said underground bins and to develop an incentive policy towards users, it is necessary for the underground bins to be equipped with an access control and user registration system. The controlled access and disposal registration system must consist of: • User identification devices installed on the input "hoppers". • Security locks that restrict use only to certified users. • Deposit weighing system. • Controlled access via "smart" cards or mobile phones. • User management and event logging software.; The weighing system must be suitable for use in high humidity conditions and resistant to corrosive agents. The weighing system must be able to record the maximum possible and minimum possible weighing weight of individual discarded waste per user and the total temporarily stored waste. The weighing system must have the capability for automatic internal calibration and shall be accompanied by a calibration certificate at least for two indicative weights from a calibrated body/laboratory according to ISO 17025.; As part of this procurement, the contractor shall deliver to the Municipality a quantity of 2000 pcs. of RFID-type "smart" cards fully compatible with the offered controlled access system, which will be distributed to users/citizens. In their financial tender, tenderers must provide a separate unit price for the offered "smart" cards.; For their more efficient operation, the underground bins shall bear an attached fullness monitoring system, consisting of sensors to be placed at a suitable point, accompanied by a measurement transmission system application and software for data management, accessible via the internet (web based system).; Purchase of Software as a Service (SaaS) platform usage rights on a server of the Municipality. Monitoring of controlled access and fullness of underground bins with connection to a telemetry management platform. The required functionality shall be provided by the contractor for a period of twelve (12) months from the commissioning of the controlled access systems, in the form of Software as a Service (SaaS). Support, reporting and results compilation services are included for a period of (24) months.
sig_94d4002af06384a9cbb9.title: Procurement and installation of underground temporary waste storage systems

sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.description: Modernisation of the central firewall system in Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. The aim of the project is the modernisation of the overall firewall and security architecture, including next-generation endpoint protection for the research association. The future solution must meet current and future requirements for information security, availability, scalability, multi-tenancy, traceability of administrative activities and economical operation. General requirements for the new firewall structure: - Multi-tier firewall structure with centrally operated perimeter firewall cluster and segmentation firewall clusters per institute, whereby different manufacturers must be provided (dual-vendor strategy) B-criterion in BM - VLAN- and IP-based institute-related segmentation - Virtual domains for segmentation of the corporate IT perimeter firewall - At least two appliances per geographical location in active-passive operation - Expansion of backbone throughput to 10 gigabits per second with the option of expansion to 40 gigabits per second without replacing the hardware, as well as loop-free network design - Number of concurrent sessions: 20.000 to 65.000; number of VPN uses per institute: at least 40 to 70 users; maximum all employees in the FVB (1.600 employees) - Consideration of QoS mechanisms for VoIP and latency-sensitive applications - Granular, association-wide uniform role and authorisation concept for administrative access - Multi-factor authentication for users (native or via identity provider) and administrators (native) - NGFW functionalities: o IPS and IDS o Application IP o Geo-IP filter - Separation of networks (e.g. laboratory networks) via VLAN - Central DNS security service, DoS defence, content filtering and advanced threat protection as well as the integration of external blacklists at the perimeter level - Powerful and practicable DoS defence - Common, multi-tenant WAF service for web applications - Platform support for VPN access for Windows, Linux and MacOS - Compliance check for all operating systems - Central management for perimeter (mandatory) and segmentation firewalls (optional) - Tenant separation with granular graduation of administration rights - Open interfaces to support REST- or XML-based APIs, Syslog, Net-Flow/IPFIX, SAML, LDAP, RADIUS and other standard market integration interfaces - Remote access: the support of established procedures with split tunnelling and carrier-grade NAT must be provided - Identification of institute affiliation, for example via certificates or naming conventions - SSL interception (inbound for published services as well as outbound for critical servers/clients - Email security, multi-tenant, optionally acquirable per institute - Sandbox functions - Out-of-band management - At least an interface for the automatic integration of certificates - IPv6 future-proofing (a conversion to IPv6 is not planned within the scope of the project) - Central, multi-tenant log management with a retention period of at least three months, local buffering or short-term fallback retention and interfaces to a potential SIEM - Tenant-related and institute-specific logging Suitable support and service services must be offered for the procured hardware, software, subscriptions and management components. These include fault clearance, maintenance, software support, manufacturer and system house support, hardware replacement, patch and release management, operational support and a comprehensible escalation process. The availability of the future solution must be set at at least 99,9 % per year. The specific SLA design, in particular response times, recovery times, service times, scheduled change windows and emergency changes, will be discussed jointly in dialogue taking into account redundancy, cost-effectiveness and operational risk. In addition, NOC services with security analysis must be provided by the future service provider. Pure SOC services are to be treated as a supplementary option or add-on. For SOC-related services, in particular monitoring, triage, analysis, alarming, initial processing, incident response, reporting chains, on-call duty, multi-tenancy, SIEM/SOAR connection, log sources, sensor technology, reporting and communication channels must be considered.
sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.title: Modernisation of the central firewall system in Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V.

sig_971ad5f0459d229fae7b.description: The contracting authority is PD Berater der Öffentlichen Hand GmbH. A client of the contracting authority has established 2021 with the 'Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings' (QNG), an umbrella brand for sustainable construction in Germany. The 'Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings' (QNG) is intended to promote sustainable construction in Germany on a broad scale and to ensure a minimum quality for 'sustainable buildings'. Furthermore, it is intended to create a legally secure basis for the allocation of subsidies, which enables grants in the construction sector to be in accordance with social goals (sustainability goals). Since 2022 the contracting authority has been supporting the client with the development and establishment of a QNG office with all associated activities, such as a hotline, operation of a website and further development of the QNG requirements with the associated publications. In order to provide up-to-date information about the seal and the processes to be followed, the QNG website https://www.qng.info/ was developed and set up in the year 2022 with an external service provider. The QNG website represents a knowledge platform that processes ongoing developments and changes, and provides users with basic procedures, interfaces and assistance. The contract is awarded in two lots: - Lot 1: Hosting, further development and maintenance of the existing website - Lot 2: Technical support (expertise pool) for the 'Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings' (QNG). The lot-specific tasks are described in more detail below. Bids may be submitted for one or both lots. Lot LOT-0001: Lot 1: Hosting, further development and maintenance of the existing website. The contractor shall undertake the continuous maintenance, operation, hosting, and provision of the server infrastructure for the operation of the already existing website. The services include: 1. Website maintenance, provision of licences 2. Website hosting and optimisation 3. Hosting and further development of an AI-based, self-learning chatbot. The contractor shall ensure a seamless transition from 01. January 2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the commissioning in Lot 1 is an EVB-IT cloud contract. Lot LOT-0002: Lot 2: Technical support (expertise pool) for the 'Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings' (QNG). The expertise pool is intended to provide support in advising on enquiries resulting from the application of the QNG in practice, as well as in the further development of the QNG requirements and the introduction and implementation phase of the revised requirements. The services include: • Support in the content-related further development of the quality seal • Support in the revision and quality assurance of the associated documents with regard to clarity and technical accuracy • Support in the creation or revision of accompanying materials such as FAQs and quick answers • Creation of training materials for certification bodies and auditors as part of the introduction of the revised requirements • Support in processing complex or technically demanding enquiries, if necessary support in the ongoing quality assurance of new FAQs and quick answers. The start of the service is 01.01.2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the commissioning in Lot 2 is a service contract. There is no fixed acceptance quantity. The estimated volume is derived from the estimated quantity specified in the price sheet. The contract is limited to 280.000 euros.
sig_971ad5f0459d229fae7b.title: Web hosting and professional support (expertise pool) for the "Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings" (QNG)

sig_988058399897c0071507.description: Complex generic drug products represent an increasing share of the generic marketplace and may have distinct user interface differences compared to reference listed drug (RLD) products. A modernized post-market surveillance approach is needed to compare clinical outcomes between complex generic products and their corresponding RLD products to monitor for potential issues with therapeutic equivalence and to inform regulatory decision making. Real-world data (RWD) combined with machine learning (ML) and/or artificial intelligence (AI) could help to identify post-market signals efficiently in an automated and repeatable fashion, facilitating timely regulatory action. The purpose of this funding opportunity is to develop and test an AI- or ML-based algorithmic RWD model for post-market surveillance of complex generic drug products.

sig_9988be44fc524f729b36.description: At the BWB sewage treatment plants and sewage pumping stations, the PI System from the company AVEVA (formerly OSIsoft) is used for the long-term archiving of process data. The Berliner Wasserbetriebe currently operate 9 PI Data Archive Servers. These are supplied with data via approx. 50 OPC Interfaces. In total, the measured values, up to 40.000 - 50.000 data points, are collected and archived in the smallest possible resolution (> 1 second). They serve as a data source for the Asset Framework, PI Vision, a simulation server, as well as for external customers who need to access live and historical data. For this purpose, the API interface of the PI System is also required. The retention of historical data goes back to the year 1999. It includes all existing measured values and data points. These are permanently mapped in the PI Data Archive and are therefore available for retrieval within milliseconds at any time. The following questionnaire is intended to evaluate whether a migration to an alternative system is possible and economically viable.
sig_9988be44fc524f729b36.title: Market exploration for PI System

sig_9a717a6eb198dcbccd00.description: Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitos (THL) is planning a tender for a condition monitoring system for its Kuopio office. THL is an independent state expert and research institute that promotes the well-being, health and safety of people. The institute's laboratories store millions of samples as well as reagents required for analytics in various storage conditions. The condition monitoring system must centrally collect temperature and alarm data from all measurement points. The primary objective of the system is to provide alarms when temperature limits are exceeded and to manage these alarms. The system must also be able to monitor and record condition data in both normal and alarm conditions. Monitoring and operational update tasks are intended to be performed by THL users. The intention is that the system will include all components required from measurement to alarm and data recording, with the exception of THL's existing sensors used in deep-freeze freezers (Pt100), which are intended to be used as part of the system. THL's Kuopio office deep-freeze freezers currently use approximately 20 Pt100 sensors. The deep-freeze freezers have a separate 4-conductor Pt-100 sensor, which is attached to the transmitter with a spring loaded connector. REGISTRATION INSTRUCTIONS FOR MARKET SURVEY (HEREINAFTER MARKET DIALOGUE): Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register by 1.10.2025 at 12:00 by email to kilpailutus@hansel.fi with the following information: - Message subject: "Olosuhdevalvontajärjestelmä Kuopion toimipisteeseen - markkinavuoropuhelu" - Message content: 1) Company name and business ID 2) Contact person's name and email address 3) Experience in supplying a condition monitoring system (in what kind of environment does the company's monitoring system operate) 4) Do you have any obstacles to using the above-described THL-owned sensors as part of your system? 5) How would the existing sensors (Pt-100) be connected to transmitters/SaaS service in your system? 6) If the information provided above is not sufficient, what information do you still need about the sensors owned by THL? 7) What is the response time for maintenance, troubleshooting, and delivery of replacement and spare equipment to Kuopio? IMPLEMENTATION OF MARKET DIALOGUE: The contracting authority will send draft materials of the tender for a written comment round as the preparation process progresses. No compensation will be paid to those who participated in the market dialogue. Hansel Oy acts in a consulting role in the market dialogue and the potential tender.
sig_9a717a6eb198dcbccd00.title: Condition monitoring system for the Kuopio office

sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.description: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety - Development and testing of approaches for the use of digitised regulations and rules in occupational health and safety Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety. Starting point of the project: Digital solutions are useful for the drafting, provision and application of technical rules in the field of occupational health and safety. This applies both to rule-making in the occupational health and safety committees at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (see https://www.bmas.de/DE/Arbeit/Arbeitsschutz/Arbeitsschutzausschuesse/arbeitsschutzausschuesse.html ), as well as to the publication of the rules by the BMAS and their application in companies as well as for advice and enforcement. In the field of standardisation, the concept "Digital Smart Standards" is available from the Digital Standards Initiative by DIN and DKE (IDiS) (see https://www.dke.de/idis ). This was applied as an example in a previous research project F 2542 of the BAuA (see https://www.baua.de/DE/Forschung/Forschungsprojekte/f2542 and project website https://digiasr.blogs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ ). A methodology for the step-by-step development of machine-readable and machine-executable testing rules was derived from this (A. Aziz, D. Napps, M. König, S. Gabriel, A. Richter, S. Voß (2025): Approaches for the transformation of technical rules for workplaces into digital rules. https://www.baua.de/DE/Angebote/Publikationen/Fokus/F2542-2). Subject matter of the contract and objectives: Based on the existing approaches and findings, a study is to be conducted to investigate the extent to which approaches for "Digital Smart Standards" can be transferred to further areas of the body of regulations and rules on occupational health and safety, and whether the occupational health and safety rules drawn up in the occupational health and safety committees can be converted into "Digital Smart Regulations", i.e. into level 2 "Machine-readable document", and further developed in future for level 3 "Machine-readable and executable content" and level 4 "Machine-readable and interpretable content". This study is the subject of the services to be provided by the contractor. The aim is to draw up recommendations for action for the further digitalisation of occupational health and safety regulations and rules in Germany. In key technical application contexts and use cases, which are to be selected in cooperation with the occupational health and safety committees at the BMAS, the processes from creation through management and provision to the operational application of rules as well as implementation options must be considered. Requirements from occupational health and safety regulations and rules must be taken into account in practice, particularly during risk assessments by employers. The contractor must therefore investigate in the project how the contents of the occupational health and safety rules can be applied in exemplary digital implementations of the risk assessment processes and in any existing data models and coordinated with further requirements. The contractor systematically compiles and evaluates the results and derives concrete recommendations for action based on them. The project contributes to making the respective body of rules clearer and easier to apply digitally for users in future, as well as to making the processes for creating, further developing, administering and providing the rules more efficient.
sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.title: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety

sig_9bbc52f64dff547fec2a.description: The Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH (GöVB) is a municipal transport company 100% owned by the City of Göttingen. It operates local public transport in the city of Göttingen and adjacent regions and ensures the daily mobility of residents and guests with its bus fleet. As a sectoral contracting authority within the meaning of § 100 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB), GöVB is responsible for the procurement of services and systems that secure the operation and further development of local public transport. GöVB pursues the goal of gradually converting its bus fleet to alternative, in particular electric, drive systems. In doing so, it makes a significant contribution to sustainable mobility, the reduction of emissions, and the achievement of the climate targets of the City of Göttingen. The expansion of the e-bus fleet is accompanied by a considerable need for modern charging infrastructure that enables efficient, reliable, and economical operational management. To support this transformation, GöVB is planning the introduction of a charging and load management system (LLEMS). This system is intended to enable intelligent control and monitoring of all charging processes at the depot and, in the future, also in scheduled service. The focus is on ensuring vehicle availability, grid and load optimisation, and the safe and economical operation of electromobility in local public transport in Göttingen.
sig_9bbc52f64dff547fec2a.title: Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH - Charging, Load and Energy Management System (LLEMS) (Market exploration)

sig_9d9ffc50e7cd2401e0ac.description: The contracting authority is tendering a contract regarding Transition In, development of the Modernised Support Systems, application operation, application maintenance, support, ordering services, including further development of the Support Systems, as well as Transition Out. The contract consists of the following 3 main services: I. Transition In, including, among other things, a secure and stable takeover of the application responsibility for the Support Systems, implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, transfer of source code and documentation, implementation of technical transition and necessary transformation, takeover of knowledge from the outgoing supplier as well as establishment of the operations organisation, including establishment of the collaboration with the operations supplier. II. Ongoing services for the Support Systems, including; a. Support, including, among other things, responsibility for Service Desk, user administration, handling of incidents, problems, service requests, early life support, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of ensuring high availability for the users; b. Application operation, including, among other things, database operation, operation of middleware, backup, restore, monitoring and logging, 2. and 3. line support, configuration, patch, and release and deployment management, cf. the operational processes, and operational reporting with high requirements for uptime and response times; c. Application maintenance, including, among other things, ongoing and preventive maintenance of the IT systems, minor changes, new versions, bug fixes, release management, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of supporting high requirements for uptime and response times; d. Governance, including close collaboration with the operations supplier, operational processes, security services, documentation and operational reporting. III. Agile development, e.g. via a design and planning phase, including proof of concept, as well as a development phase based on the supplier's product vision and advice. Development of the Modernised Support Systems takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties regarding support for the contracting authority's business goals and needs, so that the Modernised Support Systems can be implemented after a time-limited period. Development includes any new functionality as well as any re-implementation and reuse of parts of the current Support Systems. Further development of the Support Systems also takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties. It is the contracting authority's business need that all services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In Transition In, the supplier must take over the application responsibility for the Support Systems and, from the transition day, deliver ongoing services, including, among other things, application operation, application maintenance and further development, to the Support Systems. The further development will take place in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority. The supplier must also, in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority, carry out a modernisation of the Support Systems based on the contracting authority's modernisation wishes. The Support Systems are part of the overall joint municipal infrastructure, and the supplier must therefore collaborate partly with the other suppliers, including the operations supplier as well as suppliers who deliver other parts of the joint municipal infrastructure, and partly with users of the infrastructure. It is the contracting authority's business goal and need, among other things, to give parts of the current Support Systems a quality boost in the form of a modernisation that supports the Modernised Support Systems appearing attractive, reliable, future-proof and secure, so that the municipalities also in the future have a strong foundation to deliver the best digital services to the citizens in an increasingly more coherent, efficient and modern public sector.

sig_9eeb0e95df78e643035a.description: This is not a procurement notice or a request for tenders, but a market survey and request for information. The National ID forum (informal forum) has decided to organize a joint RFI event. The idea is to organize a single RFI involving several national agencies and ministries, which would maximize synergy benefits and be a cost-effective model. The ID Forum is a national informal cooperation forum that focuses on comprehensive identity management, its development, and creating a situational picture. The aim is to produce national services that develop capacity in identity management, coordinate training and information events, and improve the common situational awareness and ability to combat abuse. Identity is therefore at the heart of the forum and is dealt with within the remit of each member organization. The ID Forum consists of several Finnish agencies and ministries; Immigration Service (FIS), Border Guard Force (BGF), National Bureau of Investigations (NBI), National Police Board (NPB), Police departments, Customs, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA). The subject of the RFI and information about the procedure are described in more detail in Appendix 1.

sig_a1d31a611e6e4549cb68.description: The objective of the procurement is to acquire IT project manager and expert resources to support, among other things, the definition, programming, testing and management of the Finnish Tax Administration's new and existing systems. The expert resources will operate in projects, development tasks and ongoing service production. The purpose of the procurement is to secure specialist expertise and sufficient resources. The procurement is divided into six (6) lots, for each of which three (3) suppliers and three (3) reserve suppliers will be selected. The lots and their contents are described in more detail below. More detailed descriptions of the contents of the assignments for the procurement lots are described in the appendix Description of the subject matter of the procurement in section 3. The objective is for the contract to enter into force on 16.11.2026. The contract shall be valid for 72 months. Verohallinto develops and maintains digital services primarily as cloud-based and cloud-native solutions. The development work utilises application, integration, data and platform services provided by the Microsoft Azure cloud platform, as well as modern software development, information security and operational practices. Solutions vary in scope and criticality from mission-critical core applications to more limited services targeting specific business needs. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for cloud-based software development implemented in the Microsoft Azure environment. The lot includes in particular architecture design for cloud solutions and cloud applications, application and integration development, DevOps, the development and maintenance of cloud platforms, and the technical information security of cloud environments and applications. Key expert roles include cloud solution architect, cloud application architect, cloud software developer, integration developer, cloud DevOps specialist, cloud platform specialist and technical information security specialist.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for applications and information system solutions utilising artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and machine learning. The solutions are implemented primarily in the Microsoft Azure cloud environment, utilising the artificial intelligence capabilities offered by Microsoft Foundry and other Azure services. The solutions can be standalone AI applications or parts of broader information systems, digital services and software solutions. Expert work concerning new technologies may relate to the assessment of the possibilities, suitability, information security and risks of technologies, experiments and prototyping, software and hardware integration, the development of embedded systems, preparation for deployment, or the practical utilisation of technologies. Key expert roles for AI applications include AI application specialists, AI developers, AI solution architects, machine learning specialists and software developers participating in the implementation of AI applications.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services aimed at improving the efficiency, quality and transparency of the organisation's operational and data-driven processes through automation, hyper-automation, analytics and systematic development methods. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is primarily process automation expert services as well as process analytics and process development expert services in a cloud-based operating environment.; The Finnish Tax Administration's technological operating environment strongly includes the development of infrastructure, analytics, information security and cloud services. The Finnish Tax Administration uses the Gentax core taxation system and several smaller systems (e.g. supporting administration). The National Incomes Register and the Positive Credit Register are also the responsibility of the Finnish Tax Administration. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot includes: - project manager services for the development, creation and deployment of operating models and processes, as well as the development of related applications. The scope of impact of operational development can be internal to the organisation and/or customer-related. - technical project manager services, particularly for the areas of infrastructure and information security - Scrum master/team lead services for operational and technical development teams.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is IT service management expert services for the ServiceNow environment, as well as expert services specialised in ServiceNow development for architecture, consulting and development tasks. The tasks include ICT architecture and expert tasks in the ServiceNow modules used by the Finnish Tax Administration, including (* supplemented 4.9.2026): • ITSM (IT Service Management) • ITOM (IT Operations Management) • ITBM / SPM (Strategic Portfolio and Demand Management) • SecOps / SIR* (Security Operations) • IRM (Risk Management)* • CMDB (Configuration Management)* • IAM / AM (Access Management, Identity Management)* Expert tasks may include system development, configuration, maintenance, testing and training tasks for the modules in question, as well as related functional and technical architecture design.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is user-driven development expert services. By expert service, we mean working under the direction of the Finnish Tax Administration as part of the Finnish Tax Administration's development teams or in close cooperation with them, consulting, business sparring and/s or the implementation of various assignments. Verohallinto can also order fixed-price assignments for e.g. system accessibility audits.

sig_a2908f5e8483ee367425.description: South Lanarkshire Council are looking to notify the market of a potential future contract opportunity to deliver a Customer Experience (CX) Platform, incorporating Customer Relationship Management (CRM). The Council has undertaken a review of its customer experience and identified a potential need for a Customer Experience platform to help modernise and improve its offering. The review identified significant opportunities for improvement in customer contact channels, back-office processes, and data management. Implementing the recommendations will enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and support the Council's digital transformation goals. The Council has a legacy CRM system (Oracle) which will be out of contract in 2027. The procurement and implementation of a new CX Platform would form part of a wider Customer Experience improvement strategy that will encompass telephony, complaints, website updates and cross service process improvements. Lot 1: . This PIN notice is being published to explore potential options for a Customer Experience (CX) Platform, incorporating CRM for South Lanarkshire Council. An overview of the requirement along with a pre market engagement questionnaire is included for suppliers to provide feedback on potential solutions. The responses to this Market Engagement Questionnaire will inform the procurement strategy and requirements. It is requested that completed questionnaires are submitted to Gayle Chilton by e-mail (e-mail address detailed on the attached questionnaire) no later than 12 noon on the Thursday 02 April 2026.. Please note there is no additional documentation available for this contract at this moment.

sig_a3465975540f6b50a997.description: The purpose of the contract is the implementation of an integral platform that allows the complete data lifecycle to be managed efficiently and securely, as well as an inter-administrative data space that facilitates sharing and exchanging information reliably. Furthermore, the contract comprises the provision of services necessary for its customisation, commissioning, operational support and evolution. This includes the implementation, configuration, integration, commissioning and support of an Integral Data Governance Platform and an Inter-administrative Data Space for the Junta de Communities of Castilla-La Mancha in an on-premise modality, intended to provide the functional and technological capabilities necessary for the deployment of the Data Governance System (as established in article 15 of Decree 12/2026, of 31 March, regulating Data Governance in the Junta de Communities of Castilla-La Mancha) and to enable the sharing, management, cataloguing, governance and interoperability of data between the various units of the regional Administration, other public administrations and, where applicable, the remaining agents of the data ecosystem, under principles of security, sovereignty, trust, traceability and regulatory compliance. The platform must provide, amongst others, capabilities for cataloguing and metadata management, data governance and quality, lineage, semantic management, inventory of data sets and products, policy management, discovery and consumption of data, interoperability, secure information sharing and support for the creation of a data market (Data Marketplace), allowing progressive evolution towards an inter-administrative data space aligned with the Data Union Strategy and the Data Strategic Plan of Castilla-La Mancha 2026-2030. In addition, support services aimed at increasing and promoting a data culture within the Administration are considered, as well as all those that provide support and serve to drive the corporate strategy regarding data, including those for support and assistance in the drafting of data-related policies, instructions and procedures.
sig_a3465975540f6b50a997.title: Services relating to data governance and data lifecycle management

The agreement offers the following services: strategy and business transformation problem solving with tech solutions resources and training software licences What is out of scope? Products and services out of scope include but are not limited to: any hardware and infrastructure hosting networks or connectivity services Benefits accessible route for suppliers – accessible for all suppliers (including SMEs) and suppliers can apply to join at any time government specific terms and conditions (Ts&Cs) – these have been created based on an agile approach using the public sector contract a dynamic filtering system – giving buyers flexibility based on their requirements. Suppliers receive notifications of competitions that are relevant to their service offering and buyers can easily identify potential eligible suppliers supports innovation – suppliers can add new services (within scope) during the lifetime of the DPS, meaning buyers can keep up with fast-moving market developments open to all public sector buyers – including central government departments and the wider public sector access to Cabinet Office (CO) automation task force – receive advice and support from the task force who specialise in the implementation of automation technologies, services and licences Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Automation Marketplace DPS Understanding the opportunity, setting a strategic direction and target operating models. This filter allows buyers to build an evidence base and the sub-filters are areas to focus on. Expires: 15/11/2026 How to buy You must run a mini competition to select a supplier. There is no option for direct award. Before running your mini competition, find out which suppliers could meet your requirements using the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Marketplace. The steps below outline how to search for suppliers, create a shortlist and carry out a mini competition. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. Note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer. Navigate to the Automation Marketplace DPS under Technology, choose the ‘Access as a buyer’ option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your ‘Manage your DPS Category Exports’ page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements. When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘Save Category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your ‘Manage your Category Exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (export is to an Excel spreadsheet) Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a Further Competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. The list is valid for only 2 working days , from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point. If your Call for Competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you don’t use your list within 2 working days by clicking the ‘Search Again’ option for your export. You can use our eSourcing tool to run a Call for Competition. The tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your requirement. suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing sufficient time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from the winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a 2-day deadline for submitting evidence. If you’re satisfied with the evidence, award the contract Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder. Contact Our customer services team is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. sig_a576dd18eaa9a070c397.description: Der Landkreis Nienburg/Weser plans the new construction of a fire brigade technical centre (FTZ) in the commercial area of the town of Lemke, municipality of Marklohe. This is a replacement building for the existing FTZ in Verdener Landstraße in Nienburg. The room programme comprises approx. 8.200 m2 of usable space, as well as approx. 9.140 m2 of outdoor areas – movement and exercise areas. A building site with an area of approx. 3,4 ha is available for this purpose. As part of the project, the erection of a building automation system is planned. Building automation comprises the automation, room automation and management level for monitoring, control, regulation and visualisation of the technical systems. Two central automation focuses are planned in the project. In addition to this, automation focuses are located in the vehicle hall, workshop hall and logistics hall respectively. For room automation, room automation distributors are arranged in the respective sub-distribution areas of electrical engineering. These room automation distributors map the functions of room automation. The integration of sun protection actuators, window contacts and the valves of the underfloor heating is carried out via I/O modules, which are connected to the room automation distributors. Lighting is integrated via KNX-DALI actuators installed in the electrical engineering sub-distributions. The respective interfaces and communication paths are to be coordinated accordingly with the electrical engineering and building automation trades. For the system technology, approx. 500 physical data points and approx. 550 shared data points are planned in the project. In the area of room automation, approx. 700 physical data points and approx. 2.000 shared data points are present.
sig_a576dd18eaa9a070c397.title: Building automation
