sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.description: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are enabling extraordinary scientific breakthroughs in fields ranging from protein folding, natural language processing, drug synthesis, and recommender systems to the discovery of novel engineering materials and products. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. It appears increasingly unlikely that these critical gaps can be surmounted with increased computational power and experimentation alone. Deeper mathematical understanding is essential to ensuring that AI can be harnessed to meet the future needs of society and enable broad scientific discovery, while forestalling the unintended consequences of a disruptive technology. The National Science Foundation Directorates for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS), Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), Engineering (ENG), and Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences (SBE) will jointly sponsor research collaborations consisting of mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers, and social and behavioral scientists focused on the mathematical and theoretical foundations of AI. Research activities should focus on the most challenging mathematical and theoretical questions aimed at understanding the capabilities, limitations, and emerging properties of AI methods as well as the development of novel, and mathematically grounded, design and analysis principles for the current and next generation of AI approaches. Specific research goals include: establishing a fundamental mathematical understanding of the factors determining the capabilities and limitations of current and emerging generation s of AI systems, including, but not limited to, foundation models, generative models, deep learning, statistical learning, federated learning, and other evolving paradigms; the development of mathematically grounded design and analysis principles for the current and next generations of AI systems; rigorous approaches for characterizing and validating machine learning algorithms and their predictions; research enabling provably reliable, translational, general-purpose AI systems and algorithms; e ncouragement of new collaborations in this interdisciplinary research community and between institution s. The overall goal is to establish innovative and principled design and analysis approaches for AI technology using creative yet theoretically grounded mathematical and statistical frameworks, yielding explainable and interpretable models that can enable sustainable, socially responsible, and trustworthy AI.
sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence

sig_a7d1f416274e89243a7d.description: Henneberg Clinics - Mobile Laboratory Automation and Robotics The subject matter is the planning, delivery, integration, conformity assessment, commissioning, acceptance and service of a fully mobile robotics/automation solution for barcode-supported sample flow between intake, pre-analytics, analysis systems, special dispensing, cooling and archiving. The solution must function as an overall system with laboratory equipment, LIS/middleware, building infrastructure and operator processes. Not the subject matter of this lot are medical laboratory services, the permanent provision of laboratory personnel, or the immediate procurement of transport or cleaning robots. Laboratory equipment and laboratory IT are procured separately. However, the robotics contractor remains responsible for the complete mechanical, electrical, software, control and safety engineering integration of the overall system they offer. Target image and functional equivalence: • Permanent robotics-supported in-house laboratory operations at the Hildburghausen site from 01.01.2027; no transitional supply. The first expansion stage is the mobile laboratory robotics system. • Documented peak intake: maximum approx. 30 samples per hour. The solution must not be unnecessarily oversized for this, but must demonstrate a comprehensible operational reserve. • Fully mobile, autonomously navigating robotics systems (AMR) or functionally equivalent mobile automation solutions are permitted. Stationary robot cells, linearly guided systems and permanently installed tracks do not meet the target image. • The solution offered is not an isolated robotics island: it is seamlessly integrated into order, sample, equipment, result, priority and error management and networked via a centrally provided orchestration and fleet management software. The software and platform architecture must be provably scalable for subsequent transport and cleaning robotics at two sites of the clinic association. A common or interoperable traffic logic, building and elevator interfaces, identity and certificate management, as well as a uniform operating and service concept must be provided. The initial procurement must not create unnecessary binding to proprietary laboratory equipment or closed building interfaces. Open, documented interface specifications that can be handed over to the contracting authority are a minimum requirement; a device-side extension to SiLA 2 or a functionally equivalent open standard must be presented. The contractor must describe the entry with a robust core workflow and the subsequent expansion with additional tasks, grippers, equipment, rooms and robotics domains in a technically and commercially comprehensible manner.
sig_a7d1f416274e89243a7d.title: Henneberg Clinics - Mobile Laboratory Automation and Robotics

sig_a8f679baea262f7d8cbc.buyer_name: German Corporation for International Cooperation (GIZ) GmbH
sig_a8f679baea262f7d8cbc.buyer_original: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
sig_a8f679baea262f7d8cbc.description: Background Many developing countries and emerging economies are negatively impacted by trade constraints resulting from red tape in the form of complicated customs documents, import surveillance and border procedures that lack transparency. High transaction costs make it difficult for them to tap into global value chains and make their businesses less competitive. Many enterprises are thereby denied opportunities to grow through trade. In 2017, the World Trade Organization"s (WTO) Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) entered into force with the objective to simplify, modernize and harmonize export and import processes in order to facilitate the cross-border movements of goods. It also establishes measures for effective cooperation between customs and other relevant authorities on trade facilitation and customs compliance. Additionally, it contains provisions for technical assistance and capacity building. Measures to facilitate trade play an important role across a variety of policy areas and sectors. They have a positive effect on food security, rural development, consumer protection, investment promotion and good governance among others. Project rationale The GIZ global program "Partnerships for Sustainable Trade" (PST) has been commissioned by the German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) to establish measures that facilitate trade and support environment and climate protection. Its duration is from 07/2024 to 12/2027. The program focuses on implementing the Trade Facilitation Agreement of the World Trade Organization (WTO) and promotes cooperation between companies, business and trade associations as well as state institutions. As an implementation partner of the Global Alliance for Trade Facilitation (the Alliance), it aligns development objectives with economic interests. The Alliance supports low and middle-income countries in streamlining trade-related processes to move goods across their borders as quickly, safely, and cost-effectively as possible. The Alliance is an initiative that puts public private partnership at the heart of its approach to trade reform, believing that governments and businesses of all sizes working together represents the best way of delivering transformative, positive change. The Alliance is jointly hosted by the World Economic Forum, the International Chamber of Commerce and the Center for International Private Enterprise and works in cooperation with the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. It is currently funded by the governments of Canada, Germany, Sweden, and the European Union (EU). Program measures include: - Planning and implementing trade facilitation measures in various countries in Africa, the Balkans, and Asia; - Increasing efficiency and reducing customs clearance costs by digitising processes and commercial documents; - Simplifying import and export procedures in developing and least developed countries (LDCs) through digital solutions and public-private partnerships; - Supporting developing countries in representing their interests in the multilateral trading system and in the WTO. The program is co-funded by different donors. At the beginning of 2025, the EU joined the Alliance as a new donor through co-funding the GIZ program. The EU contribution to the Alliance focusses on strengthening trade facilitation in least developed countries. Further co-financing comes from the World Trade Organisation (WTO) for the implementation of projects of the WTO Trade Facilitation Assistance Facility and by the EU Delegation to Madagascar for the implementation of an Alliance project in the country. Structure of the PST program The overall objective of the project is: In countries of the Global South, government, private actors or non-governmental organizations are equipped with improved instruments and competencies for the further development of the multilateral trading system for a Just Transition. The program is structured in 4 different Outputs: Output 1: Selected countries of the Global South are equipped with options for action for an inclusive, economic, and ecologically sustainable development of the multilateral trading system. Output 2: Proven trade facilitation instruments are embedded in selected countries of the Global South. Output 3: Innovative, climate and environmentally friendly approaches to trade facilitation have been further developed. Output 4: Trade facilitation instruments are embedded in selected LDCs. The project countries are specified in the Terms of Reference. The PST program seeks the services of a consulting firm to provide technical experts under different short-term expert (STE) pools, which can be deployed according to the project proposals and operational plans of each project country. The services will be delivered mainly by short-term experts in form of technical and administrative services for the development and implementation of specific trade facilitation measures in partner countries. The services also cover cross-cutting areas such as stakeholder engagement, workshop and training facilitation, and process management. Specifically, in the context of the respective in-country project workplans, the experts are foreseen to provide expertise in technical fields aimed at change management and capacity building of the respective identified border agencies. The services to be delivered in the project countries include: - Conducting analyses and gap assessments on specific IT solutions or processes for Customs and other border agencies - Business process engineering of customs and logistics procedures - Technically oversee the implementation of IT solutions by IT solution providers - Support Customs and other partner agencies in developing and implementing change management plans - Developing and facilitating public-private dialogue formats - Developing training materials and conducting trainings (specifically train the trainer approaches) - Potentially, support for the scoping of Global Alliance for Trade Facilitation projects through fact finding missions and concept/proposal development[LL2.1]. Several new projects will be designed in the coming months. Potential countries for these new projects include Brazil, Cote d"Ivoire, Kenya, India, Indonesia, South Africa. Specifically, the following technical areas within respective work packages are covered through services provided by the STE pools: Work package 1. Customs modernisation and digitisation, including change management and process optimisation - Stabilizing and upgrading (ASYCUDA) and other customs management systems, - Reviewing customs management processes and drafting standard operating procedures (SOPs), - Supporting customs in piloting and rolling-out newly developed IT solutions or re-engineered processes; including specifically for airfreight and express clearance procedures. Work package 2. Support for specific Customs procedures - Improving customs workflows for tariff valuation and classification, fall-back and continuity procedures, - Development and roll-out of advance ruling systems. Work package 3. Risk management, including Authorised Economic Operator Schemes - Review existing risk management approaches, - Revision of selectivity rules, - Gap analysis of the policy and regulatory framework and on-the-ground implementation, - Development and proposal of improved risk management systems, approaches, or specific rules, adaptation or extension of existing approaches and systems to cover additional specialised cases, such as perishable goods, express shipments, or low value shipments, - Development and implementation of preferential schemes for trusted economic operators (Authorised economic operator schemes), - Pre-arrival processing of manifest information to trigger risk analysis, - Post Clearance Audits. Work package 4. Import and export permits/ certificates - Implementation of the IPPC ePhyto certification solution, - Development and implementation of processes / digital solutions for issuing (electronic) certificates for fish exports (eFish) as well as for animal products (eVet), - Digitisation of line Ministry agencies" import/export permit or certification processes (e.g. by Ministry of Agriculture, Bureau of Standards, Animal health board, etc.), - Process re-engineering, improvement of phytosanitary risk management systems, - Integration of the approvals/permits into the respective customs management systems and any other relevant platform (e.g. trade single windows), - Revision of workflows and processes. Since the focus of this tender lies on the provision of technical expertise through the mobilisation of short-term experts, the contractor is expected to implement rigorous processes for the selecting, preparing, training and steering the experts assigned to carry out the advisory services.

sig_a9621991a0ec5f1287b9.buyer_name: Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs
sig_a9621991a0ec5f1287b9.description:
Maintaining and swiftly empowering a digitally competent working society that contributes to a productive and competitive economy despite demographic change and skills shortages is in the strategic interest of the Federal Government. Securing the skills base is crucial, in particular, for the competitiveness of companies. In view of an ageing society, there is an urgent need for action to keep employees in businesses under good and healthy working conditions for as long as possible, to tap into unused domestic potential and to make the working world more inclusive and diverse. Digital technologies and, above all, Artificial Intelligence (AI) offer the opportunity to keep people with age-related, cognitive or mental impairments in the labour market or to integrate them for longer and in better health, and to create an environment suited to older people and those with disabilities. The research contract to be awarded (performance period: 2027–2028) aims to identify the opportunities and needs of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and workers with impairments regarding the use of technological support in the workplace and thus to unlock labour potential with the aid of digitalisation and AI. Since there is as yet no systematic and comprehensive presentation of this, there is a need for practice-oriented and practicable scientific research on how SMEs can support employees with impairments in the workplace through the use of new technologies (e.g. AI). A contribution is also to be made to safeguarding the experiential knowledge of employees and strengthening existing (advisory) structures by supporting higher-level institutions (e.g. inclusion offices, chambers of industry and commerce, top-level business associations) in advising SMEs on issues relating to digital transformation. The research contract is being tendered Europe-wide as a competitive dialogue with a preceding call for competition. The services may be provided by a consortium. In order to achieve the set objectives, the contractors implementing the research project must perform at least the following work packages. The precise design is to be explained by the tenderers within the framework of the competitive dialogue: 1. Basic research and needs analysis: o Conducting an empirical-exploratory study to identify and systematically present the needs of SMEs and their employees with impairments. o Preparation of an overview of suitable technological and AI-based solutions. o Suitability testing of AI technologies for specific fields of work; if they are not suitable, the need for alternative solutions is to be demonstrated. 2. Implementation strategies and implementation: o Development of implementation proposals and assistance for the implementation and long-term use of the identified technologies. o Identification and creation of target-group-appropriate information resources and channels. o Integration of feedback and evaluation through a co-creative approach. 3. Review and adaptation: o Review and testing of the developed information resources and channels, as well as their refinement and adaptation. o Examination of the effectiveness of the (AI) support instruments. 4. Dissemination including a broad-impact support service across the board: o Continuous dissemination to enhance the public profile of the project objectives and results. Addressees of the research contract: scientific institutions, universities and research institutions. Subject matter and addressees of the research measure: SMEs and higher-level institutions, which are to be involved accordingly in the implementation of the project. The perspectives of affected workers, self-representation, advisory and self-help organisations and associations of and for people with disabilities must also be taken into account. sig_a9a00a345ccc32478c62.description: The Norwegian Public Roads Administration invites contractors and suppliers to a market meeting 20 October 2026 at 9:30 a.m. at the Quality Airport Hotel Stavanger. Register via KGV by 30.09.2026 with information on how many participants from the contractor/consultant, their position and contact information (Name, email). The aim of the project E39 Smiene – Harestad is to build a new four-lane road that connects the E39 Rogfast tunnels with the existing E39 at Smiene (north of the Eiganes tunnel) and thereby contribute to a continuous four-lane and high standard road from Sandnes to Bokn. E39 Smiene-Harestad, includes i.a.: • 4.7 km of open air four lane roads, • Connection to the Smiene junction • New two-level crossings o Tasta junction o Finnestad junction and o Harestad junction • Three bridges of 98 m, 90m and 24m respectively. • Foot and cycle path • 400m Environment culvert • and related technical installations. The E39 Smiene-Harestad shall open at the same time as the E39 Rogfast. The project, together with E39 Rogfast, will be able to connect Western Norway in a new way. Western Norway and Norway are in an increasingly tough national and international competition situation for people and resources. E39 Smiene-Harestad together with E39 Rogfast will open to greater synergy, freedom and expanded living and labour market area for the population. This can contribute to increased business growth in the area. The project notice is expected to be published in 2027. One-to-one meetings can be held for a period after the market meeting.
sig_a9a00a345ccc32478c62.title: Market meeting E39 Smiene-Harestad

sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.description: The objective of the Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure (CICI) program is to advance scientific discovery and innovation by enhancing the security and privacy of cyberinfrastructure. CICI supports efforts to develop, deploy and integrate cybersecurity that will benefit the broader scientific community by securing science data, computation, collaborations workflows, and infrastructure. CICI recognizes the unique nature of modern, complex, data-driven, distributed, rapid, and collaborative science and the breadth of infrastructure and requirements across scientific disciplines, practitioners, researchers, and projects. CICI seeks proposals in four program areas: 1. Usable and Collaborative Security for Science (UCSS): Projects in this program area should support novel and/or applied security and usability research that facilitates scientific collaboration, encourages the adoption of security into the scientific workflow, and helps create a holistic, integrated security environment that spans the entire scientific cyberinfrastructure ecosystem. 2. Reference Scientific Security Datasets (RSSD): Projects in this program area should leverage instrumented cyberinfrastructure to capture metadata from scientific workflows and workloads as reference data artifacts that can help support reproducible security research, testing and evaluation. 3. Transition to Cyberinfrastructure Resilience (TCR): Projects in this program area should improve the robustness, trustworthiness, integrity, and/or resilience of scientific cyberinfrastructure through testing, evaluation, hardening, validation, and technology transition of novel cybersecurity research. The TCR area further encourages transition activities that advance the deployment and use of reproducibility in CI, workflows, and data. 4. Integrity, Provenance, and Authenticity for Artificial Intelligence Ready Data (IPAAI): Projects in this program area should enhance confidence and reproducibility in AI produced scientific results by improving the integrity, provenance, and authenticity of scientific datasets used by Artificial Intelligence systems.
sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.title: Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure

sig_ae09df885b46a839920c.buyer_name: City of Helsinki, Urban Environment Division
sig_ae09df885b46a839920c.description: This document is not a procurement notice or invitation to tender, but a request for information. The Urban Environment Division of the City of Helsinki (hereinafter referred to as the contracting authority) is preparing the procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness. The objective of the procurement is to acquire and implement an infrastructure construction monitoring system that enables the management of infrastructure project contracts in field conditions using modern digital tools. The subject of the procurement is a monitoring system in which project-related data, documents, communication and monitoring take place centrally through a single system. The system will improve the situational awareness of contracts and information flow between different stakeholders, speed up reactions to identified shortcomings and reduce the nuisance caused to city residents by infrastructure projects. This is a new procurement and currently the City of Helsinki does not have a system intended for the management and monitoring of the implementation phase of infrastructure construction contracts. Currently, project-related data is scattered across different systems, operating models vary by contract and contractor, a large proportion of communication takes place by email, and entries related to contract management processes, such as reporting, site diaries and handling of shortcomings, are made manually and on paper. The Urban Environment Division has previously piloted and test-used digital tools intended for the management of infrastructure sites, and based on these, significant benefits have been observed, especially in the preparation of inspection reports and the sharing of information between various parties. The infrastructure construction monitoring system, which is the subject of the procurement, will be acquired as a ready-made software as a service (SaaS), including software licences, support and maintenance services, complementary expert services related to the software service including product consulting, customer-specific minor development and training services, as well as implementation in the contracting authority's operating environment. The implementation includes necessary definitions, configurations, development and integration measures, testing and user training. The objective is that the acquired system will be put into use in all new infrastructure construction contracts and selected ongoing projects based on project-specific assessment. The objective of the procurement is that the acquired monitoring system has been put into use by the end of June 2026. Further information on the subject of the procurement is described in the document Description of the subject of the procurement. The purpose of this request for information is to survey the market regarding the services in question and to obtain information concerning the procurement so that the procurement can be carried out appropriately. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out this procurement. This is an enquiry/request for information concerning a planned procurement. We kindly ask you to notify us if, in your view, the response contains trade secrets or other confidential information. We kindly ask you to specify and clearly mark this information. Documents containing potential confidential information can be delivered securely via secure email at https://securemail.hel.fi Responses provided in the request for information are not binding on the supplier, and responding is not a prerequisite for participation in the subsequent actual tendering procedure. Responding or not responding to the request for information does not affect a potential supplier's position in the actual tendering procedure. No compensation is paid for responding to the request for information. We kindly ask you to answer the questions presented in the request for information Forms survey and the request for information attachment List of Requirements as comprehensively as possible. Responses are requested to be written in the fields provided alongside the questions. Responses (completed list of requirements) are requested to be returned by 17.11.2025 at 16.15 by email to kymp.icthankinnat@hel.fi The email subject line must be marked "Infrarakentamisen valvonnan ja tilannekuvan sovelluksen hankinta, vastaukset tietopyyntöön". Responses to the request for information Forms form are requested to be submitted by 17.11.2025 at 16.15 Link: https://forms.office.com/e/m2RFGkJH98

sig_ae1218b6b3b789cf0b0d.description: This NOFO aims to foster partnerships that support collaboration between CDC and the Indonesian Ministry of Health (MOH) in achieving global health security goals, implementing International Health Regulations core principles, and effectively preventing, detecting, and responding to public health threats. Projects considered for this opportunity should focus on strengthening capacity in five key public health areas: Real-Time Surveillance and Reporting, Laboratory Systems, Workforce Development, Emergency Management and Response, and Health System Strengthening and Services Delivery. These projects should build upon the existing public health infrastructure and activities initiated in the previous CDC project CDC-RFA-GH20-2120. Additionally, they should address recommendations from the Joint External Evaluation 2023, align with MOH strategic plans, prioritize gaps identified in the National Action Plan for Health Security, and incorporate robust monitoring and evaluation of program performance and progress.

sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.buyer_original: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik
sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.description: In the field of traditional software, Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) – that is, parts lists containing information about software components and their dependencies – have long been in use and are even required by the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). This requirement also applies to AI systems, yet the idea of an SBOM specific to AI systems is relatively new. Initial approaches therefore carry the risk that they do not cover all necessary aspects with regard to the transparency of the AI supply chain. In this project, the concept "SBOM for AI - Minimum Elements" published within the G7 framework is to be put into practice and a technical implementation of the defined criteria developed for this purpose. The SBOM for AI is to be generated automatically and output in a suitable format. The developed implementation is subsequently to be made available to all stakeholders in order to make an important contribution to the cybersecurity of AI systems.
sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.title: Project 1034: Technical implementation of an SBOM for AI (SBOM4AI)

sig_b1f961554688efa86265.description: KS Digital has, on behalf of the Committee Council, established a work group that shall review how the municipal sector can cooperate on the future childhood and school administration systems (OAS/SAS), digital ecosystems and possibilities for future joint procurements. The work includes both education and school administrative systems (OAS/SAS), the digital eco-system included in them, and how the municipal sector can strengthen coordination, standardisation and any future joint procurements. As a part of this work, we invite the supplier market to a dialogue. We want insight into how the market assesses developments in the area, what technological and organisational possibilities exist, and how the municipal sector and the supplier market together can contribute to a more open, coherent and future orientated digital ecosystem for the education sector. The work is anchored in a reported need from the municipalities for stronger coordination in relation to requirements, standardisation, architecture, data sharing, procurements and further development of digital systems in the area of adolescence. The aim is not to define a new system, but to assess how the municipal sector together can contribute to a more coherent, open and future orientated digital ecosystem for children, youths, guardians, employees, managers, owners and associated services. An important goal is also to contribute to a supplier market that supports this development, through clear common needs, standards and framework conditions that stimulate innovation and sustainable development of the systems. Information on the market dialogue including registration will be in the tender https://ksdigital.no/markedsdialoger-og-anskaffelser/

sig_b4cb85529a2d918a2c26.description: The purpose of this combined Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 35 and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) under 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 200.204 (henceforth referred to as “BAA”) is to solicit research proposals for submission to the U.S. Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) for funding consideration. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), for the Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C), is issued under the provisions of paragraph 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which provides for the acquisition of basic, applied, and advanced research and that part of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement. This will be done through the competitive selection of proposals, and 10 U.S.C. 4001, 10 U.S.C. 4021, and 10 U.S.C. 4022, which provide the authorities for issuing awards under this announcement for basic, applied, and advanced research. The definitions of basic and applied research may be found at 32 CFR 22.105. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA and selected for award are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public Law 98-369, "The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984" and subsequent amendments. The Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) is seeking artificial intelligence research and development whitepapers and proposals in support of new technologies and translational research-based approaches that support the identification, alignment, and exploitation of basic, applied, and advanced research. AI2C’s foundational research mission spans basic research (budget activity 6.1) and applied research (budget activity 6.2) as defined by 32 CFR 22.105 but may include advanced technology development (budget activity 6.3) and advanced component development and prototypes (budget activity 6.4) when opportunities arise to directly or indirectly help achieve AI2C’s mission. This publication constitutes a BAA for awards as contemplated in FAR 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 as well as a merit-based, competitive procedure in accordance with the Department of Defense Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARS) at 32 CFR 22.315(a) and the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment Other Transaction Guide version 2.0 dated July 2023.

sig_b520decbe8b7969a9634.description: Enhanced Information Service for Emergency Calls (EISEC) or caller line identification (CLI) enables fire control room operators to confirm the caller's location swiftly. This is a critical first step in the call handling process, since the line could be 'cut', leaving the location unknown. EISEC technology provided by call handling agencies allows the billing address of the phone from which emergency calls are being made to be displayed to the control room operator. This speeds up the information process. This technology can also be used to locate the whereabouts of mobile phone callers, identifying the cell network from which they are calling. Additional information: Provides Location of caller on emergency lines

sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.description: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse The project comprises a modern and comprehensive communications solution that integrates numerous central components. The following expectations are placed on the tendered service: In the area of telephony and voice (formerly HessenVoice), contemporary voice communication is provided that replaces and expands existing systems. In addition, the softphone functionality enables telephony to be used directly via PC or mobile end devices without the need for additional hardware. Webex is currently used as the web conferencing solution (VKS); however, the solution should also support future developments and hybrid working forms in the best possible way. In addition, chat and messaging functions create a secure and efficient platform for text-based team communication. High requirements apply to security and data protection as well as accessibility in order to offer all employees secure and inclusive access to the solution. The operator model defines clear responsibilities and processes for operation, while accompanying training measures support the introduction and foster acceptance. The solution will be fully compatible with the HessenPC and enable secure, high-performance access via the HessenNetz connection. Another component is the provision as a price-per-port Full Managed Service, which impresses with transparent pricing and comprehensive service management. Manufacturer neutrality is respected in order to avoid dependencies and ensure long-term flexibility and openness to competition. The procurement and implementation of the tendered UCC solution takes place with special consideration of the requirements for information security, data protection and interoperability with existing authorities' infrastructures. For use in public administration, compliance with the compendium for internal organisational telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement (KomTK ) published by the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) must be ensured. This guideline defines binding security measures - including technical, organisational and infrastructural requirements - for telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement and serves as a benchmark for the planning, operation and safeguarding of the offered solution. The protection of personal data is a central criterion in the selection and implementation of communication systems. The legal requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation ("GDPR") and the Hesse Data Protection Act ("HDSIG") provide for safeguarding the rights and freedoms of data subjects and consistently implementing data protection principles - such as lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality. While Unified Communications solutions are primarily designed for applications with a normal protection requirement in accordance with the specifications of the Federal Office for Information Security ("BSI") when using cloud components, there are scenarios in which a higher level of security is required. In cases where a higher level of security is required, an on-premise system is frequently used, which is operated entirely within the own IT infrastructure and can thus better meet the requirements for a high or very high protection requirement. By operating in a controlled environment, a higher degree of control over data flows, access protection, encryption as well as emergency and recovery measures can be ensured. Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solutions represent a central component of modern IT infrastructures and serve the integrated networking of a wide variety of communication and collaboration services. In order to meet the operational requirements for reliability, security, scalability and interoperability, specific technical prerequisites are indispensable. These requirements form the basis for the selection, implementation and operation of a high-performance UCC solution that ensures efficient and uninterrupted cooperation within the organisation. In order to bring about rapid project success, close cooperation between the contractor and the contracting authority is necessary. The contractor MUST closely coordinate with internal and external stakeholders on the part of the contracting authority as part of the implementation in order to take account of necessary and inevitable interactions with other systems of the contracting authority (e.g. firewall, network, etc.) as early as possible in the implementation of the project and to implement necessary adjustments and interventions on these systems as smoothly and time-critically as possible. The service contents presented in this specification MUST be provided by the contractor for the contractually defined period in full and with ultimate responsibility for the outcome, flexibly according to the respective needs of the contracting authority in the form of a "Managed Service". Within the scope of this tender, special emphasis is placed on the accessibility of the Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solution to be supplied. Accessibility means that the solution can be used unrestrictedly and equally by all users, regardless of individual impairments or restrictions. This includes in particular people with visual, hearing, motor or cognitive impairments. The detailed service requirements can be found in the respective chapters of the service specification (Chapters 1 - 7).
sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.title: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse

sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.description: UHS is seeking to engage with interested parties to discuss and refine an opportunity to become a strategic endoscopy partner to the Trust. UHS provides a regional endoscopy service to a population of 3m+, offering a comprehensive range of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Following a fire earlier this year, UHS has reviewed its long-term endoscopy requirements and is considering a new purpose-built regional diagnostic endoscopy centre situated close to the main hospital. UHS has existing endoscopy equipment to the value of approximately £8-10m. This will need to be refreshed throughout this contract. UHS has an indicative budget of £20-25m for the design and construction of the new centre. This will be designed to meet current and projected future endoscopy and motility needs, 'a one-stop-shop' and be an important centre to both trial new technology and techniques and provide training for the next generation of the endoscopy workforce. This opportunity is to explore and discuss how a partnership approach may drive better outcomes for patients, for innovation, for UHS clinicians, and for the partner[S(1.1][L(1.2]. This opportunity may include, but not necessarily be limited to: 1: Provision of endoscopy equipment to a new offsite location, both for the use of clinicians undertaking NHS clinical activity, and for use as a test bed for innovation and new technique development, and for use within a training environment. 2: Regional Training Centre: The physical co-location of experienced UHS staff, clinicians, data, patients with an industry partner seeking to promote best practice and create future workforce. 3: Joint Innovation Deal & Test Bed: The provision of a live, data-rich NHS environment to validate new technology, and techniques, for example artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic tools and ergonomic designs and potentially the exploitation of emerging shared Intellectual Property. This would also include SME and VCSE participation for research and innovation. 4: Commercial Sponsorship Opportunity with Associated Rights and Benefits: In addition to the core procurement opportunities above, there is potential to explore a complementary commercial sponsorship arrangement, which may include the provision of value-in-kind goods and/or services that support contract delivery. This strategic partnership approach would identify and agree a range of associated rights and benefits for suppliers who also become sponsors. These may include appropriate sponsor recognition, opportunities for collaboration and innovation, shared learning, thought leadership engagement, and other mutually agreed activities that support the objectives of all parties. UHS, with support from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), is trialling the integration of commercial sponsorship into this procurement opportunity to explore how strategic partnerships can deliver additional value while supporting the successful delivery of contract outcomes. Whilst this notice is not intended to create a commitment to a contract, it is running alongside a live funded NHS capital project to develop designs and take forward the concept of a regional endoscopy centre. This hybrid procurement and sponsorship model is being piloted by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and UHS, offering potential suppliers a unique opportunity to play an active role in delivering a best-in-class new facility for patients: supporting improved care, championing innovation and delivering lasting benefits for all parties. To ensure fair and open competition in any future procurement, the developing design and specification will remain supplier-neutral and will not be tailored to any specific manufacturer, supplier or solution.
sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.title: Co-Developing the 'Digestive Disease Centre' at University Hospital Southampton, Hybrid Procurement and Sponsorship Opportunity

sig_b958b4ac5ca772f5ee3b.description: The National Institute on Aging intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications for the Claude D. Pepper Older Americans Independence Centers (OAICs) award. The goal of the OAIC program is to establish centers of excellence in geriatrics research and research education to increase scientific knowledge leading to better ways to maintain or restore independence in older persons. OAIC awards are designed to develop or strengthen programs that focus on, and sustain progress in, a key area of aging research related to the mission of the OAIC program. Applicants should identify an area of focus in which progress could contribute to greater independence for substantial populations of older persons and offer opportunities for education in aging research. This area of focus should be a common theme around which all proposed OAIC activities are organized. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize the P30 activity code. Investigators with expertise and insights into this area of aging research are encouraged to begin to consider applying for this new NOFO.

sig_b995ddcaa48c6826f568.description: Open-quantity framework agreements are concluded for development services required by DB Systemtechnik. DB Systemtechnik works on extremely demanding digitalisation projects in the field of rail vehicle technology. The project portfolio thus encompasses challenges of the entire railway system, i.e. rail vehicles, their components, the infrastructure and the corresponding interfaces. For the initiation, definition, planning, control and successful completion of these technically demanding projects, DB Systemtechnik is looking for experienced partners with broad methodological expertise and industry know-how for consulting and project management services.; DB Systemtechnik uses various sensors, measurement and data loggers to acquire, process, transmit to the land side and evaluate process, diagnostic and operating data from rail vehicles and railway assets. For the development of customer-specific and standard assemblies based on embedded technology and railway-compatible measurement and sensor modules, DB Systemtechnik is looking for development partners and suppliers. The services cover all steps, from conception to the approval-ready hardware product that can be implemented in the vehicle by the client, including the necessary basic software. The suppliers are experienced in the development of railway-approved embedded hardware and software and have established certified development and production processes. They master documented series-delivery and quality processes and are experienced in supply chain and obsolescence management in the railway sector.; Within the scope of digitalisation projects in the railway sector, DB Systemtechnik develops customer-specific products which, among other things, require the development, modification and operation of specific applications. For this purpose, suppliers and development partners are sought who can efficiently develop reliable, robust and secure software solutions and use structured and proven development methods and certifiable development processes for this purpose. The suppliers have comprehensive knowledge and experience in the field of architecture, software development, CI/CD, software testing and quality assurance for embedded systems in critical environments. All software solutions must comply with the standards for approval in rail vehicles and operation in the railway sector.
sig_b995ddcaa48c6826f568.title: Developer service provider pool for DB Systemtechnik

sig_bc36d4f46e434011d441.description: It is the ambition of the Welsh Government to develop a thriving and confident agriculture sector in Wales built around innovation and growth, to rise to the challenges we face and make most of the opportunities available. In July 2025 the Welsh Government published its Sustainable Farming Scheme designed to ensure Welsh Government support for agriculture in Wales delivers against the four Sustainable Land Management objectives of the Agriculture (Wales) Act: - Produce food and other goods in a sustainable manner - Mitigate and adapt to climate change - Maintain and enhance the resilience of ecosystems and the benefits they provide - Conserve and enhance the countryside and cultural resources, promote public access to and engagement with them, and to sustain the Welsh language and promote and facilitate its use. Innovation will play a key role in delivering this scheme. In 2023, the Welsh Government published an Innovation Strategy for Wales. Innovation in food and Agri-Food Tech was seen as a key part of Wales’s future economic development. In late 2023, the Welsh Government published an Agri-tech action plan for Wales. The development and adoption of Agri-Tech and Precision Agri-Tech is a strategic area of growth for the Welsh economy and one the Welsh Government deems requiring of focussed attention and a road map for development. The action plan has four priorities: 1. Accelerate Home Grown Welsh Agri-tech Capabilities. 2. Drive on-farm adoption to achieve productivity and efficiencies (incl. Environmental) gains ‘more for less’. 3. Deliver environmental benefits and help transition to Net Zero. 4. Support educational and skills development to equip future and existing agricultural professionals to exploit Agri-tech to its fullest. SCOPE: Cattle mortality data may provide valuable information on animal health, disease emergence and herd management. However, there are opportunities to make better use of mortality data alongside wider animal health surveillance information to generate timely intelligence that supports veterinary decision-making, farmer engagement and evidence-based policy. Improving the collection, access, interpretation and communication of mortality intelligence could enable earlier identification of disease risks, encourage preventative herd health management and support the delivery of the Animal health and welfare framework | GOV.WALES for Wales, while contributing to the objectives of the Sustainable Farming Scheme. We are therefore seeking innovative technologies, digital tools, data-driven approaches or other novel solutions that improve the collection, integration, analysis and application of cattle mortality intelligence to support proactive animal health management. sig_bc517cb3a5e61dfdbab5.description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the government of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is establishing the foundations for participation in high-integrity carbon markets, including Article 6, CORSIA and voluntary carbon markets. While progress has been made through the establishment of a carbon market framework and supporting governance arrangements, further support is needed to operationalise these systems across government, strengthen institutional coordination, and enable Bangladesh to use carbon markets to support delivery of its NDC 3.0 unconditional mitigation targets. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to strengthen Bangladesh's carbon market governance, authorisation processes, MRV, reporting and institutional readiness. Working with relevant government agencies, including MoEFCC, DoE, the Power Division, Ministry of Finance and other line ministries, the project will support practical implementation of carbon market rules, CORSIA readiness, UNFCCC reporting requirements, and inclusive, high-integrity market participation. Key outputs are expected to include governance and coordination tools, an authorisation and safeguards toolkit, CORSIA readiness and reporting support, a structured government capacity-building programme, and sector readiness briefs identifying future carbon market investment opportunities. The project aims to strengthen Bangladesh's ability to participate in high-integrity carbon markets, unlock climate finance, improve institutional capability, and support implementation of national climate targets. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

sig_bcc2350d3e85d43e278e.description: Negotiated procedure without prior call for competition. The delivery can only be carried out by a specific economic operator for the following reasons: absence of competition for technical reasons. Explanation: The award of the procurement of passenger counting sensors and the necessary adjustments to the MOBILEguide software can only be carried out by INIT GmbH, as there is no competition for technical reasons in accordance with § 13 paragraph 2 no. 3 b) SektVO. The defined requirements in their extensive abundance and combination cannot be met by any other potential tenderers. In this case, only INIT GmbH is able to fulfil the listed requirements. The on-board computers used on Rheinbahn vehicles originate from the company INIT GmbH. Only the company INIT GmbH possesses the necessary technical knowledge to carry out any system additions to the on-board computer software in order to be able to connect these to the central component of the ITCS of the Rheinbahn AG. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, the software of the central component of an ITCS and the software of the on-board computers used on vehicles in public transport only possess the same processes if they are procured from the same system manufacturer. The processes are manufacturer-specific standards and as such are subject to trade secrets; they are therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, a bidirectional interface between the central ITCS and the on-board computers used on the vehicles as a mobile component of an ITCS is only fully functional if the participating interface partners are procured from the same system manufacturer. The interface is a manufacturer-specific standard and as such is subject to trade secrets; it is therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. As a result of the examination for the procurement of the central components of the ITCS, it must be determined that the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point regarding mandatory requirements to be fulfilled for the services to be procured. Consequently, a public call for competition would be misleading and the associated effort would be temporally and economically inappropriate for all market participants. The procurement law limits of the public contracting authority's freedom to define the scope of services are adhered to, provided that the definition is objectively justified by the subject matter of the contract, the contracting authority has provided comprehensible objective, contract-related and actually existing reasons for this, and the definition does not discriminate against other economic operators. An artificial and therefore impermissible restriction of competition does not exist. The date of the conclusion of the contract with INIT GmbH cannot be entered, as this day is only possible 10 calendar days after the publication of this notice. The procurement office cannot determine exactly at the time of entry when the period of 10 calendar days begins, as the publication is carried out by the Official Journal and generally takes several days that cannot be precisely determined. The procurement office therefore points out that the conclusion of the contract between the Rheinbahn AG and INIT GmbH will take place 10 days after the publication of this notice. Precise information on the deadlines for lodging appeals: §160 para. 3 GWB reads: The application is inadmissible insofar as 1. the applicant has identified the asserted infringement of procurement regulations before submitting the review application and has not complained about it to the contracting authority within a period of ten calendar days; the expiry of the period according to § 134 paragraph 2 remains unaffected, 2. infringements of procurement regulations that are recognisable from the notice are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders specified in the notice, 3. infringements of procurement regulations that only become recognisable in the procurement documents are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders, 4. more than 15 calendar days have passed since receipt of the notification from the contracting authority that it does not intend to remedy a complaint. Sentence 1 does not apply to an application for a declaration of the ineffectiveness of the contract according to § 135 paragraph 1 number 2. § 134 paragraph 1 sentence 2 remains unaffected. Name and address of the contractor: Official name: INIT GmbH Postal address: Käppelestraße 4-10; Town: Karlsruhe NUTS code: Karlsruhe Postal code: 76131 Country: Germany Internet address: https://www.initse.com/

sig_be66e1ff3b415b7ed9d0.description:
Despite a grown awareness of the consequences of plastic pollution for the marine environment, there is a persistent threat from ALDFG which is newly introduced into the marine environment or has in some cases already been located there for decades. The aim of UNSEA is therefore to systematically prevent the further input of ALDFG into the North and Baltic Seas, to reduce the negative ecological and socio-economic impacts and to identify and salvage legacy waste, particularly in ecologically sensitive areas. Both commercial, sideline and recreational fishing in the North and Baltic Seas are to be addressed. Aquaculture and mariculture as well as inland fisheries are excluded from the project scope. Existing requirements and agreements of relevant national and international legal provisions are currently still fragmented, without financial backing and are partly up for debate for various reasons. UNSEA is therefore intended to bring together the various sub-aspects in a coherent framework for action, focusing on the implementation of cost-efficient and operational measures. In doing so, it is necessary to rethink the handling of waste fishing gear from the fishing industry in a new and holistic way, to anchor circular economy principles in the management of fishing gear and thereby also address specific findings such as dolly ropes (scuff protection threads on bottom trawls) and net sections from repair work that are frequently found in the marine environment. The project is intended to provide the necessary seed funding over its term and in parallel create long-term structures with clear responsibilities for perpetuation by the federal and state governments. For the first time, a cross-sectoral mechanism is to be established and implemented, which also includes the exchange of knowledge and information. The project can build on existing legal framework conditions, recommendations from research and politics, preliminary work within the framework of measure and action plans and voluntary industry initiatives. In particular, the 2016 established Round Table on Marine Litter (RTM, www.muell-im-meer.de), which is coordinated by the Umweltbundesamt and the State of Lower Saxony, has already carried out comprehensive conceptual preliminary work that can be used as a basis for work for UNSEA. Through this, insights into the dimension of the problem were gained and suitable methods as well as existing and missing elements in the chain from search to the most environmentally sound recycling possible of ALDFG were identified. Furthermore, the results and recommendations of two pilot projects for the implementation of the recovery of lost fishing gear in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (MV) and Schleswig-Holstein (SH) are to be taken into account. While the project in MV has already been completed (https://www.wwf.de/fileadmin/fm-wwf/Publikationen-PDF/Deutschland/WWF-Abschlussbericht-Landesprojekt-Verlorene-Fischereigeraete.pdf), the publication of the final report of the SH project is expected for August 2026 with planned follow-up activities for the mapping and recovery of fishing gear waste. The work under UNSEA is to be closely coordinated with these activities to avoid duplication of work. sig_bf044cea98ad0eddb9c3.description: The subject of the procurement is the provision of maintenance and support services for telecommunications network devices and related network services (hereinafter the "Service"). The procurement covers comprehensive maintenance, monitoring, support and operational services for VR's telecommunications network environment, including network devices located in datacentres, offices, rolling stock (trains and buses) and other operational locations. The Service also includes the maintenance of certain related network services required for the operation of the telecommunications environment. The Service includes, but is not limited to, the following: - Service transition and implementation; - 24/7 monitoring of the telecommunications network environment; - Incident management and fault resolution; - Replacement of failed network devices in accordance with the agreed service levels; - Device configuration changes and other agreed maintenance activities; - Network monitoring, preventive maintenance and operational support; - Service management and designated service management personnel; - Maintenance of network documentation; - Reporting, including service level, capacity and operational reporting; - Integration with VR's agreed service management and ticketing solutions; - Other maintenance, support and expert services related to the telecommunications network environment, ordered separately where required. sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.description: The Public Affairs Section (PAS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia, highlight shared values, and promote bilateral cooperation in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Please see Section C. Program Description for more information. This Annual Program Statement (APS) outlines our funding priorities and the strategic themes we will focus on in FY2025, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Based on availability of funding, PAS Tunis will award grants, fixed amount awards, or cooperative agreements between a minimum of $10,000 and up to a maximum of $200,000 (U.S. dollars) each for projects that advance the priorities outlined in this APS. Please carefully follow all instructions in the full announcement. Proposals that fail to conform to the requirements outlined in this APS will not be considered. All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. PAS Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen cultural, educational, professional, scientific, and business ties between the United States and Tunisia through programming that highlights shared values, strengthens people-to-people ties and institutional linkages, and promotes bilateral cooperation, and makes America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Competitive proposals must focus on at least one grant priority area outlined below. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: · Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. · Programs that strengthen relationships and linkages between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and cultural institutions. · Educational, artistic, and cultural programs, including programs that strengthen English language teaching and learning, music, musical theater, dance workshops, master classes, and performances, live theatre performances, art exhibitions, and sports and culinary diplomacy initiatives that increase mutual understanding between the people of the United States and Tunisia. · Programs, including podcasts, that promote economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, or that share U.S. experiences related to addressing community challenges, including the management of water or energy resources, waste management, urban design and planning, and preparing for and mitigating natural or human-caused disasters. · Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programming, including through the use new and immersive technologies, such as VR technology. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must address at least one of the six priority areas outlined below: · Economic Prosperity and Entrepreneurship: Initiatives that prioritize mutual prosperity, expand economic and commercial links between the United States and Tunisia, promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices, and that share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of increasing economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. · INNOVATION and Collaboration in science and technology: Initiatives that promote collaboration and academic partnerships in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) between U.S. and Tunisian academic and research institutions, non-governmental organizations, and private companies, as well as programs that promote interest in STEM education among young people. · EDUCATIONAL LINKAGES AND ENGLISH LANGUAGE : Initiatives that expand collaboration and partnerships between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and research institutions through programs and professional and academic exchanges; programs to strengthen English language instruction in Tunisian universities and colleges; programs to expand the teaching of English in sign language and braille; and other programs that support and promote English language learning among Tunisian youth. · LEADERSHIP: Initiatives that provide leadership training inspired by U.S. experiences, models, and best practices to Tunisian young people (high school and university students and young professionals) to help them become effective leaders in their communities and professional field of choice. Such training may include English language, public speaking and interpersonal communication, emotional intelligence, critical thinking and problem solving, financial literacy, goal-setting, and mental health management strategies. · MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Programs that leverage the “Mega-Decade in Sports” in North America (2023-2034) when the United States will host the 2025 FIFA World Club Cup, the 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, the 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics in Los Angeles, and the 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics in Salt Lake City, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values and demonstrate American excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. · Celebrating American Excellence AND U.S.-Tunisian Enduring Partnership: Programs that 1) celebrate U.S. scientific or sport prowess, innovation, economic dynamism, agricultural strength, and national parks and tourism during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence; 2) leverage people-to-people ties and promote the establishment of U.S-Tunisian institutional linkages through cultural diplomacy, including artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities that celebrate American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, cultural heritage protection, and film during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence and the 228th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia; AND/OR 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase awareness and understanding among broad elements of Tunisian society of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation.

sig_c0523eb82f29eae8f146.description: The Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg (UKHD) is one of the largest and most renowned medical centres in Germany. Every year, approximately 80.000 patients receive inpatient and semi-inpatient treatment in its specialist clinics, and more than 1.000.000 patients are cared for on an outpatient basis. The Heidelberg campus unites scientific institutes and clinics of the UKHD, offers rich opportunities for cooperation with the life science and humanities faculties of the University, and simultaneously maintains established co-operations with internationally renowned non-university large-scale research institutions. The increasing complexity of and growing demands on the IT infrastructure in healthcare require reliable and efficient management of the IT landscape. In the context of the UKHD, it is of decisive importance that operational and clinical applications run constantly available and without faults in order to ensure optimal patient care and smooth operation. Lot LOT-0001: Provision of implementation, project and operational services for IT applications in the hospital environment. As part of this procurement procedure, the University Hospital is issuing a framework agreement for the provision of support services in IT application management (anticipated) from 1 February 2027 for the following 4 years (planned) incl. extension options. A transition that is as gradual as possible to transfer the services from operations outsourced from the existing provider to an external service provider is planned for the period Q1/Q2 2027. The complete takeover of the provision of all contractual services into regular operations is to take place by 01.07.2027 at the latest. The Centre for Digitalisation and Information Technology (ZDI) of the Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg is operationally divided into individual areas. Supported by contractors as external service providers, they assume end-to-end responsibility regarding the IT of the respective core processes of the contracting authority in order to be able to ensure secure and stable operation, but also the further development of IT performance. Directly affected by the tender and the procurement subject are the areas for Operational Information Systems (BIS), for Hospital Information Systems (KIS), for Integration, Special Systems and Archiving (ISA) as well as directly the ZDI itself. The scope of the tender covers the service requirements of the client for operational services in application management. This includes, in particular, smooth application operation, the rapid and permanent rectification of incidents and problems, as well as releases, upgrades and updates in coordination with the client. Furthermore, this encompasses other supportive project services that are in a direct or close substantive connection with the aforementioned operational services. The future contractor is expected to provide comprehensive and holistic services within the framework of a managed service in order to implement the client's requirements regarding IT architecture, IT security and IT service integration. The integration of IT services based on the ITIL v4 framework must be provided holistically for all specialist areas. In this context, the client will manage the contractor(s) and provide the IT hardware required at the client's locations as well as some of the required software licences.
sig_c0523eb82f29eae8f146.title: Provision of implementation, project and operational services for IT applications in the hospital environment

sig_c0580f79e230c910a4cf.buyer_name: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
sig_c0580f79e230c910a4cf.description: In the past almost 20 years since the founding of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries (KKW) initiative, the framework conditions, market structures, value chains and challenges for the KKW have changed fundamentally. Hardly any sector has been as strongly affected by the effects of the change brought about by transformation, the platform economy, digitalisation and artificial intelligence as the KKW, with impacts including on creative production, distribution and the exploitation of rights. The coming years will be characterised by further profound technological, economic and social upheavals. Digitalisation (especially artificial intelligence), sustainability and new forms of audience engagement have become the central drivers of change. After almost 20 years, it is therefore time to take stock on the one hand, and to look ahead and create foundations for strategic options for action on the other. In order to be able to conduct the further strategy process on an evidence-based footing, a qualitative and quantitative baseline study on future projections for the KKW is to be commissioned. The last baseline study, 'Macroeconomic Perspectives of the Cultural and Creative Industries', also produced on behalf of the BMWE, dates from the year 2009. The study is intended to develop a projection for the coming decade in order to provide strategic responses to structural changes in the sector. The aim is to critically examine the future viability of the KKW, to identify risks and to develop a forecast of opportunities and trends. The study 'Cultural and Creative Industries 2037' (working title) is intended to provide a foundation for the long-term strategic orientation of political and economic steering instruments with the help of future-oriented and forecasted scenario analyses. For a future projection up to 2037, it is therefore crucial not only to extrapolate existing growth trajectories, but to systematically include structural breaks, new value creation logics and disruptive technological developments in the forecast. The Federal Government's projections on macroeconomic growth are to be appropriately taken into account as a basis here. The study is intended to create a scientific foundation for the strategic further development of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries initiative and, in doing so, to provide in particular a long-term strategic orientation for political and economic steering instruments. The strategy is aimed prospectively at decision-makers from politics, business and administration, as well as at the actors in the cultural and creative industries themselves, who want to jointly set the course for a sustainable, innovative and economically strong creative ecosystem for the next generation.
