sig_c1114644e365759a47be.description: The present notice is not intended to initiate a procurement procedure nor to prepare one. It serves solely for market consultation. The Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) is conducting a market consultation in preparation for a procurement in the area of BayernCloud Schule (hereinafter: ByCS), which provides digital applications and services for the Bavarian school community. The contracting authority is examining the future provision, further development, integration and operation of a digital board application for the ByCS. The existing application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software. The subject of the market consultation is the question of whether suitable market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing ByCS board or its code base, or to replace the existing ByCS board with another functionally and technically suitable board application. The aim of the market consultation is to obtain reliable information on solutions available on the market and fundamentally suitable for the described requirement. In particular, it is to be investigated whether an already available or adaptable board application can meet the functional, technical, data protection and operational requirements of the contracting authority and can be integrated, operated, maintained and further developed into the ByCS environment. Within the scope of the market consultation, insights are to be gained in particular as to whether and, if applicable, by whom the described services can be provided. Lot PAR-0001: Free State of Bavaria - Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) regarding tender for info services. The existing digital ByCS board application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software for use in in-person and remote phases of teaching. The application was developed on behalf of the Bavarian State Ministry of Education and Cultural Affairs as a component of BayernCloud Schule and is continuously developed further. In doing so, the application is to fulfil the following criteria in particular: - Platform-independent (device types, operating system) - Browser-based - Responsive design - Offline app / PWA - GDPR-compliant design - Accessible according to WCAG - Collaboration - Very good writing feel / high quality of pen input with palm rejection - Suitable for primary schools -> Simplicity - Special school scripts integrable with individual menus - WOPI connection - Files can be saved offline - Sharing mechanism / permissions between teachers and pupils - Import/export of PDF files and images - Integration of websites and videos - Customisations to ByCS possible (design, repositories, CSP, ...) - Set square and compass - Import of GGS files (previous format) possible Within the scope of the market consultation, insights should be provided in particular on - the extent to which market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing board application; - whether other board applications suitable for school use are already available on the market; - whether such applications can meet the functional and technical requirements of the contracting authority; - whether and under what conditions an alternative application can be integrated into the ByCS environment; - what technical, operational and economic risks are associated with the different solution variants. Please contact markterkundung@abante.de by 20 September 2026, 23.59 hrs at the latest if you are interested in participating in the local market consultation. Your participation will not be remunerated. There is also no entitlement to participate in any procurement procedure that may subsequently follow. The decision as to whether a procurement procedure must be carried out is precisely what is to be brought about by the local market consultation. In your initial enquiry, please state as detailed as possible what qualifies you and what capacities you have to provide the envisaged services if the contracting authority decides on a procurement on the market. This is necessary in order to be able to assess the seriousness of the enquiry.
sig_c1114644e365759a47be.title: Free State of Bavaria - Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) regarding tender for info services

sig_c18c574df88e52eea3b9.description: The Home Office (HO) is the government department responsible for safeguarding the nation through border control, immigration, passport issuance, policing, fire services, counter-terrorism and drugs policies. UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) plays an integral role in delivering this vision, managing millions of applications annually, enabling foreign nationals to visit, study, work or settle in the UK. As part of the evolution of existing services, UKVI pursues the transformation and modernisation of services in a manner that enhances customer experience and ensures accurate and efficient outcomes. One of the core services delivered by UKVI is the Life in the UK test, an essential component of the route to settlement in the UK and to UK citizenship. The Life in the UK Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service (LITUK) Project is procuring a new service; enabling the continued delivery of front-end services, balancing continuity with improvements and transformation. LITUK aims to move to a 'Digital-by-Default' approach, while upholding the rigorous standards necessary to support UKVI immigration decisions. The successful provider will deliver a service that combines technological innovation with security assurance, enabling customers to demonstrate their knowledge of life in the UK with confidence and convenience throughout their UK immigration journey. sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.description: The Bars of Admission (RAKs) in Germany are corporations under public law and currently represent over 160.000 admitted lawyers. Their legal basis is formed by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). There are a total of 27 Bars of Admission in Germany. The 11 Bars of Admission issuing the tender here are actively involved in the project and contribute their professional, organisational and technical requirements to the design. The participating chambers exhibit varying organisational structures, member numbers and IT landscapes, which underlines the need for a flexible and scalable solution. However, the various Bars of Admission are essentially subject to the same legal requirements, which are primarily dictated by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). In total, the eleven participating chambers currently look after around 132.000 members, who are administered and supported by approximately 370 employees. To support their tasks, 22 chambers currently use a software solution from DATEV eG. This solution covers core administrative processes, particularly in the areas of personnel administration, billing and complaint or case management. DATEV eG has terminated the existing software solution effective 31.12.2027. This decision makes timely planning and procurement of a suitable successor solution necessary. Against this background, the eleven local Bars of Admission have joined forces with the objective of replacing the currently used software solution, procuring a suitable successor solution and successfully introducing it. The project group is led and coordinated by five Bars of Admission (Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Hamm, Munich and Stuttgart). The aim is to procure a modern, high-performance and future-proof software solution that meets the specific requirements of the chambers and completely or with enhancements maps the previous functionalities of the DATEV software. In advance, a structured survey of the technical and functional requirements was conducted. This forms the basis for the drawn-up requirements catalogue. The DATEV software currently in use and to be replaced is utilised in the chambers for the following task areas: (1) Personnel administration: Administration of master data of natural and legal persons, admissions, status changes, specialist lawyer designations, training systems, resignations and reactivations. (2) Billing: Administration and billing of membership fees, charges, credit notes, etc. (3) Complaint management: Administration of professional law procedures, in particular complaints (4) Archiving and deletion: Archiving and deletion of data records from personnel and complaint management The software is deeply integrated into the work processes of users and forms a central basis for daily administrative work. Currently, the eleven participating Bars of Admission each operate independent instances of the DATEV software. While the basic functionalities are comparable in all chambers, differences exist in the specific configuration, particularly with regard to individually defined data fields, differing data structures and chamber-individual usage concepts. The project pursues the overarching objective of identifying a suitable successor solution for the discontinued DATEV software and procuring it within the framework of a structured, voluntary tender procedure.

sig_c296d685b63f931fd290.description:
The subject of the procurement is the conclusion of a framework agreement on the provision of specialist consultancy for an identity and access management project for Stadtwerke Bielefeld. The aim of the project is the further development of IAM processes, the design of role and authorisation models, and the introduction of a central technical IAM solution. Stadtwerke Bielefeld operate a heterogeneous IT landscape with a multitude of applications and systems. The management of user identities and access rights is currently carried out partly in a decentralised and system-related manner. To improve the control of identities and authorisations, a central structure for managing digital identities is being established as part of an IAM project. The goal of the IAM project is the introduction of a central IAM service for managing digital identities and for the structured and role-based assignment of authorisations for applications and systems. For this purpose, an IAM governance structure is to be established, and a technical IAM solution is to be introduced and rolled out. Specifically, this means the further development of IAM processes, the design of a role and authorisation model, the introduction of a central IAM solution and the integration of applications (from Q3 2027) as well as the preparation of organisational structures for the future operation of the IAM service. The project is managed by an external project management team in close collaboration with the IP division of Stadtwerke Bielefeld. Over the course of the project, the following milestones are generally intended to be achieved: • Elaboration and coordination of an IAM governance structure • Elaboration of a role-rights structure for SWB • Introduction of a technical IAM solution including the implementation of a pilot • Successive rollout of the technical IAM solution across the entire SWB The subject of the procurement is the provision of external specialist consultancy to support the IAM project of Stadtwerke Bielefeld. The consultancy services comprise supporting the implementation phase of the IAM project through two roles. 1. IAM management consultancy 2. IAM process consultancy One person is intended for each role. The IAM management consultancy supports the IP division with organisational and strategic issues in connection with the introduction of the IAM service. The core tasks of the IAM management consultancy are: • Support with the organisational classification of IAM within the IT organisation • Further development of governance structures in the IAM environment • Support with the definition and filling of roles and responsibilities • Assessment of the organisational impacts of IAM structures and processes • Support with the integration of IAM into existing security and governance structures • Elaboration of decision-making bases for management and project control • Support with coordination with relevant stakeholders • Support with the further development of the organisational operating model for the IAM service • Consultancy on covering relevant regulatory requirements • Developing an introduction strategy for guidelines, processes and the tool solution • Coordinating content-related dependencies on other projects and line initiatives • Support with the vendor-neutral selection of an IAM tool solution The IAM process consultancy supports the functional design of the processes for managing digital identities and authorisations. The core tasks of the IAM process consultancy are: • Analysis of existing processes for managing identities and authorisations • Elaboration of processes for the lifecycle of digital identities • Support with the design of joiner mover leaver processes • Development and structuring of a role and authorisation model • Structuring of processes for granting and changing access rights • Support with the integration of applications into IAM processes • Design of processes for the recertification of authorisations • Analysis of existing authorisation structures in applications • Preparation of functional concepts and process documentation in the IAM environment • Support with the introduction of the processes and the tool solution • Functional support with required ancillary services and obligations to cooperate for the implementation of the tool solution • Elaboration of test cases based on the process descriptions and requirements for the tool solution For the IAM management consultancy, there is a maximum quantity of 440 person-days or 3.520 hours. For the IAM process consultancy, there is a total maximum quantity of 385 person-days or 3.080 hours. Hybrid service provision is generally permissible. A binding ratio between remote and on-site deployments cannot currently be specified. The contracting authority determines the project-related required on-site presence. On-site deployments in Bielefeld may be required in particular for project kick-offs, workshops, steering committees, coordination meetings with central stakeholders, and other appointments requiring presence. The contractor must ensure that corresponding on-site appointments can also be attended with a reasonably short lead time. The concrete scope of on-site services is determined by the contracting authority in accordance with the requirements of the project progression. The framework agreement does not establish any minimum purchase obligation on the part of the contracting authority. The quantities, hourly rates, reference quantities, requirement values and maximum quantities stated in the procurement documents serve solely to determine the contract value, the comparability of tenders and the award evaluation. There is no entitlement to the actual commissioning or utilisation of these quantities or services.

Call-offs within the meaning of these procurement documents are understood exclusively as individual commissionings of services triggered by the contracting authority within the framework of the framework agreement.

sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.buyer_original: Freistaat Thüringen, vertreten durch das Thüringer Ministerium für Soziales, Gesundheit, Arbeit und Familie (TMSGAF) vertreten durch das Thüringer Landesamt für Verbraucherschutz
sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.description:
An IT application is to be procured as a SaaS cloud solution for the digitisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF). The IT application must be compatible with the hunting statistics application from Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. This is used in the Free State of Thuringia to record bag data (data on wild animals killed by hunters). The IT application should be available both as a web application (usable in common browsers) and as a mobile app (iOS and Android operating systems). Within the scope of the tender, an app is defined as an application that must be installed on a mobile device before use by the user and can only be used there. As a rule, this takes place on a smartphone or tablet using a so-called app store. There will be two main user groups: a) administrative or laboratory staff b) non-administrative users (e.g. authorised hunters). The non-administrative users record data on killed or slaughtered animals. If necessary, they also submit applications for the testing of these animals for trichinella and/or certain wildlife diseases to the competent authorities or the competent testing facility of the Free State of Thuringia. The test results should be retrievable via the IT application. The competent authorities (veterinary and food monitoring offices of the districts and independent cities - veterinary authorities) operate the trichinella testing laboratories. These should be able to access the application data recorded by external users in the IT application via their own user interface and transmit the test results back to the applicants. In addition, laboratory software should be made available to the competent authorities, with the help of which testing activities can be documented on the basis of the application data. In the case of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, the client's laboratory at the Thuringian State Office for Consumer Protection is the competent testing facility. The laboratory software (LIMS) in use there should be able to access the information on the samples entered by the users via the HIT database. The IT application must therefore have an interface to the HIT database. A direct connection to the LIMS is not intended. The IT application is to be made available to administrative staff for mapping internal administrative processes, as well as to affected users outside the administration for data entry and application submission, and for receiving notifications from the competent authorities. While the use cases of trichinella testing, management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and the interface to the hunting statistics application are to be available permanently, the use case of management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is only to be usable and available on an ad-hoc basis. Furthermore, introductory support and training for the staff of the competent authorities should be included in the offer as an initial service. The contract is concluded via an EVB-IT cloud contract. The procurement is carried out by the client for use by all districts and independent cities in Thuringia. The use of the IT application for the aforementioned purposes is mandatory for the districts and independent cities. For hunters, however, use is optional. This means they can refrain from using the IT application. The previous analogue system for sampling will continue to be used in parallel for the time being. The 21 veterinary and food monitoring offices of the 22 districts and independent cities in the Free State of Thuringia are, among other things, responsible for receiving and testing samples of slaughtered or killed animals intended for human consumption for Trichinella spp. Furthermore, there are responsibilities with regard to granting permission for the taking of samples intended for trichinella testing by non-administrative persons. Citizens who wish to make use of the aforementioned administrative services should be enabled to record the required application data digitally in accordance with the principles of the Online Access Act (OZG), to submit the application paperlessly to the respective competent veterinary and food monitoring office, and to receive the notifications from the competent authorities. In addition, the possibility should be created to comply with further reporting obligations (e.g. the recording of hunting bags by hunters) in digital form. The testing of wild boar for Trichinella spp. only takes place if the animal is to become food. Based on experience to date, this leads to the testing of up to 30.000 head of wild boar per year in Thuringia. These figures fluctuate. In addition, the veterinary surveillance authorities are responsible for implementing regular monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens. Depending on the current animal health status, the number of samples is expected to vary between approx. 5.000 and 30.000 samples per year. Data entry and application submission as well as the receipt of notifications should also be made possible here for the respective affected citizens. The recorded data should be transmitted via the application to the State Office for Consumer Protection responsible for testing the samples. The application part for the management of ASF outbreaks should be based on the aforementioned application parts in terms of operation (esp.

the monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens) and interact with them in terms of content in accordance with the technical requirements. This application part should be activatable on an ad-hoc basis for each affected authority (veterinary authorities of the districts and independent cities and, if applicable, the client). In addition to an ASF outbreak in Thuringia, it should also be used in the context of exercises to prepare for an outbreak. A final application part includes the recording and reporting of hunting bags by hunters. This report includes all huntable animal species. For this documentation obligation, the kill data from the aforementioned application parts should be reusable, but it should also be possible to record new kill data. A corresponding interface is to be provided for the necessary data exchange with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. The hunters already have direct access to the hunting statistics application. The interface should enable them to gain access from within the IT application and thus facilitate reporting through data transfer. The application is to be provided for use by administrative personnel in the Free State of Thuringia as well as the respective affected citizens in the Free State of Thuringia. As a result, the licence and terms of use must enable use by employees of the state, the municipalities, and by non-administrative persons. The number of future users cannot be precisely quantified at present, as the use of the IT application is optional for hunters. However, the number of hunters in Thuringia can be a reference point; it amounts to approx. 13.000. In addition, there are approx. 100 administrative staff.
sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.title: Provision, operation (incl. hosting), and support of an IT application for the digitisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF), and a software interface to the hunting statistics application

sig_c5990e4963af4f52e345.description: Hanover Housing Association has been providing housing and support services across Scotland for over forty years. Managing approximately 150 homes with an aspect of care, predominantly for older people, Hanover is committed to enabling tenants to live independently within their communities. Hanover provides housing with care and very sheltered housing services which can range from light touch interventions such as reminding tenants to take medication to helping tenants with daily tasks such as personal care. Lot 1: . Hanover has initiated a Care and Support Systems Review at senior management level to address challenges caused by varied case management practices, inefficient data handling, and outdated digital tools. Two critical areas of improvement have been identified: - Care Scheduling/Planning – modernising currently paper-based processes, ensuring person-centred care and real-time updates. Although a full eMAR system is not required, medication management is a large area requiring support. - Rota Management – replacing fragmented manual scheduling with a centralised, digital platform. Through this forthcoming procurement, Hanover aims to secure a solution that will: - Improve service quality and tenant engagement through modern, digital care planning. - Increase operational efficiency and staff satisfaction via streamlined rota management. - Enhance safety, compliance, and oversight of medication management. - Provide integrated reporting, dashboards, and mobile accessibility. - Support compliance with relevant regulatory frameworks. The service will operate within a framework of continuous improvement with which the service provider will be required to engage; bringing innovation, sharing ideas, and implementing improvement measures to increase operational effectiveness/efficiency and drive out waste.
sig_c5990e4963af4f52e345.title: Provision of a Digital Care and Support System – Care Scheduling/Planning and Rota Management

sig_c5f4ed68ce0e43596109.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council intend to commission an organisation to develop and implement the creation of a local Poverty dashboard, designed to provide a clear, accessible view of child poverty across Dumfries and Galloway. The dashboard should be accessible to partner organisations and any other interested party. Dumfries and Galloway Council serve a region of around 148,000 people across the South West of Scotland, stretching from Stranraer in the West, to Moffat and Annan in the East. We are the 3rd largest local authority by area in Scotland. The latest published statistics show that the rate of child poverty in Dumfries and Galloway is 22.7%. This equates to 5,672 children and young people living in poverty in the region. For example, there are some real challenges around improving health outcomes for those experiencing poverty in the early years and to ensure that all families eligible for free school meals are reached. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway have received funding through the Scottish Governments Fairer Futures initiative. The project is early in its inception but has the long-term goal to deliver systematic change in the way public services support parents and families out of poverty. Our approach is to use existing principles and approaches to put families first, focusing on prevention rather than cure. To help achieve this, accurately measuring poverty and low income is crucial, and the availability of real-time data is vital for effective policy-making. The dashboard would have geographic layers, allowing users to explore poverty data at varying levels of granularity, offering insights into where support is most needed, with a particular focus on priority groups identified by the Scottish Government. These include lone-parent households, families with a disabled member, large families, and households with a mother under the age of 25. It is hoped that data can be gathered that will make meaningful impact to household income, targeting those who are not currently accessing all the additional help and support they can. In addition it’s important that we understand the landscape of our household in poverty, not in our dense areas of deprivation. It would be sage if this could also include pertinent health related data around missed appointments, or additional useful information which might allow for a targeted approach to reduce health inequality. The dashboard should; -Filter data by employment status, housing tenure, and age group, enabling a nuanced understanding of the different dimensions of poverty. -Be a dynamic platform with regularly updated data, that can be continually used to inform decision making. -Be publicly accessible, this openness is essential for building trust and ensuring that anti-poverty efforts are responsive to the lived experiences of families across the region. The purpose of the Poverty Dashboard is to make it easier for the Council and its partners, working with our families in poverty, to easily identify the areas of greatest need to support an evidence based and targeted approach when tackling poverty and inequality in the region.. It is anticipated that this procurement requirement will be conducted through Quick Quote portal as a non-regulated procedure, interested organisations are encouraged to express an interest to be added to the quick quote where this goes as planned.
sig_c5f4ed68ce0e43596109.title: Poverty Dashboard for Dumfries and Galloway

sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.description: The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. Functional specification: AI-based detection of dead branches 1. Introduction and objectives The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. The objective is to provide a digital tool that supports visual inspection through AI-based image analysis, thereby significantly increasing the efficiency and safety of maintenance measures. The specific technical implementation is at the discretion of the bidders. All relevant legal and regulatory requirements must be complied with during the design, development and implementation of the AI system. In particular, the contractor must ensure that the AI system to be developed is in accordance with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence (AI Act), insofar as it is applicable.2. Functional requirements for the system (service programme) The service to be provided must fulfil the following core functions, which must be demonstrated in a proof-of-concept (PoC) and in a subsequent prototypical application. 2.1. Data acquisition The system must be capable of capturing visual data (images or video sequences) from a mobile unit (e.g. a vehicle) in a quality suitable for AI analysis. Function: Automated and continuous capture of image material of the surrounding tree landscape. 2.2. AI algorithm for image evaluation The core of the application is an AI algorithm that performs an automated analysis of the captured image data. Function: Automatic detection, classification and spatial localisation (positioning) of dead branches. Requirement: The algorithm must achieve a defined minimum hit rate and reliability under various environmental conditions (daylight, shadows, weather). The results must be clearly assignable and traceable. 2.3. Frontend application (user interface) The system must provide a user-friendly interface for displaying and managing the analysis results. Function: Graphical processing of the AI results for practical use. Requirement: The frontend must enable a clear display of the detected dead branches on a map. In addition, the frontend must contain functions for validation, commenting and approval of the results by the user. 2.4. Data management and interfaces Requirement: A self-sufficient system must be offered which enables data entry and data integration and whose results can be viewed. Integration into existing IT systems of Autobahn GmbH is not intended and is not required. The AI system will be operated entirely by the contractor. The contractor must provide the data and analysis results generated during the provision of the service in electronic form. Formats must be used that are both readable by the contracting authority and machine-processable. Further technical interfaces or system connections are not part of the service to be provided. 3. Non-functional requirements Beyond the functions mentioned, the following qualities of the system are important: Scalability: The system must be designed in such a way that it can be expanded to larger data volumes and further areas of application if required. IT security: The entire architecture and data processing must comply with current IT security standards, particularly with regard to the protection of data and systems in critical infrastructure. Maintainability: The system should be designed so that it can be easily maintained and further developed. The usage rights for the developed software (AI) remain exclusively with Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. 4. Project result Proof of functionality (PoC): After the first phase, a functional proof (PoC) must be provided that demonstrates the feasibility of the AI-based detection. Prototypical application: The final result is a fully functional, prototypical application that meets all the functional and non-functional requirements mentioned above and can be tested in practice. Note: The decision regarding the specific technical implementation (e.g. programming languages used, specific AI frameworks, etc.) is left to the bidders. The decisive factor is the fulfilment of the described functions and objectives. The contract duration is 24 months from the start of the contract. Within this period, the AI system must be fully developed and provided. The data deliveries in accordance with section 2.4 must also be provided regularly within this period.
sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.title: AI-based detection of dead branches

sig_c8d8a5a5f2c5bab2ebbc.description: Spark DPS Buy emerging technology products and services, including Internet of Things (IoT), AI and automation, simulated environments, wearables and new improvements in security. Description Spark: the Technology Innovation Marketplace can help government and public sector to access new and emerging technology products. This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) uses a filter system that helps customers find suppliers. The filter system includes defined technology areas developed with customer input. It focuses on emerging technologies predicted to have the largest impact over the next 2 to 5 years. There are 8 technology areas you can filter by: Internet of Things (IoT) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation Simulated and enhanced environments Engineering/materials science Data Wearables Transport Security Each of these areas contains between 3 and 17 sub-categories. The DPS filters help customers to identify and shortlist suppliers. The 2 main filters are: problem area technology type You can also filter by: location security classification Suppliers can apply to join the marketplace at any time, and identify their areas of expertise as part of the application process. Successful suppliers need to demonstrate their ability to offer suitably innovative products that meet either of the following 2 definitions: radical innovation: offering a new product, service, process or strategy introduced into a market designed to make a significant impact by completely replacing existing technologies and methods for example, streaming services replacing video rental stores disruptive innovation: creates a new market and value network and eventually disrupts an existing market and value network displacing established market-leading firms, products and alliances for example, light emitting diodes (LEDs) replacing traditional light bulbs As well as their ability to provide innovative products, the supplier’s contract example needs to explain the benefits for the end user and must be approved and confirmed by the customer. Once an application is complete, it can take can take up to a maximum of 15 working days to assess and appoint a supplier to the marketplace. A downloadable copy of the bid pack is available on the supplier registration service . Benefits access to proven technology innovation to solve public sector problems agility and flexibility to meet the public sector’s changing technology needs this agreement has no lots, use the filter system to produce a list of potential suppliers based on your needs quality and price assessment filtered to an individual customer’s requirements an efficient tender process and approach to finding potential solutions, including the option of using a 2 stage competition process and supplier presentations can be used for any size project, there is no minimum or maximum value Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Spark DPS Expires: 15/02/2029 How to buy Make sure you have received budget approval and have read the RM6094 Spark customer guidance before using this agreement. The following instructions are for conducting a simple call for competition without use of: pre-tender market engagement (PTME) capability assessment presentation These are all also possible under the RM6094 Spark DPS. These terms are explained in the customer guide. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer Go to the RM6094 Spark DPS under Technology and choose the “access as a buyer” option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your “manage your DPS category exports” page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers. click on the link to create a new category export. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the “save category” option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your “manage your category exports” page, export the list of suppliers and contact details. Export is to an Excel spreadsheet. Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. the list is valid for only 2 working days, from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point if your call for competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you do not use your list within 2 working days by clicking the “search again” option for your export use our eSourcing tool to run a call for competition the tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool Your tender process should align with the value and complexity of your requirement. Suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing enough time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a deadline for submitting evidence for 2 days. If you are satisfied with the evidence, award the contract. Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder . Explanation of terms: Pre- tender market engagement (PTME) This is optional but recommended and allows you to communicate with suppliers ahead of issuing your final specification to ensure that the market has a clear understanding of your requirements. It also allows you to: shape your specification gather ideas on new innovations understand if there are any changes within the market that may influence your requirements This exercise is not about refining your shortlist. You must provide an outline of your specification and you can ask suppliers specific questions regarding your requirements and specification and for feedback. Capability assessment This is optional but recommended and helps you to identify which suppliers from your shortlist are going to be most suitable. It can be used to refine your shortlist or to assess if any suppliers are capable of meeting your requirement. You can use a series of yes and no questions that suppliers must pass to get to the written stage. Face to face presentation This is also optional. It happens after the evaluation of the written proposals. It is an opportunity for face to face dialogue with the suppliers who were successful in reaching this stage. Suppliers can present more detailed proposals and answer any specific questions you may have regarding their written response. sig_c979f2eadc8687b2e9fb.description: THIS INFORMATION REQUEST IS AN INVITATION TO AN INFORMATION MEETING REGARDING THE PROCUREMENT OF PTT SERVICES. ICT service production for the City of Jyväskylä has been reorganised in recent years so that the operational production of basic IT services has been largely outsourced. The upcoming procurement will ensure that the service package meets the city's current and developing needs and supports efficient, secure and reliable everyday operations throughout the organisation. Basic IT services are currently produced for the City of Jyväskylä as the following service packages: - User and support services (Service Desk, remote and on-site support, Helppari) - Workstation, device and lifecycle services - ICT environment management and operation - Server monitoring and operating services at the operating system level - Communications SPOC, terminal connection and support services. - Cyber security services (technical information security and incident management) - Service management and production management (ITSM system and system integration between the Supplier and the Customer, SLA, change management) The aim of the upcoming procurement is to reorganise the services so that the service level and user experience are consistent and predictable, service production is transparently managed and measurable, and the package supports the city's operations in a cost-effective manner. The aim is also to strengthen proactiveness and continuous development and ensure that the services take into account the special characteristics of the administrative network and educational network. The current state and objectives described above serve as the starting point for the service areas and requirements defined in more detail in the upcoming invitation to tender.

PLEASE REVIEW THE UPDATED ANNOUNCEMENT IN FULL FOR SUBMISSION TIME, UPDATED TOPIC, AND FUNDING AMOUNT AND SCHEDULE CHANGES FROM CYCLE 1** TACTICAL BEHAVIORS FOR AUTONOMOUS MANEUVER COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROGRAM (TBAM-CRP) Future Army forces will be called upon to operate and maneuver in multi-domain operations (MDO), against a modern and capable peer adversary. The battlefield of the future may impose additional constraints on maneuver forces such as disruption in communication as well as positioning services. To field a highly capable fighting force in this future battlefield, novel tactics and doctrines leveraging nascent technologies in robotics and autonomous systems (RAS) will need to be developed. Teams of RAS will serve an increasingly critical role in the future force to deliver situational awareness, defend key locations or positions, or take point in dynamic and hazardous situations. Resilience to disruptions, failures, or unexpected scenarios, is a key quality for teams of RAS to operate alongside other future Army forces. The US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Army Research Laboratory (ARL) is focused on developing fundamental understanding and informing the art-of-the-possible for warfighter concepts through research to greatly improve the scope of mission capabilities of teams of RAS, develop robust and resilient approaches to plan under extreme conditions of uncertainty, to learn coordinated strategies for groups of agents to achieve a common objective, all within a complex maneuver environment including adversaries. The Tactical Behaviors for Autonomous Maneuver Collaborative Research Program (TBAM-CRP) is focused on developing and experimentally evaluating coordinated and individual behaviors for small groups of autonomous agents to learn doctrinal as well as novel tactics for maneuvering in military relevant environments. The TBAM-CRP will leverage developments in other internal and extramural programs as well as identify new research directions to find novel solutions to these maneuver problems in analogical simulations representing complex realistic terrain. The Tactical Behaviors for Autonomous Maneuver Collaborative Research Program (TBAM-CRP) will consist of a series of sprint efforts executed with annual program reviews. Each topic will be focused on addressing a different set of scientific areas which will support the research aims of an associated ARL researcher from a related internal essential research program (ERP) or mission-funded program. The TBAM-CRP has been developed in coordination with other related ARL-funded collaborative efforts (see descriptions of ARL collaborative alliances at https://www.arl.army.mil/business/collaborativealliances/) and shares a common vision of highly collaborative academia-industry-government partnerships; however, it will be executed with a program model adapted from the Scalable, Adaptive, and Resilient Autonomy (SARA), which established a new paradigm for collaborative research. Some key properties of this new approach are described below: • TBAM-CRP sprint topics will be offered on a two-year cycle. Proposals will be solicited for a possible two-year period structured as a first-year pilot followed by a second-year option where the option may be awarded based upon progress assessed at an annual review. The FOA will be amended annually to identify a specific problem statement and scope for that specific cycle. The topics for each cycle will be chosen to address the long-term program goal. • Five new topics (Cycles 1-5) are expected in FY22, 24, 26, 28, 30. Each topic will be carefully chosen based on the previous accomplishments in the prior cycle(s), the development of new technologies and capabilities in the broader research and development communities, and the Army’s evolving needs for future capabilities. • For each topic, funding will be provided to those Recipients selected under a cooperative agreement (CA). • Enhanced Research Program funding from ARL or Other Government Agencies (OGAs) may become available during a cycle which provides a mechanism for growth and enhancement within the TBAM-CRP. A proposal should not include any discussion of the Enhanced Research Program. Recipients receiving a CA will be notified and provided details if the opportunity for Enhanced Research Program funding becomes available during their award period of performance. • There is no limitation on the place of performance, although on-site collaboration at ARL facilities and with ARL researchers as well as with other Recipients are encouraged. Research outcomes in this program must, at the very least, be demonstrated in sophisticated simulations of relevant environments. Together with ARL collaborators, these results may be adapted for higher TRL experimentation on surrogate platforms at ARL test facilities such as the Robotics Research Collaboration Campus (R2C2) at Graces Quarters, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland. • Recipients will be furnished with access to the ARL Autonomy Stack software suite as well as all relevant simulation tools and multi-agent learning support. • Recipients will be provided with information about the current state of the Autonomous Systems Enterprise (ASE) with an overview of developments in the associated collaborative research alliances including Distributed and Collaborative Intelligent Systems and Technology (DCIST), Scalable, Adaptive, and Resilient Autonomy (SARA), as well as internal ARL essential research programs including the AI for Maneuver and Mobility (AIMM), Emerging Overmatch Technologies (EOT), and Versatile Tactical Power and Propulsion (VICTOR). Capabilities demonstrated in simulation should reflect significant appropriate developments. This midpoint review is expected to take place as a mini symposium where Recipients can share results with one another along with the ARL community to foster further collaboration. • At the end of the second year, a capstone demonstration will be executed by those Recipients receiving an option to their award in a set of simulated relevant environments, either those environment scenarios provided by the Government and other program performers, or optionally of a specific environment developed by the Recipient to exhibit their developed capability. Any system level capability demonstration that can be made with the internal ARL collaborator or description of capability development and program contribution can also be made at this time. These system demonstrations are expected to coincide to foster further integration and adoption with related internal research programs as well as partner organizations from within the DEVCOM, other Army and DoD service branches and agencies, in addition to other government agencies. Proposals that follow the requirements of the FOA will be evaluated in accordance with merit-based, competitive procedures. These procedures will include evaluation factors and an adjectival and color rating system. A review team, consisting of a qualified group of Government scientists and managers will evaluate the compliant proposals and provide the results of that evaluation to the decision-maker for the Government. Relevant internal research program materials approved for public release and contact information will be provided to potential proposers during introductory presentations to help facilitate identification of collaboration between proposers and individual ARL researchers or internal research programs. Additional connections to ARL programs can be identified during the proposal review process. Eligible applicants under this FOA include institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, and for-profit organizations (i.e., large and small businesses) for scientific research in the knowledge domains outlined throughout this Funding Opportunity. Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDC) may propose as well, with effort as allowed by their sponsoring agency and in accordance with their sponsoring agency policy.

Abertay University is seeking to engage with the market to understand the availability of solutions capable of delivering a modern, integrated digital experience platform, or integrated set of platforms and services, to support the University's website, intranet and web/mobile portal requirements. The University is seeking to improve student recruitment and conversion, enhance staff and student engagement, strengthen digital communications, simplify content management and provide a more joined-up and personalised digital experience across its key digital channels The scope includes: - A public-facing website serving as the University's primary digital channel for student recruitment and conversion, marketing and communications, promotion of courses and research, and engagement with prospective students, partners and external stakeholders. - A staff and student intranet platform providing audience-specific content and communications. - A web and mobile portal experience (currently delivered through the myday platform) providing staff and students with personalised access to university services, learning resources, communications, academic information and other digital services. sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.description: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services. The procurement will comprise two Lots: Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue. The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate. The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. Dynamic Market Participation Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register. Supplier registration: CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370) The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline. Lot 1: Core Commercial Data. Lot 1 covers the supply and licensing of core commercial optical EO data for use across the UK public sector. The scope of Lot 1 may include: • Current commercial optical EO data products. • Historic imagery to support temporal analysis, seasonal comparison and change detection. • Associated metadata and quality assurance information. • Licensing rights and permissions required to support public sector access and use. Data delivery, integration support and associated technical services required to support the Authority's intended delivery model. Lot 2: Specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Lot 2 - eligible UK public sector organisations may procure specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities from the awarded supplier via call-off. The scope of Lot 2 may include: • Routine monitoring data services • Higher resolution and tasked data services • Historic and archive data services • Analytics and monitoring services • Validation and decision-support services • Field evidence collection services • Data access, hosting and delivery services associated with specialist EO products and services • Implementation, training and user support services required to support operational use The Lot 2 contract will not create a commitment by the Authority or any User to place a Call-Off Order.
sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.title: Earth Observation: Data Products and Services for the UK Public Sector 'Public Sector EO'

sig_cd24866af8aff1b503e6.description: The Sir John Brunner Foundation Multi-Academy Trust (Cheshire) is undertaking pre-market engagement in relation to a proposed procurement for the management of community lettings and facilities hire across part of its estate. The initial scope is expected to include Middlewich High School and Sir John Deane's Sixth Form College, with the possibility of future extension to other Trust sites, subject to suitability, value for money and operational requirements. The Trust's wider estate includes The County High School, Leftwich and (from November) primary academies in the Northwich area. The Trust is seeking to understand the market for managed lettings services and to inform the development of its final specification, procurement route and commercial model. The proposed requirement is expected to involve the management, marketing, booking, administration and operational delivery of lettings and community use of school and college facilities outside core educational hours. The Trust's objectives are to: increase utilisation of facilities outside normal school and college hours; improve and expand access for local clubs, voluntary organisations and community groups; support sustainable community use, particularly for local and regular users; ensure safeguarding, site security, supervision and operational control during lettings activity; reduce the administrative and operational burden on academy staff; protect the condition, readiness and availability of facilities for core educational use; increase income through improved utilisation and broader use of facilities, rather than relying solely on price increases; and establish a professional, compliant and scalable lettings model capable of operating across multiple academy sites where appropriate. The facilities potentially within scope include, but are not limited to, indoor sports halls, outdoor pitches, all-weather/3G or astro facilities, playing fields, performance and assembly spaces, classrooms, specialist teaching areas, changing rooms, car parking and ancillary facilities. The final list of facilities will be confirmed following engagement with the market. The Trust is particularly interested in engaging with providers able to deliver one or more of the following models: a fully managed lettings service, including marketing, bookings, customer management, income collection, staffing, supervision, safeguarding, compliance and reporting; a managed bookings and staffing model, including provider-led marketing, customer management and revenue administration, with operational delivery agreed between the provider and the Trust; and/or advice on appropriate commercial structures, including revenue share, guaranteed income, management fee or hybrid models. At this stage, the Trust does not intend to pursue a software-only booking platform as the primary solution, as the requirement includes a need for operational delivery, staffing and site supervision, particularly at Middlewich High School. However, the Trust welcomes feedback on systems and technology used to support managed lettings services. The Trust anticipates that any future contract would require the successful provider to demonstrate robust arrangements for: on-site staffing and supervision; safeguarding, site security and incident escalation; access control, opening, closing and site handover; cleaning, facility reset and reporting of damage or defects; customer service and complaints management; protection and transition of existing community users where possible; pricing strategy and affordability for local community users; financial reporting, reconciliation, VAT information and income remittance; performance reporting and attendance at formal contract review meetings; and orderly exit and transfer of booking/customer data at the end of the arrangement. The Trust is considering a phased implementation approach, with Sir John Deane's Sixth Form College and non-pitch lettings at Middlewich High School potentially commencing first, followed by Middlewich High School pitch or astro lettings at a later stage to allow appropriate transition and notice for existing users. The estimated value of the initial opportunity is currently expected to be in the region of £420,000 to £480,000 or more over an initial three-year period, based on estimated gross lettings income across the sites. This estimate is indicative only and will be reviewed as the commercial model, scope and contract structure are developed. The final classification and value of any subsequent procurement will be confirmed before the formal tender stage. The purpose of this pre-market engagement is to: understand supplier capability and capacity in the managed school and college lettings market; test the proposed scope, delivery model and phasing; understand appropriate commercial models and risk allocation; identify key operational, safeguarding, staffing and financial considerations; inform the Trust's final specification and procurement documents; and ensure that any subsequent procurement is proportionate, transparent and capable of delivering best value. Participation in this pre-market engagement will not confer any advantage in any subsequent procurement process. Information shared by the Trust will be made available on a consistent basis where appropriate, and any future competition will be conducted in accordance with the Trust's procurement obligations, including the principles of transparency, equal treatment and non-discrimination. Interested providers are invited to respond to this notice and may be invited to participate in a site visit. Any future procurement opportunity will be advertised separately, and the Trust reserves the right not to proceed to procurement following this engagement. Lot 1: .

sig_cd466be3f2abdf82a02e.description: This requirement is for the development of computer vision (AI) tools for pelagic fisheries CCTV. The project will consider the development of an automated image analysis system to isolate (and quantify) activities (and animals) associated with pelagic fisheries, with a focus on the capture of UCB species in CCTV-observed fishing events of a given subset of vessels subject to mandatory Remote Electronic Monitoring (REM). The project will focus initially on counts of UCB events, but the intention would be to gather biological data on the individual animals caught e.g. classification to the finest possible level and estimates of size. The results will be used by Scottish Government Marine Directorate (SGMD) Compliance (for regulation infringement detection) and SGMD Science for bycatch rate estimation, as part of wider observer programmes, and to inform future revisions to REM technical specifications. The ultimate goal of this development work is to design, implement and test a UCB detection and classification system, including the supply of relevant CCTV footage from vessels in Scottish Waters. Lot 1: . This system should be capable of being integrated into REM review software to automatically process and analyse video sequences from fishing trips to identify relevant events, count UCB events, and subsequently identify, count and measure all UCB individuals. It is important to point out that such a system should also be able to handle a realistic range of environmental noise such as variability of the location within the field of view, due to differing vessel layouts, in which events / animals have been detected, occlusions, pose variations, and lighting conditions. It is envisaged that this will be done in a probabilistic way, and that human intervention and further analysis will be suggested when the uncertainty exceeds a preset threshold (as there will be sections of footage in which identification will be very difficult due to occlusion). The system should be easily maintained and upgraded and will remain the property of the Scottish Government. This project will consider the development of interim stages towards fully automated image analysis tools for identifying and characterising atypical fishing activity events indicative of UCB species presence. In addition, the AI tools will subsequently determine the number (and, potentially, the size) of a subset of UCB observations via cameras as part of the mandated REM of eligible pelagic fishing vessels in Scottish waters. Attention would focus initially on the recorded numbers of UCB events as well as counts and size measurements for sea mammals (inc. cetaceans, seals), sharks / skates / rays, seabirds, and non-target bony fish. The results / products will be used by SGMD scientists to increase the efficiency of video review tasks, optimise the technical specifications of electronic monitoring systems for this fishery, estimate bycatch mortality rates, and identify fishing practices where mitigation measures may be required to protect vulnerable species. Specifically, this study will aim to: a) Develop a graphical user interface (GUI) to facilitate the viewing, sharing, collation, analysis and annotation of CCTV video footage from pelagic fishing vessels; b) Instruct and assist with the calibration of camera systems (if required) to ensure field-of-view and lens distortion correction in length measurements; c) Develop detection algorithms to detect, classify (to the most detailed taxonomic level feasible), and measure individuals of UCB species passing through the dewatering separator from representative video footage; d) Develop detection algorithms to determine when activity is taking place on-deck or in-water in relation to catch handling and apply facial recognition to anonymise the recorded footage; e) Develop detection algorithms to detect, classify (at the minimum level of mammals, elasmobranchs, non-target fish, and seabirds) and measure (inter alia) individuals of ETP species on deck or in-water from representative video footage. Suppliers should provide imagery from a minimum of 3 vessels. However, it is desirable that imagery is inclusive of both freezer vessels and refrigerated / chilled water vessels, vessels with differing deck layouts and catch handling configurations; and vessels from multiple flag states. Imagery provided to Scottish Government for annotation within the GUI must be anonymised regarding its metadata and have had facial recognition blurring methods applied. Suppliers must arrange to have access to suitable CCTV footage from Scottish Waters, either within their own data storage architecture (if they are an REM service provider) or via partnership with an REM service provider / pelagic fishing boats. It is anticipated that the project will be entirely computer lab-based, as all required video footage is being collected on an on-going basis as a matter of routine.
sig_cd466be3f2abdf82a02e.title: Development of computer vision (AI) tools for REM of pelagic Fisheries

sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.description: Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) constitute the overwhelming majority of economic activity in Jordan. MSMEs account for over 99% of all enterprises, employ around 60% of the formal private-sector workforce, and contribute 40% of Jordan Gross Domestic Product (GDP), making them crucial for economic growth, resilience, and job creation. Despite this importance, MSMEs still face obstacles in accessing appropriate and diversified financial products. Access to formal credit remains limited for many MSMEs. According to the Central Bank of Jordan (CBJ) National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 2023-2028, only 28.3% of formal MSMEs had a loan or line of credit from a financial institution, highlighting a significant financing gap for smaller firms in Jordan. Financial exclusion is especially pronounced for underserved segments such as informal and women-led enterprises, which often face higher collateral requirements, limited credit histories, and lower formal borrowing rates. Financial inclusion, defined as access to and use of appropriate, affordable, and sustainable financial products and services, remains a priority in Jordan. The CBJ is pursuing ambitious targets to increase overall financial inclusion, reduce gender gaps, and enhance MSME access to finance, including through digital channels and tailored products. The NFIS aims, for example, to increase MSMEs access to formal lending at an average annual rate of 4% for four years. In a similar vein, Jordan"s Green Finance Strategy 2023-2028 aims to mobilize green investments and position the financial sector as a regional leader in sustainable finance. The strategy highlights that a 92.5% of the Jordan National Determined Contribution (NDC) target cost is to be financed by international support and mobilized private capital. As Jordan advances its Green Finance Strategy, a central priority was establishing clear and credible standards for what qualifies as "green" across the financial system. The Jordan National Green Taxonomy, published in February 2026, provides this clarity by offering a common language for the financial system to classify sustainable economic activities in a transparent and consistent way. By anchoring investment decisions to science-based criteria, the taxonomy helps ensure that future capital flows genuinely support Jordan"s low-carbon, climate-resilient transition. Against this backdrop, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GIZ-implemented project, Innovative Approaches for the Financial Inclusion of MSMEs in Jordan (I-FIN), takes a holistic, market-driven approach to strengthening inclusive green finance in the country. The project operates across the policy, institutional, and market levels, helping to improve the broader enabling environment, upgrade the technical and operational capacities of financial service providers, and ensure that enterprises can confidently access and benefit from green finance solutions. The overall objective of the project is to ensure that MSMEs in Jordan benefit from a more inclusive financial system that enables inclusive access to green finance and supports environmentally sustainable and resilient business growth, also with a focus on women-led enterprises. The assignment is structured around four interrelated work packages, 5 key experts, complemented by two pools of experts. Work Package 1: Planning and Inception: aims to review, research, and analyse all relevant information to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the assignment and to refine the implementation approach. Work Package 2: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Inclusive Green Credit Guarantees and Risk-Sharing Mechanisms: strengthens the staff and institutional capacities of the Jordan Loan Guarantee Corporation (JLGC) in the area of MSMEs inclusive green finance, through tailored staff capacity development and institutional advisory services across seven operational areas: product development and/or adaptation, risk documentation and/or management, strategy development, monitoring, reporting, setting up of an operational unit, and cooperation with Fintechs. Work Package 3: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Financial Services Providers: strengthens the institutional capacities of 5 financial services providers across the same seven operational areas and builds the capacities of at least 120 employees (50 of which are women) in the financial service sector. This work package may target public and private financial services providers, while Activity 3.7 targets financial sector associations, training providers, and academic institutions. The Contractor is expected to ensure strong coordination and alignment with a parallel complementary intervention delivering sector-level standardized training, including regular information exchange, harmonization of approaches, and avoidance of duplication. Work Package 4: Advancing Financial Service Providers' Capacity to Access and Mobilize International Climate Finance: supports financial services providers in submitting at least 3 project outlines (1 of which related to the water sector) for mobilising international climate finance in relation to MSMEs to relevant national actors, in close coordination with the CBJ, Ministry of Environment, and industry associations. All support under this assignment shall be aligned with international best practices and relevant national frameworks, including, but not limited to, the Jordan National Green Taxonomy, ensuring consistency with evolving regulatory and policy developments in the green finance landscape.
sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.title: 10021232 - Supporting the Financial Institutions Green Transition

sig_cef5f71f644c84e946c9.description: YOU CAN STILL INFLUENCE DURING THE MARKET SURVEY PHASE! At the City of Turku, we want to make high-quality procurements and cooperate with companies. We are therefore conducting a market survey before the publication of the actual contract notice. The goal is to inform about the upcoming tendering process, survey the markets for the subject of the procurement, and obtain comprehensive information on the availability of the service, implementation possibilities, and potential suppliers. We will also ask suppliers participating in the market dialogue for comments on the minimum requirements and quality criteria in the procurement documents. The goal of the market dialogue is also to go through the scheduling and implementation of the upcoming tendering process. This is an invitation to a market dialogue concerning the energy consumption monitoring service planned by the City of Turku. Turun kaupunki monitors energy consumption in approx. 600 buildings, of which over 200 have district heating. A measurement hub, which provides more accurate consumption data, can be found in approx. 70 buildings. The goal is to create a digital service that produces energy consumption monitoring, which performs the expert's manual work steps, producing as highly refined information as possible on consumption changes with easy views, explanations, and follow-up measures. The goal is to make consumption monitoring as automatic as possible by reducing manual work steps, such as determining the start time, occurrence, and overall effects of increased consumption. The user should automatically receive the most important prioritised key observations and easily see the analysis of the observation. Proposers must account for this in their budget, per the instructions provided in Section 7.3 of ROSES-25 A.1 Earth Science Research Overview . NOTICE: July 30, 2026.
