Mandatory Notices of Intent are due by August 20, 2026, and proposals are due October 20, 2026. Any proposal not preceded by an on-time NOI will be declined without review. Proposals submitted to this program will be evaluated using dual anonymous peer review, see Section 4.4. Proposers to this program element are strongly encouraged to use the optional Earth Science Division template for the required summary table of work effort of the proposal; templates are available at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/templates-for-earth-science-division-appendix-a-roses-proposals. NOTICE: Research security training required starting August 5, 2026. All PIs and any Co-Is that would spend ≥ 10% time on a proposed grants or cooperative agreements must certify they have taken research security training. NASA will be satisfied with the four online research security training modules on the National Science Foundation's (NSF) Research Security Training website at https://www.nsf.gov/research-security/training or the SECURE Center condensed version of the four modules at https://www.secure-center.org/ctm This synopsis is a generic summary that is posted for each of the many individual "program elements" in NASA’s Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 solicitation. For specific information on this particular program element download and read the PDF of the text of this program element by going to Tables 2 or 3 of ROSES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table2 and https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table3 , respectively, click the title of the program element of interest, a hypertext link will take you to a page for that particular program element. On that page, on the right side under "Announcement Documents" the link on the bottom will be to the PDF of the text of the call for proposals. For example, if one were interested in the Solar System Science program (NNH25ZDA001N-SCUBED) one would follow the link to the NSPIRES page for that program element and then to read the text of the call one would click on “C.2 Solar System Science (.pdf)” to download the text of the call. If one wanted to set it into the context of the goals, objectives and know the default rules for all elements within Appendix C, the planetary science division, one might download and read “ C.1 Planetary Science Research Program Overview (.pdf) ” from that same page. While the letters and numbers are different for each element within ROSES (A.10, B.3, etc.) the basic configuration is always the same, e.g., the letter indicates the Science Division (A is Earth Science, B is Heliophysics etc.) and whatever the letter, #1 is always the division overview. In 2025, most program elements will be set up for application via Grants.gov only if requested at least 30 days in advance of the due date. For more on Grants.gov submissions see Section IV(b)v of the ROSES Summary of Solicitation, that may be found at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Science Mission Directorate (SMD) released its annual omnibus Research Announcement (NRA), Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 (OMB Approval Number 2700-0092, CFDA Number 43.001) on February 21, 2025. In this case "omnibus" means that this NRA has many individual program elements, each with its own due dates and topics. All together these cover the wide range of basic and applied supporting research and technology supported by SMD. Awards will be made as grants, cooperative agreements, or contracts depending on the nature of the work proposed. However, most extramural research awards deriving from ROSES will be grants, and many program elements of ROSES specifically exclude contracts, because contracts would not be appropriate for the nature of the work solicited. Funded Co-Is at government labs will receive inter- or intra-agency transfers . The typical period of performance for an award is three years, but some programs may allow up to five years and others specify shorter periods. In most cases, organizations of every type, Government and private, for profit and not-for-profit, domestic and foreign (with some caveats), may submit proposals without restriction on teaming arrangements. Tables listing the program elements and due dates (Tables 2 and 3 ), a table that provides a very top level summary of proposal contents ( Table 1 ), and the full text of the ROSES-2025 "Summary of Solicitation", may all be found NSPIRES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . Frequently asked questions for ROSES are posted at http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/faqs . Questions concerning specific program elements should be directed to the point(s) of contact for that particular element, who may be found either at the end of the individual program element in the summary table of key information or on the web list of topics and points of contact at: http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/program-officers-list . General questions concerning ROSES-2025 may be directed to the office of the SMD Deputy Associate Administrator for Research at sara@nasa.gov . Not all program elements are known at the time of the release of ROSES. To be informed of new program elements or amendments to this NRA, proposers may subscribe to: (1) The SMD mailing lists (by logging in at http://nspires.nasaprs.com and checking the appropriate boxes under "Account Management" and "Email Subscriptions"), (2) The ROSES-2025 blog feed for amendments, clarifications, and corrections to at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/solicitations/roses-2025/ , and (3) The ROSES-2025 due date Google calendars (one for each science division). Instructions are at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/library-and-useful-links (link from the words due date calendar).

sig_cf9535f03041162a3dab.description: The ITZBund requires services in the area of software lifecycle management (SLM) for deployed software development and project management solutions. The tendered services comprise services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts, as well as demand-oriented new and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The client, who can call off services commissioned by its customers, is authorised to call off. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place within the ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases allow operation at the client's customers with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the outset are tendered in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services This specification of services considers the subject matter of Lot 4: The subject matter of this lot is the provision of an open source issue tracker including associated training, support, further development and migration services. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract term of 4 years, an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 150.776 staff hours (SH) or 18.847 person days (PD) results for the estimated calculatory costs.

sig_cf981629d7c6c9d2a3a7.description: Instrument for particle size and shape characterisation of natural and industrial granular materials. Lot 1: . Instrument for particle size and shape characterisation of natural and industrial granular materials e.g.: -Volcanic flow particles (ash, lapilli, pumice, scoria etc.) derived from pyroclastic density currents, fallout deposits, lahars and debris flows. -Industrial particulate materials relevant to construction. -Soils -Construction materials (concretes, mortars, lightweight aggregates, composites) -Agricultural amendments and granules (including Biochar) -Polymer/composite additives -Energy storage materials (electrodes, conductive carbons) Materials will range from coarse granules to fine powders, typically irregular, porous, low-density and black. Essential requirements (minimum) Measurement capability -Measures both particle size distribution and particle shape in one instrument or tightly integrated system. -Image-based technique (e.g. dynamic image analysis or equivalent) suitable for irregular, opaque, carbonaceous particles. -Provides at least: -Size metrics: equivalent diameter, D10/D50/D90, full distribution. -Shape metrics: aspect ratio, circularity/roundness, and at least one compactness/solidity/convexity parameter. Size range and performance -Usable size range: -Lower limit ≤ 1μm -Upper limit ≥ 5 mm -Capable of analysing polydisperse samples in a single run. -At least 50,000 particles analysed per standard measurement (for powders). -Repeatability better than 3 % RSD on D10/D50/D90 for suitable reference materials. Sample handling and dispersion -Dry dispersion unit for low-density, porous, angular powders and granules: -Controlled feed (e.g. vibratory feeder or equivalent). -Adjustable dispersion energy/pressure. -Wet dispersion capability: -Recirculating wet cell for suspensions of soils, biochar and carbon powders. -Compatibility with at least water and common alcohols (e.g. ethanol or isopropanol). Shape analysis and classification -Shape parameters computed for all measured particles or size classes. -Ability to filter and analyse particles by size and/or shape (e.g. size range, aspect ratio range). -Display and export of representative particle images for documentation and publications. Software, data handling and reporting -Method/SOP editor for storing and recalling measurement conditions. -Export of size and shape data in standard formats (e.g. CSV, Excel). -Overlay and comparison of multiple measurements. -Configurable reports (number/area/volume distributions, cumulative and density plots, basic shape statistics). Calibration and practical aspects -Calibration/verification with traceable particle size standards in relevant ranges. -Documented traceability to relevant particle sizing standards (ISO/ASTM or equivalent). -Design suitable for dusty, abrasive, black powders, with straightforward cleaning of the dispersion path. -Enclosed optics and standard laser/electrical safety compliance. -Access to local service and technical support. 3. Desirable (nice-to-have) features Extended capabilities -Integrated laser diffraction module (wet and/or dry) using the same dispersion units, providing sub-micron coverage (≈0.1 μm or lower). -Dedicated fibre/rod analysis (length, width, L/W ratio) for fibrous chars/carbon fibres. -Extended upper size limit to ≥ 10 mm for large granules and aggregates. -Interchangeable optics/lenses to optimise measurements for fine powders vs coarse granules. Advanced dispersion and handling -Multiple dry disperser configurations (gentle and aggressive). -Integrated anti-static measures (e.g. ioniser) for very fine, low-density powders. -Low-volume wet cells (few mL) for expensive or low-yield materials. -Integrated, controllable ultrasonic dispersion (power and time) with logging. Automation and integration -Optional autosampler for unattended measurement of multiple samples. -API or scripting interface for method control and automated data extraction. -Database/LIMS connectivity for long-term storage and retrieval of results. Robustness -Wear-resistant materials in nozzles and flow paths. -Design that minimises cross-contamination.

Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen TKIO procurement system (hereinafter procurement system) forms a central part of the contracting authority's research, development, innovation and competence development activities and procurement platform. It forms the structure of a cooperation model regulated by an agreement between the subscriber and the research, development and innovation partners. The purpose of the services to be competed in the procurement system is to produce research data, development services and innovations as a basis for the subscriber's development activities and management. The procurement system is divided into categories as follows: Category 1 Innovation services Category 2 Development of service systems Category 3 Project services Category 4 Strategic development Category 5 Scientific communities In addition, the subject matter of the procurement includes piloting and experimentation services as well as continuous development and management services for the subscriber's use. The subject matter of the procurement and the operation of the procurement system are described in more detail in the appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system". The minimum requirements for each category and the competence requirements for applicants at the establishment stage are described in more detail in this call for participation. The subscriber shall define the subject matter and requirements of the assignments to be competed in the procurement system in more detail in each internal call for tenders of the procurement system. The procurement system shall be valid until 31.10.2029, during which time the internal call for tenders of the procurement system shall be carried out. The subscriber may extend the validity of the procurement system with a new contract notice. Suppliers may apply to join the procurement system at the establishment stage and later during its validity by submitting a request to participate in accordance with the call for participation. The procurement procedure is two-stage. To be able to submit tenders, a supplier must first submit a request to participate and be admitted to the procurement system. After this, the supplier may submit tenders by responding to the call for tenders sent by the contracting authority. The contracting authority shall carry out internal competitions within the procurement system in the future as needed. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All applicants meeting the suitability requirements shall be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. Actual procurements shall be made through internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system, in which the subject matter of the procurement is described and specified. Participation in the internal competitions of the DPS is not possible unless the supplier has been admitted to the procurement system. The submission of a request to participate and admission to the procurement system does not oblige the supplier to submit a tender, but suppliers may submit tenders at their discretion. The contracting authority estimates that the value excluding value added tax of the planned procurements covered by the dynamic purchasing system at the time of publication of the call for participation is 5,6 million euros, taking into account all procurements potentially made within the system. The estimate is preliminary and based on the procurement need known at this time. The contracting authority does not commit to any procurement quantities or minimum purchase obligations with this notice. Category 1 Innovation services includes the generation of innovations and futures research. The purpose of innovation services is to produce innovative solutions and new methods for the organisation and production of services in an impactful way. Innovation can also aim, for example, at anticipating the demand for services and substantive change needs. Innovations include, for example, digital operating models, solutions related to the innovative utilisation of technology, or the utilisation of robotics and artificial intelligence in social welfare and healthcare services. Central to innovations is the consideration of customer experience, quality, impact and cost perspectives. Innovations may also relate to operational monitoring models, measurement of results or strategic work. The result of an innovation may also be a commercialised product or service. Category 1 Innovation services additionally includes Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.; Category 2 Development of service systems is expert service, the purpose of which is the development of services, service processes, service networks and service systems. The development of service systems includes the collection and analysis of data on the current state, needs and impact of services. The data is utilised in development activities. The development of service systems may include the production of various methods and tools for the subscriber's needs to support the implementation of changes. The service may include the implementation of stakeholder involvement, for example through service design or equivalent means. The development of service systems may also include coaching service, the purpose of which is to support the subscriber in development activities and the consolidation of results. Category 2 Development of service systems additionally includes - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.;

Category 3 Project Services includes the entire project process management for the subscriber's research, development and innovation activities. Project services include project planning services, project management services and project services. Category 3 Project Services also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 4 Strategic development consulting is an expert service intended to provide the subscriber with comprehensive support for development activities and change management, from the perspectives of organiser management and service production. Strategic development consulting produces versatile and comprehensive information, expertise and insights into the development of social and health services and specialised medical care, as well as large-scale integration projects. The consulting offers expert knowledge for promoting the effectiveness, customer-orientation and quality of innovation and development activities in social welfare, health services and specialised medical care, as well as for the design, analysis and implementation of new operating models and process complexes. The strategic development consulting expert service includes versatile expertise in improving the effectiveness and productivity of social and health services, financing systems, improving service accessibility, designing service systems and networks, developing data-driven management capabilities and future forecasting. Strategic development can also include service production management services, which can be used to achieve significant cost savings when service production and the producer field in accordance with procurement contracts can be managed more systematically and purposefully. The service production management service can also help the contracting authority to find consistent and replicable operating processes for managing service providers, with which better service effectiveness, customer satisfaction, quality and cost-efficiency can be achieved. Category 4 Strategic development also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 5 For the scientific community, the procurement system acts as a cooperation platform and procurement channel towards the scientific community, such as universities, higher education institutions, educational institutions, centres of expertise and research institutes. Services procured from the scientific community in the procurement system may include services considered to be scientific activities, which in their content complement projects implemented within the framework of TKIO cooperation. Scientific activity may include any research activity and services in accordance with the subject of the procurement system, but a scientific and research perspective is always emphasised in these services. Services and research activities may be such that the benefit obtained accrues for use in operations other than those of the contracting authority. Services procured from the scientific community may also be research and development services where the benefit obtained accrues exclusively for use in the contracting authority's operations and the contracting authority compensates for the service performed in full. The nature of the service is specified in each call for tenders within the procurement system. Services can also be ordered from the scientific community directly without a call for tenders within the procurement system, if the conditions for the procurement act's scope exemption concerning research and development services (9 section 1 subsection 13 point) are met. Category 5 Scientific community also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.

sig_d023a5cb7fe963cb3088.description: Tenderers are hereby invited to a market dialogue in connection with the procurement of an electronic board for FACT to health companies in the Helse Sør-Øst Market dialogue, which is a part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out because the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from potential suppliers, possibly also from other interested parties. As a part of this process, suppliers are invited to provide input to the procurement prior to the announcement. The Contracting Authority requests written input on as many of the following points as possible: Short presentation of interested party: Description of experience with the Fact Board. What does the tenderer consider to be its core activity and main competence? Tenderers are requested to give a short description of customers who currently use the system, including possibly which parts of the system are used and for which user groups. Points we would like feedback on: Give a description of the tenderer ́s system and how this covers the needs/purposes described. What are the main features and advantages? What type of delivery model/operational model can be delivered (SaaS, other)? Does the tenderer have input on how any environmental requirements can be set for the system? Price models: Which price models do the tenderer operate with and what price models do the supplier recommend? Can the supplier comply with other models if the contracting authority sees it appropriate? What factors affect the price of the tenderer's system? Quality and security: What requirements do the tenderer have in relation to quality of the system? What measures does the tenderer have that ensure that information security and privacy are safeguarded, with particular focus on sensitive areas such as patient safety? Where is the solution installed? Where are the personnel operating and maintaining the system? What kind of support and training do the service provider offer to ensure users get the most out of their solution? Which support and maintenance services does the tenderer offer? Other: How does the supplier work on innovation and further development of the product? How does the supplier ensure that the systems remain relevant in line with technological developments in the market? Are there special developments in the market that the Contracting Authority ought to take into consideration in designing a future-oriented agreement? Which SSA templates think the tenderer is best suited for the delivery and why? Are there any other elements that the contracting authority should pay particular attention to? What should, in accordance with the tenderer ́s view, be emphasised in any future procurement? Furthermore, it may be of interest, if relevant for interested party, to hear about the tenderer's experience from similar public tenders, possibly in comparable countries (preferably countries within the EU). Deadline for written feedback from interested parties: 19.11.2025 This is only a prior information notice to get information on the market and to have a dialogue with relevant suppliers. The actual competition may be announced at a later date. Sykehusinnkjøp HF is assisting Sykehuspartner HF and HSØ with implementation of the market dialogue. See the www.sykehuspartner.no and www.helse-sorost.noFor further information about the contracting authority, please register or questions about the market survey in the Mercell communication module. After this market survey, the contracting authority will assess the need to hold meetings(s) with relevant interested parties.

sig_d0d035a1e770e77ef1bb.description: Assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 The subject of the contract is the assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 (formerly Police 20/20 programme). Programme P20 was created to implement the Saarbrücken Agenda and is a multiproject spanning several implementation levels and years (target picture 2030+). Its core mandate is to replace the heterogeneous police IT landscape and to unify and harmonise all information systems of the German police forces taking into account applicable legal frameworks. For this purpose, uniform, modern procedures are to be provided that can be used by all police forces of the Federation and the Länder according to equal standards. In order to achieve the target picture 2030+ of police casework through programme P20, a step-by-step approach is pursued. In total, more than 45 projects currently fit together as individual building blocks to form the overall programme P20. Important intermediate pictures have already been achieved. A further important intermediate step is to be achieved in the year 2028.
sig_d0d035a1e770e77ef1bb.title: Assumption of technical programme management for programme P20

In order to meet these obligations and objectives, strengthening the economic independence of women and men and promoting economic equality is a declared goal of the Federal Government. This goal has been incorporated into both the Annual Economic Report 2026 and the 7 Poverty and Wealth Report of the Federal Government. Imparting economic orientation knowledge over the life course (e.g., financial consequences of part-time work, care work, and tax bracket selection) is a central lever for this. The work of the "Economic Independence" office is also intended to build upon this. sig_d10bd8bbd65a8a032f32.description:
Investitionsbank Schleswig-Holstein (IB.SH), the central promotional institute of the federal state with currently just under 900 employees, is looking for three framework agreement partners as IT service providers for the provision of IT support services in the field of IT security. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- It is intended to conclude the framework agreement attached to the documents as Appendix 1, the agreement on data processing on behalf with the three bidders who meet the minimum criteria and occupy places 1-3. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The support services specifically required by IB.SH will be called off taking into account the work and project situation, qualification and availability in the context of mini-competitions. The arrangement of these individual call-offs is regulated in Appendix 3 framework agreement (see section 2 of the framework agreement). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- A framework agreement is to be concluded between IB.SH and three service companies. The framework agreement regulates commissions placed on the one hand by IB.SH and comprising the following services: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Description of activities: • Support for the client in technical and technical-organisational matters of IT security / cyber security based on the strategies, policies, roles and responsibilities specified by the client; the list of services is not exhaustive. • Elaboration, concretisation, updating and monitoring of technical IT security standards, technical specifications, operating processes, runbooks and implementation guidelines within the framework of existing internal specifications. • Risk-based assessment, classification and implementation support of technical IT security requirements from operations, change management, projects, architecture, service provider management, regulatory requirements and internal guidelines. • Support for technical IT security, digital operational resilience, recovery and restoration capability and continuity of critical IT services, including technical preparatory work for scenario analyses, emergency exercises, alternative procedures, fallback/exit scenarios and measure tracking. • Initiation, evaluation, implementation and tracking of operational security measures for IT infrastructures, applications, platforms, end devices and operating environments, including on-premises, private cloud, public cloud, hybrid cloud, multi-cloud as well as SaaS/PaaS/IaaS environments. • Coordination, evaluation and further development of technical security architectures, inter alia network and zone concepts, segmentation, firewalling, encryption, PKI, DNSSEC, proxy/gateway services, IAM/PAM, endpoint security, server/client hardening, cloud, container/Kubernetes and API security as well as secure administration models. • Initiation, support, evaluation and tracking of vulnerability analyses, penetration tests, technical security reviews, configuration and hardening checks, readiness checks as well as red/purple team or comparable technical security exercises. • Monitoring and evaluation of external reports on vulnerabilities, threats, attack patterns and security-relevant industry developments as well as derivation, support and documentation of technical measures. • Support with security monitoring, logging, detection and response, in particular for SIEM/SOC requirements, log source onboarding, use case design, alert tuning, detection engineering, SOC provider management, triage processes, playbooks, escalation paths and security-related reporting. • Technical support for handling, containment, analysis, documentation and follow-up of IT security incidents including interfaces to incident, problem, change, emergency and service provider management. • Technical-professional control, evaluation and tracking of service provider reports, security proofs, action plans, audit findings and audit points. • Maintenance, updating and quality assurance of technical IT security documentation, runbooks, control descriptions, verification documentation and technical security concepts. • Technical-professional preparatory work for inspections, audits, revisions and regulatory proofs; the performance of original inspection, audit or control functions is not covered by this. • Support for the data protection officer in technical questions as well as coordination and cooperation with the information security officer / information security management • Carrying out awareness-raising measures for employees on the subject of IT security • Proactive identification, evaluation and target-group-oriented preparation of technical IT security topics within the client's area of responsibility. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The support services specifically required by IB.SH will be called off taking into account the work and project situation, qualification and availability in the context of mini-competitions. The arrangement of these individual call-offs is regulated in the framework agreement (see section 2 of the framework agreement).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The IB.SH expects an annual workload of approx. 1.250 person-days. There is no entitlement to the purchase of a minimum quantity. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The following maximum quantity for the services to be provided applies to this framework agreement in relation to the advertised period: 6.000 person-days. Upon reaching the maximum value, this framework agreement ends automatically without the need for termination. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

sig_d1aa86289da9fcd67343.description: Subject and objective of the procurement The subject of the procurement is mobile robotics technology solutions suitable for the urban environment, which perform tasks in the air, on the ground, or in water. This open call for tenders seeks 6–9 pilots to be implemented. The goal is to obtain information on new and innovative solutions that are suitable for challenging urban environments and support the city's services, maintenance, and decision-making. A particular goal is to help small and medium-sized enterprises solve challenges for which there is an acute need, and to grow their business. Blue City – Digital and safe water city Helsinki can be the world's first city that continuously monitors, measures, and secures its water areas with the help of mobile robotics. The goal is to develop autonomous water robots and data solutions that monitor water quality, map the bottom, and support water and maritime safety. 1. Safe beaches and harbours The goal is to develop an automatic monitoring and tracking system that improves the safety of beaches, harbours, and sea areas. The system detects risks and anomalies in time, tracks the movements of swimmers, and identifies emergencies in real time. Robotics can also be utilised in rescue and retrieval tasks, identification of foreign objects, and monitoring the condition of channels. 2. Smart water quality monitoring and stormwater management Water quality monitoring is currently slow and point-based. The goal is to create a real-time water situational picture based on robotics and data analytics, which enables rapid reaction to anomalies. The solution can monitor turbidity, oxygen content, temperature, electrical conductivity, and nutrient concentrations, as well as automatically take water samples for further analysis. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own new robotics solution related to the water environment, which brings added value to the City of Helsinki and its residents. The solution must utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data that can be utilised in the city's various service areas, for example in the development of infrastructure, safety, or environmental management. Urban Sky – Smart and managed urban airspace Urban airspace is a new infrastructure where drones and sensors operate as part of the city's everyday life. The goal is to build a safe and coordinated airspace where mobile robotics supports monitoring, maintenance, and decision-making. 1. Smart construction site monitoring Monitoring and supervising construction sites takes a lot of resources and is often manual. The goal is to improve the safety, transparency, and productivity of construction sites by monitoring progress and anomalies in real time. 2. Predictive maintenance – detection of leaks and thermal anomalies The city loses significant amounts of energy and water every year due to unnoticed leaks and heat losses. The goal is to develop a system based on air robotics and thermal imaging that identifies leaks and anomalies at an early stage and supports predictive maintenance. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own robotics solution utilising airspace that supports the safety, monitoring, or energy use of the urban environment. The solution must utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data that supports the city's services and decision-making. Smart Ground – Functional and sustainable city all year round A functional and sustainable city utilises mobile robotics, data, and the circular economy so that the city's infrastructure, maintenance, and logistics work seamlessly every day of the year. It is the city's nervous system that maintains vitality and the smooth running of services without interruptions. 1. Infrastructure condition monitoring and modelling The city has thousands of kilometres of streets, cycle paths, and tunnels, the condition of which is laborious and fragmented to inspect. The goal is to develop a solution that provides a continuous, up-to-date, and automatically updating view of the state of the city's infrastructure. 2. Automation and logistics of winter maintenance In the year 2028 dumping snow into the sea will be prohibited, which requires new ways to manage snow collection and processing. The goal is to develop a predictive and data-driven robotics solution that supports snow collection, transport, storage, and melting in an environmentally friendly and cost-effective manner. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own robotics solution suitable for the ground environment, which improves the operation of the city's infrastructure, maintenance, or logistics. The solution can utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data beneficial to the city, for example about the environment, traffic, or energy use.
sig_d1aa86289da9fcd67343.title: Urban Mobile Robotics – We are looking for companies to implement robotics pilots

sig_d35a7d3ffd39ee9f9280.description: PURPOSE NIOSH intends to support the Centers of Excellence in Total Worker Health® (TWH). These Centers will conduct rigorous research and translation activities to prevent harmful exposures, improve working conditions, and advance worker well-being. The Centers will develop practical, scalable solutions for employers and workers. All projects must use the NIOSH Worker Well-Being Questionnaire (WellBQ) and share data with the HERO Worker Well-Being Clearinghouse. Large Research Projects require economic evaluation. PRIORITY AREAS • High-risk occupations: First responders, vehicle mechanics, and technicians, with emphasis on occupational exposures, related health risks, and prevention strategies • Young workers, SMEs • Chronic disease • Mental health, stress • Substance use disorder • Artificial intelligence (AI), digital technologies This is a multi-component NOFO. COMPONENT STRUCTURE Percentages indicate maximum share of total budget. Overall Component (Required) Provides Center leadership and integration. Applicants should show strong coordination, scientific direction, and alignment across projects. Administration, Evaluation, and Emerging Issues Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports management and Center-wide evaluation. Applicants should describe oversight, data governance, and quality assurance.Optional activities include emerging issues and shared research resources. Outreach, Dissemination, and Impact Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports communication, worker/employer engagement, training, translation, implementation, and dissemination strategies. Research Projects (Required; about 60 to 70%) Includes all research activities. Applicants may propose a mix of projects. Research project distinctions are based on scope and complexity rather than cost. Projects should demonstrate scientific rigor and potential for sustained impact. Small Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 3 years) Exploratory, feasibility, early-stage intervention, surveillance, or measurement studies. Priority areas: high-risk occupations, young workers, SMEs. Should show innovation and potential to expand. Large Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 5 years) Multiyear etiologic, mechanistic, intervention, or translational studies. Priority areas: chronic disease, mental health, substance use disorder. Economic evaluation is required. Projects should include strong design and analytic plans. Pilot/Feasibility Program (Optional; 12–18 months) Short-term studies generating preliminary data or testing AI/digital technology approaches.
sig_d35a7d3ffd39ee9f9280.title: NIOSH Centers of Excellence for Total Worker Health® (U19)

sig_d4b3bb2658f98ccda497.description: The subject of the contract is the "Operation, Maintenance, Support and Upgrade of the information systems 'Registration for First Grade Primary School' and electronic applications for admission to Model Schools, Public Onassis Schools, Model Ecclesiastical Schools and Experimental Schools". The subject of the contract focuses mainly on: • Operation, Maintenance and Technical Support Services (Phase A): concerns both systems, throughout the duration of the contract, which cover, by way of example: preventive and corrective maintenance, patch management, backup/restore, monitoring, alerting, management and optimisation of AWS infrastructure, load testing and enhanced readiness (on-call) during peak periods, as well as technical support for system administrators. sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.description: The subject of the procurement is a work ability management system as a SaaS service. The procurement includes the delivery of the system, planning and implementation of the deployment, execution of necessary integrations, and ongoing maintenance and support services. In addition, the contracting authority has the option to procure separately agreed minor development during the contract period. The supplier is responsible for ensuring that the system can be deployed in a controlled manner and that it is integrated into the contracting authority's key back-end systems, such as HR and identity management systems. The migration of legacy data can be carried out as expert work as a separately ordered option in accordance with the hourly rate for expert work stated in the price appendix. The contracting authority shall decide on the implementation of the option at its own discretion during the contract period, and the contracting authority is under no obligation to implement the option or order related services. The system must support the contracting authority's work ability management operating models and processes, in particular early support practices, management of sickness absences, identification and prevention of work ability risks, and support for return to work. The objective of the solution is to improve the timeliness of work ability measures, increase operational transparency, and strengthen data-driven management at all levels of the organisation. The system must provide an up-to-date overall picture of the work ability situation at the employee, unit, and organisational level. It must form a clear, user-friendly, and intuitive whole regarding work ability management processes and offer views and access rights according to user roles. User groups include at least line managers, HR work ability specialists, management, and system administrators. Line managers must be able to utilise the system in their daily work ability management work, while for management, the system must offer summary views, reporting, and analytics to support strategic decision-making. The system must enable versatile reporting for different time periods and organisational levels and offer visual views, such as trends, comparisons, and key performance indicators to support decision-making. The supplier must carry out the deployment in cooperation with the contracting authority so that the solution meets the contracting authority's functional needs and the deployment supports a smooth transition to production use. The objective of the procurement is to improve the effectiveness of work ability management, reduce costs caused by sickness absences, strengthen proactive management, and support the staff's work ability, performance at work, and continuation in work. The system must be a modern, secure, scalable, and easy-to-use solution that supports the long-term development of the contracting authority's operations.
sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.title: Procurement of a work ability management system

This request for information is aimed at collating those views from market participants. Framework participants will be expected to provide a range of Fair Work First measures. This notice is issued for information only and does not constitute a call for competition. Scottish Government and the Scottish Ministers shall have no liability for any costs, however incurred, by those attending any information days, attendance at meetings, or involvement in the proposed procurement process. sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.description: The NSF Engineering Directorate (ENG) has launched a multi-year initiative, theProfessional Formation of Engineers, to create and support an innovative and inclusive engineering profession for the 21 st century. Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) refers to the formal and informal processes and value systems by which people become engineers. It also includes the ethical responsibility of practicing engineers to sustain and grow the profession in order to improve quality of life for all peoples. The engineering profession must be responsive to national priorities, grand challenges, and dynamic workforce needs; it must be equally open and accessible to all. Professional Formation of Engineers includes, but is not limited, to: Introductions to the profession at any age; Development of deep technical and professional skills, knowledge, and abilities in both formal and informal settings/domains; Development of outlooks, perspectives, ways of thinking, knowing, and doing; Development of identity as an engineer and its intersection with other identities; and Acculturation to the profession, its standards, and norms. The goal of the Research in the Formation of Engineers (RFE) program is to advance our understanding of professional formation. It seeks both to deepen our fundamental understanding of the underlying processes and mechanisms that support professional formation and to demonstrate how professional formation is or can be accomplished. Ultimately RFE aims to transform the engineer-formation system, and thus the impact of proposed projects on this system must be described. Principal Investigators (PIs) should provide a roadmap detailing how they envision the proposed research will eventually broadly impact practice within the engineer-formation system, even if these activities are not within the scope of the submitted proposal. In order to accomplish its goals, RFE welcomes proposals in two categories: Research Projects, and Design and Development Projects. Research Projects address fundamental questions of professional formation, while Design and Development Projects provide new approaches to achieving professional formation. Additional details are provided below. Projects in both categories should address the iterative cycle in which research questions that advance understanding are informed by practice and the results of research are, in turn, translated into practice. In other words, proposals should explain how the research results will travel, translate, transfer, or scale. Successful projects identify specific target audiences, effective communication channels, and novel partnerships to ensure effective propagation and scaling. Proposal titles should begin with either “Research:” or “Design and Development:” as appropriate. Research Projects Research proposals are particularly welcome in the following areas: Research that addresses lifelong learning by the engineering workforce. Research on the impact of engineering education research. Proposals addressing this topic could investigate questions such as: How can we measure the impacts of engineering education research? What are effective strategies for scaling reforms? How can we translate knowledge from research to practice? What are the roles of technologies, networks and communities in achieving impact? RFE does not support efficacy, effectiveness, or scale-up studies for specific interventions. Research that addresses culture change in engineering education. Included in this topic are investigations of normative cultures of engineering at any level in the engineering education ecosystem and how these cultures may disadvantage certain groups. Research that addresses engineering formation at the two-year college level in both formal and informal settings. Research that addresses engineering formation at the graduate education level in both formal and informal settings. Research that investigates engineering in P-12 settings. Research in this area could include understanding of approaches to engineering in P-12, how to develop engineering ways of thinking, or the relationship between practices within the sciences and mathematics and engineering thinking. Research on the transitions between education levels, e.g., from high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. Research that addresses the relationship between engineering and the public. Proposals addressing this topic could consider the social impact of engineering solutions, citizen engineering, education of an informed public, etc. Research that develops or adapts novel methodologies and frameworks appropriate for studying the professional formation of engineers, and especially minoritized, marginalized, or underserved populations. Research that addresses ways in which new technologies (such as artificial intelligence and machine learning) are changing engineering education. Research to transform engineering education so that all students encounter environmental and social sustainability principles as an integrated part of their education and are equipped with the tools needed to incorporate these principles into their future research, careers, and innovations. Proposals submitted to the Research Projects category should have clear research questions informed by an appropriate theoretical framework and a research design that includes sampling, data collection, and data analysis methods. This category will not support proposals that seek funding primarily to develop tools, curriculum, or laboratories, or that seek to implement classroom innovations that have already been shown to be effective in engineering. The program will evaluate the value of proposals by considering the impact and the cost. Research track projects that are small, exploratory, or speculative are especially encouraged. Larger Research track projects should have a correspondingly larger impact. Design and Development Projects RFE supports Design and Development projects (see https://www.nsf.gov/publications/pub_summ.jsp?ods_key=nsf13126 ) that seek to develop and test new approaches in the following areas related to engineering education : Graduate education. Undergraduate education in new engineering technologies and environmental sustainability. Transitions between education levels, for example high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. P-12, especially approaches to develop engineering thinking, or providing links between engineering, science, and mathematics. Proposals in this category should propose the design and development of new approaches that are informed by existing literature and theory. There should be clear objectives and the evaluation plan should be designed to determine if those objectives have been met. Projects cannot be solely demonstration projects but must add to the engineering education literature to inform future work.
sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.title: Research in the Formation of Engineers

sig_d6f8e6164bb579dcf08e.description: New operational control system [ELS] The Fraport AG, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is a world-leading airport operator. The company was founded in 1924 and operates Frankfurt Airport, one of the most significant air traffic hubs in the world. Furthermore, Fraport is involved in the management and operation of several other airports worldwide. Fraport currently operates the software (SW) ELDIS III from the company eurofunk at the Frankfurt am Main site as a KRITIS and LuftSIG-relevant system in the security control centre with the service areas of works fire brigade, rescue service and security as an operational control system, and in the integrated passenger flow control centre as a workflow system. The system currently in use is foreseeably reaching its technical limits, so that a replacement is necessary. The functions to be replaced by new systems include operational control and force deployment, hazard report management and the provision of geoinformation in the form of a geoproxy. Maintenance, servicing, service and support are also required for all new systems. Applicants must sign a confidentiality agreement provided by Fraport (see informational documents) and submit it together with the application to participate. After the call for competition, an indicative tender round will initially be carried out as part of the tender phase, which will then be followed by one or more binding tender rounds. Within the indicative tender round, the tenderers may propose changes to the contract, service description and annexes. Fraport will decide on their acceptance or rejection. The contracting authority points out now that the contractor must mandatorily provide the following evidence in the event of being requested to submit a binding tender: 1. All persons deployed in the project and in all maintenance, service and support services are German-speaking at least at level B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) and are provided from a time zone UTC +0 to +3. 2. Proof of full access to the control of development resources and unrestricted authorisation to modify and expand the offered software and hardware. Due to the importance of the overall system to be procured here for the maintenance of flight operations and the mandatory framework schedule to be adhered to, Fraport may withdraw from the entire contract if the contractor culpably fails to provide, or fails to provide in accordance with the contract, services marked as "already available" in terms of hardware and software functions at the time of contract conclusion. The scope includes the delivery, agile (additional) development, commissioning with migration of legacy systems of a new operational control system for the security control centre and the integrated control centre for operational control and force deployment, the training of the employees of the Fraport AG as well as maintenance, service and support services.
sig_d6f8e6164bb579dcf08e.title: New operational control system [ELS]

sig_d74f2de21ded711320f5.description: The Espoo Region Joint Authority for Education (Omnia) is planning to put out to tender financial and payroll administration and HR systems and related services. The systems would be procured as a SaaS service, and for some areas of finance, payroll administration and HR, the procurement of the service is also being considered, whereby, for example, payroll would come to Omnia as a comprehensive service. The content emphasis and scope of the tender (only statutory services or broader, system procurement as a SaaS service or extensive comprehensive service procurement) will be specified further before the publication of the contract notice. Regarding statutory financial and payroll administration functionalities, Omnia's current goal is for the new solution (or comprehensive service) to be in use from 1.1.2027 onwards. Omnia invites suppliers to participate in a market dialogue, the goal of which is to obtain a comprehensive picture of the systems and services available on the market. With the help of the information obtained, Omnia will evaluate what kind of benefits they produce and how they would be suitable for Omnia's needs. The market survey is open to all suppliers that have systems or services belonging to this solution entity to offer. The focus of the market survey is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where the key functionalities are already implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or only at the concept level is not desired in this context. WRITTEN REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Omnia offers all suppliers an open opportunity to provide their comments in writing and to submit possible service descriptions and other attachments by email. Written observations are requested by Mon 13.10.2025 at 12.00 via the Forms form: https://forms.office.com/e/x36eWVynyU. Service descriptions and other attachments can be submitted on the same schedule by email to emma.strengell@kpmg.fi. Omnia may request a meeting or additional information from those participating in the request for information if it considers it necessary.

sig_d79a916f8bc033b751fc.description: This is a request for information, which is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to gather information concerning the subject matter of the procurement for a future competitive tender. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent competitive tender. To ensure the success of the future competitive tender, it would nevertheless be important for potential tenderers to provide the contracting authority with the requested information as comprehensively as possible. The request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the request for information or its appendices, and the competitive tender may also be left unperformed. The subject matter of this request for information is key cabinets and a system that enables the management of physical keys and other items to be handed over, the administration of handovers, and the centralised management of key cabinet solutions. The purpose is to survey the capability related to systems, the market situation of additional services, products, contract terms and conditions, and supplier pricing. We kindly request a response to the questions we have presented, which are in the appendix "Request for information and questions" to this request for information. The subject matter of the procurement is key cabinets, as well as a system entity that enables the management of physical keys and other items, the management of handovers and archiving, and the centralised management of key cabinet solutions. Responses to the request for information must be submitted no later than 6.11.2025 by 23.59 by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. The information provided will be treated confidentially. In the request for information response, tenderers are kindly requested to state their willingness to participate in a market dialogue meeting. Based on the responses received, Istekki will select, at its own discretion, 1-5 tenderer(s) to present their equipment and services in an approximately one-hour meeting via Teams. Detailed information on responding and the market dialogue, as well as provisional dates for the meetings, have been notified in the appendix "Request for information and questions". Respondents to the request for information will not be paid compensation for producing the request for information or for participating in any presentation events related to the request for information. The tender service automatically creates deadlines for submitting questions and responding to the request for information. Instead of these deadlines, the deadlines in the request for information document shall be observed. Any additional questions must primarily be submitted as part of the request for information responses. The contracting authority will not publish additional questions submitted during the request for information stage.

sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.buyer_original: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark
sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA) is in the process of streamlining the management of its development cooperation. Part of this effort concerns the simplification of the procurement process of key consultancy services relating to development cooperation. Consultancy contracts are currently procured individually by the case worker responsible for the programme or project. Case workers are MFA staff from MFA services at home in Copenhagen and abroad. In the procurement of individual contracts, they are responsible for the choice of procurement modality, the planning, preparation and management of the tender and contracting process. This process is often lengthy, and can have implications on programme and project timelines. Moreover, the fragmentation of the process makes it difficult to use the feedback from case workers on the fulfilment of the assignments. This makes it challenging to harvest learning from past performance and ensure a sustained quality of services. It is in this context that the MFA wishes to consolidate the procurement of consultancy services through a framework agreement with multiple contractors. The streamlining of the management of Danish development cooperation entailed a revision of the Danida – Aid Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/). This foresees a delegation of key tasks to external consultants, primarily appraisals, and thereby an expected rise in the number of consultancy services to be requested. It is therefore an opportune time to seek a more streamlined procurement process of consultancy services. AMGs contain the policies, guidelines, and tools for the MFA’s development cooperation assistance. They cover different forms of Danish development cooperation modalities. The AMG’s Bilateral Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/guidelines-for-programmes-projects-country-strategic-frameworks-and-hard-earmarked-multilat-support) and Financial Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/financial-management) constitute the basic set of procedures for all Danish bilateral development cooperation. The guidelines outline the processes and requirements for the preparation, formulation, quality assurance, approval, implementation, completion and closure of Danish bilateral programmes and projects. The framework agreement is expected to solely cover bilateral development cooperation programmes and projects designed and implemented by Denmark. Therefore, the expected scope of work of consultancy services solely pertains to Official Development Aid (ODA) funds. The framework agreement is also expected to be divided into two lots. Under each lot, the MFA expects to conclude a framework agreement with between three to seven contractor to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during the term of the framework agreement, specifically the terms for award of contracts with/without reopening of competition amongst the contractors on the framework agreement. The expected lots reflect the thematic areas and priorities of Denmark’s Strategy for Development Cooperation: Lot 1: Climate change, environment, private sector development, enabling environment and financing. Lot 2: Governance, response to conflicts, forced displacement, irregular migration, health and education. Each lot is expected to require the provision of the following services pertaining to the design and implementation phases of bilateral development cooperation programmes, namely: Formulation of bilateral programmes and projects. This may include preparatory work in the formulation process if and as needed. Appraisal of the design of bilateral programmes and projects as a quality assurance milestone prior to approval. This includes external appraisals and early appraisals of larger or high-risk programmes/projects. Review of bilateral programmes and projects under implementation. This can span inception, midterm and technical reviews as part of the MFA unit’s monitoring and reporting cycle. The estimated values of the procurement and the lots are preliminary estimates.
sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.title: Consultancy framework agreement for formulation, appraisal and review of Danish development cooperation programmes and projects

sig_d9979f0b8c35ebe15197.description: NOTE! This is not a call for tenders, procurement notice or prior information notice, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning. Espoon kaupunki has initiated the preparation for the procurement of a shared vehicle monitoring tool and is inviting suppliers to a market dialogue. The objective of the procurement of the shared vehicle management tool is to implement monitoring in accordance with the micro-mobility permit (18 section) referred to in the Act on Transport Services (3030/2025) within the area of the City of Espoo. The management tool is used to collect and monitor shared vehicle movement data and to set operating rules and restrictions for them. The tool aims to improve urban safety and facilitate urban planning based on shared vehicle usage and regulatory data. The subject of the procurement is a shared vehicle monitoring tool procured as a service as follows: - System as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) - Commissioning and customisation of the service for Espoo - Application maintenance services - Further development and expert services of the system according to Espoo's needs. The functionalities of the shared vehicle monitoring tool are aimed to cover the following: - Basic functions of the management tool, i.e. collecting and displaying usage data of approximately 6000 shared vehicles to the user. - Real-time and visual user interface for monitoring shared vehicles, i.e. displaying map-based information regarding shared vehicles and traffic operators based on the location data of the shared vehicles to the user. - Setting area- and shared-vehicle-operator-specific rules and restrictions for shared vehicles, as well as providing the user with notifications based on the rules and restrictions. - Analysis functions of the collected data as well as scenario analyses (proposals) on rules and measures to be set based on the collected data. - Reporting and statistical functionalities. - Management of user roles and access rights. The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation regarding the procurement of the shared vehicle monitoring tool. Espoon kaupunki wants to hear potential suppliers' thoughts on the implementation of the procurement procedure and the preparation of the call for tenders. SCHEDULE FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue will tentatively be conducted in two phases: 1. Via Teams tentatively during week 51. The contracting authority reserves the right to invite 3-5 suppliers to the first phase of the dialogue based on the responses to the request for information. The objective of this first phase is to familiarise oneself with the products on the market, for example through supplier demos. 2. Tender documents will be sent to those who have registered for the market dialogue for comments approximately during weeks 51-2. The second phase of the market dialogue will be conducted electronically. Written material will be sent to all those who have registered for the market dialogue for review approximately during weeks 51-2. The dialogue of the second phase will cover the content of the preliminary call for tenders, the requirement specification and the contractual terms. The contracting authority reserves the right to additional dialogues as the market survey progresses. The contracting authority's objective is to launch the actual procurement procedure in the spring of 2026 and the implementation project by May 2026 at the latest, so that the new system can be taken into use in the summer of 2026. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND REGISTERING FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE We kindly ask suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue to register in writing by 10.12.2025 at 16.00 to the address hankinta@espoo.fi. Clearly title your registration message, e.g. "Market dialogue: Procurement of shared vehicle monitoring tool - registration [Company name]". Please provide the name of your contact person at the same time. The market dialogue and the information provided therein shall not bind any participating party, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the subsequent actual tender contest. The official call for tenders will only be published after the market dialogues have ended. Responses will be handled confidentially.
sig_d9979f0b8c35ebe15197.title: Market dialogue invitation and request for information: Procurement of a tracking tool for shared vehicles

sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.description: DSB wishes to gain a better understanding of SAP RISE, and therefore an invitation to a market dialogue concerning this is extended. Background: DSB currently uses an SAP S/4HANA solution, which supports a large number of administrative business processes in the company. S/4HANA runs on-premises via an infrastructure and operations agreement with TCS. This agreement expires in the summer of 2028, which is why DSB must carry out an EU tender presumably in 2027. Against this background, DSB is considering whether the tender should comprise either: - Infrastructure and operation services regarding SAP S/4HANA based on on-premises or, - migration of DSB’s SAP S/4HANA solution to a SaaS solution in a private cloud – which is currently marketed under the name SAP RISE. Therefore, DSB wishes via market dialogue to gain insight into what suppliers in the market offer related to SAP RISE. DSB expects the individual supplier to provide a total overview of deliverables and commercial terms. DSB wishes, among other things, answers to: 1) Description of the current market. 2) Description of the supplier's footprint in the market. Generally and regarding SAP RISE. 3) Contract setup including interfaces to SAP SE. 4) Listing of services linked to the service: 4.1) Which services are delivered as standard? 4.2) Which services can be purchased additionally? 4.3) How are these services designed with regard to SLAs? 5) Description of cooperation model. 6) How and according to which structure does settlement of ongoing operations take place? 7) Description of model for transition and settlement of this. Preferably with TCO assessments. 8) Description of hardware, data centres, and geography used. 9) Description of IT security model and IT security management. DSB expects to conduct interviews with a selection of suppliers in December 2025 and January 2026. The purpose of the interviews is to gather information on which solutions and services are offered in the market. DSB plans to conduct market dialogue meetings with a maximum of six suppliers. If more than the six suppliers apply, DSB will make a representative selection among the expressions of interest received.
sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding SAP RISE

sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the creation of a Validation Center to serve as a dedicated hub for the comprehensive evaluation and characterization of AI-enabled, image-based, multimodal CDS tools developed by the PRIMED-AI Consortium, to ensure these tools are reliable, reproducible, and generalizable. The Validation Center will focus on verification, validation, interoperability, and uncertainty quantification to comprehensively characterize performance of the CDS tools developed by the program. The core functions of the Validation Center will involve the systematic validation of PRIMED-AI Consortium deliverables, including those emerging from award recipients under the Playbook, Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnerships, and Model-to-Clinic NOFOs.
sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.title: Validation Center for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U54 Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_db5951a98f9d30d176d3.description: Welcome to submit tenders for Migrationsverket. Migrationsverket hereby invites suppliers to submit tenders in this procurement of a contact centre. The procurement relates to a new contact centre platform (hereinafter referred to as the System). The System shall handle the answering of telephone calls and e-mail messages from the general public and manage the routing and follow-up of incoming cases (emails and incoming calls). The System shall provide functionality for Callback and a module for scheduling. Queue and individual statistics shall also be handled in the System. After the implementation of the System is completed, approximately 200 concurrent agents and 20 administrators are estimated to work in the System. Migrationsverket receives approximately 1 400 000 incoming calls and 400 000 emails per year in the current contact centre system. The System needs to be dimensioned to cope with the demand, which may vary over time. The System shall be hosted as a private cloud service. The core functions of the System – that is, the management of calls, e-mails and the scheduling module – shall be hosted in a server hall owned or exclusively rented by the supplier (or its subcontractor) and this shall have its physical location within the EU/EEA. The supplier shall have full technical and administrative control over the hardware, network and operating platform in the server hall. Migrationsverket will provide a separate service for encrypting free text in incoming e-mail messages before they reach the System. This encryption service shall be hosted locally by Migrationsverket. The technical design of the service is not yet fully defined, but will be developed in dialogue with the supplier during the implementation project. The System shall be able to handle e-mail flows where free text content is encrypted upon receipt and decrypted close to the client in the agent's web browser through a component provided by Migrationsverket. The supplier is not responsible for the development or operation of this encryption service, but shall ensure that the System is technically compatible with its mode of operation and supports secure handling of encrypted e-mail messages in accordance with the specification of requirements. Integrations with the Windows environment and Migrationsverket's telephony operator shall be included. In the procurement, the tenderer shall tender: A private cloud service that is complete and fulfils the mandatory requirements set out in the procurement and the evaluation requirements accepted by the supplier.An implementation project that includes planning, integrations, configuration of system settings, fine-tuning and testing of the System to a fully operational condition.The System shall be set up in a test and training environment, as well as a production environment.Integrations with Migrationsverket's system, which appear in the Specification of Requirements.Necessary documentation for the implementation of integration(s).Documentation.Training.Option regarding, inter alia, a screen sharing function (co-browsing) and chat functionConsultancy services in connection with the System.Services for support, fault clearance and further development of the System
sig_db5951a98f9d30d176d3.title: Kontaktcenter
