sig_db984e9fe7f8b57441ff.description: To map various ticketing processes, the State Office for Finance (LfF) requires a new ticketing system, which must be operated in the state-owned data centre of LDI (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud). The new procedure is intended to replace the previously used SAP SOLUTION MANAGER 7.2 with the SP stack 20 - as of 11/2025 - and the previously used ticketing procedure Zammad. The new procedure is also intended to map tickets from other, non-SAP-based areas. The complete implementation of the new ticketing system (including the necessary connection to downstream systems, acceptance testing and multiplier training) is to take place by 31.07.2027. Productive use of the new ticketing system must therefore be ensured for all connected users (including users from other authorities in the federal state of Rhineland-Palatinate) from 01.08.2027 at the latest. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract. Lot LOT-0001: Ticketing system. The subject of the procurement is the creation of the overall system described in the procurement documents, including the establishment of operational readiness by the contractor on the basis of a works contract, as well as system service and the further development of the overall system. The overall system consists of a client-specifically adapted, standard ticketing system software (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud of LDI / rental) that meets the requirements of modern ticket processing by the client, including associated client-specifically created or adapted integrations into the client's IT system in accordance with the further regulations, in particular in accordance with the functional and technical specifications of the client, cf. specification of services. This includes, inter alia, the integration of the ticketing system software into the SAP landscape operated by the client, inter alia connection to transport management, the mapping of various evaluations and reports, the establishment of knowledge bases and migrations from various source systems. To produce the overall system, the software must, inter alia, be set up and configured, in particular user accounts created and data imported in accordance with the specification of services or system environment, the software connected via interfaces to various tools of the client, the required automation established, high interoperability with the named third-party systems established, tested, test instances set up and operated, and the onboarding process successfully completed, including interface integration with the third-party systems and training courses. Productive use after acceptance of the overall system must be contractually possible for all connected users of the client, cf. specification of services, by 01.08.2027. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract.
sig_db984e9fe7f8b57441ff.title: Ticket system

sig_dc7d4b0214ccaf561bc6.description: The Landesverband Lippe, a public-law body, intends to modernise the Externsteine information centre and stage the surrounding area in Horn-Bad Meinberg digitally as an integrated "Externsteine Experience World". The Externsteine, which attract around 600.000 visitors per year, are to be further developed into a sustainable, interactive and low-barrier experience venue. The visitor centre, which is currently not accessible and technically obsolete, forms the central starting and experience point. Lot LOT-0001: LVL Externsteine. The subject of the procurement is the modernisation of the Externsteine information centre and the digital staging of the surrounding area into an integrated "Externsteine Experience World". What is being procured is a concept together with its implementation, meaning on the one hand the conceptualisation including all planning services and official approval and authorisation procedures, and on the other hand the complete implementation including any construction services, IT services and further services (such as support and training). The contract is awarded as a staged contract: Upon the award of contract, solely stage 1 (drawing up of the concepts) is commissioned, whereas the implementation services (stage 2) as well as the granting of licences, technical support and training (stage 3) are tendered as options, on the calling-off of which the contracting authority decides within five months after acceptance of stage 1. The concept, the planning of the implementation and the implementation itself are to be designed freely by the contractor, but must meet certain minimum requirements based on the actual situation coupled with the available budget and the statutory provisions. General requirements: - The Externsteine and the entire surrounding area are subject to nature conservation, and all services to be conceptualised must be consistent with the requirements arising therefrom. The contractor must ensure that both the concept already and the complete implementation comply with all nature conservation law requirements. This also includes all necessary measures taken for the implementation of the concept. - The historical documents and data on the Externsteine are provided by the Landesverband Lippe and the Externsteine Conservation Association and are not to be compiled by the contractor, but are to be prepared didactically and scenographically, digitalised and compiled depending on the type of use. - This project is funded in part by a subsidy from the State of NRW and is therefore to be conceptualised and implemented in such a way that all funding law provisions are fully complied with. - A Progressive Web App or a mobile app for iOS and Android is to be conceptualised, programmed and made available for download in the common app stores, which contains natural history, geological and historical information on the Externsteine and depicts the area including paths and sights, and the app must also contain the link to the homepage so that current information can be accessed directly. Further content is to be conceptualised and implemented by the contractor. Further functions that allow visitors to experience the site actively must be present - a WhatsApp scavenger hunt is to be conceptualised as well - Every software must be compatible at least with ChromeOS and Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of performance - every hardware must be compatible at least with ChromeOS, additional compatibility with Microsoft Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of performance, is desirable. Information centre requirements: - Insertion of inspection openings everywhere where information technology is installed and/or will be installed - Replacement of obsolete hardware - Utilisation of the existing screen openings in the walls and the central X made of painted wood - No structural changes to the basic structure of the rooms - Preservation of the analogue stations in the display cases - Installation (indoor) including furnishing with software, licences and a moderation dashboard of a social wall; the moderation is taken over by the Landesverband Lippe - At least production and installation of a tactile relief of the Externsteine formation and the Descent from the Cross relief as a 3D print - Revision and modernisation as well as new creation of digital content including didactic aspects - Expansion of the use of the cinema - Digital content must be provided on physical data carriers (USB sticks, locally on a PC) in order to enable simple exchange and to be able to offer an integrated visitor experience even in the event of an internet outage; the file formats must be playable independently of the operating system - Excluded from this are contents whose existence is purely online (SocialWall, App) - Creation of barrier-free access to contents - Reliable and easily analysable visitor counter - Sign stating that the measure is subsidised according to the specification from the approval notice. Further specific requirements can be found in sections V and VI of the specification of services (Appendix B01). The project is financed in part from public subsidy funds. Binding under funding law are a total budget of 620.000 EUR (thereof 372.000 EUR subsidised, distributed across financial years 2026 and 2027) as well as a cost breakdown of 255.000 EUR furnishings/scenography, 25.000 EUR construction costs and 340.000 EUR technology costs. sig_dcc46098575b55940870.description: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover 1. Background The Region Hannover has set itself the ambitious goal of being climate-neutral by the year 2035. The energy-efficient refurbishment of the building stock is a central component for achieving this goal. In particular, improving the thermal insulation of buildings offers considerable potential for reducing CO2 emissions and increasing energy efficiency. In order to raise awareness among owners of residential and non-residential buildings regarding potential heat losses and refurbishment needs, a comprehensive thermal imaging map is to be created. The aim is to create a low-threshold information basis through a visually prepared presentation of thermal radiation data. The interactive online map should make it possible to classify one's own building stock in a regional context and initiate further steps if necessary. By linking with the advisory services of the climate protection agency Region Hannover (KSA) as well as existing funding programmes, the project is intended to trigger concrete refurbishment measures. 2. Contents and procedure The subject of the contract is the supply of thermographic digital orthophotos (DOP), i.e., distortion-free and georeferenced thermography recordings, for the area of Region Hannover. The contractor's delivery service includes carrying out the flight including preparation as well as the transmission of the processed data.

sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT AND MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the planned procurement is the acquisition of expert services for the establishment, development and operation of a centralized AI and Data Factory service (hereinafter the “AI & Data Factory”). The AI and Data Factory will support the Contracting Entity in developing, deploying, maintaining and continuously improving data, artificial intelligence, machine learning and analytics solutions and capabilities throughout their lifecycle. The AI and Data Factory service may include, but is not limited to, the following services: Decision Intelligence and Data Platform services Design, development, testing, deployment and continuous lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions, including business intelligence, data science, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and agentic AI, as well as related data platform capabilities. The services may include, for example: - design and implementation of data, business intelligence, advanced analytics, machine-learning and AI solutions; - continuous development, maintenance, monitoring and lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions; - continuous validation and quality assurance, including model behaviour, outputs, end-result quality, data quality and data usage; - development, deployment and operation of AI and AI agent governance practices; - development, operation and continuous improvement of data platforms; and - other AI-, data-, analytics- and technology-related expert and consulting services supporting the objectives of the procurement. Data Governance and Management services Data governance and data management services may be provided as part of projects, continuous development activities and ongoing data management operations. The services may include, for example: - external data sourcing, data content development, data validation and data migration; - continuous data quality monitoring and improvement; and - development, implementation and follow-up of master data management processes for agreed data domains. The services are expected to be delivered in close collaboration with the Contracting Entity’s internal experts and other suppliers. The preliminary allocation of responsibilities between the Contracting Entity and the Supplier or Suppliers will be further specified based on the procurement preparation and market dialogue. The Contracting Entity intends to select 3 - 5 or more Suppliers. The final procurement and service delivery model, including the number of Suppliers and the allocation of responsibilities, will be determined during the preparation of the procurement. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The Contracting Authority seeks market input on the planned scope of the procurement, service model, preliminary service descriptions, procurement structure, competence requirements, commercial models and other elements relevant to the successful establishment and operation of the AI Factory. Suppliers are encouraged not only to comment on the Contracting Authority's preliminary proposals, but also to challenge the proposed approaches and suggest alternative, innovative or more effective solutions and operating models based on their experience, market practices and emerging AI capabilities. The Contracting Authority particularly welcomes ideas that may improve the scope, structure, flexibility, scalability, commercial model or long-term effectiveness of the procurement. The purpose of the market dialogue is to utilize market expertise in developing the procurement and to ensure that the final approach is feasible, proportionate, future-proof and aligned with market capabilities, while enabling innovation and the effective adoption of evolving AI technologies, services and operating models. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE - Market dialogue: H2/2026 - Publication of the Invitation to Tender: Q1/2026 - Evaluation of tenders: H1/2027 - Procurement decision: H1/2027 - Contract commencement: H1/2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a Prior Information Notice. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The Prior Information Notice includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest by email to tommi.aarnio@vr.fi no later than 28 September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize written consultation rounds, joint market dialogue sessions and, where considered appropriate, bilateral meetings with selected suppliers. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, timetable and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.

sig_dde1696066b8d991bfd1.description: The objective is to manage user identities, roles, and permissions centrally, in an automated and audit-proof manner in the future. The scope of services includes the provision of the IAM software, complete implementation and integration into the existing IT infrastructure, the migration of existing data, comprehensive testing, and ongoing German-language support. The solution must be operated entirely within the ALDB infrastructure. The licences are to be provided for a minimum term of two years, with a maximum of four years. Functionally required are, in particular, joiner, mover, and leaver processes, role and permission management, access requests, approval workflows, identity governance, administration, reporting, audit logging, and interfaces to existing systems such as Active Directory, HR systems, databases, and Kubernetes environments. In addition, a secure backup and recovery concept, a minimum availability of 95 % per month, and regulated training and acceptance processes are provided for. Operational go-live is to take place following a successful test and acceptance phase, at the latest by 01.12.2026. An exit concept must be provided for the end of the contract. The project comprises the following service components: a) Provision of the IAM software solution (on-premise) The contractor must provide the offered Identity & Access Management (IAM) solution as an on-premise solution. This includes all software licences, including all modules and functionalities required to fulfil the functional, technical, and security-related requirements defined in this specification of services. Licencing must enable the management of the intended number of user identities, roles, permissions, target systems, and applications, as well as demand-driven scaling to support future expansions of ALDB's IT landscape. b) Consulting services, implementation, and integration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, implementation, configuration, parameterisation, integration, commissioning, test support, and professional and technical guidance throughout the entire project duration. The scope of services includes, in particular, the integration of the IAM solution into ALDB's existing IT infrastructure, including the connection of all agreed source and target systems, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Kubernetes environments, and other business-critical applications. Furthermore, the organisational structure, the role and permission concept, identity lifecycle management, provisioning and de-provisioning processes, approval workflows, access requests, recertification processes, and audit and reporting functions are to be implemented and configured. All implementation and integration work must be carried out in such a way that ALDB's ongoing business operations are not impaired. c) Testing Following the award of the contract and prior to operational go-live, a test environment must be provided that largely corresponds to the subsequent productive environment. Comprehensive functional, technical, integrative, security-related, and professional acceptance tests must be carried out prior to go-live. Operational go-live may only take place after the successful completion of all tests and written approval by ALDB. d) Migration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, execution, and documentation of the migration in coordination with the contracting authority. As part of the migration, all user identities, roles, permissions, organisational structures, configurations, and all data required for the operation of the IAM solution must be transferred completely, consistently, and without data loss into the new system. The migration must be carried out in such a way that interruptions to productive operations are reduced to a minimum and the integrity of all data is ensured at all times. e) Customer Support The IAM customer service to be provided by the contractor comprises technical support, operation, maintenance, and continuous further development of the implemented Identity & Access Management solution in accordance with ALDB's functional and technical requirements. The service meets KRITIS requirements and is German-language support. The scope of services includes, in particular, incident and problem management, error analysis and troubleshooting, software updates, hotfixes, patches, and security-related updates, as well as support for configuration changes, change requests, extensions, and the integration of additional source and target systems. Furthermore, the contractor supports ALDB in optimising existing identity and access management processes, further developing the role and permission concept, and implementing new functional and regulatory requirements.

sig_dde965056278242d7989.description: The KVB intends to replace its existing SAP HCM landscape, which is also used for the group company KSG, by way of a carve-out and to transform it to SAP SuccessFactors as a full cloud solution. In particular, Employee Central, Employee Central Payroll, Time Tracking, Learning, Onboarding, and WalkMe Premium for SuccessFactors are to be introduced. SAP S/4HANA, SAP Integration Suite, and SAP BW on HANA are to be included in particular. The required SuccessFactors licences are already available and are not the subject of the contract. In addition, an optional quota of up to 1.000 person-days is provided for supplementary services. Full productive operation is scheduled for no later than 01.06.2028. Details regarding the scope of services and binding requirements can be found in the service description and the other tender documents. The following binding minimum requirements or knock-out criteria apply to the tender phase: 1. The personnel deployed for the provision of services must possess sound to long-standing, extensive, and in-depth experience and knowledge regarding SAP HCM and SuccessFactors. The bidder must guarantee this in its tender. 2. The bidder must guarantee that the provision of services complies with the current state of the art and recognised technical rules as well as the principle of sensible, appropriate, and economical use, also with regard to further costs such as, in particular, operating costs. In justified cases of doubt, compliance with these requirements must be proven at the contractor's expense. 3. The project language is German. All documentation, minutes, reports, planning, and training materials must be written entirely in German. Meetings, workshops, and training sessions must be conducted in German. The specialist personnel deployed must have a fluent command of the German language in both speech and writing. If German is not the native language, at least a German language diploma of level C1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required. 4. All of the bidder's employees, including external subcontractors and freelancers, must comply with the provisions of the General Data Protection Regulation. The bidder may only deploy persons for whom a written declaration of consent to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation is available. 5. The offered solution must in particular meet the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation, the Federal Data Protection Act, the principles for the proper keeping and storage of books, records, and documents in electronic form, and for data access, as well as other statutory retention and documentation obligations. 6. Completed personnel-related processes, data sets, documents, and records may only be deleted or archived after the expiry of the respective applicable statutory or professional retention periods. The corresponding process must be designed in a legally compliant and audit-proof manner and documented by means of procedural documentation. Failure to meet any of these minimum requirements will lead to the exclusion of the tender. The individual and sub-criteria, their weighting, the evaluation method including the linking of price and performance, the scoring scale, any minimum scores, as well as the information and evidence to be submitted will be provided uniformly to the selected applicants with the invitation to submit the indicative initial tender. sig_dec3d929cc52ef9a1f14.description: Already in 2008 the Klinikum Altmühlfranken in Weißenburg was extended by a specialist medical centre. Now the hospital is to be comprehensively refurbished and extended in two construction phases – due to the age of the building and deficits in the space available and functionality. Part of this application for construction and equipment planning is the 1. construction phase BA1 and here the two sub-construction phases BA1A and BA1E. BA1 – 1. construction phase. In the first construction phase, the existing functional wing is replaced by a new building (BA1A) and subsequently refurbished or converted for subsequent uses (BA1B). In addition, the existing entrance hall is extended and renewed (BA1E). BA1A - New building: The new building in the south-east of the property is planned as a compact structure with an ideal floor plan organisation and direct connection to the main entrance. All highly installed core functions of the hospital are concentrated and accommodated in the new building: - Basement: CSSD, laboratory, changing rooms, archive, laundry exchange point, services - Ground floor: Central emergency admission / central accident and emergency with new patient transport access and outpatient entrance, radiology, endoscopy, functional diagnostics, obstetrics - 1.upper floor: Operating theatre department with same-day surgery, intensive care medicine, on-call service - 2.upper floor: Services. The floor plan provides for a centrally located public access axis in an east-west orientation, to which the individual functional areas and vertical access with lift core are attached. On the 1.upper floor, an inner courtyard is also formed, which ensures the lighting of the respective departments. Optimum processes of hospital operation are achieved in this custom-built new building, and the primary functional deficits of the existing building are eliminated. Due to the self-sufficient construction of the new functional wing BA1A, ongoing operations in the existing building can be continued without impairment. BA1E - New building / refurbishment of entrance hall: Through the new building and its connection to the existing building, a new entrance situation and thus a new forward-looking urban planning appearance of the hospital is created at the same time. For this purpose, the existing entrance hall at entrance level is extended/straightened, thus creating a clear, unambiguous access. The entrance hall at the central location of the hospital is gutted and general functions are accommodated here: - Ground floor: Service facilities with reception/mailroom, pastoral care and social service area - Upper floors: Access with lounge areas. During this refurbishment, a provisional main entrance can be located from the north at the transition to the new building. BA1B - Refurbishment of existing building, outlook (not part of this BAP): After relocation of the core functions of the hospital into the newly constructed building BA1A, the original functional wing is converted accordingly and the following functions are located here: - Basement: Supply/disposal, storage, house and transport service, maintenance/repair, waste disposal, pharmaceuticals, services - Ground floor: Physical therapy, medical service, on-call service, catering with visitor/staff cafeteria with outdoor area - 1.upper floor: Medical service, administration - 2.upper floor: Prayer room, services. As part of the gutting, as a major structural intervention, an inner courtyard is formed on the 1.upper floor for the purpose of lighting the adjacent functions. The entire refurbishment can be carried out in one go, only 4 / 7 the existing catering in the 1.basement initially remains and is dismantled and converted accordingly after completion of the new catering on the ground floor. BA2 - 2. construction phase, outlook (not part of this BAP): In the second construction phase, nursing care is then to be modernised at Klinikum Altmühlfranken Weißenburg. This results in two possibilities: - Refurbishment and extension of the existing nursing wards - New nursing care buildings next to the newly constructed functional wing BA1A, which allows an ideal connection to new nursing blocks in its positioning and floor plan layout. Data-image-video management system consisting of built-in, display monitors and audio system as well as maintenance services
sig_dec3d929cc52ef9a1f14.title: Extension and refurbishment of Klinikum Altmühlfranken Weißenburg 1. BA (sub-construction section 1a)

sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.description: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m2, comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.
sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.title: Digital system for registering cleaning and deviations.

The intention is to continue the activities launched four years ago by re-establishing the purchasing system. sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.description: Background and purpose Arendal is located in the central part of Sørlandet. The municipality has approx. 46,000 inhabitants. Arendal municipality has a decentralised school structure with 16 municipal primary and secondary schools, organised as independent entities with separate rectors and management groups. The schools include both combined 1st - 10th schools and pure primary schools (1st - 7th years), as well as a resource centre with tenders across the stages. The municipality has a total of approx. 5,000 pupils in the primary and lower secondary schools. Arendal municipality is in an ongoing change of the school structure. Two primary schools (1st – 7th years) and the secondary school for one school have been decided to be folded. The changes are planned to be implemented from 01.01.2027. The overall responsibility for the school area is at the school office, which follows up on joint priorities, quality work and regulations, and acts as a link between the political level and the schools. The cooperation between the school office and the schools will take place, among other things, through fixed meeting points and joint development work, at the same time that each school adapts the work to local needs. The adult education is organised as a part of the municipality ́s training and is also a user of relevant digital services. Arendal municipality needs a joint system for the administration, distribution and access management of digital teaching aids in primary and secondary schools. The municipality has used a system for this purpose over time and has developed good experience with procurement, licence management and access management in this area. The procurement will be carried out as a result of the expiry of the existing agreement and shall ensure the continuation and further development of this work. Information on the procurement and process is in the document Konkurransegrunnlag_Digital Platform for schools. Scope The estimated annual scope is challenging to estimate. This is connected with the complexity, changes in the school structure and a market with different actors. We estimate that the annual turnover will be NOK 3.0 million excluding VAT, which over 8 years will be NOK 24 million excluding VAT. The contract will have a valid amount of NOK 30 million excluding VAT during the contract period. The estimated scope is based on experiences with the current supplier, market dialogue and indicative prices in the market. The estimated scope is not binding for the contracting authority. The following is not included in this procurement: - Learning platform (LMS) and educational follow-up. - functionality connected to artificial intelligence (KI) - other school administrative systems. The procurement is for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and a learning tool. Handling printed teaching aids is not included. The procurement does not include discipline specific teaching aids or individual applications. Reservations All conditions that the tenderer has for the tender shall be stated in the point conditions in the requirement specification document. Alternative tenders Alternative tenders cannot be submitted. Documents Please see the attached documents. Note that the tenderer shall fill in information in the attached documents.
sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.title: Platform for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and learning tools.

sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.description: Ards and North Down Borough Council is currently preparing to initiate a procurement process to appoint an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down. The Holywood Innovation Hub is a project funded through investment from the Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) and Ards and North Down Borough Council. It will focus on micro and small businesses within the digital, creative and screen industries: providing facilities and a secure environment to meet specific security, connectivity and technical needs. The proposed hub is intended to provide accommodation for the creative technology sector, specifically for start-up and smaller firms seeking to grow within the sector. It would also seek to provide accommodation for larger established 'anchor' tenants and potentially act as a short-term flexible base for FDI projects supported by NI Screen. The proposed hub is also intended to create an ecosystem within the creative technology sector: improving skills and employability across Ards and North Down and the overall Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) region. A primary reason for market failure in this sector is stated as a lack of suitable accommodation. This project will address this situation, supporting the growth of firms in the digital creative sector beyond the initial 'work from home' phase. The capital funding requirement for the proposal is £8,921,200 from the BRCD, with a further contribution of £1.1m from Ards and North Down Borough Council (ANDBC), further funding is required from the private sector to unlock this funding. ANDBC intends to appoint an operator for the Innovation Hub at an early stage of project development. The operator will assume management responsibilities and associated risks as set out in the final contractual structure. The operator will be appointed prior to the procurement of the Integrated Consultancy Team (ICT) responsible for the design of the Innovation Hub, enabling operational requirements and commercial considerations to be incorporated into the design and helping to maximise the hub's long-term economic performance. Prior to initiating the procurement, the Council is undertaking an Expression of Interest (EoI) and Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Exercise . This EoI/PME exercise is being conducted pursuant to section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023 for the purposes of: (a) developing the Council's requirements and approach to the procurement; (b) designing conditions of participation and award criteria; (c) preparing the tender notice and associated tender documents; and (d) identifying suppliers capable of performing the proposed contract. The pre-market engagement is intended to facilitate high-level conversations to identify potential interested suppliers and capabilities to inform the Council's procurement approach. A summary of the opportunity is detailed in the brochure and questionnaire documents that can be accessed via the CfT documents area (Resource ID 6717503) on the eTendersNI platform (https://etendersni.gov.uk).
sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.title: ANDBC Preliminary Market Engagement Exercise - Appointment of an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down

sig_e1694d00333cf54e6db8.description: Bergen municipality shall procure a new financial system, delivered as a cloud service. The new system shall replace the current financial system (UNIT4 ERP, UBW Economy), which the municipality has used since 2003. The contract also includes operation/management, further development and user support. The new financial system shall cover the municipality ́s need for finance, accounts, incoming and outgoing invoices and project accounts. Areas that the financial system shall support are: Accounts, including registration and bookkeeping, remittance, asset management and duty management. Outgoing invoices, including invoicing, income management and follow-up of payment. Incoming invoices, including invoice receipt, invoice processing, invoice matching, processing deviations and following-up payments. Project accounts, including hourly registration, administration and follow-up of projects and the generation of the invoice basis. Performance management and reporting, as well as financial insight and control. Register and master data, such as, for example, the customer register, supplier register and site register. Integrations and exchange of data between different systems. A change of system involves a great opportunity for Bergen municipality to get an ICT system, which not only covers basic functionality for the financial area, but supports modern and efficient financial processes and that ensures the best possible utilisation of the resources. Tenderers shall offer services and systems/cloud services that cover the needs and requirements stated in the SSA-Cloud agreement with annexes and annexes. Bergen municipality would also like additional services such as consultancy services/consultancy services, training services beyond the need for establishing the service and options for expanded user support. The contracting authority for the procurement is Bergen municipality, c/o the City Council Department for Finance.

sig_e1bcda544514a7ae6fc7.description: Fife Council intends to notify the market of a forthcoming procurement for a software solution to manage public access computers across council libraries and facilities. The solution will deliver end‐to‐end functionality for PC booking/sessions, print/copy/scan management, user authentication, and secure payments, with hosting, support, and maintenance services. Lot 1: . The product that will be procured will need to cover the following. PC Booking The system must support booking of public PCs. PC bookings must be configurable by location to reflect site‐specific arrangements. Self‐Service and Staff‐Assisted Booking Members of the public must be able to make PC bookings independently. Staff must be able to create or manage PC bookings on behalf of members of the public. Ability for patrons to book PCs in advance (online, kiosk, staff-assisted). Walk-up access with immediate log-on if PCs are available. Integration with Printing Services The solution must integrate with the existing printing system. It must provide print release functionality and support payments for printing. Library Management System Integration The solution must link to the Spydus Library Management System using LCF protocol for providing borrower authentication. Authentication must ensure only eligible borrowers can access PCs and services. Browsing History Reporting The system must provide reporting on user browsing session history to meet MAPPA agreement requirements. Borrower Type Management & Internet Restrictions The system must manage borrower types to enforce restrictions on internet browsing sessions. Restrictions must be configurable by borrower type or age ranges. Reporting & Analytics The system must provide a variety of statistical reports, including usage, bookings, printing, and browsing session activity. Reports must support operational monitoring and compliance requirements. Export options (Excel, CSV, BI tools). Security & Compliance GDPR-compliant handling of personal data. Role-based access control for staff and administrators. Audit trails and logging of user activity. Accessibility & Usability Compliance with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Simple, intuitive user interface for both patrons and staff. Technical Requirements Ability to manage and update programs, shortcuts (internet etc) and windows updates / patches centrally / remotely. Ability for Users to access USB memory Sticks on Public Access PCs Peripherals - System must work with standard peripherals e.g. scanners / headsets Nice to have - Reimage from local drive partition if local PCs. If cloud managed then this would already be in solution but PCs on site would likely become Cloud Managed and allow remote rebuild.. This PIN is for market information and does not initiate the procurement process. No tender documents are available at this stage.
sig_e1bcda544514a7ae6fc7.title: Public Access PC Booking, Print Management, and Authentication Solution

For further information, please contact vergabestelle@bsh.de --- Lot PAR-0000: Market exploration/expression of interest pursuant to Section 28 paragraph 1 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV) regarding a service concession for the promotion of the German flag. The German flag state administration stands for high quality, safety and social standards as well as for effective promotional instruments, in particular in training promotion. At the same time, the financial and procedural framework conditions of other flag state administrations and registers frequently appear more attractive to shipping companies - inter alia due to greater service orientation, greater decision-making flexibility and in some cases pronounced economic advantages. The Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport (BMV) is therefore considering the award of a service concession to a so-called intermediary who is, inter alia, to acquire sea-going ships for the German flag, advise on re-flagging and de-flagging, look after existing shipping companies and promote the German flag. The target group comprises owners, contractual shipping companies, ship managers or similar with their registered office in Germany. From a prospective perspective, sea-going ships in foreign ship registers that are authorised to fly the German flag may also be covered by the intermediary. This market exploration is intended to examine whether there is market interest in the considered solution and whether, if applicable, proposed solutions can be made that would make participation more interesting for you. We therefore invite you to express your interest in this service concession. This is not a procurement procedure. It is a non-binding information request that serves solely for market exploration pursuant to Section 28 paragraph 1 of the VgV. --->You can request a product profile sheet at vergabestelle@bsh.de for further information. sig_e24c76052c5125d06fac.description: Society relies on chemical processes to turn raw materials into useful products. The Chemical Process Systems (CPS) program invests in fundamental research on chemical and biochemical processes to make them more efficient, sustainable, and resilient. New CPS technologies for manufacturing, biotechnology, critical minerals, energy, food, and other national priorities will help make the U.S. more competitive and secure. Research supported by the CPS program covers the full breadth of chemical and biochemical process innovation. It spans reaction engineering and molecular thermodynamics; reactor design; catalysis; electrochemical systems; separations; and process design. The program encourages proposals that connect the molecular scale to process and plant scales. The CPS program explores active-site structure and function, reaction mechanisms, in situ and operando characterization, durability, and device-level integration. Microreactors, membrane and catalytic reactors, atmospheric plasmas, and other novel configurations are of interest. The program supports research in catalysis and electrochemical systems to produce, use, and store energy, to reduce waste, to process polymers, and to synthesize fuels and chemicals. This includes process and materials innovation to support the nuclear fuel cycle. The CPS program also targets chemical and biological separations that are efficient and scalable. Research includes the design of membranes, sorbents, and specialized interfaces. Advances can be used in gas separations, the recovery of critical minerals, bioprocessing, and protein and water purification. The program supports research in process design and optimization that uses tools such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and uncertainty quantification. CPS research also explores quantum information science and engineering; quantum simulation and sensing, for example, may accelerate the discovery of materials and improve process models. Partnerships: To speed discovery and innovation, NSF partners with federal agencies, industry, international groups, and others. Current opportunities are at NSF ENG Partnerships.
sig_e24c76052c5125d06fac.title: Chemical Process Systems (CPS)

sig_e5740702950e74e82984.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 from a merger of the railway and postal bus services. The transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer district, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg district, the Euskirchen district and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brühl and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban conurbations with sparsely populated, more rural areas. sig_e5d463b07d7476d5424b.description: New installation of a digital alerting system using the POCSAG standard (2 MHz band) for non-police emergency response in Landkreis Emmendingen to replace the analogue 5-tone alerting. The subject of the procurement is the supply, installation and commissioning of a network-wide digital alerting system to the POCSAG standard in the 2 MHz band for emergency services and disaster relief organisations in Landkreis Emmendingen, including migration from the existing analogue 5-tone alerting, the supply of end-user devices, and maintenance and service provision. The procurement procedure in question covers the installation of 37 digital alerting transmitter sites within the district area, including antenna and lightning protection engineering as well as the electrotechnical upgrading of the structures for these sites. Furthermore, a total of four digital tone generators (two fixed installations and two mobile emergency tone generators) as well as network and IT technology for the central system engineering at the location of the Emmendingen Integrated Control Centre will be installed. The contract is divided into four lots. Lot 1 covers the digital alerting system engineering, in particular the supply, assembly, commissioning and configuration of the digital alerting transmitters and digital tone generators with subsequent service provision on the basis of an EVB-IT service contract with a fixed term of 24 months. Lot 2 comprises antenna engineering and mast construction, specifically the supply and assembly of antenna masts and lightning protection and earthing components. Lot 3 describes the necessary electrical work. Lot 4 comprises the procurement of end-user devices based on a basket principle with call-offs by the respective authorised municipalities or relief organisations. Lot LOT-0001: Digital alerting system engineering. Supply, assembly and commissioning of the central and decentralised system technology of the digital alerting system (including digital tone generators, digital alerting transmitters, switches, software), including system integration, testing, training and the conclusion of an EVB-IT service contract limited to the first 24 months. Lot LOT-0002: Antenna engineering and mast construction. Supply, assembly and commissioning of antenna systems (2 MHz, GPS, LTE), antenna carriers and mast constructions, including lightning protection and earthing measures and structural verification, as well as coordination with property owners. Lot LOT-0003: Electrical work. Execution of all electrical connection and installation work at transmitter and technical sites, including power supply and documentation in accordance with DIN VDE 0100-600. Lot LOT-0004: End-user devices (basket principle). Supply, installation, configuration and commissioning of end-user devices for receiving the alarm messages transmitted via the components of lot 1, as well as components for the remote programming of these end-user devices (server-client structure) and central components for implementing a call-back functionality from and additional alarm information to the end-user devices via the mobile communications network. The procurement of the end-user devices takes place via a framework agreement based on the basket principle with call-offs by the authorised municipalities and relief organisations.

Our vision is to create a fully branded, inclusive, and functional workwear and PPE solution that unites every colleague across our organisation reflecting who we are, what we stand for, and the pride we take in serving our communities. We will deliver a modern, high‐quality uniform range designed from the ground up to support the unique needs of our operational, maritime, port, and shore‐based teams. Rooted in the heritage of Caledonian MacBrayne and our communities, our workwear will combine safety, comfort, durability, and unmistakable brand identity in every garment. Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Through clear uniform standards, easy maintenance guidance, and from warehouse to home/work distribution processes, we will set and uphold a new standard for how our brand is worn and represented. Powered by digital self-service ordering tools, our workwear transformation will enhance operational efficiency, improve stock management, and allow us to scale sustainably. Cross-functional collaboration at the early stages will ensure that every voice is heard and every role is understood, creating a sense of ownership, pride, and confidence in the final solution. By learning from industry-leading transformations and working with expert partners, we will introduce a workwear range that not only serves practical needs but also strengthens culture, improves staff experience, and supports our organisation’s evolution. This is more than new uniform, it's an opportunity to reinforce our brand, celebrate our heritage, empower our people, and deliver a workwear experience that is fit for the future.

sig_e72a9726007480567ec2.description: The Board of Trustees for the National Galleries of Scotland ("NGS") wish to award a Contract for the Provision of Audience Research Services. The Service Provider is required to conduct Audience Research to provide insight and analysis about our visitors in order to support the Organisation’s 2030 Strategy, Business Plan and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), special projects and inform organisation-wide strategic planning. The Service Provider shall be a member of, accredited by, or operate in accordance with the standards, codes of conduct and professional requirements of the Market Research Society (MRS) or an equivalent recognised professional body for market research, social research, insight or analytics. This Contract shall primarily provide Fieldwork Surveys and associated Project Management, Client Data Access, Analysis and Reporting for each of our four gallery sites. Services will be agreed to on an “as required” basis with no commitment to a minimum volume of work. NGS may, at its absolute discretion, require the Service Provider to provide Audience Research Services at this fifth site, currently under construction, at any time during the Contract term. If permitted by applicable procurement legislation, where additional audience research requirements arise during the Contract term that constitute an extension of the Services, NGS reserves the right to procure such additional services from the Service Provider. For full details of the Contract Requirements please refer to the associated Tender and Contract Documents. The Service Provider must have a clear understanding of the contract requirements and the organisational needs of NGS. As part of the tender exercise, the Service Provider must detail a robust and flexible methodology for conducting Audience Research Services that will meet all data capture requirements. There is no commitment to a minimum spend over the duration of the Contract. Under this Contract, no minimum spend is guaranteed. The agreement will be non-exclusive i.e. NGS reserves the right, in certain, circumstances, to procure out with the Contract Agreement, as and when required. In the event of unsatisfactory performance by the successful Service Provider and the termination of the contract by either party, NGS reserves the right to negotiate the continuance of the services with the second and third placed Service Providers. Lot 1: . The procurement will be conducted through the use of the Open Procedure. Service Providers must complete and submit both an SPD and Tender response. Economic Operators may be excluded from this competition if they are in any of the situations referred to in Regulation 58 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015. Given the nature of the contract, Tenderers must comply with minimum security requirements. The Service Provider must obtain valid Cyber Essentials Basic (or equivalent) certification prior to the Contract Commencement Date and maintain throughout the Contract term including any extension periods. It is desirable that the Service Provider hold current ISO/IEC 27001 (or equivalent) certification or otherwise Tenderers must demonstrate equivalent information security management arrangements as part of the quality assessment. Full details are set out in the Tender and Contract Documents. The maximum available budget to deliver the Core Contract Requirements is 60,000 GBP per annum excluding VAT. Tenderers are required to submit pricing that can be delivered within this annual budget for Years 1 – 5 of the Contract, including any optional extension periods. Any Tender exceeding the maximum available budget, may be deemed unaffordable and may be excluded from further consideration. Tenderers must provide fixed prices for Years 1 – 3 of the Contract, and indicative prices for Years 4 & 5. The prices submitted for Years 4 and 5 shall represent the maximum prices payable during any extension period unless NGS approves a formal change request due to the Service Provider sufficiently demonstrating exceptional circumstances. Cost Control Mechanisms for Years 4 & 5 are detailed under Schedule 2 of the Contract Agreement. For this Tender Competition, and for commercial evaluation purposes, NGS reserves the right to assess affordability against a maximum annual budget of 60,000 GBP for each contract year, including any optional extension periods. NGS reserves the right not to award where it considers submitted pricing to exceed available funding. Information in respect of Optional Contract Requirements, and estimate additional spend, has been provided at section V1.3 ‘Additional ‘Information’. The ‘Estimate Total Contract Value’ provided at II.1.5, includes both estimate spend for Core Contract Requirements and estimate spend for Optional Contract Requirements.. The top three highest scoring Tenderers (price & quality combined score) will be invited to a Tender Presentation stage on 4th and/or 5th November 2026 (dates may be subject to change). Full details provided in the Tender Documents.

sig_e76cad13ba556c235e05.description: ITZBund requires services in the area of software lifecycle management (SLM) for software development and project management solutions in use. The aim of this tender is to conclude a framework agreement to ensure the operation as well as the maintenance and (further) development of the existing Cloud software development and project management platform and associated specialist applications of ITZBund. In addition, sovereignty is to be strengthened through the expansion of open source tools to be procured. ITZBund understands open source to be software whose source code is freely available. In principle, everyone is permitted to use, analyse, modify and pass on this software free of charge and without restriction in terms of content regarding the object and source code. Specifications of the respective relevant open source licence, in particular regarding licence texts, copyright notices or copyleft effects, remain unaffected. The services advertised encompass services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts as well as demand-oriented new developments and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The contracting authority, who can commission services commissioned by its customers, is authorised to call off services. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place within ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases permit operation at customers of the contracting authority with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the outset are advertised in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed Cloud software development and project management platform - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed Cloud software development and project management platform - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services This specification of services considers the subject matter of Lot 5: The subject matter of this lot is the provision of an open source wiki including associated training, support, further development and migration services. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract period of 4 years, an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 162.608 person-hours (ph) or 20.326 person-days (pd) results for the estimated calculatory costs.

sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) that builds upon its investment in data-driven approaches for the purpose of defining molecular mechanisms of resilience in the presence of various types of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) risk. The goal of this NOFO is to build a robust program that integrates epidemiologic, genomic, and mechanistic research through the use of data driven, systems-based approaches (including the use of artificial intelligence and/or machine learning methods) to discover the molecular/cellular determinants of resilience to AD/ADRD risk across representative populations. The initiative will support the generation of high-dimensional molecular data from brain and peripheral tissues, including longitudinal data, to enable dynamic modeling of resilience mechanisms and to discover molecular predictors of resilience. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. The request for information is used to gather information for procurement planning. The Hippos area being built in Jyväskylä offers an international-level complex for physical activity, hobbies and sport. The simulation system is used to create simulation exercises resembling genuine interaction and customer situations for teaching purposes. The system enables the recording, saving and real-time control of situations. The matters presented in the request for information are preliminary and may change as the procurement preparations progress. This notice is a market survey used in the preparation of the procurement by Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences. sig_ea971947a93b5580d449.description: MARKET CONSULTATION The subject of the market consultation is the procurement of a maintenance operations management system for the tracks of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The most central task of the operations management system is to support day-to-day maintenance management by offering various functionalities for equipment and work management ranging from work planning to work reporting, as well as enabling various tracking functions, for example with regard to accumulated work and costs. Another key factor for the system is to support information-driven management, i.e., to provide, inter alia, up-to-date information on maintenance activities carried out on assets and the resulting costs, as well as potential consequential effects over the entire lifecycle of the equipment. The system's functionalities should offer the target organisation the opportunity to implement maintenance operations characteristic of its operations in a process-driven manner, such that the system supports the execution of the process at different stages of the process, in accordance with the functionalities required of it. The efficient implementation of maintenance processes, ensuring both personnel and information security, requires strong support from the operations management system with which operations are managed and monitored. The operations management system should provide an open interface for the target organisation to monitor and manage maintenance operations between different stakeholders, such as in situations where maintenance is procured either partially or entirely as a service. In addition to the primary functionalities of maintenance management, the operations management system should cover a wide range of various functionalities supporting operations. The functionalities of the system can be roughly classified as follows: - Equipment management - Work management - Reports and analysis - Mobile application - User management - Cost tracking - Contract management - Inventory management - Procurement The task of the operations management system is to act in connection with day-to-day maintenance management as part of the broader system architecture of Väylävirasto. For this reason, various integrations with other operational and administrative systems of Väylävirasto will also be necessary. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for carrying out the market consultation and procurement is: - Market consultation, technical dialogue (commenting on material) September-October 2025 - Market consultation, bilateral negotiations (approx. 3-6 companies) October-early November 2025 - Year 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market consultation, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject matter of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure, nor does it prevent participation if the supplier has not participated in the dialogue. TECHNICAL DIALOGUE AND BILATERAL DISCUSSIONS The market consultation is organised in two phases: 1. As a technical dialogue, where potential suppliers are asked to familiarise themselves with the service description and requirement specification and to answer the contracting authority's preliminary questions (carried out in September-October by email in accordance with registrations) 2. As bilateral discussions, where the contracting authority invites 3-6 suppliers to discussions. The contracting authority will send invitations to the discussions to the selected suppliers as soon as possible. The discussions will take place during October-November 2025 (the following times are preliminarily reserved, participants are requested to reserve the times in their calendars where possible): - Mon 27.10 at 9.30-11 - Mon 27.10 at 14-15.30 - Wed 29.10 at 14.30-16 - Fri 31.10 at 12-13.30 - Mon 3.11 at 14-15.30 - Wed 5.11 at 12-13.30 The times will be confirmed to the suppliers selected for the bilateral negotiations approximately two weeks before the time. In addition to the above, the contracting authority reserves the right for a later scheduled commenting period on draft versions of the final tender documentation and for answering the contracting authority's new questions related to the subject matter of the procurement. INSTRUCTIONS FOR REGISTRATION The supplier must notify its interest in participating in the market consultation by 20.10.2025 at 12.00 by sending a message to tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi and virpi.kukkonen@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Ratojen kunnossapidon toiminnanohjausjärjestelmä - markkinavuoropuhelu". The supplier is requested to provide the following information in the message: - name, email address and telephone number of the supplier's contact person - a brief description of the supplier (e.g., the company's line of business and main services) - a brief description of the solution offered by the supplier for the procurement subject to the market consultation - information on whether the solution is an already existing solution or a concept under development - the supplier's previous deliveries and references (corresponding to the subject matter of the procurement) The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice, as well as the dialogue draft materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative procurement information. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.

sig_eaf83c3f102e15c95de4.description: The Integrated Rhine Programme (IRP) is a project of the State of Baden-Württemberg (BW) which comprises a total of 13 flood retention basins (FRBs) in various planning and implementation stages on former floodplains between Basel and Mannheim. The IRP specialist information system (FIS IRP) is to be developed as a central repository of the IRP for the safeguarding of relevant data. The project management and consultancy for the client (CA) for this IT project are being commissioned. The services to be provided in this context include the division of the IT project into realistic, economical implementation stages, cost estimates, the preparation of tender documents, in particular the specification of requirements and the acceptance catalogue, for the programming or development of the FIS IRP, the professional and technical support of the CA in procurement processes, and project management during implementation and programming. An optional contract is to be awarded: as a mandatory service, the contractor (CO) is to support the first implementation stage in the development of the FIS IRP; support for further implementation stages is aimed for (options). Table 1 within the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents) provides an overview of the services to be provided by the contractor with the timeframe envisaged by the CA. Included services mainly comprise, but are not limited to, the preparation of the tender for the programming of the FIS IRP for the 1 implementation stage (with a focus on the creation of the specification of requirements, in which requirements from later implementation stages or the overall project must also be taken into account), the professional and technical support of the CA in the procurement process, and project management during implementation and programming. In the further course of the project, the commissioning of comparable services for the support of further implementation stages is aimed for (optional contract). More detailed provisions on the provision of services can be found in the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents). The final specification of requirements will be submitted to the successful applicants with the invitation to submit a tender. The FIS IRP is planned as a modular specialist information system with the modules "Operating Data", "Ecology", "Groundwater and Surface Water Models", "Groundwater and Surface Water Data", and "Structures". The FIS IRP is intended to secure the data long-term, make it available for display (including viewing in a geospatial data viewer) and enable cross-cutting evaluation of the data across the entire IRP. The CA has described the FIS IRP with its modules in technical concepts in which the precise contents, functionalities and general technical requirements for the FIS are formulated without specifying particular software or a development environment. The procurement documents contain a brief description of the technical concept (Annex 2). For individual modules, local database applications or data repositories in the form of medium-term implementation solutions have already been created. The applications must be further developed, also for integration into the specialist information system. In the phased development of the FIS IRP planned for the future, the initial focus is on the integration of dynamic factual data, i.e. operating and monitoring data, as well as the development of the geospatial data viewer.
