sig_ec27b75e698309d4bfb2.description:
An IT application for the digitalisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector and management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is to be procured as a SaaS cloud solution. The IT application must be compatible with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. This is used in the Free State of Thuringia to record bag data (data on wild animals killed by hunters). The IT application should be available both as a web application (usable in common browsers) and as a mobile app application (iOS and Android operating systems). Within the scope of the tender, an app is defined as an application that must be installed on a mobile device before use by the user and can only be used there. As a rule, this takes place on a smartphone or tablet using a so-called app store. There will be two main user groups: a) administrative or laboratory staff b) non-administrative users (e.g. those authorised to hunt). The non-administrative users record data on killed or slaughtered animals. If necessary, they also submit applications for the examination of these animals for trichinella and/or certain animal diseases to the competent authorities or the competent testing facility of the Free State of Thuringia. The test results should be retrievable via the IT application. The competent authorities (veterinary and food monitoring offices of the districts and independent cities - veterinary authorities) operate the trichinella testing laboratories. These should be able to access the application data recorded by external users in the IT application via their own user interface and transmit the test results back to the applicants. In addition, laboratory software should be made available to the competent authorities, with the help of which testing activities can be documented on the basis of the application data. In the case of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, the client's laboratory at the Thuringian State Office for Consumer Protection is the competent testing facility. The laboratory software (LIMS) in use there should be able to access the information on the samples entered by the users via the HIT database. The IT application must therefore have an interface to the HIT database. A direct connection to the LIMS is not intended. The IT application is to be made available to administrative staff for mapping internal administrative processes as well as to affected users outside the administration for data entry and application submission, and for receiving notices from the competent authorities. While the use cases of trichinella testing, management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector and the interface to the hunting statistics application are to be available permanently, the use case of management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is only to be usable and available on an ad-hoc basis. Furthermore, introductory support and training for the staff of the competent authorities should be included in the offer as an initial service. The contract is concluded via an EVB-IT cloud contract. The procurement is carried out by the client for use by all districts and independent cities in Thuringia. The use of the IT application for the aforementioned purposes is mandatory for the districts and independent cities. For hunters, however, use is optional. This means that they can refrain from using the IT application. The previous analogue system for sampling will initially be continued in parallel. Lot LOT-0000: Provision, operation (incl. hosting) and support of an IT application for the digitalisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) and an interface to the hunting statistics application. The 21 veterinary and food monitoring offices of the 22 districts and independent cities in the Free State of Thuringia are, among other things, responsible for receiving and testing samples of slaughtered or killed animals intended for human consumption for Trichinella spp. Furthermore, there are responsibilities with regard to granting permission for the taking of samples intended for trichinella testing by non-administrative persons. Citizens who wish to make use of the aforementioned administrative services should be enabled to record the required application data digitally in accordance with the principles of the Online Access Act (OZG), to submit the application paperlessly to the respective competent veterinary and food monitoring office and to receive the notices from the competent authorities. In addition, the possibility should be created to comply with further reporting obligations (e.g. the recording of hunting bags by hunters) in digital form. The testing of wild boar for Trichinella spp. only takes place if the animal is to become food. Based on experience to date, this leads to the testing of up to 30.000 head of wild boar per year in Thuringia. These figures fluctuate. In addition, the veterinary monitoring authorities are responsible for implementing regular monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens. Depending on the current animal health status, the number of samples is expected to vary between approx. 5.000 and 30.000 samples per year.

Data entry and application submission as well as the receipt of notices should also be enabled here for the respective affected citizens. The recorded data should be transmitted via the application to the State Office for Consumer Protection responsible for testing the samples. The application part for the management of ASF outbreaks should be based on the aforementioned application parts in terms of operation (esp. the monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens) and interact with them in terms of content in accordance with the technical requirements. This application part should be activatable on an ad-hoc basis for each affected authority (veterinary authorities of the districts and independent cities and, if applicable, the client). Use should take place not only in the event of an ASF outbreak in Thuringia but also in the context of exercises in preparation for an outbreak. A final application part includes the recording and reporting of hunting bags by hunters. This report includes all huntable animal species. For this documentation obligation, the bag data from the aforementioned application parts should be reusable, but it should also be possible to record new bag data. A corresponding interface is to be provided for the necessary data exchange with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. The hunters already have direct access to the hunting statistics application. The interface should enable them to gain access from within the IT application and thus facilitate reporting through data transfer. The application is to be provided for use by administrative staff in the Free State of Thuringia as well as the respective affected citizens in the Free State of Thuringia. As a result, the licence and terms of use must enable use by employees of the state, the municipalities and by non-administrative persons. The number of future users cannot be precisely quantified at present, as the use of the IT application is optional for hunters. However, the number of hunters in Thuringia can be a guide; it amounts to approx. 13.000. In addition, there are approx. 100 administrative staff.

This is a fixed-price contract and must include all costs associated with delivery, including project management, user research, service design, WordPress development, accessibility testing, quality assurance, knowledge transfer, stakeholder engagement, travel, subsistence, overheads, licences and any other expenses. Suppliers will be required to submit a breakdown of costs by deliverable and milestone as part of their tender response About the work Why the work is being done Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) is seeking to improve the accessibility, usability and effectiveness of its website to better support health and social care professionals, partner organisations, citizens and communities across Scotland. User testing and stakeholder feedback have identified challenges relating to navigation, information architecture, content discovery and overall user experience. These issues can make it difficult for users to find and access important information, resources, tools, standards, frameworks and publications. HIS wishes to adopt a people-led, user-centred approach to improve access to information and digital services while building internal capability to sustainably manage and develop the website in the future. The project will focus initially on two directorates, creating reusable design patterns, templates and approaches that can subsequently be applied across the wider HIS web estate. The successful supplier will undertake discovery, user research, service design, accessibility improvement, WordPress development, implementation and knowledge transfer activities. The contract is expected to commence in November 2026 and all contracted deliverables must be completed by 30 June 2027. Problem to be solved Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) has identified challenges with the usability, accessibility and effectiveness of its website. User testing and stakeholder feedback have highlighted difficulties with navigation, information architecture, content discovery and overall user experience. These issues make it harder for users to find and access important information, resources, standards, tools, frameworks and publications, reducing engagement and limiting the impact of nationally important content. HIS is seeking a supplier to help create a more user-centred, accessible and sustainable digital service. Working within the existing WordPress platform, the supplier should focus on understanding user needs and applying a people-led design approach to improve how users find, access and interact with content. The initial scope focuses on two HIS directorates and aims to create reusable design patterns, templates, components and approaches that can later be adopted across the wider HIS web estate. The successful supplier will also be expected to build internal capability through knowledge transfer, coaching and guidance. sig_ef12262962b8538c2af0.description: On behalf of the Danish Tax Administration, the Agency for Development and Simplification (UFST) would like to invite suppliers to a market dialogue on a new system for handling new EU legislation in relation to the FASTER directive, which is intended to ensure better, simpler, and more uniform procedures for the relief of excess withholding tax on cross-border investments. The directive is intended to ensure that EU countries have the necessary tools to effectively tackle tax fraud and abuse. The directive can be found here FASTER. With this market dialogue, UFST seeks to gain important knowledge from potential suppliers on the market who have experience from similar areas or solutions. UFST would also like to investigate whether there is a standard solution on the market already that can meet our needs or whether there are plans to develop a solution to support the FASTER directive. The market dialogue should provide insight into whether a standard solution exists or is planned to be developed that can support our needs in relation to: 1. Reporting of several detailed information on dividends from certified financial intermediaries 2. Digital tax certificate residences (eTRC), so that investors only need to obtain one digital certificate from their home country to document which EU country they are residents in 3. A system for ‘relief-at-source’ of dividend tax that will integrate with our existing system-portfolio Examples of business and technical needs (non-exhaustive): • The solution must exchange data to other relevant IT systems in UFST • The solution must integrate access to external foreign IT systems including, for example, a common EU portal • The solution must provide access and the possibility of approval and deregistration of Danish investors • The solution must enable automatic reporting of control data from the certified financial intermediaries • The solution must support case processing so that administrative users can handle situations where reported control data is deficient • The solution must enable the issuance and revocation of eTRCs • The solution must enable the approval and deregistration of certified financial intermediaries • The solution must issue and enforce powers of attorney • Handling of access control and compliance with logging and security requirements • Automatic control of submission data In addition, UFST is interested in what considerations the suppliers make in relation to which technologies and technology stacks the solution is expected to be built on, and whether the solution is implemented in Cloud or On Premise. In addition, it is particularly interesting to have solutions from suppliers that can document experience with larger common solutions in OECD and/or the EU. For the development of the standard solution and its ongoing maintenance, UFST would also like to clarify how the supplier generally intends to ensure: • Maximum automation of workflows • Full compliance with the FASTER directive and functional support of it • User-friendliness, overview (e.g. status), and reporting options • Compliance with existing legislation in the area.
sig_ef12262962b8538c2af0.title: Market research of system support for the implementation of the EU directive FASTER (Fast Track Assured and Safer Tax Excess Refunds)

sig_ef1b4cdc34ab50c1d6ec.description: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.
sig_ef1b4cdc34ab50c1d6ec.title: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast

sig_ef8a23b520edd78e6d5f.description: The purpose of the tender is to contract operational services related to the crop monitoring and yield forecasting activities of the JRC.D.5 unit (MARSOP). Implementing Article 25 of the horizontal regulation of the Common Agricultural Policy REG (EU) 2021/2116 on Monitoring Agricultural Resources (MARS), JRC.D.5 provides DG AGRI with timely, independent, and high-quality information on crop state and development, including quantitative forecasts of agricultural yields and production in the EU and neighbouring countries. This information is used by DG AGRI to ensure food security and for decision-making in agricultural markets. The JRC provides matching staff for agricultural analysts and experts producing monthly JRC MARS Bulletins for Commission-internal and public use, which are well received by private sector stakeholders, academics and the general public. Such services have been outsourced since 2000 (MAROSP1-6), financed through a co-delegation with DG AGRI. The operational services sustain the operation and further development of the MARS Crop Yield Forecasting System (MCYFS) at the heart of the crop monitoring activities at D.5. For the current procurement, we plan to organize the operational services for the MARS System in three different lots: - Lot 1: Acquisition and processing of agro-meteorological information - Lot 2: Acquisition and processing of satellite data - Lot 3: Processing of agronomic information from crop models and statistics. Lot 1 - Acquisition and processing of agro-meteorological information: The objective of Lot 1 is to acquire and process in near real-time (NRT) agro-meteorological data for ingestion and use in the MARS System. The sources of meteorological data to be acquired and processed are basically two: observed weather data from meteorological stations in Europe, and modelled weather data generated at the European Centre for Medium-range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) at various lead times. Data processing includes quality control, spatial and temporal aggregation, and NRT ingestion into the MARS System. Lot 2 - Acquisition and processing of satellite data: Lot 2 supports the remote sensing infrastructure of the MARS System for Europe and global coverage with specific, tailored products. The service comprises NRT data collection, pre-processing and computation of derived products for the remote sensing satellites MODIS/VIIRS as well as Copernicus products. Lot 3 - Processing of agronomic information from crop models and statistics: Services of this lot include the NRT execution of crop growth models over Europe driven by weather data for specific target crops as well as NRT processing of the Water Satisfaction Index at global level. The repeated collection and quality-control and processing of agricultural statistics, pheonological data, and other agronomic information is an intrinsic part of this lot.
sig_ef8a23b520edd78e6d5f.title: Operational Support to In-Season Crop Monitoring and Yield Forecasting Activities (MARSOP7)

sig_f0e24f0a815eeb1b6a10.description: HUS requests your tender for a software service that manages HUS Pharmacy's enterprise resource planning, covering the operational areas described in the appendices. Processes and data concerning HUS Pharmacy's medication management will be configured into the software service to be procured. The software service must integrate with the systems used by HUS in its other enterprise resource planning (e.g. Oracle Fusion Cloud). The appendices to the call for tender (appendix 0 and appendices 1: Description of current operations) describe the scope of current operations through verbal descriptions by operational area. The purpose of the descriptions is to familiarise the tenderer with HUS Pharmacy's current operations. The appendices (appendices 2: Description of target state) describe the requirements set for the subject of the procurement by operational area using various process descriptions and listed requirements. The purpose of this is to express to tenderers the minimum requirements set for enterprise resource planning. In addition, objectives for developing current operations are described. Our intention is to replace the current system with a software service (SaaS) that enables process development and guarantees a qualitatively stable operation. HUS is seeking a SaaS-based software service, which must be based on software that is already in production use and ready-made, and a solution configured from it for the contracting authority. The project schedule is planned such that the software service will be implemented during the year 2028. The project will be initiated with a definition phase, in which the made descriptions are refined against the software service offered by the winning tenderer, thereby ensuring that the software service in question meets the set requirements and offers a clear development path. In this definition phase, the implementation project plan is also refined to such a level that the parties can commit to the execution of the project. The definition phase is invoiced on a time basis, for a maximum of 50 000 euros and for a duration of no more than four months. The appendix Description of the implementation project explains in more detail what must be produced during the definition phase. After the definition phase, both parties have the option, if they so wish, to withdraw from the project. Following the definition phase, the contracting authority and the tenderer will negotiate the target workload and price for the project in the manner presented in the call for tender. Other appendices to the call for tender describe requirements related to the implementation phase, ongoing services, and information security. The software service must be capable of being integrated in a conventional manner into various administrative systems. The interfaces of the software service are presented in the appendix "Integrations". Oracle FINA interfaces are individually described in more detail in appendix 2.9.3. The appendix "Draft Agreement" covers operations during both the implementation phase and ongoing services. The appendix "Price Form" describes the calculation of the comparative price of tenders and the procedures for establishing the target price.
sig_f0e24f0a815eeb1b6a10.title: e-Forms 2023 / EU / HUS 486-2023 Pharmacy enterprise resource planning system as a software service

sig_f1a6632c8b8048d5313d.description: The aims of the project are to produce an evaluation of the SLC’s rural land market reporting to generate insights and improvements for future reporting. The evaluation will focus on several elements: 1) Impact – this objective is to understand the use of the report and its effects, outcomes and the extent to which reporting is effective in informing policy and decision making. There is a comparative element for this. 2) Process – understanding the effectiveness of the current approach, how the reporting process is working, assessing potential improvements to the methodology, and considering expansion of the coverage of reporting to other areas. 3) Economic Value – understanding value for money and costing the tangible benefits of the reports compared to the costs. What are the wider economic benefits to participants, public finances and society? 4) Analysis and Recommendations – the above steps inform the analysis and evaluation to understand to what extent and degree of progress towards the reporting aims are being made, and any recommendations for improvements. The report should, where appropriate, include advice for the SLC for future land market reports. Lot 1: . sig_f3269264b960a2e789a5.description: Organisational, professional and technical consultancy services for an omnichannel transformation project. The Audi BKK is planning to implement a future-proof omnichannel platform for customer advice in order to ensure consistent, seamless and personalised support across all relevant communication channels. In addition to connecting to existing systems of the Audi BKK, new digital contact channels for customer communication are to be provided, networked with one another and further optimised or automated. To prepare for the implementation of an omnichannel platform and to create the necessary organisational, professional and technical prerequisites, the contracting authority is hereby tendering for advisory support services to accompany and implement measures in the omnichannel context. Based on a completed as-is analysis and determination of the status quo, organisational, professional and technical measures and objectives have been derived. The results are documented in an omnichannel roadmap and are divided into a conception phase and a transformation phase (see attached annex). The concepts and optimisations developed (and potentially still emerging) during the conception phase are to be consolidated and driven forward by the contractor in their implementation and execution. The contractor shall effectively manage, methodically implement and document the omnichannel transformation process. The contractor shall support the technical and functional requirements for a suitable omnichannel platform during the derivation and survey phase in order to ensure a robust catalogue of requirements for the subsequent tendering and procurement of an omnichannel platform. The objective of this tender is to conclude a contract with a contractor for a period of two years, with planned contractual extension options. The contracting authority estimates the scope of the contract at approximately 800 consultant days.

sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.
sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?

sig_f407665173fc522d220b.description: Ballerup Kommune wishes to purchase a system that can handle the municipal salary negotiation process for all stakeholders. In a municipality, salary negotiations take place with the involvement of both employees, managers, and trade unions and employee representatives, which makes the task complex. The salary negotiation process involves data from several systems and many different stakeholders: HR, managers both centrally and locally, employee representatives and trade unions, as well as all employees in Ballerup Kommune. Today, the task is handled through manual updating and circulation of Excel sheets with a high risk of errors and GDPR breaches. The purpose of the purchase is to ensure a quality boost of data in salary negotiations, make it more person-independent and transparent for the stakeholders. There is also a desire to reduce the time spent by HR, employee representatives and managers in connection with the salary negotiation process. Ballerup Kommune has prepared a requirements specification and would like to invite suppliers to a market dialogue based on this requirements specification and, naturally, a demonstration of the supplier's solution. It is important to note that a development project is not desired, but rather a standard solution that supports our requirements. The market dialogue will be held at the following times: d. 6. October 2025 10.00-15.30 d. 7. October 2025 12.00- 15.30 d. 9. October 2025 11.30- 15.30 2 hours are allocated per supplier. Suppliers who may be interested in participating in a market dialogue are requested to show their interest by writing to Ballerup Kommune via Mercell no later than 1. October 2025, stating which date and time among the three possible ones above. Ballerup Kommune reserves the right to reject any interested companies if there are too many interested parties or if the company has a solution that is currently only on the drawing board.
sig_f407665173fc522d220b.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding intended procurement of salary negotiation system

sig_f42dfbd119f70092f405.description: INTRODUCTION Mid Ulster District Council is preparing a procurement for the renewal, supply, management and optimisation of its Microsoft enterprise licensing, associated CSP services and specialist Microsoft expertise. This pre-market engagement exercise will help the Council understand available market models, risks, pricing approaches, support arrangements and proportionate requirements before any formal procurement is issued. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE The objectives are to confirm market interest, test the most suitable agreement route and service model, identify risks or dependencies, understand pricing and governance options, and inform the Council's procurement strategy. This is not a procurement process and responses will not be evaluated as part of any future tender. BACKGROUND INFORMATION The Council's Microsoft estate includes Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, Azure, server licensing and associated Software Assurance requirements. Market input is sought on CSP, Enterprise Agreement or other Microsoft agreement routes, billing options, licence optimisation, tenant support, adoption, security and compliance support, escalation and access to qualified Microsoft expertise. STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS MUDC wishes to establish a contract with a suitably experienced Microsoft CSP partner to provide: • licensing renewal, supply and management through CSP, Enterprise Agreement or another suitable route; • licence optimisation, proof of licence, inventory records, renewal tracking and compliance reporting; • Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, security, compliance, identity, endpoint and server licensing expertise; • support for billing, subscription changes, incidents, Microsoft escalation, account governance and roadmap advice; The Council also wishes to understand transparent pricing structures, including margins, discounts, billing models, separate professional services rates and how best to separate user subscriptions, device subscriptions, Azure consumption, server licensing, trial/free SKUs and advisory services. Responses should assist the Council in considering proportionate partner status, accreditations, insurance, service capability, support model and future evaluation balance between price, quality and added value. 5.0 PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT APPROACH INDICATIVE PROCUREMENT TIMEFRAME 7.0 Indicative milestones: PME published 10th September 2026 ; responses due via eTendersNI by 3.00 pm on 24th September 2026; procurement launch October , contract award December ; licensing renewal / contract commencement 31st January 2027. Lot 1: .

sig_f47670163e5812efefba.description: The Initiative D21 e.V. ("contracting authority") is a non-partisan, non-profit network of business, politics, science and civil society that campaigns for the promotion of digital transformation in Germany. Through studies, recommendations for action and dialogue formats, it supports the development of a high-performing, inclusive and future-oriented digital society. The subject of the tender is the execution, evaluation and documentation of two population-representative surveys within the scope of the project "The digital society - understanding, shaping, strengthening. Mechanisms, levers and success conditions of digital transformation (DiGeVe)" for the Initiative D21. Based on the collected and evaluated data, two publications are to be produced in the years 2027 and 2029. The project is funded by monies from the Federal Ministry of Education, Family, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth. The Initiative D21 is a leading non-profit civil society actor and the largest non-partisan network for the digital society in Germany. With around 140 member organisations from business, science, politics and civil society, the association, as an independent platform, combines social benefit with technological innovation. The association regularly publishes evidence-based studies, such as the D21 Digital Index and the eGovernment MONITOR. These studies provide a sound data basis for a digital transformation that both promotes equal opportunities and social progress and secures economic and state future viability. The studies are published on the association's website. The contractor (hereinafter referred to as the contractor) must carry out two large-scale quantitative primary surveys. To this end, the development and programming of the survey design, including the programming of questionnaires, are to be provided by the contractor (see chapter 2.1 of the specification of services). The contractor must regularly coordinate with the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the CA) regarding the content development and design of the questionnaires. The contractor must operatively carry out these data collections (see chapter 2.2 of the specification of services). Operational execution includes at least sampling as well as field management via the weighting and delivery of the quality-assured raw dataset. The data determined as a result of the data collection are to be prepared and statistically evaluated in two runs (see chapter 2.3 of the specification of services). In doing so, the contractor is to design complex statistical analyses and coordinate them jointly with the CA. Subsequently, the statistical analyses are to be carried out. The CA reserves the right to perform quality assurance on the results of the statistical analyses. The substantive interpretation of the results remains with the CA. The contractor must continuously cooperate with the CA (see chapter 2.4 of the specification of services). For further details, see the procurement documents.
sig_f47670163e5812efefba.title: Main study DiGeVe - Data collection & evaluation

sig_f64fbd7b1b6867fc525b.description: The City of Helsinki's Culture and Leisure Division is developing data-driven management and, in connection with this, visitor counting for its locations and related solutions. Visitor data is one of the most important key performance indicators for operations: visitor data is used, among other things, for resource allocation, operational planning and development, and for assessing the impact of operations. The goal of the visitor counting service is to collect comparable and accurate visitor data from the division's locations as automatically as possible for analysis and reporting needs. The SaaS (Software as a Service) provided by the supplier includes at least: • production of visitor data from the counting target according to the needs defined by the division • transmission of visitor data by providing an interface (interface service) for transferring data to the division's data warehouse • transmission of visitor data by providing a user interface (user interface service) for viewing the data • collection of visitor data from devices, as well as monitoring and reporting of data accuracy and coverage (incl. verification counts for measurement at defined intervals) • devices used for visitor data collection as a lifecycle service (HaaS service, Hardware as a Service): - installation, commissioning, maintenance, servicing, functionality testing and calibration of devices - monitoring of device operation - removal and recycling of device installations. The contracting authority is currently surveying the procurement of a new data platform and will put it out to tender in approximately late 2026. By submitting a tender, the tenderer undertakes to assist with integrations and to provide an interface from the visitor counting service to the data platform. The estimated total value of the procurement excluding VAT is 1 680 000,00 euros. The estimated value includes the actual contract period of two (2) years and, in addition, one (1) two-year (2) option period. The procurement is divided into three (3) different lots: - lot 1: indoor locations - lot 2: outdoor locations - lot 3: multi-purpose outdoor locations. The tenderer may submit a tender for as many lots as they wish. Tenderers will be selected for the framework agreement based on the most economically advantageous tender. Qualitative requirements (quality criteria) have been set as minimum requirements for the devices and services to be procured, which the offered devices and services must meet. In addition, the price comparison will compare the maximum prices per lot (hereinafter ceiling price) from cheapest to most expensive. The supplier provides a ceiling price according to the most demanding example location of the lot defined by the contracting authority. Based on the tender competition, a framework agreement will be concluded for the subject of the procurement, to which five (5) contract suppliers who have submitted the lowest ceiling price per lot will be selected, unless there are fewer tenderers meeting the requirements. The suppliers selected for the framework agreement do not have exclusive rights to the procurements covered by the framework agreement, but the contracting authority has the right to procure the same subject of procurement also from outside this framework agreement. The contracting authority also does not commit to specific procurement volumes during the framework agreement. A more detailed description of the subject of the procurement is described in this invitation to tender and its appendices. The locations in the lot have one or more entrances to the site. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different indoor locations. Such locations include, for example, libraries, youth centres, cultural centres and sports halls. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 80 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have one or more restricted or unrestricted entrances. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different outdoor locations. Such locations include, for example, fenced tennis courts, skate parks, events in urban space, beaches, outdoor islands and trails. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 82 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have several restricted or unrestricted entrances to the space and it includes several service points or spaces. Breakdown of visitor data is essential. Such locations include, for example, sports parks. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 38 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.
sig_f64fbd7b1b6867fc525b.title: Procurement of visitor counting as a comprehensive service, framework agreement 2026-2028 (2028-2030)

sig_f6fe09a24878199d77b7.description: Numera Palvelut Oy (hereinafter Numera or Contracting Authority) requests your tender for a joint procurement concerning Printing and information services (Multifunction devices and related services) in accordance with the call for tender documents. The procurement is not divided into lots; instead, a single supplier will be selected, with whom Numera will draw up mutual procurement contracts.: The competitive tendering is conducted via an open procedure. The selection criterion used for the competitive tendering is the most economically advantageous tender, and the comparison criterion is [the best price-quality ratio]. Detailed information on scoring and comparison criteria is presented in the section Criteria for the subject of the procurement of the call for tender. If several tenderers achieve the exact same score with their tender, the Contracting Authority will draw lots to determine the winner. Drawing lots is an accepted method in procurement law case law. Parallel tenders and alternative tenders are not accepted. The procurement contract shall be valid for a fixed term of two (2) years. Thereafter, the contract shall continue until further notice. Numera's customer communities using the joint procurement and potentially joining it during the contract period are stated in appendix one (1) of the draft agreement. The procurement contract shall enter into force once the procurement decision has become legally binding or the Market Court has granted an enforcement permit for the procurement decision, and both contracting parties have signed a written procurement contract. The notice period for terminating the contract is six (6) months for both contracting parties. sig_f75214932dc650000c29.description: The tender process comprises a contract for the contracting authority's procurement of the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The procurement of an enterprise resource planning system is part of the contracting authority's new strategy to create a greater degree of uniformity in the IT area across the contracting authority's organisation with a view to realising both financial and quality benefits. "Uniformity" does not mean that all units in the organisation must use identical solutions, but that IT decisions are made on the basis of common principles, procedures and guidelines. In this way, coherence, standardisation where possible, and flexibility where necessary are ensured. The purpose of procuring a new ERP system is thus to achieve a higher degree of standardisation and harmonisation of processes across the organisation. This is intended to ensure simpler workflows, reduced complexity and more cost-effective operation. The contracting authority wishes the new ERP system to offer modern technological capabilities, including support for machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI) and other tools that can contribute to increased automation and decision support. Likewise, easy access to new functionality via ongoing upgrades is a central requirement, so that the organisation can quickly exploit new opportunities without extensive customisation. The ERP system must function as the central core of the organisation's transaction layer, where all significant data and processes are collected and handled. This is intended to ensure data consistency, transparency and support an integrated ecosystem of surrounding applications. The annual value of the contract is estimated at three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. In addition, there is a one-off implementation with an expected cost of three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. The duration of the contract is set at 10 years, which gives a total estimated contract value of 33 million DKK excl. VAT. The total volume is indicative only and based on historical data and can therefore not be considered a guarantee of future turnover.
sig_f75214932dc650000c29.title: Competitive procedure with negotiation regarding a contract for the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system for Kredsløb A/S

sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.description: The far-reaching impact and rate of innovation in the computer and information science and engineering fields has been remarkable, generating economic prosperity and enhancing the quality of life for people throughout the world. More than a decade ago, the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE) established the Expeditions in Computing (Expeditions) program to build on past successes and provide the CISE research and education community with the opportunity to pursue ambitious, fundamental research agendas that promise to define the future of computing and information. In planning Expeditions projects, investigators are strongly encouraged to come together within or across departments or institutions to combine their creative talents in the identification of compelling, transformative research agendas that look ahead by at least a decade and promise disruptive innovations in computer and information science and engineering for many years to come. Now funded at levels up to $15,000,000 for seven years, Expeditions projects represent some of the largest single investments currently made by the CISE directorate. Together with the Science and Technology Centers and the National Artificial Intelligence Research Institutes that CISE supports, Expeditions projects form the centerpiece of the directorate's center-scale award portfolio. With awards funded at levels that promote the formation of large research teams, CISE recognizes that concurrent research advances in multiple fields or sub-fields are often necessary to stimulate deep and enduring outcomes. The awards made in this program will complement research areas supported by other CISE programs, which target particular computer and information science and engineering fields. Additionally, CISE offers Innovation Transition (InTrans) awards for teams nearing the end of their Expeditions as well as Secure and Trustworthy Cyberspace (SaTC) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) Frontier projects. The goal of InTransis to continue the long-term vision and objectives of CISE’s center-scale projects. Through InTrans awards, CISE will provide limited funds to match industry support.
sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.title: Expeditions in Computing

sig_f84f33b219fc3a9f720d.description: The BMWE intends to tender a contract for the "FRAUEN unternehmen" (WOMEN in business) office. The office is to develop the content of the new priorities specified by the BMWE and develop new measures to sensitise girls and women to professional self-employment together with the "role model entrepreneurs" (VUs). In order to prevent or counteract social conditioning and to promote a cliché-free choice of career, the intention is to increasingly address general education schools in addition to vocational schools and universities. It is in the interest of the contracting authority (CA) to cooperate with other programmes/projects funded by the BMWE, such as the SCHULEWIRTSCHAFT-PREIS or the BMWE initiative group "Gründung in school" (Founding in school), and, where sensible and possible, to develop proposals for cooperation in order to exploit potential synergies. Furthermore, the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative is also a measure from the joint action plan "More female entrepreneurs for the SME sector". As part of the action plan, the office also participates actively as a member of the network. Through suitable measures, the topic of "female entrepreneurship" is to be placed more strongly in the public eye. To this end, a greater reach in social media is also to be achieved. Furthermore, a targeted expansion of the circle of active VUs is expected, in particular to include female entrepreneurs from the fields of skilled crafts, STEM, AI and digitalisation, from the East German federal states and rural areas, as well as those female entrepreneurs who have themselves taken over a business. The core tasks of the contract include, in particular, the provision of personnel, basic equipment for carrying out network coordination and project management, travel activities, and internal and external communication, including the annual preparation of a media concept (details in the respective work package). The following services are to be taken into account: - AP 1: Central contact point for VUs and all those interested in the initiative - AP 2: Matching of VUs with the target group - AP 3: Development and expansion of the external network/addressing multipliers and network partners - AP 4: External communication – strengthening the general visibility of the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative as well as the commitment of the VUs within the framework of the initiative - AP 5: Internal communication – strengthening the internal network of VUs and supporting the exchange of experience among VUs - AP 6: Monitoring, evaluation of the initiative and preparation of results - AP 7: Targeted expansion of the circle of VUs Lot LOT-0000: Office of the BMWE initiative "FRAUEN unternehmen". sig_f8ae74998e3e5212bd22.description: The subject of the contract is the upgrade and expansion of the multi-channel citizen information and service system 1555, which has been operated by 1/10/2022 as a single service hub for citizens and businesses regarding matters falling within the remit of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and its supervised bodies. As part of the upgrade, the digital architecture and software subsystems, such as the web portal, knowledge base, artificial intelligence solutions and ticketing, are being enhanced so that 1555 can gradually transition from a predominantly voice-centric model to a balanced service model, where more complex and sensitive cases remain with human service through the reinforcement of specialised representatives, while simpler cases are closed via self-service services and automation. Specifically, the use of AI solutions is provided for both citizens and representatives, such as IVRs and AI agents for intent recognition and routing to digital solutions or appropriate specialised representatives, agent assist tools that retrieve content from the knowledge base to reduce errors and handling time, as well as analytics to understand requests and better plan staffing. At the same time, interoperability at the infrastructure or service level with the Citizen Request Management System (CC ticketing) and the utilisation of data from ticketing and the knowledge base are being enhanced, with provision for continuous improvement through feedback and conversation analysis. The operation of specialised consultants will be expanded and enhanced so that citizens have even greater access to personalised information. Digital systems will be further upgraded and new ones introduced with the aim of enhancing service delivery. A team of experts will be able to carry out targeted studies on specific subject matters of the serviced bodies, and surveys may also be conducted to further strengthen the bodies through the project. The development and management of the project are organised into work packages as follows: I. Public communication and service structure II. Technical Infrastructures III. Satisfaction surveys and Quality Assurance IV. Strengthening of bodies on specific subject matters – special surveys V. Project management VI. Service training Upgrade and expansion of a multi-channel citizen service system 1555

Lot 1: . The Council requires a hub where users can access the system and have the ability to find any needed legislation or regulation to help ensure that whatever project they are working on is compliant with government law and standards. A portal is currently used for this requirement that has 2 parts. The first part is the Construction Information Service legislation and technical information management solution. This service ensures that Fife Council will have access to the correct, current and complaint business critical information year-round. This service provides the Council access to 27,000 full-text PDFs with the ability to save, view, print, download, copy and paste any of these documents. There are over 350 publishers that add documents to this service. Fife Council require something equal in quality and quantity to this. The second part of the portal is Occupational Health & Safety Information Service. This single source library holds more than 90,000 documents from more than 400 publishers. The focus of this service is Health, Safety, Environmental and Fire. This service relates to risk management, hazardous substances and operations, control principles, movement of people and vehicles. Fife Council also require something that is equal in quality and quantity to this part of the portal. Overall, the current solution allows access to over 2.3 million industry standards, over 10 thousand engineering manuals, handbooks, reference books, over 76 million technical articles, journals and books, over 107 million patents, patent applications, unity models and abstracts and over 39 million industry-to-industry reference links across all hosted content

sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.description: The Technische Universität Darmstadt is among the leading technical universities in Germany and is characterised by innovative research and an international orientation. The university is structured into 13 departments and over 120 institutes. This structure is supplemented by eight directorates, which handle central administrative tasks such as student services, financial and personnel affairs, construction management and international affairs, thereby ensuring the smooth operation of the university. In total, the TU Darmstadt comprises around 24.300 students and about 5.200 employees. A special role is played here by Directorates IV (Real Estate Management) and V (Construction Management and Technical Operations), which are responsible for the administration and management of a total of 210 buildings on the campus. In the course of these demanding tasks, the directorates have relied on SAP ERP software with various modules since 2000. Since 2004, the SAP RE-FX (Real Estate Management) and SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) modules have been used in the aforementioned areas. For construction management, 2019 SAP PS (Project System) including the construction add-on from PROMOS was implemented. Currently, however, many internal processes in the field of building management and maintenance are mapped outside of SAP, as only a small part of the technical requirements can be implemented in SAP. sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.description: The subject of the procurement is the nurse call, fall detection, and movement monitoring systems to be introduced in Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala. Nurse call systems are used in the social, health, and rescue sectors in hospitals, senior centres, care homes, enhanced assisted living units, health centre inpatient wards, rehabilitation units, and other operating environments requiring round-the-clock care and supervision. In addition, the systems are utilised in home care support services and special units where clients may have a sudden need for assistance that requires a response. Nurse call systems are a core part of daily care and nursing work, as well as client and patient safety. They ensure that requests for assistance are forwarded without delay to the right personnel and that nursing staff are able to prioritise their tasks according to the urgency of the situation. At the same time, they support the occupational safety of staff, for example in threatening and hazardous situations, and enable the monitoring, reporting, and development of operations. The importance of nurse call systems is particularly emphasized in situations where clients' functional capacity is impaired, memory disorders are common, or the need for care is continuous. In such cases, the system's operational reliability, ease of use, and integration with other systems are not merely technical features, but factors that directly affect the quality and safety of care. The objective of the procurement is to ensure that the solutions in use meet current and future needs. This requires the systems to be scalable, compatible with other technologies, and capable of adapting to various care environments without complicating the use of the systems. At the same time, it is ensured that the solutions to be procured fulfil obligations regarding data protection, information security, and official requirements. Overall, nurse call systems are a critical part of the functionality of the service system, and their procurement must be carried out in a way that long-term supports the quality, safety, and cost-efficiency of services. The aim of the tendering procedure for the framework arrangement is to find up to five suppliers capable of delivering a nurse call system to the sector's sites that can handle traditional nurse calls (a client/patient can call a nurse to the room) and additionally utilise new technology that allows the system to proactively alert a nurse to the client's/patient's location in connection with risk situations (e.g., getting out of a bed, falling). The new technology aims to improve client/patient safety within the limits defined by law. A nurse call system is required in all new and renovated hospitals, senior centres, etc. In addition, the social, health, and rescue sector has several sites where a nurse call system was procured in the past but has become obsolete, and for which the supplier no longer provides maintenance and support. These obsolete systems must be replaced with new ones. The solutions that are the subject of the procurement will primarily be acquired as a comprehensive service provided by the suppliers selected for the framework arrangement. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tenders.
sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.title: Nurse call systems

sig_fa36135e9c87227e1d5d.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information, through which the South Karelia Wellbeing Services County invites system suppliers to register for a potential procurement. This is a request for information/market dialogue, through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying potential system suppliers for a shift planning and working time management system. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social and healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 5 500 professionals from various fields. The vision is to be a pioneering community, which is why the wellbeing services county has accessible services, the healthiest population in Finland, and the happiest employees. Strategic priorities include impactful services that meet people's needs, as well as a skilled and motivated frontline team. The goal is, among other things, that all services are clearly guided by indicators derived from operational impact and that operations are organised in an economically sustainable manner. The personnel programme of Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is based directly on the main strategy guiding the organisation, where one of the key priorities is investing in personnel. Well-being personnel do the right things in the right way and serve their customers in the best possible way. Realising these requires efficient, secure, and user-friendly solutions. The shift planning system plays a central role in supporting the smoothness of everyday operations, the well-being of personnel at work, and cost-efficiency. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer comprehensive solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The information obtained can be used to assess what kind of solutions are on the market, what benefits they produce, and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Understand system functionalities and key use cases 2. Clarify integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 3. Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 4. Survey delivery and service models 5. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers, which can be used to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where key functionalities are already implemented. Presentations of solutions under development or only at the concept level are not desired in this context. Registration for the market dialogue is made by the service provider's response regarding the system on offer. Marketing videos are not accepted as responses. The response must indicate the following: - What ready-made solutions and services they offer - In what kind of environments the solutions have been implemented (example descriptions, not mandatory references) - Key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue. All participants are offered equal opportunities to receive information about the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, and no procurement decisions will be made based on it. If the contracting authority considers it necessary, the possibility of holding individual meetings is reserved. The market dialogue will focus particularly on how the solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but subject areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: - Usability - Mobile use of the system - Technical features - The system as a support for well-being at work - Personnel and competence - Data-driven management and reporting - Implementation, training, and change management - Continuous service and development - Pricing and lifecycle services. Participating suppliers are requested to provide presentations on different use cases. Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions through demos or practical example situations. The wellbeing services county will provide questions and use case examples in advance, which will guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared equally. The market dialogue will be carried out as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 120–150 minutes. The supplier has the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. The wellbeing services county will also present pre-defined questions that support the equality and comparability of the discussion. Meetings will be held on the following days: 15.9., 18.9., 23.9. and 28.9.2026. The exact time will be agreed upon with the registered suppliers based on the order of registration and the coordination of schedules. The language of any presentations/meetings is Finnish. Registrations and brochures about the systems are requested to be sent by 11.9.2026 at 12:00 to the email address: hankinnat@ekhva.fi. This request for information/market survey does not request, and no tenders are given to this request for information; instead, this ONLY requests information related to the procurement. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not affect the tenderer's position in a potential call for tenders. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (supplier) to participate in a call for tenders, and responding to this notice is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual call for tenders later. The grounds for the decision-making of the call for tenders will be specified during the process. Those participating in the market survey do not have the right to receive compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement in question. The submitted material will be treated as confidential in accordance with Section 24 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities, subsection 1, point 20.
sig_fa36135e9c87227e1d5d.title: Request for Information/Market Dialogue: Rostering and working time management system

sig_fcbf12f92719f165318a.description: PSD Scotland intends to procure a Service Integration and Management contract for the transition, stabilisation and continued delivery of selected national digital services supporting health and care across Scotland. The successful supplier will act as prime contractor and provide a single point of accountability for end-to-end service delivery, integration and performance. The supplier will also be responsible for the management of any subcontractors and dependencies with other providers and Authority teams. The initial priority will be to maintain continuity and stabilise these business-critical services as they transition away from the existing National IT Contract, while establishing a strong foundation for subsequent improvement and modernisation. Lot 1: . PSD Scotland intends to procure a Service Integration and Management contract for selected national digital services supporting clinical, operational and administrative functions across NHS Scotland. The procurement will establish replacement arrangements for services currently delivered under the National IT Contract, which is due to expire on 31 March 2028. The principal objective is to maintain uninterrupted delivery of these business-critical services throughout transition and thereafter. The anticipated scope includes services and applications supporting Primary and Community Care, National Screening and Child Health, together with other services confirmed in the procurement documents. Depending on the requirements of each service, the contract may include application support, maintenance and development, as well as the associated infrastructure, platform, integrations and data services. IT Service Management capabilities are also required for end-to-end operation. The detailed application scope, service boundaries and allocation of responsibilities will be defined in the tender documentation. The successful supplier will act as the prime contractor, providing a single point of accountability for the contract. The supplier will be expected to coordinate its subcontractors and work effectively with the Authority’s retained teams and other internal and external providers. Service continuity will take precedence during the initial transition, followed by stabilisation to address supportability, resilience, cyber security, regulatory compliance and technical-debt risks. Once services have been stabilised, the supplier will support proportionate and staged modernisation through software and infrastructure engineering practices. Intended outcomes include: -Secure, compliant and resilient services -Clear and measurable service performance -Visibility of costs and dependencies -Improved value for money The supplier will also be expected to support knowledge transfer, effective service ownership, data portability and robust exit arrangements, reducing long-term supplier dependency and preserving future competition. The Authority will retain accountability for strategic direction, governance, business outcomes and service ownership throughout the contract.

With this invitation, we request tenderers interested in the procurement to register and participate in the dialogue concerning the procurement. The dialogue seeks information on the tenderers operating in the market and the features of the services offered in relation to the contracting authority's needs. sig_fded948ea627b084551a.description: The U.S. National Science Foundation Directorate for Engineering (NSF ENG) supports foundational research for electrical, communications and computing systems through the following programs: The Electronic, Photonic, Magnetic, and Quantum Devices (EPMQD) program supports foundational engineering research on novel classical and quantum devices, exploring matter’s electronic, photonic, and magnetic properties to enable new applications. The Circuits and Systems for Communications and Sensing (CSCS) program supports foundational engineering research on classical and quantum aspects of advanced components, systems, and signal processing for communications and sensing. The Energy, Power, Control, and Learning (EPCL) program supports foundational research on systems and control, learning, optimization, artificial intelligence, and networked multi-agent systems, and their applications, with emphasis on power and energy systems. NSF ENG anticipates a portfolio of ENG: Electrical, Communications, and Computing Systems (ECCS) awards with a range of budgets and durations. Estimated program budget, number of awards, and average award size/duration are subject to the availability of funds. NSF ENG is particularly interested in intellectually ambitious and potentially transformative foundational research. Proposals need not promise a near-term product, deployment, or commercial outcome, nor need they address later-stage development to be competitive.

sig_ffca1b8fec1781953c67.description: The tender process comprises the conclusion of one (1) contract regarding the Contracting Authority's procurement of the development of an AI-based simulation tool for training child interviews. Based on this tender, one (1) joint contract will be concluded between the supplier and the Responsible Contracting Authority, cf. point 1.2 of the tender conditions, which acts on behalf of all participating contracting authorities. The Responsible Contracting Authority is Professionshøjskolen Absalon, which is authorised to manage all rights and obligations under the contract and acts as the contracting party towards the supplier. The supplier may therefore only direct claims against the Responsible Contracting Authority. Other participating contracting authorities are not direct contracting parties and are not liable either individually or jointly for the performance of the contract. Professionshøjskolen Absalon, in collaboration with the other university colleges, Red Barnet, Barndom Uden Vold and Ole Kirk’s Fond, is offering a contract for the development of an AI-based simulation tool, which is referred to in the tender documentation as the Solution. The purpose is to strengthen the competencies of social workers and social work students to conduct interviews with children in vulnerable situations, including children who may have been exposed to violence or abuse. The Solution must create a realistic, safe and learning-oriented training environment where users can prepare for child interviews, conduct interviews with digital avatars, receive guidance and feedback from a Tutor and subsequently analyse their interviews for the purpose of learning and reflection. It must be capable of being used in social work education, in continuing and further education programmes and in municipal practice. The first version, which this tender covers, must provide the possibility for speech- and text-based interaction with four avatars aged 9–11 years, representing different backgrounds and case types. In addition, there is a Tutor who supports the user before, during and after the interview through preparatory information, ongoing professional hints and subsequent debriefing. The Solution must accommodate both full interview processes and shorter modules where individual interview techniques can be trained in isolation. In the long term, the ambition is to expand the solution with more advanced modalities such as facial expressions and body language as well as real-time analysis of non-verbal communication. The Contracting Authority therefore wishes to attract suppliers who can not only deliver the tendered solution but can also think visionarily in terms of creating a future-proof and innovative platform. The Responsible Contracting Authority provides an extensive knowledge base in the form of practice-oriented cases, anonymised child interviews and the expertise of professionals, and will also contribute actively with professional sparring during development. The tenders will be evaluated on feasibility and risk assessment, functionality and security, the realism of the avatars, the professional quality of the tutor as well as the overall user experience and technical robustness. The Responsible Contracting Authority is entitled to terminate the contract at Partial Delivery Day 1 (POC), solely for the purpose of bringing the project to an end, if it turns out during Partial Delivery 1 - POC that there are technical challenges which make it impossible to develop a suitable and usable Solution for the purpose that the contract supports, cf. point 31.2.1 of the Contract. However, it is the clear intention of the Responsible Contracting Authority to complete the development of a complete Solution that functions according to its purpose. Due to the established budget, the Contracting Authority has set a price ceiling for the Delivery Consideration. The Delivery Consideration, including the price for the Clarification Phase and the Delivery, cf. Contract Annex 01 – Schedule, must thus be a maximum of five (5) million DKK excl. VAT. Within the established price ceiling of five (5) million DKK excl. VAT, the Contracting Authority wishes to promote solutions that combine high technical quality and a high level of innovation. With this tender, the Contracting Authority aims to support a competition that is not only based on price, but also on the Tenderers' ability to think long-term and visionarily. The Contracting Authority therefore explains the strategic and technological ambitions for the Solution in order to encourage tenderers to present proposals that reflect a future-proof and technologically advanced approach. At the same time, it is important for the Contracting Authority that the Solution can be operated sustainably within the financial frameworks that apply to the joint operations of the university colleges. The Contracting Authority therefore wishes to enter into a contract with a Supplier who can ensure creativity and technical ingenuity in relation to developing a Solution that meets the desired needs, but which can at the same time be operated by the university colleges jointly - where interview flow is weighted higher than visualisation of the child's non-verbal language.
